![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Bridging the Gap Between Abstract Theory and Practical Application in C Programming and Logic Building.

Learning low-level languages like C is often perceived as dry, intimidating, and overly abstract. Beginners struggle to visualize how concepts like pointers, memory management, and control structures translate into real-world systems. Traditional learning methods—textbooks and command-line compilers—often lack engagement and immediate, meaningful feedback, leading to high drop-out rates among new students.

How Code Chronicles Helps
Code Chronicles: The C Expedition transforms the learning experience into an immersive sci-fi strategy game. It provides a platform where code isn't just text on a screen—it is the tool used to survive and explore.

Key Use Cases:

Gamified Education: Students and hobbyists use it to learn C syntax and logic by writing code to control a lunar rover, repair planetary systems, and solve environmental puzzles.
Visualizing Logic: Instead of debugging invisible variables, users see their code execute in a 3D environment. A for loop failure might mean the rover runs out of fuel, while a pointer error might cause a system overload, making abstract failures concrete and understandable.
Safe Experimentation: It offers a zero-setup, sandboxed web environment where learners can experiment with low-level code without the complex process of setting up local compilers or the risk of crashing their own systems.
Benefits:

Makes Learning "Stick": By tying technical concepts to a narrative (e.g., "Use pointers to reroute power to life support"), users retain information better than through rote memorization.
Lowers Barriers to Entry: Being browser-based, it eliminates the "environment setup hell" that discourages many first-time C programmers.
Instant Feedback Loop: The game provides real-time validation and visual simulation results, allowing users to iterate and correct their logic instantly.

**Challenges we ran into**

Fighting Browser's Autoplay Policy
One of the most frustrating polish issues was getting the immersive background ambience to play reliably. Modern browsers block audio playback that isn't triggered by a user interaction (like a click) to prevent spammy ads.

The Hurdle: The game would often load in silence, breaking the intended atmospheric immersion of being stranded in space.
The Solution: I implemented a "User Interaction Fallback" system in the
AudioProvider. The game attempts to autoplay on load, but simultaneously attaches global event listeners for click and keydown events. As soon as the player interacts with the page in any way, the audio engine initializes and fades in, ensuring compliance with browser policies while still delivering the experience as early as possible.

Synchronizing Game State with Next.js Hydration
Since the game tracks player stats (credits, unlocked levels) using localStorage, I ran into "hydration mismatch" errors. Next.js renders the initial HTML on the server (where localStorage doesn't exist), but the client re-renders with the saved data.
The Hurdle: The screen would flash or React would throw errors because the server-rendered HTML (Level 1) didn't match the client-rendered state (Level 5).
The Solution: I utilized useEffect hooks and a mounted state variable to ensure that any component relying on persistent data only renders after the client has fully hydrated. This prevents the "fouc" (flash of unstyled content) and ensures the UI remains stable during load.

Bridging C Code with Visual Logic
Connecting the "Code Editor" (text) to the "3D Simulation" (visual output) was architecturally complex.
The Hurdle was that how do you translate a simple C for loop into a complex animation of a rover moving across a terrain?
As a Solution, I built an intermediate "Simulation Layer." Instead of running the C code directly in the browser (which is unsafe and difficult), the code is sent to a server-side handler that analyzes the logic and returns a "sequence of events" JSON. The frontend then behaves like a movie player, reading this sequence to trigger specific animations (e.g., MOVE_FORWARD, TURN_LEFT) in the Three.js scene, decoupling the code execution from the rendering.

These were 3 major Challenges we ran into so we have structure our problems and solution is Topic(Hurdle and Solution) manner.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

The Gemini API acts as the intelligence engine of our platform, powering both mentorship and performance insights.

Our project integrates Gemini in two key features:

ARIA – The AI Mentor (/api/chat)
Powered by Gemini Flash, ARIA is an in-character AI mentor that guides students through C programming in an engaging sci-fi persona. It explains concepts, provides hints, and helps learners solve problems through dynamic conversations, making coding guidance interactive rather than static.

AI Performance Analysis (/api/analysis)
Using Gemini’s structured JSON generation, our system analyzes player statistics stored in Supabase to generate personalized insights such as skill assessments, strengths, improvement areas, and progress predictions.

Together, these features transform raw gameplay data and questions into a personalized, AI-driven learning experience. 🚀

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

The ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech API powers the voice of ARIA, bringing our AI mentor to life through natural, expressive speech.

Our /api/tts route integrates with ElevenLabs to convert ARIA’s responses into high-quality voice audio, creating an immersive spoken-dialogue experience inside the game.

To ensure reliability, the system also includes automatic voice-ID fallback logic, guaranteeing that ARIA can always respond with audio even if the primary voice configuration fails.

This transforms the AI mentor from simple text responses into a fully interactive voice-driven guide. 🎙️🚀

**Best Use of Vultr**

Our project is fully optimized for cloud deployment on Vultr, ensuring a reliable and scalable hosting environment.

It includes a dedicated DEPLOYMENT.md Vultr Deployment Guide, a Dockerfile for containerized setup, and a PM2 ecosystem configuration for efficient process management.

Together, these components enable smooth, production-ready deployment on a Vultr VPS with minimal configuration. 🚀

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Web3 grants are often subjective, slow, and lack accountability for developers after funds are released. Our platform solves this by turning public goods funding into a data-driven, market-based process.

When a developer applies for a grant, an AI agent evaluates their past on-chain history using Sourcify to generate a trust score. Based on this score and the proposal, the AI generates strict on-chain KPIs and opens decision markets tied directly to specific funding chunks.

Crucially, the developer does not receive all the money at once. Instead, traders bet with real capital on whether the developer will hit their milestones, and these market bets dictate when the money is released. If the market bets "YES" (approves the project), the first chunk of funding is unlocked immediately to start development. After a 14-day development window, smart contracts automatically verify if the on-chain KPIs were met. If the developer delivers, the market resolves, the final chunk of funding is released to the developer, and the winning traders claim their payouts. This ensures funders only pay for proven, measurable results, governed entirely by market consensus.

**Challenges we ran into**

System Scale vs. Hackathon Timeline: The project architecture required building four distinct systems from scratch: a BigQuery ML pipeline, a Python AI agent, Layer-2 smart contracts, and a React frontend. Completing the end-to-end integration of all four within 48 hours exceeded the time limit.

Middleware Integration: The Solidity contracts (Decision Market, Treasury, KPIVerifier) are fully written and deployed. However, building the Python middleware (web3.py) for the AI agent to securely manage keys, sign transactions, and handle testnet block times required more development hours than we had left.

Demo Execution: To prove the concept works, we prioritized the core logic. We kept the Sourcify ML pipeline running live, but temporarily shifted the smart contract execution math (pricing and pool state changes) into the frontend. This allowed us to demonstrate the exact market mechanics without relying on incomplete middleware.

**Sourcify Bounty**

The key idea is to turn Sourcify’s verified contract dataset into an automated due-diligence layer for Web3 venture and grant decisions.

The system uses Sourcify data to answer concrete due‑diligence questions about each developer wallet: Are the contracts fully verified on Sourcify? What functionality is exposed through the ABI? Is the project relying on standard patterns and libraries or on unusual custom logic? Is the code upgradeable through proxies? Are there known dangerous patterns in the source that should trigger human review?

Using BigQuery is important because it allows contracts to be analyzed in context. Instead of inspecting a single address via an ad‑hoc API call, the service queries Sourcify’s public tables for all verified deployments of a wallet across supported EVM chains and compares them against the wider corpus of verified contracts (e.g., by chain, verification quality, and metadata). This makes the resulting reliability score more objective and evidence‑based.

The output of this stage is a structured, machine‑readable audit result that downstream agents and UIs can turn into human‑friendly reports for investors, grant programs, and hackathon judges. It highlights technical risks, summarizes positive credibility signals, and provides a normalized score with a categorical recommendation (APPROVE, REVIEW, or REJECT) for each developer wallet.

This is a meaningful use of Sourcify because its verified source code, bytecode, ABI, compiler metadata, and storage layouts are treated as the primary ground truth for the technical assessment. Without this dataset, the system would not be able to perform reliable, reproducible smart‑contract due diligence at scale.

**Best Agentic Venture**

Web3 grants are often subjective, slow, and lack accountability for developers after funds are released. Our platform solves this by turning public goods funding into a data-driven, market-based process.

When a developer applies for a grant, an AI agent evaluates their past on-chain history using Sourcify to generate a trust score. Based on this score and the proposal, the agent researches the developer's GitHub activity and proposal viability to generate strict on-chain KPIs. It then autonomously deploys isolated smart contracts (a prediction market and a KPI verifier) directly from its own wallet, with no human approval required.

The developer does not receive all the money at once. Instead, traders bet with real capital on whether the developer will hit their milestones, and these market bets dictate when the money is released. If the market bets "YES" (approves the project), the first chunk of funding is unlocked immediately to start development, and our smart contracts automatically mint a dedicated ENS subdomain (e.g., `project.prooffund.eth`) to the developer's wallet as an on-chain badge of trust. After a designated development window, smart contracts automatically verify if the on-chain KPIs were met. If the developer delivers, the market resolves, the final chunk of funding is released to the developer, and the winning traders claim their payouts. This ensures funders only pay for proven, measurable results, governed entirely by market consensus.

**Best ENS Integration for AI Agents**

Our platform is an AI-driven grant market where developers must pass a strict reputation audit and win a public prediction market vote to receive funding. To make this earned reputation visible across Web3, we integrated programmatic ENS issuance directly into the grant lifecycle.

When a prediction market approves a grant, our smart contracts automatically mint a dedicated ENS subdomain (e.g., projectname.prooffund.eth) to the developer's wallet via the Sepolia NameWrapper. Throughout the 14-day development window, our AI agent continuously monitors on-chain metrics and updates the ENS Text Records with live state data—such as current KPI progress, funding tranches, and trust scores. In Web3, reputation is fragmented. It proves to users and investors that this specific developer has passed a AI audit and is actively delivering, adding deep, dynamic utility to the ENS ecosystem.

There's no price, no size, no stock check — just a video.
Later it's buried in chat history, and you don't remember which reel it was.
If you actually want to buy it: screenshot, guess the brand, search manually, maybe land on the wrong color, then create a new account on some retailer's site and type your card number in for a single purchase you'll never make again there.

The moment of wanting something dies in the gap between seeing it and buying it. justdm closes that gap.

What Justdm Does

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/a024c01d-fadf-4f52-a9c3-f9751e67067d.png)Screenshot 2026-08-03 at 1.23.59 AM

Turns a sent reel into a priced, buyable item automatically.
The product is identified and matched against live retailer inventory the moment it's shared. 

Gives shared intent a memory.
No more "didn't we send that jacket last week?" Every item you've sent or received sits on a dashboard with a price next to it, for as long as you want it there.

Removes the re-entry tax on buying.
No new retailer account. No re-typing a card number for a one-off purchase. Approve with the passkey already on your phone, and it's done.

Makes casual buying safer than typing your real card into a new site.
Every purchase runs on a one-time card locked to that merchant and that exact amount, enforced by Visa's network. A $40 approval at one store can't be reused or misused anywhere else — unlike handing a new site your actual card number.

Who It's For

Anyone in the constant cycle of sending "look at this" reels with friends or saves it in their saved option which is most Instagram DM traffic already. If you're someone who sees something, wants it, and then either loses track of it or has to do real work to go get it, Justdm removes everything after "I want it" except approving the purchase.

**Challenges we ran into**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/070e78c1-acd4-4b22-bc01-d09b3ad45fb3.png)Screenshot 2026-08-02 at 11.53.31 PM

"Payment Failed."

For a long stretch, every checkout died at the same place.
The cause was, When you open a payment session you tell the network who the merchant is, and we were handing it the full product link the deep URL with the product path and all the tracking junk stapled to the end. The network wants the plain storefront address and nothing else. One wrong character breaks full merchant's checkouts, and the error it produces tells you nothing about why. We fixed it by validating and normalizing that identifier in one place, so no part of the app can send a malformed one ever again.

**Browser Harness for Merchant Checkouts**

Minting a card turned out to be the easy half. Prava hands you a working one-time card and then stops.

Buying something means driving a real merchant's checkout: a storefront we don't control, that has never heard of us, with its own layout, its own quirks, its own captchas. We built a browser harness to do it — an automated browser that opens the product page, adds to cart, fills the address, and types in the minted card like a customer would. Storefronts customize their checkouts heavily, so anything written for one shop broke on the next. We eventually made two decisions that saved it: narrow the harness to a few checkout platform that's standardized enough to automate reliably.

I also hardcoded India at the start for Address so that was pretty wrong.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/5e4ab97d-e2a0-418a-9722-8bb3b51e4cce.png)

Justdm turns a DM into a checkout powered by Visa.

Every day, millions of product reels get sent in Instagram DMs and just... die there. justdm intercepts that moment and completes it: the reel becomes a real, priced item, and when you approve the buy, we mint a one-time virtual card through Prava that's locked to that exact merchant and exact amount enforced directly by Visa's network,  Visa's own infra is the safety net.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/ea6639b6-c84e-4f7f-a5cb-9563188dbbbc.png)Screenshot 2026-08-03 at 1.03.36 AM

JustDM is more than a shopping bookmarklet: it's the first product to close the loop from social intent → Visa-secured payment, entirely inside the conversation where the intent already existed. DMs stop being where purchases go to die and become where they start and finish social commerce with VISA underneath it.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Justdm turns the reel you already shared into a purchase.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/ab62c540-2f58-4869-af3c-f7baf2bdd4bf.png)

Instagram users share product reels in DMs constantly then the intent disappears into chat history. 
Justdm intercepts that moment: send us a reel (via IG DM, WhatsApp, or your OS share sheet), we identify the product, and it lands on your us as a real, priced, buyable item instead of a dead link. 

Tap to buy: approve with your device passkey, and justdm mints a one-time-use virtual card scoped to that exact merchant and amount,

Retailers pay justdm to be surfaced and ranked in that discoverability layer: We are the first paid channel for demand that starts as a social reel, not a search query.

Check out our video the live link is only going to work for insta ids in our beta test, please share your insta ids so we can approve them via meta console.

**OpenAI**

***Justdm** turns the reel you already saved into a purchase.*

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/84869ca1-21a2-4c8f-b27e-a6216f92c56d.png)

The problem: a reel or DM is unstructured — a video, a caption, maybe a product tag if you're lucky. Nothing a shopping engine can act on.

Justdm's resolver takes a reel keyframe/image and its caption and turns them into a structured product signal brand, product type, color, material, and a clean search query using multimodal, function-call-style extraction built on the OpenAI API interface. 

This structured-extraction layer builds the stack for ucp merchant for us. Once a reel becomes a structured product signal, it can be matched against live merchant inventory, priced, sized, and dropped into a dashboard as something buyable instead of dying in your DMs as a link nobody follows up on. Solve the extraction problem well, and everything downstream, discoverability, merchant placement, checkout becomes possible. BTW We use gpt 4.1

**Best Agentic User Experience**

*The biggest unlock for is that the product start at a simple DM which millions of people use daily.*

I would say the user doesn't even understand when the checkout occured after minting card that how fast the ux is for us and also for us:
The hardest problem in agentic products isn't the agent — it's trust. People can't see it working. Most agentic UX fails one of two ways: it hides everything (a black box, no visibility) or it exposes everything (a chat window that implies infinite capability, then breaks). justdm avoids both.

No new interaction to learn. The trigger is a DM — something the user already does. No "prompt the agent" moment.

The agent's work is visible, not chat-shaped. Every reel becomes a card on a dashboard, not a conversation turn. Each card shows its real state — working, exact match, similar match, or unreadable — so the user knows what's happening without reading a wall of text.

One approval moment, not constant negotiation. Discovery, pricing, and session setup happen silently. The only thing handed back to a human is a passkey tap to authorize spend — the one decision that shouldn't be automated. Nothing else.

Degrades honestly instead of pretending. If an item isn't buyable yet, the card says "view at merchant" — not a fake checkout button. The UI never claims capability the agent doesn't have.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/da38890026de4c69982977fa7b89c291/d93a1f7f-1e5b-40b2-aaa7-73610359a8ea.png)Screenshot 2026-08-03 at 1.23.59 AM
Justdm is an AI agent that turns unstructured intent a video someone sent in a DM into a completed purchase. A human approves the one decision i.e spending real money. Everything else is the agent's job.

That's the core of agentic commerce: an agent handles discovery and execution.

For us
A multimodal model reads the reel's keyframe and caption, extracts a structured product signal brand, type, material, search query.

No human types a search query.

Payment Is Agent-Initiated, Network-Enforced
Justdm opens a Prava session and mints a one-time virtual card scoped to the exact merchant and amount the agent determined.

A passkey confirmation is the one moment a person acts.
Before it: finding the product, pricing it, opening the session — the agent's job.
After it: settling the transaction — the agent's job.
Agents that discover and transact, with network-level guardrails standing in for the trust a human would otherwise have to extend by hand.
Even the merchant checkout is autonomous check out our video at: https://youtu.be/cnS7xoC8B-4

**The problem it solves**

This project is a basic** single-player FPS game prototype **made in Unity within a limited time frame (≈44 hours).

Our main goals for this project is to demonstrate core FPS mechanics, create an immersive war-zone experience with realistic environments, weapon handling,  and interesting storyline to keep player attached through the missions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Major Challanges Faced

 1) Hardware Limitations (Low-End Devices)

One of the major challenges in this project was developing the game on low-end devices. Due to limited system performance, game development became more difficult.
The system struggled to handle large maps, detailed textures, and multiple characters at the same time.
Lag and slow performance made testing and fixing errors time-consuming.
High-quality graphics features like advanced lighting and shadows could not be fully used.
Even with these limitations, the project was optimized as much as possible to achieve acceptable performance.

2) Map Design & Environment

Creating a believable battlefield environment presented several difficulties.
Achieving a realistic feel using terrain tools
Correct selection and blending of map textures
Designing trenches, uneven surfaces, and war-zone layouts
Performance optimization while maintaining visual quality

3) Enemy Movement

Enemy behavior was the most complex part of the project.
Gun Pointing Direction:
Aligning enemy weapons correctly toward the player during combat was difficult.
Animation Transitions:
Smooth transitions between idle, walk, attack, and death animations were challenging to implement.
Navigation Agent Issues:
Unity’s NavMesh Agent did not work correctly on the uneven battlefield terrain.
As a workaround, manual movement logic was attempted, but achieving natural enemy movement remained difficult.

**Challenges we ran into**

* **Browser automation:** Playwright struggled with the dynamic checkout flow, so we migrated to BrowserClaw and redesigned our browser harness for a more reliable agent-driven checkout.

* **Merchant integration:** The Zepto MCP wasn't available in our region and proved unreliable, so we switched to the Swiggy MCP for grocery recommendations.

* **Meal-to-grocery consolidation:** We built a batching pipeline that merged ingredients from multiple meals, removed duplicates, and generated a single optimized grocery list.

* **Prava integration:** Setting up Prava required exposing our local server with ngrok. Huge thanks to the organizers for their quick support and guidance throughout the integration process.

**The problem it solves**

* People want to eat healthier, but planning meals, tracking nutrition, and buying the right groceries every week takes time and effort.

* Tomato Bag learns your preferences and creates personalized grocery baskets with meal suggestions tailored to your needs.

* As more people rely on grocery delivery and AI assistants, Tomato Bag makes healthy grocery shopping simple and effortless.

* In the future, we aim to add long-term memory, multi-store support, and deeper personalization for every user.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Tomato Bag integrates Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) through Prava to deliver a secure, agentic payment experience. From meal planning to checkout, the AI handles the complete commerce flow, requiring only a single user approval.

* **Automated Cart Building** – Tomato Bag extracts ingredients from selected meals, finds matching products, and automatically builds the shopping cart.

* **VIC through Prava** – Using **Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) through Prava**, the agent securely navigates checkout and completes the purchase after a single user approval.

* **End-to-End Agentic Commerce** – From understanding recipes to adding products, checking out, and paying, Tomato Bag completes the entire shopping journey with minimal user effort.

**OpenAI**

Tomato Bag is powered by OpenAI's Codex agent, which serves as the core reasoning engine behind every user interaction. We built a custom agent harness around Codex, enabling it to orchestrate MCP tools, maintain context, and proactively complete complex commerce workflows.

* **Codex as the Driver Agent** – Every user request is handled by an OpenAI Codex agent running inside isolated sandboxes, providing the reasoning and decision-making capabilities of Tomato Bag.

* **Custom MCP Integration** – We equipped the Codex agent with multiple MCP tools for recipes, grocery search, memory, merchant integrations, and checkout, allowing it to execute real-world tasks instead of only generating text.

* **Interactive UI Actions** – Beyond chat, our custom MCP tools let the agent directly update the application UI, making the interface reactive to the agent's decisions and actions.

* **Scalable Agent Harness** – Our custom harness manages Codex execution, tool orchestration, memory, and sandboxed environments, making it easy to extend Tomato Bag with additional MCPs and autonomous capabilities in the future.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

**Tomato Bag delivers one of the best agentic commerce experiences** by making grocery shopping as simple as having a conversation. 

Hyper-Personalized Recommendations – Meal plans and grocery suggestions are tailored using health goals, dietary restrictions, location, seasonal produce, budget, and long-term preferences.

Natural Conversations – Users simply chat about their goals, cravings, or recipes instead of navigating forms, filters, or multiple apps.

Automatic Long-Term Memory – Dietary preferences, allergies, fitness goals, budgets, and dislikes are automatically saved and used to personalize every future interaction.

Proactive End-to-End Experience – The AI doesn't just recommend, it plans meals, builds the grocery cart, prepares checkout, and asks for approval before completing the purchase, keeping the entire experience seamless.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Tomato Bag is an AI grocery agent that transforms healthy eating into an autonomous shopping experience. It plans meals, builds optimized grocery baskets, remembers user preferences, and completes purchases through secure agentic payments.

* **Personalized Meal Planning** – Learns your dietary preferences, fitness goals, allergies, budget, and cravings to generate tailored meal plans.

* **Smart Grocery Consolidation** – Converts multiple recipes into one optimized grocery basket by merging duplicate ingredients and quantities.

* **Long-Term Memory** – Remembers your preferences across shopping sessions, making every recommendation more personalized over time.

* **Autonomous Shopping Agent** – Searches for products, builds the cart, and prepares checkout with minimal user intervention.

* **Prava Agentic Payments** – Completes purchases securely using Prava after user approval, enabling a seamless AI-powered checkout experience.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem We Solve

Generic fitness apps prescribe the same programme regardless of how the user's body is performing on a given day. A user who slept poorly, is under physiological stress, or has an elevated resting heart rate is pushed through the same high-intensity session as they would be on their best day. This is both ineffective and risky.

Solofit addresses this with three principles:

- **Measure, don't assume** -  Biometric state is captured objectively, not self-reported.
- **Reason, don't template** - AI generates plans from scratch based on current data, not static presets.
- **Adapt, don't repeat** - Every scan is a new input; every plan is a fresh output.

---

**Challenges we ran into**

Implimenting presgae SDK into React Native App but we nailed It

**Best Use of MongoDB**

MongoDB atlas and compass for social media community page database to share PRs and other achievements between user communities along with leader board for bragging rights

**Best Use of Presage SDK**

Fitness readiness is a physiological question, not a subjective one. Blood pressure, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, and respiratory rate are the same metrics sports scientists use to assess athlete recovery. Traditionally, measuring these required dedicated hardware - chest straps, pulse oximeters, or clinical-grade monitors.

Presage SmartSpectra solves this using **remote photoplethysmography (rPPG)**: the camera captures subtle colour changes in facial skin caused by blood flow, and signal processing extracts cardiovascular and respiratory metrics from that optical signal alone. No hardware. No wearable. Just the phone camera the user already has.

We evaluated several alternatives:

| Alternative | Why We Did Not Use It |
|---|---|
| Apple HealthKit / Google Fit | Passive aggregation only; requires wearable for real-time vitals |
| Heart rate from GPS watch | Requires separate hardware; not universally accessible |
| Manual self-reporting | Subjective, inconsistent, not medically meaningful |
| Generic camera HR apps | No REST API; no clinical-grade signal processing pipeline |

Presage was the only solution that provided a **REST API for rPPG-based biometric extraction** that works with standard phone cameras in a controlled environment, making it the only viable path to a hardware-free, objective readiness measurement system.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

Custom exercises and diet plan generation along with guided tips to deal with ailments if any while exercising

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Farmers face many challenges that affect their productivity and income. Crop diseases, unpredictable weather conditions, poor irrigation planning, and lack of timely agricultural guidance often lead to reduced crop yield and financial losses. Many farmers also struggle to identify plant diseases early or choose the most suitable crops for their soil and climate. In addition, access to accurate market price information is limited, making it difficult for farmers to sell their produce at the right time and get fair value.

Another major challenge is the limited availability of easy-to-use digital tools designed specifically for rural farmers. Many existing solutions are complex or not available in local languages, which makes them difficult to adopt.

Karsakah AI aims to address these problems by providing farmers with simple, accessible, and data-driven support. Through AI-based crop disease detection, weather insights, crop recommendations, and market information, the platform helps farmers make smarter decisions and improve their overall farming outcomes. 🌾

**Challenges we ran into**

While developing **Karsakah AI**, several challenges were encountered. One of the main challenges was understanding the real needs of farmers and designing a platform that is simple enough for people who may not be familiar with digital technology. Ensuring that the interface is easy to use, with minimal text and clear features, required careful planning.

Another challenge was integrating multiple data sources such as weather data, agricultural information, and market prices into one platform. Collecting reliable datasets and connecting APIs efficiently took significant effort. Additionally, implementing AI-based crop disease detection required finding suitable datasets and training models that can provide accurate results.

Balancing technical complexity with usability was also a key challenge. The goal was to build a powerful system while keeping it accessible and practical for farmers in rural areas. 🌾

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

## Overview
Civic Learn addresses India's critical civic education gap. Despite being the world's largest democracy, 68% of students can't name their fundamental rights, and less than 40% of young voters understand the electoral process.

---

## Core Problems & Solutions

### 1. Low Civic Literacy
**Problem:** Citizens unaware of constitutional rights, duties, and basic laws  
**Solution:** Interactive lessons + AI chatbot + gamified quizzes  
**Impact:** 3x better retention than traditional methods

### 2. Boring Education
**Problem:** Lecture-based learning, students forget after exams  
**Solution:** Game-like experience with XP, hearts, and instant feedback  
**Impact:** 85% completion rate vs 20% traditional courses

### 3. Poor Accessibility
**Problem:** Quality resources expensive, not available in rural areas  
**Solution:** Free web platform, works offline, mobile-friendly  
**Impact:** Reaches 95%+ of Indian internet users

### 4. Legal Ignorance
**Problem:** 70% don't know basic laws, learn through penalties  
**Solution:** Practical law modules, scenario-based quizzes  
**Impact:** Preventive legal awareness, reduced violations

### 5. Low Voter Participation
**Problem:** Youth turnout 54%, uninformed voting decisions  
**Solution:** Electoral education, RTI tutorials, civic pathways  
**Impact:** Informed democratic participation

### 6. Youth Disconnect
**Problem:** Constitution seen as old, irrelevant  
**Solution:** Modern UI, community features, real-world relevance  
**Impact:** Active, responsible citizens

---

## Who Uses It

**Students:** Fun learning, better grades, lifetime civic awareness  
**Teachers:** Ready curriculum, progress tracking, higher engagement  
**Citizens:** Self-paced legal knowledge, understand rights/duties  
**Rural Users:** Free access, works on basic phones

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into**
One of the biggest technical hurdles I faced while building this project was a persistent database connection error after deploying the Next.js app to Vercel.
The Bug
After deployment, the app started throwing this error on every request that needed to fetch user progress data:

**Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND db.bclxmxvffswramiifjmt.supabase.co
    at async o.queryWithCache...
    [cause]: Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND ...**

The query was trying to connect to Supabase using a direct PostgreSQL connection, but it kept failing with a DNS resolution error.

**Root Cause Discovery**

I initially thought it was a credentials issue or that the Supabase project had paused. After checking the dashboard and logs, I noticed the connection string was using the **Direct connection:**

postgresql://postgres:[PASSWORD]@db.bclxmxvffswramiifjmt.supabase.co:5432/postgres

When I opened the Supabase dashboard, I saw a clear warning: "Not IPv4 compatible" with a note saying "Use Session Pooler if on an IPv4 network".

This was the key insight — Supabase’s direct database connections are now IPv6-only in most regions, while Vercel (and most serverless platforms) still primarily operate on IPv4. The hostname simply couldn’t be resolved from the Vercel runtime.

**How I Solved It**

I switched from the Direct connection to Supabase’s Transaction Pooler (the recommended option for serverless applications):

Went back to the Supabase Dashboard → Connect page.
Changed the connection method from "Direct connection" to "Transaction Pooler".
Copied the new connection string (using port 6543).
Updated the DATABASE_URL environment variable in Vercel.
Redeployed the application.

I also added ?pgbouncer=true to the connection string (since I’m using Drizzle ORM) for better compatibility with the pooler.

**Outcome**
The error disappeared immediately after the new deployment. The app now connects reliably, and performance is actually better because of connection pooling.

**Key Takeaway**
This experience taught me how important it is to read platform-specific warnings (the "Not IPv4 compatible" banner) and to always use the correct connection method for serverless environments. What looked like a mysterious DNS error was actually a common mismatch between modern database hosting and serverless infrastructure.

**Challenges we ran into**

YOLO detection accuracy: Overlapping people sometimes caused duplicate or incorrect detections, so we had to adjust the confidence threshold and restrict detection to the person class.

Risk classification: YOLO detects objects, but it doesn't directly understand situations like “kidnapping” or “danger.” We had to design a separate risk-analysis layer for our prototype.

Video processing: Processing CCTV footage frame-by-frame and generating annotated videos required optimization and testing.

Live vs prototype data: Connecting real-time CCTV and GPS was beyond the prototype scope, so we used prerecorded CCTV footage and simulated GPS data to demonstrate the workflow.

Deployment: Getting all dependencies and video/model files working correctly on Streamlit Community Cloud was another challenge.

Integration: Connecting the AI detection, backend, dashboard, location monitoring, and emergency-alert concept into one working flow required multiple rounds of testing.

**The problem it solves**

Women’s safety systems are often reactive, requiring the person at risk to manually press an SOS button or ask for help. In situations where they may be unable to do so, traditional systems can fail to respond in time.

SHIELD addresses this gap by combining AI-powered CCTV monitoring, risk analysis, location tracking, and emergency response into one platform. It monitors activity, identifies potentially unusual situations, categorizes risk levels, and provides a mechanism for rapid emergency notification.

In short: SHIELD aims to shift women’s safety from “responding after an emergency” to “detecting and responding to risk earlier.”

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

The Odinson Vibration Monitor addresses the need for affordable, accessible vibration and seismic activity monitoring in various applications:

- **Structural Health Monitoring**: Provides low-cost solution for monitoring vibrations in buildings, bridges, and other infrastructure to detect potential structural issues before they become critical
- **Earthquake Early Warning**: Functions as a digital seismometer prototype capable of detecting abnormal motion patterns that could indicate seismic activity
- **Industrial Vibration Analysis**: Enables monitoring of machinery and equipment to detect imbalances, misalignments, or bearing failures that could lead to costly downtime
- **Research and Education**: Serves as an accessible platform for students and researchers to study vibration patterns, signal processing, and sensor integration

The system makes vibration monitoring accessible by:
- Using inexpensive, off-the-shelf components (MPU6050 sensor, Arduino)
- Providing real-time visualization through both web interface and matplotlib display
- Offering multiple alert mechanisms (Telegram, sound, visual)
- Storing data persistently for later analysis
- Including both live monitoring and historical data viewing capabilities

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges we ran into

During development, we encountered several technical hurdles that required creative solutions:

### Datetime Format Error
**Problem**: `ValueError: Invalid format string` when generating CSV filenames due to using `%s` (seconds since epoch) instead of `%S` (seconds) in `strftime` format string.

**Solution**: Corrected the format string from `%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%s` to `%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S` to properly represent hours, minutes, and seconds.

### Port Already in Use
**Problem**: `OSError: [WinError 10048] Only one usage of each socket address...` when trying to start the Flask server, indicating port 5000 was already occupied.

**Solution**: Implemented process cleanup by identifying and terminating existing processes using the port with `netstat` and `taskkill` commands before starting the application.

### Serial Port Permission/Access Issues
**Problem**: `PermissionError(13, 'Access is denied.')` when attempting to open COM3 serial port, typically caused by another process holding the port or insufficient permissions.

**Solution**: Added robust serial connection handling with:
- Automatic retry mechanism with exponential backoff
- Graceful reconnection logic when serial communication is interrupted
- Clear error messaging to guide users on resolving port conflicts
- Mock data mode for development/testing when hardware isn't available

### Matplotlib Unresponsiveness
**Problem**: The matplotlib figure window became unresponsive and stopped updating due to the main thread being blocked in a tight loop without processing GUI events.

**Solution**: Replaced `time.sleep(0.016) + flush_events()` with `plt.pause(0.001)` which properly processes TkAgg GUI events while maintaining adequate update frequency for smooth visualization.

### Data Loss on Program Termination
**Problem**: When stopping the program with Ctrl+C, CSV files were incomplete or empty because daemon threads were terminated abruptly before flushing buffers.

**Solution**: Implemented graceful shutdown sequence:
- Added global `running` flag to control all worker threads
- Changed threads from daemon to non-daemon so they can be properly joined
- Created Flask shutdown endpoint (`/shutdown`) for clean server termination
- Added Ctrl+C handler that sets `running=False`, joins threads, and closes resources
- Made CSV file line-buffered (`buffering=1`) for immediate data flushing

> Track what you play, rate and review games, build

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![neon](https://img.shields.io/badge/neon-333333?style=flat-square) ![Drizzle ORM](https://img.shields.io/badge/Drizzle%20ORM-333333?style=flat-square)

**How Did You Use Claude?**

Two different things, kept distinct on purpose rather than blurred into one "we used Claude" claim.

**Claude Code, at build time — the actual mechanism by which this exists.** The entire hackathon build ran through Claude Code as the engineering agent: reading the pre-existing codebase to find the real boundary, designing the abandonment heuristic in `lib/claude/play-history.ts` (a single earned trophy with no recent activity as proof of a dropped session — PSN's API exposes no playtime, so this was the only way to get real signal), building GAME's deterministic retrieval and baseline-relative ranking in `lib/claude/game-engine.ts`, writing the migration and verification scripts, wiring the retrieval pass into the live home page (`app/home/page.tsx`, `lib/data.ts`, the "For You"/"Surprise me" UI), sourcing and implementing the real brandbook logo from Figma, and writing the README this answer is consistent with. This is a build-time tool, not a runtime feature — disclosed as exactly that rather than left implicit or reframed as an API integration it isn't.

**The Claude API itself — designed, not wired in.** Three modules sketch a judgement layer on top of the deterministic retrieval, each on a `.md` system prompt loaded from disk (`prompts/`, never inlined):

- **Taste-spec compiler — Opus** (`prompts/taste-spec.md`). Would read a player's full labelled play history and compile it into stated behavioural principles, each citing the exact titles that support it (e.g. "abandons crafting-heavy RPGs past hour 9, 3 of 3 titles"). The hardest reasoning in the design — inferring a pattern nobody stated, across dozens of titles, while staying honest about thin samples.
- **GAME slate — Opus** (`prompts/game-match.md`). Would take the taste spec plus GAME's 36-game shortlist and pick one game per lane, arguing it. The `blind_spot` lane is adversarial by design — it would have to argue *against* the player's own revealed preference using evidence from their own library, and is allowed to reject a weak candidate rather than force-fill the slot.
- **Verdict — Sonnet** (`prompts/verdict.md`). Would predict finish-or-abandon for any single game against an already-compiled spec — bounded, cheaper reasoning for the interactive, called-repeatedly path, with the spec sitting in a cached prompt prefix so repeated verdicts pay only for the per-game delta.

We chose not to wire these in for this submission and to say so plainly rather than demo a mocked call: the code is real and typechecks, but none of it has executed against the live API, and the product that's actually live at app.iplayd.games doesn't depend on it. What shipped is the deterministic half, built end-to-end with Claude Code, and honest about exactly where the line sits.

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://app.iplayd.games/home

**How you are solving it?**

**Disclosure, upfront.** This repository is the pre-existing iPlayd codebase — a live product with real users, built before this hackathon. Organiser permission to build on it was confirmed. The git tag `hackathon-start` marks the exact boundary; `git diff hackathon-start..HEAD --stat` is the complete, verifiable hackathon diff. No pre-existing file was refactored — every change is additive: two new Postgres tables, new `lib/claude/*` modules, a new `mcp/server.ts`, a real brandbook logo/wordmark, and purely-additive wiring into `app/home/page.tsx` and `lib/data.ts` (new imports, new functions appended — nothing existing was touched).

**What we built in the window:**

1. `lib/claude/play-history.ts` — reads the existing PSN/Xbox/Steam sync tables and labels every game `completed` / `abandoned` / `playing` / `untouched`. The hard part was abandonment: PSN's trophy API exposes no playtime, so a single earned achievement with no recent activity is treated as proof of a real, dropped session. That one heuristic took this account from 2 detectable abandonments to 40 — the difference between no signal and a usable model.

2. `lib/claude/game-engine.ts` — GAME (Gamers Algorithmic Match Engine). Deterministic retrieval scores every candidate on genre affinity, measured against the *player's own* baseline completion rate rather than a fixed prior — this account finishes 1 game in 9, so a naive 0.5 prior would rank their strongest genre as below average. Retrieval narrows the pool to a 36-game shortlist across three lanes: `backlog` (their own unfinished games), `adjacent` (unowned games inside their demonstrated taste), and `blind_spot` (a genre they've never touched, quality-gated, argued against their revealed preference).

3. Shipped to the actual product, not left as a script — `/home` on app.iplayd.games has a "For You" section (backlog + adjacent, ranked by affinity) and a "Surprise me" button (samples one `blind_spot` pick per click, shown in a modal with real cover art, genres, and rating, plus a "surprise again" resample action). Both call the same verified retrieval function, `previewCandidates()`, live in production right now.

**A deliberate constraint: the shipped product makes zero calls to the Claude API, anywhere, at build time or runtime.** Every recommendation is 100% deterministic — real trophy and playtime data in, statistics out, no external dependency, no key required, fully auditable. Three further modules (a taste-spec compiler, a GAME reasoning pass, and a verdict engine — all designed to call Opus/Sonnet on top of this same retrieval layer) are written and typecheck, but were deliberately left unwired for this submission rather than half-demoed. See the next answer for why that's still a real, disclosed use of Claude.

Full README with real command output against production data: https://github.com/priyanshuratnakar/iplayd

**What is the problem your project solves?**

Storefronts rank games by what sells — pre-orders, wishlist adds, launch-week revenue. None of that signal survives the purchase, so nothing in gaming today ranks by what a player actually *finishes* versus quietly abandons. Every recommendation engine in the industry is built from what publishers and storefronts can see: what you bought, what you wishlisted, what you clicked. None of them can see the thing that actually characterises a player — the hour they put a game down and never came back.

iPlayd is a live cross-platform tracker (PlayStation, Xbox, Steam) at app.iplayd.games, with real synced trophy and playtime data across thousands of games. That data already holds the signal nobody else has. This account alone — 252 games — has 40 abandoned titles against only 5 completed. An 8:1 ratio a fixed-genre or "similar users" recommender throws away entirely, because it has no concept of a player's *own* baseline completion rate, only a population average.

The problem: there is no demand-side signal layer in gaming. We built one — a taste layer that reads abandonment as data, not noise.

> Last financial agent you will ever need

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We built TARS because we kept overspending without really noticing. You open an app, order, pay on UPI, and it's done before you've thought about it. Budgeting apps only tell you what happened after the money's already gone, and nobody's helping with the small everyday stuff  the cab, the food order, the quick grocery run which is honestly where most of our money quietly disappears.

So TARS just lives in your chat. You can ask what you can afford this week, or tell it to order food, groceries or a cab, and it compares options, picks the cheapest, and checks it against your budget before paying. It always asks before it spends, and the money goes through your own UPI we never hold it. You can also just talk to it in your own language, which matters for a lot of people who don't type in English.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part wasn't the ordering, it was trusting our own numbers. The whole "can you afford this" idea falls apart if the balance is wrong, and reading bank SMS is a pain every bank writes them differently, and your inbox is full of OTPs and offers mixed in with real transactions. Our first version kept miscounting. We fixed it by pulling a bunch of real messages off our own phones, throwing away anything that wasn't a transaction before it hit the model, and then letting the model pull out the amount, merchant and category. 

Swiggy was the other one. Getting whitelisted for their MCP, and then getting our order flow to line up with what it actually sent back, took longer than we thought. 

And with only 48 hours, we couldn't get every category into iMessage. So we picked the flow we most wanted to prove  ask a money question, order food, and actually pay through Prava  got that fully working in iMessage, and left cab and grocery in the app for now.

**OpenAI**

OpenAI models are the brain of the agent  they read what you're asking in plain language or voice, pull clean spending data out of messy bank SMS, and handle the deciding and comparing. We lean on GPT-4o-mini for most decisions so each one is cheap enough to run on every small spend, even a ₹200 order.

**iMessage Agent**

We built TARS to work right inside iMessage using Linq. You text it a money question  like how much you can spend on food this week and then order food in the same thread, ending in a real payment. No app to open, it lives where people already message. In the 48 hours we got the finance question, food order and payment flow fully working in iMessage; the other categories run in our app for now.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

TARS runs the whole commerce loop as an agent it works out whether you can afford something, compares where to buy it, and completes the payment, all from a chat. What makes it different is that it's spend-aware: it checks your budget and asks before it buys, so it's making a money decision with you, not just placing orders. In the demo it takes a food order end to end, from the question to paid, through the Prava sandbox.

### CardGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cardguard-6a37) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Harshittgupta/CardGuard) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ReLCHp16nBc) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ReLCHp16nBc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomous purchasing agent with Visa security

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Webhook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Webhook-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zod](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zod-333333?style=flat-square) ![Playwright](https://img.shields.io/badge/Playwright-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vitest](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vitest-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Getting a $15 subscription approved at most companies means Slack pings, forgotten approvals, and finance chasing down what got expensed three months later. CardGuard fixes that. Employees just text what they need over iMessage or our web portal and small, pre-cleared purchases (under $25) go through instantly, no paperwork. Anything bigger triggers a one-tap Face ID approval to a finance manager. Under the hood, Prava mints a single-use virtual card locked to that exact merchant and dollar amount at the Visa network level, so even if something went wrong, it physically can't be misused elsewhere. We also catch duplicate SaaS subscriptions before they start draining the budget, and keep spend policy in plain code never in the AI's hands so there's nothing a prompt injection could talk its way around.

**Challenges we ran into**

Sandbox cards vs. real checkouts - Prava's test cards get declined by live payment gateways, which is expected but made it hard to prove the flow actually works end-to-end. We solved it by capturing full evidence anyway: Browserbase session replays, screenshots, and step logs, then reporting settlement status back to Prava's API to get real Visa confirmation tokens.

Login walls - Platforms like Figma and OpenAI require an existing account before you even reach checkout, which a browser agent can't just talk its way past. So we built dynamic merchant routing that maps requests to guest-checkout vendors instead, letting the agent complete a real purchase without hitting a login screen.

Accidental approvals from link previews - iMessage and Slack auto-fetch links to generate previews, which would've silently "opened" (and technically pre-authorized) a purchase before a human ever saw the message. We fixed this by making the link itself read-only only an explicit, passkey-confirmed action can actually release funds.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

CardGuard deeply integrates Prava's API layer to leverage Visa Intelligent Commerce network capabilities throughout the end-to-end purchasing lifecycle:
1. Mandate Setup Session (POST /v1/sessions): Establishes authorize-only sessions with merchant_scope: "listed", binding the authorization at the card-network level strictly to designated vendors (e.g., Figma, Oswaal Books, DeoDap).
2. Network-Enforced Card Minting (POST /v1/mandates/{id}/charge): Mints single-use virtual card credentials (token, dynamic CVV, expiry) locked to an exact merchant and dollar cap. Out-of-merchant or over-cap charges return THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED directly from Visa's network rather than software logic.
3. Closed-Loop Settlement Reporting (POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/report-status): Reports post-checkout status (APPROVED/DECLINED) with verbatim merchant gateway responses back to Prava, receiving verified Visa network confirmation tokens for 100% auditability.

**OpenAI**

CardGuard uses the OpenAI API (GPT-4o) in src/services/policy/extractor.ts as the natural-language intelligence layer that powers conversational spend processing:
1. Structured Intent Extraction: Converts unstructured, multi-seat, or complex employee messages (e.g., "Buy $45 Figma subscription for 2 designers") into strict, typed Zod schemas—extracting merchant name, unit price, quantity, currency, expense category, billing cadence (one-time vs. monthly), and purpose.
2. Extraction Confidence Scoring: Computes a numerical confidence score (0.0 to 1.0) on every extraction. Low-confidence parses (< 0.75) automatically trigger human approval, preventing ambiguous orders.
3. Strict Policy Isolation: Evaluates extracted intent against a pure, deterministic policy engine in code. The LLM has zero context or control over spend ceilings or approval rules, making the system completely immune to prompt injection financial exploits.

**iMessage Agent**

CardGuard integrates Linq's iMessage partner API and webhooks to deliver a completely passwordless, conversational employee purchasing experience:
1. Inbound Webhook Processing (/webhooks/linq): Listens for incoming employee SMS/iMessage purchase requests, normalizing requester phone identities to enforce $500 monthly user spend budgets.
2. Conversational Status & Approvals: Formats and dispatches real-time iMessage updates for mandate creation, policy auto-approvals, and passkey authorization links directly to manager handsets.
3. Passkey Approval Routing: Sends HMAC-signed, link-previewer-safe approval URLs via Linq iMessage so managers can authenticate sign-offs with Face ID / Touch ID in seconds.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

The whole point of CardGuard is that money moves without friction, but never without control. You can ask for a purchase however's easiest text or web and watch it move through a live progress timeline. Approving something is just Face ID, nothing more. And everything every card, every mandate, every approval lives in a dashboard built like a real fintech ledger, right down to a button that tries to abuse the system just to prove it can't.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

CardGuard is a full autonomous purchasing agent for corporate spend. It strings together Prava's card-issuing API, OpenAI for reading intent out of plain text, WebAuthn passkeys for approval, and a Stagehand/Browserbase agent that actually completes checkout using single-use cards locked to a merchant and a dollar cap at the Visa network level.

**The problem it solves**

At the end of the day, Resonator is a game. And like every great game ever made, its highest purpose is simple to make you forget, for a little while, that the world outside exists.
We've poured original mechanics, a handcrafted story, and genuine creative sweat into every room, every interaction, every line of dialogue. But none of that matters as much as this if someone picks this up after a brutal day, loses themselves in it for an hour, and puts it down feeling something they didn't expect to feel, we've done our job.
That's the bar every game developer secretly measures themselves against. Not downloads. Not reviews. Not awards.
Did it take someone somewhere else for a while?
If yes it was worth building.

**Challenges we ran into**

There were multiple challenges we ran into while making this project, such as designing the level, implementation of the level design and game mechanics

Few specific challenges which were too hard to forget were:
- mixamo animation issue: I downloaded a model from mixamo and since it was too big i tried reducing it which added extra nodes messing up the entire animation, it took wayy too long to figure out the root cause
- at once point i had 1968 errors cause i forgot to map the keybinds
- building atmosphere as non-artists: it was hard designing the level, plots, game theory and so much more as a team of 3

**Game Development**

Resonator is a first person psychological horror game set in a research facility gone wrong. You play as a researcher who wakes up after an explosion, surrounded by chaos, with one goal  survive and find your way out.
The facility's test subjects, people who were experimented on without consent, have broken free. They're hostile, they're dangerous, and they're everywhere. Your only lifeline is your partner's voice on the walkie talkie, guiding you floor by floor toward safety.
But the deeper you go, the more the cracks start to show. In the environment. In the story. In her.
Resonator isn't about jump scares. It's about discovery. Every document you find, every room you enter, every conversation you have with her slowly repaints the picture of what actually happened here.
The partner is powered by ElevenLabs, making her a genuinely adaptive presence who remembers everything you've uncovered and responds in real time.

**ElevenLabs**

We used ElevenLabs to generate conversations, SFX and Effects for our game, so that the player can have a immersive experience

### Bharat GPT
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bharat-gpt-69ae) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Anvesh-21/BharatGPT) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Base%20Batches%20003:%20Student%20Track-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://base-batches-student-track-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Voices of Bharat 🇮🇳, Powered by AI

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

***1. Civic Knowledge is Fragmented and Unverifiable***
Today, public discussions, governance proposals, and civic insights exist across: Social media platforms, Government portals, News websites, Private AI tools.

These systems are: Centralized, Easily manipulated, Not cryptographically verifiable, Detached from persistent identity.
When AI generates civic summaries or policy insights, there is no transparent audit trail, no immutable record, and no way to verify long-term integrity.
Trust is assumed — not proven.

***2. No Onchain Reputation for Civic Contribution***
In Web3, reputation is mostly financial: Token holdings, NFT ownership, DeFi participation.

There is no structured onchain system for:
Civic participation, Governance contributions, Policy discussion, Knowledge building.

Students and young citizens who actively engage in meaningful civic discussions receive:
No portable proof of contribution, No verifiable credentials, No programmable governance identity.
This limits coordination and long-term participation.

***3. Governance Systems Are Opaque and Hard to Scale***
Most governance processes today: Lack structured digital coordination, Have low transparency, Are vulnerable to spam and misinformation, Provide no AI-assisted clarity.

Even DAOs struggle with: Proposal overload, Low-quality participation, No reputation gating, No structured contribution tracking.

There is no AI-assisted governance layer that is onchain-native and reputation-backed.

***4. AI Civic Systems Lack Accountability***
AI tools today generate civic insights, summaries, and interpretations — but: Outputs are mutable, No cryptographic anchoring, No tamper-evident record, No long-term traceability.

As AI becomes more influential in shaping public reasoning, lack of auditability becomes a systemic risk.

**Challenges we ran into**

*Building Bharath GPT surfaced both architectural and conceptual challenges.*

**1. Designing Onchain-Meaningful Interactions**

The core challenge was ensuring the project was genuinely onchain — not just a Web2 AI app with wallet login.

**Solution:**
Identified which interactions affect trust, Restricted onchain logic to reputation, governance, and anchoring. Kept AI inference offchain for efficiency. Anchored critical outputs cryptographically.
This preserved decentralization where it matters most.

**2. Soulbound Reputation Design**

Creating a non-transferable reputation NFT system required careful logic design: Preventing transfers, Maintaining credibility over time, Designing upgradeable reputation tiers, Avoiding sybil exploitation.

**Solution:**
Implemented non-transferable ERC-721 structure. Designed modular reputation scoring logic. Integrated wallet-based gating mechanisms. 

**3. AI + Blockchain Integration Complexity**

AI systems are probabilistic, while blockchain is deterministic.
Bridging these two required: Separating computation layers. Anchoring outputs via hash commitments. Designing verification flow without overloading gas

**Solution:**
Store only cryptographic proofs onchain. Keep heavy inference offchain.vMaintain integrity through verifiable commitments.

**4. Gas Optimization on Base**

Even on Base (low-cost L2), governance systems must remain efficient.

**Solution:**
Minimized on chain storage. Used event logs strategically. Designed lean proposal structs. Avoided unnecessary state writes. 

**5. Governance Design Trade-offs**

Balancing: Open participation, Quality control, Sybil resistance, Accessibility, Required iterative design thinking.

**Solution:**
Reputation-gated proposal thresholds. Tier-based governance access. Modular voting extensions for future upgrades.

> Intelligent Insights, Smart Investments

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most retail investors especially students and beginners — want to learn stock trading but face two major barriers:

Financial risk : Real trading requires real money. Mistakes are costly and discouraging.
No intelligent feedback loop : Generic trading apps don't explain why a stock might move or give AI-driven context to help users learn.
FinPanda solves both. It's a zero-risk paper trading simulator that lets users practice buying and selling stocks with $1,00,000 of virtual money, backed by real live market data. On top of that, it integrates a machine learning volatility model and Monte Carlo simulation engine to generate price predictions, sentiment analysis on live financial news, and AI-powered stock suggestions — giving users the tools institutional traders use, for free.

**Challenges we ran into**

Serverless Architecture Limits

Issue: Moving from an Express server to Vercel's serverless functions broke our internal API calls since routes were no longer running persistently on localhost.
Fix: Implemented dynamic host detection to route internal requests to the correct serverless domains in production.
React Router & OAuth 404s

Issue: Refreshing pages or returning from Google OAuth caused 404 errors because Vercel was looking for static files that didn't exist in our SPA.
Fix: Configured smart SPA fallback rewrite rules in vercel.json to route all non-API traffic smoothly back to index.html.
Python ML Server Deployment

Issue: Our ML models failed to build on Render because the default Python version (3.14) lacked pre-compiled wheels for our specific Scikit-Learn requirements.
Fix: Pinned the exact runtime to Python 3.11.9 in a render.yaml config to ensure fast, stable dependency installations.
API Contract Mismatches

Issue: The UI expected complex, enriched data payloads (like live stock prices inside the watchlist GET response) which the backend wasn't originally providing.
Fix: We heavily refactored the Node.js API to cross-reference our database with the Finnhub API, injecting real-time market data into nearly every route before serving the client.
Visualizing the Monte Carlo Data

Issue: The prediction chart was completely blank. The backend was returning 100 parallel final prices, but the frontend expected a single sequential daily price path.
Fix: We rewrote the simulation output to generate a distinct "timeSeries" daily walk that the React charts could accurately plot over a 30-day timeframe.

Team **Agra metro ke fans** -- Kartikay Arya, Abhishek Barya, Shaurya Patel, Anurag Panda

> Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas - With AI

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

“Log aksar bolte hain - India is not for beginners.
Aur jab baat government services ki aati hai, toh yeh aur bhi complicated ho jaata hai.”
India mein crores logon ko government services ki zarurat hoti hai 
jaise PAN card, driving licence, passport, scholarships, aur welfare schemes.
Lekin problem yeh hai ki:
Information alag-alag government portals par scattered hoti hai
Language complex aur technical hoti hai
Process samajhna aam citizens ke liye difficult hota hai
Is complexity ki wajah se log cyber cafés aur middlemen par depend ho jaate hain, jo simple forms fill karne ke bhi unnecessary charges lete hain.
Result yeh hota hai ki:
citizens ko correct information nahi milti
government services access karna time-consuming ho jaata hai
aur digital governance ka real benefit ground level tak nahi pahunch pata.
Isliye problem simple hai:
Citizens ko ek aise system ki zarurat hai jo government procedures ko simple language mein samjha sake, guide kare, aur application process ko easy bana sake.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building Bharat Saathi, one of the biggest challenges was collecting reliable government information.
Most government portals don’t provide structured APIs, so we had to scrape data from multiple sources like government websites, PDFs, and video transcripts.
Each source had a different format — some were HTML pages, some were scanned PDFs, and some were long documents — so converting all of that into usable knowledge was a major challenge.
To solve this, we built a data pipeline that extracts text from these sources and converts it into embeddings so it can be searched semantically.
Another challenge was connecting this knowledge to the AI system in a reliable way.
We implemented a Retrieval Augmented Generation architecture, where the system first searches the knowledge base and then sends the relevant context to the language model to generate accurate responses.
But ensuring that the system always gives a response was tricky.
Sometimes the vector retrieval could fail, and sometimes the LLM API could have latency or errors.
So we designed a fallback architecture where:
if RAG works, the system uses retrieved knowledge + LLM reasoning
if retrieval fails, the system still answers using LLM reasoning
and if the LLM is unavailable, the system shows retrieved knowledge directly
This ensures that Bharat Saathi never becomes unavailable for the user.
Another interesting challenge was automation for government forms.
Different forms require different fields, so we designed a dynamic form-question engine where the AI identifies the service, asks the required questions step-by-step, and maps the answers to form fields.
We also connected this with a user profile stored in the database, so basic information like name, date of birth, and address can be reused automatically instead of asking the user repeatedly.
Overall, the biggest challenge wasn’t just building an AI chatbot —
it was connecting multiple systems together: data scraping, knowledge retrieval, AI reasoning, and automation, so that the experience feels seamless for the user.
