![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cloudinary](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloudinary-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Whatsapp API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Whatsapp%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

KrishakSarthi — AI-Powered Agriculture Assistant for Every Farmer
Tagline
From smartphone to WhatsApp — one AI companion covering crop planning, disease detection, and market access for India's 140 million farming households.

The Problem
Most Indian farmers don't have access to timely agronomic advice. Agricultural extension officers are stretched thin, internet literacy is low, and existing agri-apps require a smartphone and stable connectivity. Farmers lose crops to diseases they could have prevented and miss market opportunities because they can't find buyers.

What We Built
KrishakSarthi is a full-stack AI agriculture platform with three deeply integrated layers:

Mobile App (React Native + Expo)
A farmer-friendly Android/iOS app with large touch targets, high-contrast green UI, and full trilingual support (Hindi, Bengali, English).
AI Crop Disease Detection — photograph a diseased leaf; Gemini Vision identifies the pathogen, severity, and treatment within seconds
Crop Prediction Engine — combines live weather data with soil and location inputs to recommend the best crop for the season
Crop Planner + Calendar — step-by-step guided farming plan with a visual activity calendar
Document Analyzer — farmers photograph government forms, seed packets, or invoices and get plain-language summaries
AI Chatbot — RAG-powered conversational assistant backed by a curated agriculture knowledge base
Farmer-Buyer Marketplace — supply chain screen connecting farmers directly with verified buyers; live GPS location sharing for last-mile logistics
Daily Routine Tracker — task scheduler tailored to crop growth stages

RAG Knowledge Backend (Node.js + Vercel)
A Retrieval-Augmented Generation API that turns agriculture PDFs and documents into an intelligent Q&A engine.
PDF ingestion pipeline chunks and embeds agricultural documents into Pinecone vector store
Queries are semantically searched, top chunks retrieved, and answers synthesized by Gemini with source citations
Exposes a clean REST API (POST /api/chat) consumed by both the mobile app and WhatsApp service
Multi-language translation layer for Hindi ↔ English responses
3. WhatsApp Bot (Node.js + Meta Cloud API)
For farmers who only have a basic WhatsApp account.

Hooks into Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API via webhook
Farmers ask agriculture questions in Hindi or English and get back RAG-powered answers — no app download needed
Natural-language Crop Planning: farmer types "5 acre mein basmati dhan, Sodepur, 15 June se" — the bot extracts all fields, confirms, generates a full 90-day farming plan PDF, and delivers it back over WhatsApp
Voice call support for farmers who prefer speech

Challenges We Solved

Zero-connectivity farmers: WhatsApp channel needs only basic 2G; no app install required
Multilingual NLP extraction: Free-form Hindi messages parsed by Gemini to extract structured crop fields (crop name, area, location, date) reliably
PDF over WhatsApp: Generated PDFs uploaded to Meta Media API and delivered as WhatsApp documents, not just text
Encoding pipeline: Built a robust ingestion pipeline to chunk, embed, and upsert heterogeneous agriculture PDFs with metadata preserved for source citations
Impact Potential
Targets 140M+ smallholder farmers in India who rely on WhatsApp daily
Reduces crop loss from undetected disease with sub-10-second AI diagnosis
Bridges the farmer-buyer gap directly in the app, cutting out middlemen
Works in the language the farmer is most comfortable in

Challenges we ran into
RAG queries took 30+ seconds, exceeding Twilio's hard limit
Solution: Implemented async job queue with polling mechanism—respond immediately to Twilio, process in background, caller polls for result
Audio Processing Pipeline

WhatsApp Integration Challenges
Multi-Turn Conversation State

Keeping conversation context across multiple message exchanges for crop planning
Handling WhatsApp message retries (duplicate IDs)
Solution: Redis-based session storage with auto-expiration
Language Support (Hindi/English Mix)

WhatsApp media upload constraints (file size limits)
Proper multipart form-data formatting for PDF uploads
Solution: PDF generation with size optimization and chunked delivery
Rate Limiting & Quota Management

Handling API rate limits from multiple providers simultaneously
Managing quota exhaustion gracefully
Solution: Multiple API key rotation and fallback models

**Slash (Open)**

We chose the Open Innovation track because OutreachX integrates multiple modern technologies and APIs to build a flexible outreach platform. The system combines communication APIs, automation tools, and real-time analytics to create a scalable solution for managing campaigns. By bringing together different technologies in an open and adaptable way, the platform enables organizations to improve how they connect with people and manage large-scale outreach efforts more effectively.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

MediSaathi solves the gap between what doctors prescribe and what actually happens at home after the visit.

Helps patients understand prescriptions and reports by converting complex, handwritten, or technical medical documents into clear, structured information.

Makes medication intake safer by sending timely reminders, showing medicine images, and tracking taken, missed, or delayed doses.

Reduces treatment errors by generating adherence reports so doctors know whether a medicine failed due to biology or non-compliance.

Simplifies follow-up care by summarizing doctor instructions and lab reports, reducing confusion after consultations.

Improves continuity of care by turning out-of-clinic patient behavior into reliable, clinician-readable data instead of assumptions.

**Challenges we ran into**

Inconsistent and handwritten medical inputs reduced OCR accuracy, requiring contextual LLM-based extraction.

Medicine adherence tracking had edge cases like missed and delayed doses, solved using a state-based logic.

LLM outputs were sometimes unstructured, fixed by enforcing strict structured responses.

External chatbot APIs caused latency and privacy concerns, addressed by self-hosting Mistral via Ollama on Vultr.

Rapid development led to API and CORS issues, resolved through standardized API contracts and request mocking.

**Google Gemini**

We use Gemini as an intelligent OCR and understanding layer to convert unstructured medical documents into structured, clinically meaningful data. It interprets handwritten prescriptions, extracts dosage and instructions, and enables reliable medication scheduling and adherence tracking rather than just raw text extraction.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/2b7aee4e84d14625ad28b0e0b064ab15/2294015a-a142-46ff-a762-6c6b867016b7.jpeg)

**Vultr**

We use Vultr as our high-performance inference layer to deploy a self-hosted Ollama-based Mistral model that powers the MediSaathi medical chatbot. Vultr provides GPU-ready, low-latency infrastructure, allowing us to run the LLM close to our backend with full control over model behavior, data flow, and privacy. By hosting Mistral on Vultr instead of relying on third-party APIs, we enable secure, scalable, and cost-efficient contextual reasoning over patient data, making the chatbot reliable for healthcare use while keeping sensitive medical information within our own infrastructure.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/2b7aee4e84d14625ad28b0e0b064ab15/26c1fe55-1728-47aa-ad29-6169b46f19fd.jpeg)

**ElevenLabs**

We use ElevenLabs to give MediSaathi’s chatbot a natural, human-like voice. The chatbot’s medically contextual responses are converted into clear spoken explanations, improving accessibility for elderly users, low-literacy patients, and hands-free usage, while keeping all medical reasoning and data handling within our secure backend.


![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/2b7aee4e84d14625ad28b0e0b064ab15/5615ea4f-c5b2-4b09-bd38-f8ecb60804cc.jpeg)

### offroad Semantics

> Imbalance-Aware Semantic Segmentation

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![Keras](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keras-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Colab](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Colab-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![U-Net](https://img.shields.io/badge/U--Net-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🧩 The Problem It Solves

Accurate understanding of visual scenes at the pixel level is a fundamental challenge in computer vision. Traditional image classification or object detection models fail to capture fine-grained spatial details, especially in complex environments where multiple classes overlap or appear at different scales.

In semantic segmentation, this problem becomes even harder due to:

Severe class imbalance (dominant background vs rare foreground classes)

Ambiguous boundaries between regions

High sensitivity to noise and lighting variations

Over-reliance on pixel accuracy, which can be misleading in real-world datasets

As a result, many models produce biased or oversimplified predictions, often collapsing to a single dominant class and failing to generalize to unseen data.

🚀 What This Project Enables

This project introduces an imbalance-aware semantic segmentation framework that produces reliable and interpretable pixel-level predictions, even in complex scenes.

🔍 Practical Use Cases

Scene Understanding
Automatically segment different regions (sky, terrain, vegetation, objects) from an image for better environmental analysis.

Autonomous Systems
Helps self-driving vehicles and robots understand surroundings by identifying drivable areas, obstacles, and terrain types.

Remote Sensing & Geospatial Analysis
Enables land-cover classification from satellite or aerial imagery for urban planning, agriculture, and disaster monitoring.

Medical & Scientific Imaging (Adaptable)
Can be extended to segment organs, tissues, or anomalies where class imbalance is common.

⚡ How It Makes Existing Tasks Better

✅ Handles class imbalance effectively using Dice-based and combined loss functions

✅ Prevents misleading performance metrics by replacing pixel accuracy with IoU/Dice scores

✅ Improves generalization through early stopping and validation-driven training

✅ Provides interpretable outputs, enabling failure-case analysis and model debugging

✅ Reduces manual labeling effort by automating pixel-wise annotation tasks

🛡️ Why It Is Safer and More Reliable

Unlike naive segmentation pipelines, this system is designed to:

Avoid dominant-class bias

Detect subtle regions that are often ignored

Produce consistent predictions on unseen data

This makes it suitable for high-stakes applications where incorrect segmentation could lead to unsafe or costly decisions.

🎯 In One Line

This project transforms raw images into meaningful, reliable pixel-level insights by addressing the core challenges of semantic segmentation—class imbalance, overfitting, and poor generalization.

**Challenges we ran into**

⚠️ Challenges I Ran Into (and How I Solved Them)
🧠 1. Model Collapsing to a Single Class

Problem:
During early experiments, the segmentation model consistently predicted a single class for every pixel, resulting in uniform-colored output masks despite diverse ground truth labels.

Root Cause:

Severe class imbalance in the dataset

Over-reliance on pixel accuracy, which rewarded majority-class predictions

Use of standard categorical cross-entropy without imbalance awareness

Solution:

Replaced accuracy with Dice coefficient and IoU for evaluation

Switched to Dice loss and combined Dice + Cross-Entropy loss

Analyzed class distribution at the pixel level to validate imbalance

This change allowed the model to learn meaningful boundaries instead of defaulting to the dominant class.

📉 2. Misleading Training Metrics

Problem:
Training accuracy appeared reasonable, but validation performance degraded and predictions failed on unseen data.

Root Cause:
Pixel accuracy does not reflect segmentation quality when most pixels belong to a single class.

Solution:

Removed accuracy as a metric

Introduced Dice coefficient as the primary optimization and evaluation metric

Interpreted training curves using loss and Dice trends instead of accuracy alone

This provided a more realistic view of model performance.

🖼️ 3. Incorrect Prediction Visualization

Problem:
Even after improving training metrics, prediction outputs still appeared as solid-color masks.

Root Cause:

Direct visualization of raw softmax outputs

Hard argmax collapsing uncertain probabilities into a single dominant class

Solution:

Visualized per-class probability maps before applying argmax

Verified correct mask decoding during inference

Used probability-aware interpretation to confirm the model was learning

This revealed that learning was happening, but was being hidden by improper visualization.

🧪 4. Unstable Validation Performance

Problem:
Validation loss fluctuated heavily across epochs, indicating poor generalization.

Root Cause:

Over-training without convergence monitoring

High model complexity relative to dataset size

Solution:

Introduced Early Stopping with validation-based monitoring

Restored best-performing model weights automatically

Tuned training duration to stop at the optimal point

This stabilized validation performance and prevented overfitting.

🔁 5. Reproducibility and Debugging Complexity

Problem:
Frequent changes in model behavior made debugging difficult and results hard to reproduce.

Solution:

Modularized training, evaluation, and visualization code

Standardized configuration files for hyperparameters

Documented training workflow and reproducibility steps clearly

This made experimentation more systematic and reliable.

🎯 Key Takeaway

Most challenges were not architectural, but analytical—understanding why the model behaved a certain way and fixing the training strategy accordingly.
Addressing these issues transformed the project from a naive segmentation attempt into a robust, imbalance-aware deep learning system.

**Open Innovation**

How this project fits into the Open Innovation track

This project fits the Open Innovation track by presenting a flexible and reusable semantic segmentation framework that can be adapted across multiple real-world domains beyond a single predefined use case.

Rather than focusing on a narrow problem, the system addresses a fundamental challenge in computer vision—accurate and reliable pixel-level understanding under class imbalance and complex visual conditions. The techniques developed in this project, such as imbalance-aware loss functions, robust evaluation strategies, and failure-driven model refinement, can be readily extended to applications including autonomous navigation, remote sensing, environmental monitoring, and medical imaging.

The project encourages open experimentation and extension, allowing future teams or developers to:

Plug in new datasets and classes

Swap model backbones or encoders

Adapt the pipeline for different environments and constraints

By prioritizing generalization, interpretability, and reproducibility, this work aligns with the spirit of open innovation—creating solutions that are not only technically sound but also broadly applicable and scalable across domains.

**Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation Challenge - LLMs and AI**

This project directly addresses the Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation Challenge by developing a deep learning–based system capable of performing robust pixel-level scene understanding in complex, unstructured outdoor environments.

Offroad scenes are inherently challenging due to:

Irregular terrain and natural objects

Severe class imbalance (dominant ground regions vs sparse obstacles)

Ambiguous boundaries and varying lighting conditions

Our approach focuses on these exact challenges by:

Implementing semantic segmentation models (U-Net–based architectures) for offroad scene parsing

Using imbalance-aware loss functions (Dice and Dice + Cross-Entropy) to avoid dominant-class bias

Evaluating performance with IoU/Dice metrics instead of misleading pixel accuracy

Performing failure-case analysis to understand real-world limitations in offroad environments

The resulting system produces reliable and interpretable segmentation maps, which are essential for downstream offroad applications such as autonomous navigation, terrain understanding, and robotic perception.

By emphasizing robustness, generalization, and class-awareness, this project aligns closely with the goals of the track and demonstrates how modern AI techniques can be applied to challenging offroad perception tasks.

### AI Hallucination Detection-Watchdog
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-hallucination-detectionwatchdog-0897) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Rijja-explore/Hallucination-Watchdog) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Cloudflare for AI Safety

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

WATCHDOG solves the growing problem of unsafe, hallucinated, or misleading outputs generated by Large Language Models (LLMs). As AI systems are increasingly integrated into healthcare, education, finance, and governance, incorrect or harmful responses can lead to serious consequences. Traditional AI deployments rely entirely on the model’s internal safety mechanisms, which are not always reliable. WATCHDOG acts as a real-time safety gateway that analyzes every AI response before it reaches the user. It enforces ALLOW, WARN, or BLOCK policies based on risk scoring, contradiction detection, and verification mechanisms—ensuring responsible AI usage and increasing trust in AI-powered systems.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was designing an accurate risk detection and enforcement logic that minimizes false positives (blocking safe content) and false negatives (allowing harmful content). Balancing safety with usability required refining scoring thresholds, contradiction checks, and verification workflows. Another challenge was handling API rate limits and fallback mechanisms without breaking the system flow. Deployment complexities, dependency conflicts (e.g., spacy/blis builds), and maintaining seamless frontend-backend integration also required careful debugging. Ensuring that the enforcement decision (ALLOW/WARN/BLOCK) aligns correctly with the actual LLM response was technically demanding but critical for system credibility.

**Agentic AI / ML**

WATCHDOG aligns strongly with Agentic AI because it functions as a supervisory agent overseeing another AI system. Instead of a single LLM operating independently, this architecture introduces a governance layer that evaluates, verifies, and controls outputs before delivery. In agentic frameworks, systems consist of multiple agents with specialized roles—generation, evaluation, decision-making, and enforcement. WATCHDOG acts as a policy-enforcement and reasoning agent, applying structured checks (risk scoring, RAG validation, contradiction analysis). This moves beyond passive AI usage into controlled, decision-aware AI ecosystems—an essential step toward scalable, autonomous, and responsible AI systems.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fumoney-ba60) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/bhagyarana/FUMONEY) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.fumoney.in) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Push%20to%20Prod%20Hackathon:%20Building%20at%20the%20Frontier-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pushtoprod-india.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> An AI CFO for Indian salaried professionals.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://www.fumoney.in

**What is the problem your project solves?**

**The problem: India's salaried middle class has money but no map.**

- ~90M salaried Indians earning ₹6L–₹30L/yr plan retirement on **WhatsApp forwards and a relative's advice**
- Their financial life is scattered across 8 places — salary slip, EPF portal, 3 mutual fund apps, a loan statement, an insurance PDF
- **Nobody knows their number.** Not the corpus. Not the date. Not what a ₹40L home loan costs them in retirement years
- Existing tools are either **calculators** (one number, no context) or **investment apps** (they sell you products)

**Why it matters**

- India has **no social security net**. A missed decade of compounding is unrecoverable
- Inflation quietly halves purchasing power every ~12 years — medical inflation runs at 11%
- The cost isn't abstract: under-insuring, over-buying a home, or a 5-year-late SIP start each cost **₹50L–₹2Cr** by retirement

**The impact**

Give someone one honest number and the levers behind it, and financial anxiety becomes an arithmetic problem. That's a solvable thing.

**How you are solving it?**

**A financial operating system, not a calculator.** Three layers:

### 1 · A deterministic financial engine — accuracy is the product

- Pure, tested TypeScript: FIRE corpus, SIP, EMI, inflation, fitness score, SIP allocation, paycheck distribution
- **156 unit tests across 10 suites**; every formula verified against hand calculation within ₹1
- India-native by default: ₹ Indian grouping (lakh/crore), separate general / education / medical inflation, EPF·PPF·NPS·ELSS·SGB as first-class assets
- One number out the front: **the corpus that buys your freedom**, plus a 0–100 Financial Fitness Score across 5 pillars

### 2 · An AI CFO that acts, not just answers

- Claude tool-use agent runs over the user's real data — reads the snapshot, runs FIRE scenarios, models loan prepayment, projects goals
- **Proactive Money Review**: scans the whole plan and surfaces the single highest-rupee finding ("your ₹4L FD matures in 12 days")
- **Voice briefings** in 11 Indian languages, so a plan can be *heard*, not just read

### 3 · A product built for trust

- **Agent tools never write.** Every change comes back as a confirmable diff card; the server re-validates and re-computes on confirm
- **Row-Level Security on all 17 tables** — a user can only ever reach their own rows
- **No bank linking, no UPI access.** Users type their own numbers. Nothing to breach
- Every projection carries a projection-not-advice disclaimer. **Free forever — no paid tier, so no incentive to sell products**

**Also shipped:** 7-step onboarding with draft persistence, 10 dashboard modules, a paycheck distribution guide, and a full PDF financial report.

**How Did You Use Claude?**

Claude is **both the product's brain and its co-builder.**

### In the product

- **`claude-opus-5` is the default model** across the app (`claude-haiku-4-5` as the fast-tier fallback), via the Anthropic SDK — plus a rule-based responder so the app never goes dark
- **Agentic tool-use loop** (`/api/ai/agent`) with 7 tools over the user's real financial state:
  - `get_financial_snapshot` · `run_fire_scenario` · `model_loan_prepayment` · `project_goal`
  - `propose_create_goal` · `propose_update_goal` · `propose_delete_goal`
- **The safety design that matters:** write tools return *proposals*, never database writes. The user approves a diff card; a separate confirm route re-validates every field and **recomputes the money server-side**. An LLM that misreads one sentence can't delete someone's retirement goal
- **Engine computes, Claude narrates.** In Money Review, all rupee figures are detected in pure, unit-tested TypeScript — the model's only job is to pick the finding that matters most and say it like a human. Model-authored arithmetic is untestable and wrong often enough to lose trust
- **Adaptive thinking + effort control** on Opus 5 for genuinely hard planning questions
- **Vision-ready doc parsing, BYOK support** (bring your own Anthropic/OpenAI key), 3 premium calls/user/IST day quota, AES-256-GCM encrypted key storage

### In building it

- Built end-to-end with **Claude Code**, driven by a custom `CLAUDE.md` + a **22-skill agent library** (`verify`, `financial-calc`, `design-review`, `a11y-audit`, `new-migration`, …) that encodes this repo's conventions so quality doesn't depend on my memory

### Experimental Hackathon Build
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/talk-me-out-of-it-641c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Archived experimental build from a past hackathon.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![prava](https://img.shields.io/badge/prava-333333?style=flat-square) ![visa](https://img.shields.io/badge/visa-333333?style=flat-square) ![senso](https://img.shields.io/badge/senso-333333?style=flat-square) ![Linq](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linq-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most shopping technology is designed to help people discover more products and check out faster. But many shoppers do not need more encouragement to spend—they need help answering a more important question:

**Should this purchase happen at all?**

**Talk Me Out of It** is an AI-assisted shopping decision tool that helps people pause before an impulse purchase. Shoppers can virtually try on an item, then answer five practical questions about their wardrobe, budget, lifestyle, care requirements, and likelihood of actually wearing it.

Transparent, deterministic rules produce one of four recommendations:

**Buy It
Try It in Store
Borrow or Rent
Walk Away**

AI supports the decision without controlling it. **OpenAI** explains the verdict in clear, conversational language, while **Senso** provides source-backed context and makes the agent’s authority boundaries visible to the user. Neither system can independently change the verdict or initiate a transaction.

When a purchase genuinely makes sense, the user reviews the exact merchant, product, size, currency, and amount before deciding whether to continue. The demonstrated sandbox authorization flow then adds explicit human checkpoints:

- A **Visa** card credential secures the card layer.
- Passkey confirms that the person approving the next step is present.
- **Prava** manages the product-specific approval, one-time card credential, and authorization return to the application.
- The human remains responsible for the final decision.

This separation makes shopping both smarter and safer:

**AI advises. Rules decide. Humans authorize.**

Talk Me Out of It reduces impulsive and regretted purchases without blocking legitimate ones. It gives shoppers a clearer way to evaluate what they want, understand why a recommendation was made, and retain control throughout the transaction process.

A separately validated **Linq** integration also demonstrates how the experience can be shared with a shopping friend through iMessage after the purchase journey.

**The problem it solves**

Most shopping agents are designed to help people buy faster. But many shoppers do not need more encouragement to spend—they need help deciding whether a purchase should happen at all.

**Talk Me Out of It** combines virtual try-on with five practical purchase questions to produce one of four clear recommendations: **Buy It, Try It in Store, Borrow or Rent, or Walk Away.**

When the recommendation is Buy It, **OpenAI** explains the reasoning in plain language. The user then reviews the exact merchant, product, size, currency, and amount before explicitly confirming or cancelling. Only after that informed human decision does **Prava** complete the sandbox transaction.

The product is designed to reduce impulsive purchases while **preserving a clear, trustworthy path to checkout when the purchase genuinely makes sense**.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part was not creating a payment session—it was designing a commerce flow that remained trustworthy from recommendation to checkout.

### 1. Separating recommendation from authorization

The existing product already produced a deterministic verdict: Buy It, Try It in Store, Borrow or Rent, or Walk Away. The challenge was preventing a `BUY_IT` recommendation from being treated as permission to spend.

I solved this by adding two separate human decisions:

1. The user chooses to continue from `Buy It` to `Review Purchase`.
2. The user reviews the merchant, product, size, currency, and exact amount before confirming or cancelling.

OpenAI may explain the existing verdict, but it cannot change the verdict or initiate payment. Prava is only called after explicit confirmation.

### 2. A payment session is not a completed purchase

During technical testing, I confirmed that Prava could create a sandbox session, return a hosted checkout URL, and report a `pending` status. However, that alone did not prove that the merchant checkout had completed.

To avoid showing a false success state, I treated each stage separately:

- session created;
- user authorization completed;
- merchant checkout submitted;
- final transaction result returned;
- success, failure, cancellation, or expiration displayed to the user.

The product only shows a completed purchase when a real sandbox result is available.

### 3. Adding commerce without breaking the existing product

Talk Me Out of It already had a virtual try-on and five-question decision flow. Adding merchant selection, purchase review, payment, and transaction results introduced several new states without changing the original experience for users who should not buy.

I handled this by keeping the existing verdict engine intact and adding the transaction flow only after a `BUY_IT` result. The other three recommendations continue to end without payment.

### 4. Protecting credentials and maintaining a clean build history

The project uses multiple external services, including YouCam, OpenAI, and Prava. All secret keys are stored only in server-side environment variables and are excluded from the repository and logs.

I also kept the pre-hackathon technical research separate from the official build branch, so the final submission can clearly distinguish the existing product, preflight validation, and work completed during the hackathon.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part of the project was integrating the payment and authorization flow while the Sandbox behavior, documentation, and production-readiness requirements were still evolving.

From the user’s perspective, the hosted payment experience looked fast and polished. From the developer’s perspective, however, the process involved several stages that were not always clearly separated:

- creating a session and product-specific approval,
- generating and validating a one-time card,
- confirming the user through Passkey,
- receiving authorization,
- submitting the credential to the merchant,
- and determining whether a transaction had occurred.

During development, I encountered server-side instability, confusing Sandbox credential details—including inconsistent CVV guidance—and production requirements that were clarified later. Some steps also required developers to interpret reference UI designs rather than follow one stable, end-to-end implementation contract.

The final merchant-checkout stage depended on browser automation. Product approval, one-time card issuance, Passkey confirmation, and authorization return were successfully demonstrated, but the automation failed before the card could be submitted to the merchant. Later guidance clarified that production eligibility also required an expected test-card/insufficient-funds decline from the merchant.

The hardest product problem was therefore not only making the integration run. It was ensuring the interface never overstated what had happened.

I addressed this by defining explicit transaction states:

- decision completed,
- human review required,
- authorization started,
- one-time card issued,
- Passkey confirmed,
- authorization received,
- merchant checkout pending.

I also embedded the hosted authorization experience directly into the application, added a fallback path, and kept every transactional action behind explicit human confirmation.

This allowed the product to distinguish clearly between:

**Authorization received**

and:

**Merchant purchase completed**

That distinction became a central trust principle:

**AI advises. Rules decide. Humans authorize.**

The experience reinforced that financial infrastructure requires stable credentials, precise state definitions, reliable server behavior, and clear production criteria. Ambiguity can make it difficult for users to understand what they approved and whether money actually moved.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

AI helps the shopper make a clearer purchase decision, while **Visa** provides a familiar layer of payment trust.

Through **Prava**, the sandbox flow demonstrated product-specific approval, **Passkey** confirmation, and one-time **Visa** card issuance. The AI cannot proceed without explicit human authorization.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Talk Me Out of It solves a clear consumer problem through a working public product, not only a concept.

It already combines **virtual try-on**, tested decision logic, grounded AI explanations, human-controlled authorization, and a separately validated sharing flow. Future paths include retailer integrations, affiliate commerce, and premium decision tools.

**OpenAI**

The OpenAI API powers **the explanation layer of the live product**.

Deterministic rules produce the verdict, while OpenAI explains the shopper’s trade-offs without changing the result or initiating payment. Codex supported implementation, testing, and failure-state review.

**iMessage Agent**

Linq extends an individual shopping decision into a trusted social conversation.

The integration was validated through successful backend API responses and real delivered iMessages. I plan to make this **sharing** and second-opinion feature part of the future product.

**Agent Commerce Discovery & Trust**

Senso makes the agent’s knowledge and authority boundaries visible.

It retrieves official Talk Me Out of It documentation and displays **source-backed context** directly in the purchase flow, helping users **verify the verdicts**, payment states, and limits of the AI.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

The experience **turns impulse shopping into a clear journey**: try on the item, answer five questions, receive a verdict, understand the reasoning, and review the purchase.

The agent is playful and honest, but the user always knows what the AI decided, what supports it, and what still requires human approval.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Talk Me Out of It treats commerce as a decision problem before treating it as a conversion flow.

**Virtual try-on**, **practical questions**, **grounded AI explanations**, **human review**, **payment authorization**, and **social sharing** each appear at the right stage. The goal is to reduce regret and friction without removing human control.

Crystal Chang

### AllScale Subscription Warden
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/xssx-9104) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/slucifersz/subscription-warden) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomy for the agent,hard limits on the spending

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Giving the agent authority without giving it unbounded spending power.

The naive fix — just restrict what the agent can do — kills the point of having an agent. Instead I fully separated decision from enforcement: the agent decides freely, a deterministic Warden independently vetoes anything outside the user's authorization, and a single Scheduler is the only charge initiator. This way the agent can be as smart (or as wrong) as it likes and still cannot overspend.

Timeouts vs. declines — the double-charge trap.

Early on, a charge that timed out (outcome unknown) was being retried like a normal failure — which risks charging the user twice. A decline is safe to retry, but a timeout is not. I fixed this with an idempotency rule keyed on subId:period:attempt: declines retry under a new reference, timeouts replay the same reference and never create a new one. Both paths are now locked down by acceptance tests (declined → 3 distinct references; timeout → 1 reference replayed 3×).

Making "rail-agnostic" true, not just a claim.

It's easy to say the core doesn't depend on a specific payment provider. To prove it, I added an executable isolation test that asserts the 14 core files leak no vendor/adapter import — and a portability test that runs the full loop against a stub rail with no Prava at all. If someone accidentally couples the core to a vendor, the test fails.

**The problem it solves**

As AI agents begin to handle recurring payments — subscriptions, renewals — on a user's behalf, a core trust problem appears: how do you give an agent real decision-making power while guaranteeing it can never spend beyond what the user authorized?

Subscription Warden solves this with a separation-of-powers design:

The Agent only decides — renew, renegotiate, retry, pause, cancel, or escalate. It sees only redacted facts (amount, cycle, merchant, history) and never touches a payment credential.
The Warden enforces. Even when the agent says "renew," the Warden independently re-checks every decision against deterministic bounds — the per-period authorized amount, the cumulative cap, and the authorized merchant scope. Exceed any of them and the charge is vetoed. The agent's word is never enough; the boundary decides.
The Scheduler is the only component that can move money, with full idempotency: an explicit decline retries under a new key, while an unknown/timeout outcome replays the same key — structurally preventing double-charges.

No single component ever holds both "decide" and "charge." The core is also fully rail-agnostic: 14 core files carry zero vendor dependency (enforced by an executable isolation test), so swapping payment rails is swapping one adapter. It integrates Prava as the rail, with OpenAI available as an optional decision agent.

Who it's for: anyone building agent-driven commerce who needs an agent to act autonomously on payments without handing it unbounded spending power.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Subscription Warden is agentic commerce at its highest-stakes point: the moment an agent moves money. It targets recurring payments — where an agent must act autonomously, period after period, without a human approving each charge.

The core contribution is a separation-of-powers model that makes an autonomous payment agent safe to deploy:

The agent decides (renew / renegotiate / retry / pause / cancel / escalate) but never touches a credential and never moves money.
The Warden independently enforces the user's authorization — per-period cap, cumulative cap, merchant scope — and vetoes any charge that exceeds it, no matter what the agent decided.
The scheduler is the sole charge initiator, with idempotency that distinguishes a decline (retry under a new key) from a timeout (replay the same key), structurally preventing double-charges.

It integrates Prava as the payment rail, and the core is fully rail-agnostic (enforced by an executable isolation test), so the same safety model works across providers. An optional OpenAI-backed agent shows the design holds even when decisions come from an LLM — because the Warden enforces the boundaries regardless of what the model says.

In short: it lets agents transact on your behalf with genuine autonomy but bounded authority — the trust foundation agentic commerce needs to move real money.

> The AI that shops for you

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

India is one of the biggest market for e-Commerce, but for a decade nothing has changed. This Hackathon gave us the chance to change the Indian e-commerce market.

## Solution
The user tells the products they require in natural language, for example: "get me a pair of shoes and pants in color red." AI asks them a few questions to better understand  preferences, then through MCPs, the user is shown products based on the said preferences. Users select products by swiping left/right.

### Other Features
- LinQ based price drop alert system
- Voice and image based input support
- Input validation system that informs users if a product can be found through MCPs or not
- Support for 20+ MCPs including Swiggy, Lenskart, Pulmona, Instamart
- GPT 5.6, Luna is the AI agent doing the heavy lifting
- AI recommendation system for products
- List mode: dump your entire shopping list, AI finds you your products with your preferences, you can lay back and chill out 😁️

## Why Is It Useful Today?
Current e commerce websites put way too much overload on the consumer. They have to pass through dark patterns, manually compare products, and check out every time by filling in the details. All this can be sped up and simplified using AI. AI needs to be quietly integrated into daily life without getting the attention of others. AutoCart does this perfectly. It does the hard part of comparing and finding products based on user preferences, while you take the final shot of selecting the final product you purchase.

## What Do You Plan to Build Next?
If we had the resources, we would first get first party MCP access from vendors, since most don't return images. A user is afraid of purchasing the product if there is no image to see, and this is a huge drawback in our project because most of our product images are not displayed. We would work together to fix the issue.
Secondly, charge 2% per purchase to keep the business sustainable.
We would also fix some bugs we could not fix due to time constraints. 
Adding a memory mode so the model understands user preferences better after each purchase.

> AI in your inbox that keeps you moving.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Swift](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Travel disruptions force people to juggle airline notices, merchant searches, delivery deadlines, policies, and payments at the worst possible moment. Tavra is an iMessage-native travel recovery agent that understands what went wrong, finds a trustworthy recovery option, gets exact user approval, and completes the purchase through Prava. Senso verifies the policies and merchant context behind the decision, while OpenAI coordinates the recovery workflow. I started with delayed baggage and plan to expand Tavra into a broader travel continuity agent for any urgent disruption.

Use case: Tavra helps travellers recover when delayed baggage leaves them without essential items before an important meeting or event.
Through iMessage, it finds a trustworthy recovery bundle that can arrive in time, gets exact purchase approval, pays securely through Prava, and returns proof of the completed order with an option to file it directly with the airline for reimbursement.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest challenge was keeping the iMessage conversation consistent while Linq webhooks, image extraction, location sharing, and OpenAI responses completed at different times. Delayed or duplicate events sometimes produced replies that no longer matched the conversation. I fixed this by serializing work per chat, deduplicating event and message IDs, assigning each turn a revision, and discarding stale asynchronous responses.

Prava and merchant checkout also required careful debugging. Payment approval did not automatically mean that a merchant order had been attempted, and merchant availability in the UAE sandbox was limited ( I request for this to be taken into account while judging ). We traced every payment state, separated approval from checkout, added idempotency and exact-total validation, and recorded the expected sandbox merchant decline as evidence. This made the flow reliable without claiming that an order succeeded when the merchant had not confirmed it.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Tavra uses Prava’s payment infrastructure to translate user intent into tightly scoped purchasing authority. The approval is restricted to a specific merchant, products, amount ceiling, expiry time, and one-time checkout. If the price, merchant, product, or delivery terms change, Tavra blocks the transaction and asks for fresh approval instead of silently exceeding the user’s intent.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Tavra begins with a focused and urgent problem which is helping travellers recover from disruptions that require an immediate purchase, but has a larger path toward becoming a complete travel continuity agent. Future versions can help travellers prevent problems before departure, recover from a wider range of disruptions, and reconcile expenses and reimbursement evidence afterward. The product can be distributed directly to travellers or through employers, travel platforms, insurers, airlines, and card issuers.

**OpenAI**

OpenAI powers the intelligence and orchestration behind Tavra. It interprets disruption messages and screenshots, extracts the traveller’s objective, identifies missing information, turns policy context into structured constraints, and coordinates the Senso and Prava tools. Sensitive payment rules remain deterministic in code, while OpenAI handles the ambiguous reasoning and natural conversation required to turn a stressful travel incident into a clear recovery plan.

**iMessage Agent**

Linq is Tavra’s primary product interface rather than a notification layer. Travellers can forward an airline notice or screenshot, answer clarification questions, review recovery options, receive the Prava approval link, and get transaction updates and the Recovery Receipt inside the same iMessage conversation. It also incorporates a custom built iMessage extension to keep a lot of the functionality directly inside iMessage. This allows Tavra to help someone in the messaging interface they already use while travelling.

**Agent Commerce Discovery & Trust**

Tavra uses Senso’s verified context to evaluate airline or company policies and compare merchant delivery, return, and product information before making a purchase. Senso materially affects the decision. For example, Tavra can reject a cheaper merchant when its delivery promise cannot be verified. After checkout, Tavra records the verified merchant outcome so future recovery decisions can use evidence from previous transactions. It uses a complete feedback loop.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Tavra demonstrates the complete agentic-commerce loop: it receives a real-world travel problem, understands the traveller’s objective and constraints, evaluates recovery options, obtains permission, and completes the transaction through Prava. The agent does not stop at recommendations; it takes the workflow from disruption to a visible purchase outcome and Recovery Receipt that it can then file with the airline.

**The problem it solves**

Buying is easy to browse and hard to finish: people juggle tabs, incomplete totals, shady sellers, and group prefs, then still leave chat to check out, unsure what an agent is allowed to spend. Cascade turns a natural-language ask into a verified, policy-bound purchase with passkey-scoped authority and a receipt back in the same thread.

**Challenges we ran into**

Prava MCP shopping vs REST credentials tripped up, test keys don’t auth MCP, and production MCP hosts can’t be treated as sandbox, so we fail closed on checkout until the path is explicitly safe.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Cascade implements intelligent commerce as agent-proposed buy → user-approved, merchant- and amount-scoped payment authority → deterministic checkout and receipt. Spend never moves on model output alone; typed code rebinds offer, contract, and total before authorization. That gives agents a safe commerce path without exposing payment credentials or unbounded spend.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Every shopping agent can find products; almost none can take irreversible money with proof of authority. Cascade is the missing layer. Contract, evidence, passkey-scoped spend, checkout, receipt, so agents become operators, not search boxes. That’s the wedge: whoever owns governed purchase becomes the rails for agentic commerce.

**Participation Credits (Already Claimed)**

-claimed participation credits

**OpenAI**

Cascade uses OpenAI for structured intent extraction, turning a free text ask into a typed purchase draft before any merchant or payment step. The model proposes; LangGraph orchestration and deterministic services own ranking, spend, and checkout. That keeps OpenAI in the interpretation layer while money stays outside the model.

**iMessage Agent**

Cascade uses Linq as a messaging adapter: inbound events become missions, and clarifications, BUY links, progress, and receipts can return in-thread. The same governed kernel powers web and MCP. Linq is the channel, not a separate commerce stack. Webhooks are signed, deduped, and fail-closed so chat ingress never invents spend authority.

**Agent Commerce Discovery & Trust**

Cascade uses Senso as the evidence plane for agent commerce: live quotes come from merchants, while seller, catalog, and policy claims are grounded only in approved ingested sources. Unverified offers never rank, so discovery stays trust-bounded instead of hallucinated. That separates “what we found” from “what we can prove” before any spend is requested.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

We have a great UI!

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Cascade turns a natural-language ask into a verified, policy-bound purchase with passkey scoped Prava authority, agents never hold the wallet. Models propose; deterministic code owns money and state. The same kernel is exposed over MCP so other agents can buy without credentials.

### TwinGuard AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/twinguard-ai-8cde) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://theta-zen2-me-f8x7.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IQOuVXpDPmQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HexaFalls%202-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hexafalls2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Resolving confusions and saving lives.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Serverless Database Issues: Vercel’s serverless environment caused MongoDB connection timeouts, forcing us to write a custom global caching solution to keep the database stable.
AI & Voice Latency: Integrating Gemini (AI) and ElevenLabs (Voice) caused slight delays; we had to heavily optimize our API calls to ensure emergency voice alerts felt instantaneous.
Hardware Constraints: Handling device camera permissions for the QR scanner across different mobile browsers required building robust fallbacks so the app wouldn't crash.
Security vs. Speed: We had to design an authentication flow that was highly secure for HIPAA compliance, yet fast enough (using PINs/Biometrics) that it wouldn't slow nurses down during emergencies.

**The problem it solves**

In high-pressure Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs), fragile preemies—especially multiple-birth infants like identical twins—are exposed to critical safety risks due to identity confusion and administrative overload. Legacy hospital systems treat every patient as an isolated entry, leaving a massive blind spot when adjacent incubators hold twins who share matching surnames, identical parent demographics, and nearly indistinguishable physical appearances. Exhausted clinicians performing fast-paced shifts are at constant risk of cross-contaminating expressed breast milk or misadministering weight-sensitive medications between siblings, while losing up to 30% of their time to tedious, manual charting on clunky interfaces. TwinGuard AI bridges this gap by merging proactive, dual-patient safety cross-checks with zero-friction clinical documentation to eliminate medical errors and save valuable nursing hours.

The Identical Twin Link Protocol (Twin-to-Twin Engine)
The Twin-to-Twin Link Protocol is a context-aware safety engine that actively links sibling incubator slots in real time (e.g., Bed NICU-04A Baby Ethan and Bed NICU-04B Baby Evan). Unlike traditional barcode scanners that blindly verify one patient at a time, TwinGuard automatically recognizes high-risk similarity indices and enforces a dual-slot verification check whenever a nurse scans a patient wristband, breast milk bottle, or medication syringe. If a clinician accidentally attempts to give Twin B’s milk bottle or medication to Twin A, the system immediately flags the proximity conflict and blocks the administration before an error reaches the infant. Beyond instant interception, this feature continuously tracks prevented mismatches as Near Misses to calculate a live Ward Safety Score (~98%) and maintains an audit-ready Activity Log, giving head nurses and risk management teams complete oversight over unit compliance.
AI Voice Notes (Speech-to-Text Clinical Assistant)
The AI Voice Notes feature serves as a hands-free clinical copilot designed to eliminate documentation friction and combat nurse burnout. By tapping into speech-to-text intelligence, doctors and nurses can dictate observations, treatment updates, or care plans on the go without stopping to type manually or stepping away from the incubator. Crucially, the system features accumulated note retention, meaning new voice entries build upon previous clinical history without overwriting past observations, creating a complete, chronologically searchable record of patient care. These spoken entries automatically sync with the patient profile, streamline shift handoffs, and can be exported as structured PDF reports for hospital-wide records.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

It helped us to generate audio

**Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**

It helped us to use it as a database for our project

**Healthcare**

TwinGuard AI fits the healthcare track perfectly because it tackles three major industry pain points:

i)Patient Safety: Uses QR scanning and AI to actively prevent fatal clinical errors (e.g., giving the wrong medication or mixing up twins).

ii)Provider Burnout: Replaces tedious typing with Voice-to-Text charting, saving nurses valuable time.

iii)Smart Infrastructure: Upgrades hospital software from passive databases to active "AI Co-pilots" that issue real-time voice alerts to catch mistakes before they happen.

One of the main challenges was designing a meaningful workflow using Google AI Studio instead of relying on a single generic prompt. Another challenge was defining a realistic project scope as a solo developer. To overcome this, I focused on core functionality—issue reporting, AI-based categorization, and status tracking—rather than adding complex features. **The problem it solves**

Traditional complaint systems are often slow, fragmented, or inaccessible, resulting in delayed responses and lack of accountability.

By providing a digital, AI-assisted reporting platform, NagarNetra makes it easier for people to raise issues, understand their category, and track progress in a transparent way. This reduces manual effort, improves communication between citizens and authorities, and helps ensure that civic problems are identified and addressed more efficiently and safely.

> Your Gateway to Real-time Space Exploration

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Space and astronomy information is often scattered across multiple websites, applications, and data sources. A user interested in tracking the International Space Station, checking night sky conditions, learning about constellations, monitoring upcoming celestial events, or exploring planetary data typically has to switch between several different platforms.

StarTrek addresses this problem by bringing these features together into a single, interactive, and easy-to-use platform.

### How StarTrek Helps

🛰️ **Real-Time ISS Tracking**

* Provides live information about the International Space Station, including location, altitude, velocity, and crew data.
* Eliminates the need to search across multiple ISS tracking websites.

🌙 **Night Sky Observation Assistance**

* Helps users determine whether current conditions are suitable for stargazing.
* Provides moon phase information, visibility analysis, and observation recommendations based on location.

✨ **Astronomy Education**

* Makes learning about constellations, planets, and celestial phenomena more engaging through interactive visualizations and structured information.
* Simplifies access to educational astronomy content.

☄️ **Celestial Event Monitoring**

* Allows users to stay informed about important astronomical events such as eclipses, meteor showers, and planetary conjunctions.
* Centralizes event information and countdowns in one place.

🪐 **Unified Space Exploration Experience**

* Combines multiple astronomy tools into a single dashboard, reducing complexity and improving accessibility for students, enthusiasts, and curious learners.

By integrating real-time data, educational resources, and interactive visualizations, StarTrek makes space exploration more accessible, informative, and engaging for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges during development was working with **real-time external APIs**. Since StarTrek relies on live space and astronomy data, some API requests occasionally failed due to timeouts, rate limits, or temporary service unavailability. This sometimes caused missing data or inconsistent updates in the interface.

To solve this, we implemented:

* Error handling and fallback mechanisms
* Graceful degradation when APIs were unavailable
* Cached and backup responses where possible
* User-friendly loading and status indicators

Another challenge was **integrating multiple independent modules into a single cohesive platform**. The ISS Tracker, Night Sky Command Center, Constellation Explorer, Celestial Events Database, and Planetary Explorer were developed in parallel, making consistency across the application a challenge.

We addressed this by:

* Establishing a common component structure
* Using TypeScript interfaces for consistent data handling
* Maintaining a modular architecture with reusable components
* Regularly reviewing and testing integrations between modules

We also encountered several TypeScript and build-related issues while preparing the production deployment. Some components expected different data structures than what was being returned from APIs or local datasets, which caused type errors during the build process.

To overcome this, we:

* Refined our type definitions
* Standardized API responses
* Performed frequent production builds to catch issues early
* Improved validation and error handling throughout the application

Overall, these challenges taught us valuable lessons about working with real-time data, debugging large codebases, collaborating within a team, and building scalable web applications under hackathon time constraints.

### Smart Web Application Firewall
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/smart-web-application-firewall-3c29) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sutirtha0505/waf-proxy) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/qs_xXEpvuPE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Synchronicity%20S2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://synchronicity-s-2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> BERT based Web Application Firewall

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cybersecurity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cybersecurity-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Modern web applications are constantly targeted by attacks such as SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Command Injection, Path Traversal, SSRF, and automated bot traffic. Traditional Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) rely heavily on static signatures and manually maintained rules, making them ineffective against new, evolving, or previously unseen attack patterns. Security teams must continuously update rules, review alerts manually, and investigate suspicious requests, resulting in increased operational overhead and delayed threat response. 

## How It Helps

This AI-Driven Smart WAF automates the detection and mitigation of malicious web requests by combining machine learning, real-time traffic analysis, and human-assisted validation. Instead of depending solely on predefined signatures, the system analyzes request behavior and content to identify both known and unknown attack vectors. 

### Key Benefits

* **Detects unknown attacks** that may bypass traditional rule-based WAFs.
* **Reduces manual rule management** through adaptive machine learning.
* **Provides real-time protection** against application-layer threats.
* **Minimizes false positives** using confidence-based decision making.
* **Learns continuously** from supervisor feedback and newly discovered attack patterns.
* **Maintains service availability** through zero-downtime model updates and version-controlled deployments. 

## What People Can Use It For

### Web Application Protection

Protect websites, APIs, SaaS platforms, e-commerce applications, and internal enterprise systems from malicious traffic before requests reach the backend server.

### Automated Threat Detection

Identify attacks such as:

* SQL Injection
* Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
* Command Injection
* Local/Remote File Inclusion
* SSRF
* CSRF
* Brute Force Attacks
* HTTP Floods
* Request Smuggling
* Business Logic Abuse
* Other emerging attack vectors 

### Security Operations Support

Assist security analysts by automatically handling high-confidence threats while forwarding uncertain cases for human review.

### Security Research & Training

Create continuously growing, labeled datasets of real-world web attacks that can be used for retraining, threat analysis, and security research.

### AI-Assisted Defensive Security

Provide organizations with an intelligent security layer capable of adapting to changing attack techniques without requiring constant manual rule updates. 

## Why It Is Better Than Existing Approaches

| Traditional WAF                  | AI-Driven Smart WAF               |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Static rules                     | Adaptive machine learning         |
| Detects known attacks            | Detects known and unknown attacks |
| Manual rule updates              | Continuous learning               |
| High maintenance effort          | Automated improvement             |
| Fixed detection logic            | Evolves with new threat data      |
| Limited contextual understanding | Analyzes full request behavior    |

The result is a smarter security layer that improves detection accuracy, reduces operational workload, and adapts to evolving cyber threats without disrupting protected applications.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

Building an AI-driven Web Application Firewall within a hackathon timeline came with several technical challenges.

### 1. NVIDIA Triton Inference Server on Apple Silicon

Our original plan was to deploy the AI model using NVIDIA Triton Inference Server for high-performance model serving. However, Triton is primarily designed for NVIDIA GPU environments and does not provide straightforward support for Apple Silicon (M-series) systems.

Since a significant portion of our development was performed on Apple Silicon devices, we faced compatibility issues during setup and testing. To overcome this, we temporarily switched to a lightweight FastAPI-based inference service for local development while keeping the architecture modular so Triton can be integrated later in GPU-enabled production environments.

---

### 2. Running DVWA on macOS

Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) is one of the core components used to test our WAF against real attack scenarios. Running DVWA natively on macOS proved challenging due to dependency mismatches involving PHP, Apache, MySQL, and Docker networking configurations.

To solve this problem, we containerized the entire DVWA environment using Docker and standardized the deployment process across all team members. This ensured everyone could test the WAF against the same target environment regardless of their operating system.

---

### 3. Real-Time WAF and AI Integration

A major challenge was integrating the WAF request pipeline with the AI engine while maintaining low latency. Every incoming HTTP request must be intercepted, transformed into structured data, analyzed by the model, and then either allowed or blocked in real time.

We addressed this by designing lightweight API endpoints, minimizing request preprocessing overhead, and implementing health-check mechanisms so the WAF can quickly determine whether the AI service is available before forwarding requests.

---

### 4. Designing a Multi-Class Attack Taxonomy

Web attacks come in many forms, and creating a classification structure that covers SQL Injection, XSS, SSRF, Command Injection, Path Traversal, Brute Force attacks, and other vectors required significant planning.

We solved this by designing a hierarchical attack taxonomy with unique numeric labels for each attack type. This structure allows future attack vectors to be added without requiring major architectural changes.

---

### 5. Handling Low-Confidence Predictions

Machine learning models are not always certain about their predictions. Automatically blocking legitimate traffic based on uncertain predictions could lead to false positives and poor user experience.

To mitigate this risk, we introduced a Human-in-the-Loop workflow. Requests with low confidence scores are routed to a supervisor dashboard where they can be manually reviewed and labeled. These validated samples are later used to retrain and improve the model.

---

### 6. Dataset Preparation and Labeling

Building a high-quality cybersecurity dataset was one of the most time-consuming tasks. Public datasets often contain inconsistent formats, missing metadata, or attack categories that do not align with our requirements.

We addressed this by creating a custom preprocessing pipeline and defining a standardized request representation that could be used consistently across training, inference, and future retraining workflows.

---

### 7. Continuous Learning Without Downtime

One of our goals was to allow the AI model to evolve over time without interrupting traffic inspection. Replacing a model while the WAF is actively processing requests can introduce downtime and reliability issues.

To solve this, we designed a version-controlled deployment workflow where newly trained models are validated first and only promoted to production after passing performance checks, ensuring uninterrupted protection.

These challenges significantly influenced the final architecture and helped us build a more practical, scalable, and production-oriented security solution.

**Open Innovation**

## Open Innovation

Our project combines **Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Cybersecurity** to create an adaptive Web Application Firewall capable of learning from real-world attack data.

The solution leverages modern AI/ML techniques to improve threat detection while incorporating human feedback to continuously enhance model performance. By combining expertise from multiple domains—cybersecurity, machine learning, backend engineering, frontend development, and DevOps—the project demonstrates a multidisciplinary approach to solving modern security challenges.

The platform is designed to evolve as new attack vectors emerge, making it an example of open innovation where AI-assisted security systems can continuously learn, adapt, and improve over time. The architecture can be extended to support new datasets, attack categories, detection models, and deployment environments, encouraging future collaboration and research in intelligent cyber defense systems.

### Relevant Tracks

* Artificial Intelligence (AI)

**The problem it solves**

**ICU monitoring** today is broken in a predictable way. Bedside monitors fire alarms when a single vital crosses a threshold -a heart rate too high, an SpO₂ too low -long after a patient has already begun to deteriorate. This approach is purely reactive, generates enormous alert fatigue for clinical staff, and completely misses the early warning signs of conditions like sepsis, which unfold gradually across multiple physiological systems over time.
SENTRI ICU solves this by shifting ICU surveillance from threshold-triggered alarms to continuous temporal intelligence. Instead of reacting to isolated readings, **SENTRI** analyzes rolling windows of the latest six vitals per patient — tracking trends, acceleration patterns, and baseline deviations simultaneously. An XGBoost model trained on engineered temporal features detects deterioration trajectories before they become crises, generating explainable, human-readable clinical insights like "heart rate rising steadily" or "respiratory distress worsening" rather than a generic alarm. When high risk is confirmed, the system autonomously escalates through Telegram and Gmail workflows, delivers AI-generated nurse summaries via Llama 3.3, and logs persistent alerts to MongoDB — closing the loop from detection to clinical action without requiring manual intervention.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Rolling-window inference with correct chronological ordering** was the most technically demanding piece. Maintaining a strict temporal sequence across continuous vital streams -ensuring each prediction window contained exactly the right six readings in the right order ;required careful backend state management. Any ordering error silently corrupts the model's feature engineering and produces meaningless predictions.
**Simulating realistic physiological deterioration** proved far harder than simply generating noisy random vitals. True ICU deterioration follows momentum-gradual, correlated changes across heart rate, SpO₂, blood pressure, and respiratory rate that mirror actual septic progression. We built a scenario queue system with progressive physiological logic to produce clinically plausible trajectories rather than statistical noise.
**Balancing sensitivity against alert fatigue** was an inherent tension throughout. A model too sensitive floods staff with false positives and recreates the exact problem we were solving. We tuned the risk classification thresholds and temporal feature weights carefully to surface meaningful deterioration signals while suppressing noise from transient vital fluctuations.
**Synchronizing four concurrent systems** in real time — the streaming vitals backend, the FastAPI ML inference layer, the canvas waveform renderer, and the live dashboard UI — required precise state management and timing control on the frontend to prevent drift, stale predictions, or visual desync across panels.

**AI & ML**

The core is a real ML pipeline, not a wrapper. The project doesn't just call an LLM API and call it "AI." At its heart is an XGBoost classifier trained on hand-engineered temporal features — heart rate slope, SpO₂ decline rate, respiratory distress progression, blood pressure deviation — that runs continuous inference on a rolling window of patient vitals. This is classical supervised ML applied to a structured healthcare problem.

**Best use of n8n**

How SENTRI ICU fits the n8n track:

- n8n  acts as the escalation layer between ML prediction and human action

- Triggers automated Telegram and Gmail alerts on high-risk deterioration detection

- Delivers AI-generated nurse summaries through the workflow, not just raw alarms

- Logs and persists alerts to MongoDB with acknowledgment support

- Demonstrates n8n in a genuinely high-stakes, time-critical clinical environment
