### Keynection
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/keynection-28ca) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/therealhamad/keynection/tree/replit) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Smart Actions At Your Fingertips

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chrome Extension](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome%20Extension-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Switching between Gmail, Slack, Notion, Linear, and docs to share a link, send a summary, or log a task is slow and breaks flow. Keynection solves that by putting a single command palette (Alt+Space / Option+Space) on top of any tab.

What people use it for:

- Share and summarize in one place — From an article or doc, they can “Email this page”, “Summarize for Slack”, or “Save to Notion” without opening each app. The extension uses the current page (or selection) and Claude to draft the message or doc; they review, edit, and send.

- Turn selections into actions — Selecting text exposes actions like “Email selection”, “Share to Slack”, “Save to Notion”, “Extract tasks”, “Create Linear issue”, or “Schedule meeting from text”. That turns copy-paste-and-manual-formatting into a short flow.
- Standups without tab-hopping — “Generate Standup Update” pulls the last 24 hours from GitHub, Notion, and Google Calendar, then drafts a standup. They tweak and copy or post to Slack instead of manually checking each tool.
- Fewer context switches — Gmail, Slack, Discord, Notion, Google Docs/Sheets/Calendar/Drive, GitHub, and Linear are available from one overlay. 
- Credentials live in the extension (API keys, OAuth, webhooks); no required backend, so setup stays in the browser and data stays under the user’s control.

How it makes tasks easier/safer:

- Easier: One shortcut and search instead of opening multiple tabs and apps. Context-aware suggestions (e.g. “Email this page” mainly on article-like pages) reduce noise. AI drafts are editable before sending.
- Safer: Users add their own API keys and OAuth in extension Settings; the extension talks directly to each service from the browser, so there’s no central server that stores or proxies their credentials.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Keyboard input affecting the underlying page
With the overlay open, arrow keys and Enter were still moving focus and triggering actions on the page (e.g. Google search). Fix: The overlay’s key handler now calls stopPropagation() and preventDefault() for all keys while the palette is open, and only the overlay handles them. Typing in the search box and submitting forms (e.g. Cmd+Enter) is handled inside the overlay so the page stays inert.
2. OAuth redirect URI mismatch (Google)
Using Google OAuth from the extension failed with redirect_uri_mismatch because the redirect URI wasn’t in the Google Cloud project. Fix: The extension uses chrome.identity.getRedirectURL(); we surface that exact URI in Settings and document that users must add it in Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials → their OAuth client → Authorized redirect URIs. One-time setup per user.
3. API calls failing from the content script (CORS)
Direct fetch() calls from the content script to Gmail, Notion, GitHub, etc. were blocked by CORS. Fix: All external API calls go through the background script (service worker). The content script sends messages to the background, which performs the fetch and returns the result. The extension’s host permissions allow those origins, so the background script isn’t subject to the page’s CORS rules.
4. Claude API key not persisting in Settings
After saving the Claude key, it sometimes disappeared on refresh or wasn’t available when generating standup. Fix: Save logic was overwriting storage with the current form values; if the key field was empty (e.g. hidden or not yet filled), it wrote an empty string. We changed it to: read existing claude_api_key from storage first, and only set a new value when the user actually entered a non-empty key; otherwise we keep the existing value. We also added error handling after chrome.storage.local.set() and made the Save button type="button" so it never submits a form by accident.
5. Keeping the architecture simple (extension-only integrations)
We explored using a Replit backend and server-side “connectors” for integrations, but that added complexity and still required users to manage secrets. Fix: We moved to an extension-only model: all integrations (Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Drive, Linear, Notion, GitHub, Slack, Discord) are configured and used from the extension via API keys, OAuth, or webhooks stored in chrome.storage.local. The optional server is only for things like logging; the core product works without it and stays easier to reason about and deploy.

**Hackathon Prizes**

Used both Replit + Claude AI for building Keynection

> AI-Powered Styling Intelligence

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Computer Vision](https://img.shields.io/badge/Computer%20Vision-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Most people struggle to know what truly suits their body type, skin tone, and occasion. Fashion choices are often based on guesswork, leading to low confidence and poor styling decisions.

AI Aura Farmer transforms fashion into a data-driven, AI-powered experience by combining body analysis, virtual try-on, and structured aura scoring.

How It Works (Flow)

User Authentication
Users securely log in using a verified authentication system.

Upload Image
The user uploads a photo, which is securely stored in the backend.

AI Body Analysis
The system analyzes:

Skin tone

Body type

Height category

Proportions

A structured physical profile is generated.

Smart Outfit Matching
Based on the detected attributes and selected occasion, the system filters a tagged clothing database to recommend compatible outfits.

Virtual Try-On
The selected outfit is digitally applied to the user’s image while preserving:

Face identity

Body proportions

Skin tone

Lighting consistency

Post Creation
The user selects up to three looks and creates a post for evaluation.

AI Aura Evaluation
Multiple AI judges evaluate the look based on:

Color harmony

Proportion fit

Social impact

Luxury aesthetic

Trend relevance

An AI Aura Score is generated.

Community Voting
Other users contribute aura points through reactions and feedback.

Leaderboard & Badges
Users earn badges and rankings based on their cumulative aura score.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Faced

One of the biggest challenges was selecting the right model for Virtual Try-On.
There are many image generation models available, but most either:

Altered facial identity

Changed body proportions

Modified skin tone

Produced unrealistic fabric textures

Finding a balance between realism, speed, and cost was difficult.

Fortunately, Replit’s Gemini integration for image generation helped simplify experimentation, allowing us to iterate quickly and integrate VTON directly within the Replit ecosystem.

### FUMONEY - Your Financial OS
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fumoney-your-financial-operating-system-075a) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.fumoney.in) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Clarity Before Every Financial Decision

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer Motion](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer%20Motion-333333?style=flat-square) ![React hook form](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20hook%20form-333333?style=flat-square) ![shadcn/ui](https://img.shields.io/badge/shadcn/ui-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**95% of Indian salaried professionals invest without knowing their exact retirement number.**

They use 3 spreadsheets, 2 SIP calculators, and still can't answer: *"What happens to my retirement if I take a ₹50L car loan?"*

FUMONEY fixes this in under 5 minutes.

### What people use it for:

- **Know your real FIRE number** - Not with generic 6% inflation. With *actual* Indian rates: 9% for education, 11% for medical, 7% for real estate. This alone can mean a **₹40 lakh difference** in your retirement corpus.

- **Ask "What If" and get real answers** - Type *"What if I get a 30% salary hike?"* and watch your retirement age, monthly SIP, corpus, and fitness score **recalculate in 3 seconds**. Powered by AI, grounded in math.

- **One score for your entire money life** - The Financial Fitness Score (0-100) measures 5 pillars: emergency fund, insurance coverage, debt ratio, savings rate, and goal coverage. No vague advice - a number that moves when you take action.

- **Spot insurance gaps before it's too late** - Most Indians carry 3x income cover when they need 10x. FUMONEY shows the gap as a clear progress bar, not buried in policy documents.

- **Plan every goal with its own inflation** - Your child's IIT fees in 2040 inflate at 9%. Your house inflates at 7%. Your vacation at 6%. Each goal gets the right math, the right SIP, and a priority rank.

- **Replace your ₹50,000/year financial advisor** - Full dashboard, FIRE projections, goal tracking, AI simulations, insurance analysis - **free**. The entire financial picture that advisors charge lakhs for, accessible to a 25-year-old earning ₹8L.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Financial Accuracy vs. User Simplicity

The calculation engine handles compound interest with monthly compounding, category-specific inflation (6 different rates), FIRE multiplier methodology, and SIP future value projections. Every formula was **cross-verified against Excel spreadsheets and established bank calculators**. The challenge was making a 28-year-old with zero finance background understand their numbers in 10 seconds - not 10 minutes.

### 2. Making AI Not Hallucinate Numbers

The AI simulator needed the user's *entire* financial profile - income, expenses, 7 asset types, 5 loan types, insurance policies, goals, retirement settings - to give useful advice. But LLMs hallucinate numbers. The solution: **the financial engine calculates every number first**, then the AI wraps those *verified* calculations in natural language. The AI never invents a rupee amount.

### 3. Indian Number Formatting Everywhere

`₹24,50,000` - not `₹2,450,000`. Indian numbering (lakhs/crores) breaks the international grouping system. Every chart tooltip, every animated KPI counter, every slider label had to be individually wired to `Intl.NumberFormat('en-IN')`. One miss and the entire dashboard loses trust.

### 4. Real-Time Recalculation Without Jank

The retirement planner has 4 interactive sliders. Moving *any one* triggers a cascade: recalculate FIRE corpus → recalculate required SIP → regenerate 30-year projection → re-render the area chart + year-by-year table. Solved by keeping the **entire financial engine as pure functions with zero side effects** - making memoization trivial and re-renders instant.

### 5. Row Level Security Across 13 Tables

Every table needed RLS policies tracing ownership back to `auth.uid()` - either directly or through the `financial_plans` foreign key chain. One misconfigured policy = data leakage between users. Built a **unified RLS pattern** that cascades through the entire schema and tested every query path to ensure zero cross-user access.

### 6. 7-Step Onboarding Without Drop-off

Collecting salary, expenses, 7 asset types, insurance details, loans, AND a risk profile quiz - without the user closing the tab at step 3. Solved with **Zod validation per step** (instant feedback, no surprise errors at the end), a persistent progress bar, and smart defaults so users can skip what they don't have yet.

**Hackathon Prizes**

**1. This problem is real - and nobody's solving it.**
95% of Indian salaried professionals don't know their retirement number. Not because they're lazy - because no free tool connects salary, SIPs, EMIs, insurance gaps, and goals into one picture. Financial advisors charge ₹50,000/year for this. FUMONEY does it in 5 minutes, for free.

**2. Built entirely from scratch in 5 hours.**
No templates. No boilerplate starters. Every line - from the 13-table database schema with Row Level Security, to the pure TypeScript financial engine with 15+ calculation functions, to the AI decision simulator powered by Claude - was written from scratch between 11 AM and 4 PM.

**3. This isn't a calculator - it's a full operating system.**
- 7-step onboarding with Zod validation at every step
- 5 real-time KPI cards with animated counters
- FIRE retirement planner with interactive sliders and year-by-year projections
- Goal-based planning with category-specific Indian inflation (education 9%, medical 11%, real estate 7%)
- Financial Fitness Score (0-100) across 5 weighted pillars
- Insurance gap analysis with coverage adequacy tracking
- AI Simulator - type "What if I take a ₹50L home loan?" and your entire financial future recalculates in seconds
- 4 data visualizations (portfolio projection, asset allocation, goal timeline, insurance gaps)

**4. India-first, not India-adapted.**
INR in lakhs and crores. SEBI-aligned assumptions. Post-tax returns. EPF, PPF, NPS, ELSS tracked natively. Built for the 22-44 year old earning ₹6L-₹30L - not a Western app with a currency swap.

**5. Production-grade, not demo-grade.**
Row Level Security on all 13 tables. TypeScript strict mode with zero `any`. Supabase Auth with protected middleware. Zod validation on every form and API route. Unit tests on every financial calculation. Responsive across mobile, tablet, and desktop. Legal pages (privacy, terms, disclaimer) included.

**6. The AI doesn't guess - it calculates first.**
Most AI demos hallucinate. Our simulator runs the financial engine first (verified math), then wraps the results in Claude-powered natural language advice. The AI never invents a number.

**7. Market timing is perfect.**
India's mutual fund SIP accounts crossed 10 crore in 2025. The FIRE movement is exploding. Yet the gap between free SIP calculators and expensive advisors remains wide open. FUMONEY sits exactly in that gap.

### drishti
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/drishti-2c6b) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drishti-hackathon.replit.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> STEM by ear for blind learners.

![JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Pillow](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pillow-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chrome Extension](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome%20Extension-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3​](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

91.5% of blind students in India drop out between Class 8 and Class 9. Out of 334,670 visually impaired students enrolled nationally, only 15% reach secondary education. The dropout cliff happens when STEM content becomes inaccessible.

Why Students Drop Out: Two Main Barriers:

1. Diagrams and Figures Are Invisible
Screen readers skip or misread circuit diagrams, graphs, geometry, chemistry structures, and biology illustrations. Students often hear silence or generic alt-text like "image" where visual understanding matters.

2. Math and Formulas Are Gibberish
Screen readers read symbols character-by-character:
"x²" becomes "x-s-q-u-a-r-e-d"
"∫(x²)dx" becomes "integral sign open parenthesis x superscript 2..."
"H₂SO₄" becomes "H subscript 2 S O subscript 4" with awkward pauses
Mathematical fluency is hard when every expression has to be decoded mentally.

The Language Gap
Most accessible content is English-only, which excludes rural students who use Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Bengali, and similar languages as their first language.

**What Drishti Does**
Describes Diagrams in Spatial Terms
Uses Claude Vision AI to explain diagrams with clear positioning, e.g. "100-ohm resistor on left, 9-volt battery in center, 220-ohm resistor on right, connected in series," and then asks follow-up questions like "What is the total resistance?"

Converts Math to Natural Speech
"x²" → "x squared" (Hindi: "x varg", Tamil: "x vargam")
"∫x dx" → "integral of x with respect to x"
Works for equations, chemical formulas, and other math expressions.
Teaches Interactively in 10 Indian Languages
Describes a concept → asks a question → evaluates the answer → generates practice problems.

Adjusts difficulty from performance and flags topics where the student struggles.
Available in Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Malayalam, Punjabi, and Odia via Sarvam AI.

Chrome Extension on Web Pages
Alt+D on diagrams, Alt+M on math, Alt+A to answer, Alt+P for practice.
Works on web content: YouTube, Zoom (web), Wikipedia, and online textbooks.
No separate app; access stays inside the browser.

But to show it work inside replit, just appended a frontend too to play around with. But originally its an Extension / intelligence layer.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. No audio playback (Manifest V3)
Service workers have no DOM, so new Audio() and speechSynthesis don’t exist in the background. Playback was moved into the page via chrome.scripting.executeScript, where Audio and speechSynthesis are available.

2. CORS blocks image extraction
Canvas and fetch for cross-origin images hit CORS. Fix: Fall back to chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab() when DOM extraction fails.

3. Service worker stops mid-request
Workers shut down after ~30s idle, but vision + translate + TTS often take longer. A keep-alive (getPlatformInfo every 20s) runs during those flows so the worker stays active until they finish.

**The problem it solves**

## 🎯 The Problem it Solves

Traditional antivirus software can only detect threats **they've seen before** using signature databases. This leaves a dangerous gap:

- **Zero-day attacks** go undetected until signatures are created (days/weeks later)
- **Fileless malware** operates in memory without disk artifacts
- **Heavy resource usage** (15-30% CPU, 2GB+ RAM) slows down systems
- **Update dependency** requires constant internet connection

**KARAN-KAVACH solves this by:**
- ✅ Detecting **unknown threats** by monitoring suspicious behavior patterns
- ✅ Catching **memory-based attacks** (buffer overflows, code injection, heap sprays)
- ✅ Using **<2% CPU** and **<90MB RAM** — ultra-lightweight
- ✅ Working **offline** without cloud dependencies
- ✅ Providing **real-time protection** with instant threat blocking

**Who should use it:**
- Security professionals testing endpoint protection
- System administrators protecting critical servers
- Researchers studying malware behavior patterns
- Anyone wanting lightweight, proactive security monitoring

**The problem it solves**

Healthcare today is mostly reactive, not preventive. People often ignore early symptoms, forget important details during doctor visits, and have no structured way to track their health daily. Doctors, on the other hand, receive incomplete or unorganized patient history, making early diagnosis difficult.

Additionally, medical data privacy is a serious concern...patients have little control over who can access their sensitive health information, and emergency situations often lack quick access to critical medical history.

**Challenges we ran into**

- **Blockchain-style security with Supabase:**
Supabase is a traditional database, so implementing blockchain-like encryption and strict data isolation required custom logic on top of it.
 
- **Gemini AI integration:**
Connecting Gemini AI to health data was challenging while ensuring it did not behave like a medical diagnosis system.

- **Unique access key for doctors:**
Designing a secure, one-time, time-limited access key for each doctor visit and validating it correctly was complex.
 
- **Balancing security and usability:**
Ensuring strong data privacy without making the user or doctor flow complicated required careful design decisions.

**Open Innovation**

This project applies AI and blockchain technologies to healthcare, focusing on preventive care, data privacy, and secure doctor–patient collaboration.

1. Information Overload
Investors are bombarded with conflicting financial news and data. Sentimark consolidates price data, technical indicators, and ML-powered predictions into a single, easy-to-understand dashboard.

2. Emotional Decision Making
Many retail investors make impulsive decisions based on fear or hype. By providing data-driven forecasts using XGBoost machine learning models, Sentimark helps users make more rational, evidence-based investment choices.

3. Lack of Technical Analysis Skills
Not everyone understands RSI, moving averages, or volatility metrics. Sentimark presents these complex indicators visually through intuitive charts and plain-language insights.


4. Time-Consuming Research
Manually tracking S&P 500 stocks and analyzing trends takes hours. Sentimark automates this process, delivering instant analysis for any stock symbol with just a search.

Who Benefits:

- Retail investors seeking data-driven insights without expensive subscriptions
- Beginner traders learning to understand market patterns
- Busy professionals who need quick, reliable stock analysis
- Students studying financial markets and ML applications

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/05559d9e6e014261ac5c96981026d84a/b7b2e632-c53c-4dee-8dd1-37b1c9cd476d.png)

**Quantifying the Markets - Machine Learning**

Democratizes institutional-grade analytics for students and retail traders.
Sentimark directly addresses the core objective of Track 5: Quantifying the Markets by transforming raw financial data into actionable, interpretable intelligence using Machine Learning.

1. Analytical Rigor & Feature Engineering: In strict adherence to the track deliverables, we engineered specific quantitative features including Rolling Volatility (Standard Deviation), Moving Averages (MA20/MA50), and Lag Returns. Instead of feeding raw prices into a black box, our feature engineering layer specifically captures market momentum and risk, satisfying the requirement for "logical feature choice."

2. ML Modeling & Forecasting: We moved beyond basic linear trends by implementing a Random Forest Regressor (Ensemble Learning). This allows Sentimark to detect non-linear patterns in price action and forecast directional trends with greater accuracy than traditional statistical methods, fulfilling the mandate for "ML models for pattern detection."

3. Visualization & Interpretation: To address the "Insights & Interpretation" criteria, we built an interactive dashboard that doesn't just output a number. It visualizes the Volatility and Price vs. Moving Average crossovers in real-time, enabling retail investors to interpret the "why" behind the prediction and distinguish market noise from genuine signals.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/05559d9e6e014261ac5c96981026d84a/66d69702-db35-4f59-93d9-a38bb49febb3.png)

### Market Shock Intelligence System (MSIS)
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/market-shock-intelligence-system-msis-4195) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/archangel2006/MSIS) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://msis-fintech.my.canva.site/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PayLoad'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pay-load.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> When Markets Shift, Models Break: Regime Insights

![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Colab](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Colab-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Seaborn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Seaborn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# Problem 

- Financial markets behave very differently during **calm periods, volatility build-ups, and crisis events.**
- However, most traditional machine learning models treat all market periods the same, making them unreliable exactly when **risk awareness matters most**.

This leads to:
- Poor understanding of **when market risk is increasing**
- ML models and strategies **failing silently during stress periods**
- Over-reliance on prediction accuracy **without understanding uncertainty**

---

# Market Shock Intelligence System (MSIS) 

It helps users:

1. Identify **different market regimes** (calm, stressed, crisis) from historical data
2. Understand **volatility build-up** before major drawdowns
3. Evaluate **how models and strategies behave** across regimes, not just overall accuracy
4. Explain when and why ML models become unreliable, **improving risk awareness**



Instead of asking  
> ***What will the market do tomorrow?***

MSIS answers: 

> ***What kind of market are we in, how risky is it, and how trustworthy are our models?***

---

## Who Can Use This?

1. **Students & researchers** learning quantitative finance and ML
2. **Analysts & traders** studying risk and strategy robustness
3. **Institutions & regulators** interested in market stress analysis

**Challenges we ran into**

# 1. No True Labels for Market Regimes

Markets don’t come with labels like “calm” or “crisis,” which made supervised learning impractical for regime detection.

### How we addressed it

We used unsupervised clustering on returns, volatility, and drawdowns, and then interpreted the clusters based on observed risk behavior.

---

# 2. Model Performance Breakdown During Market Transitions

Some supervised models looked fine on average but performed poorly during sudden market shifts.

### How we addressed it:

Instead of optimizing accuracy alone, we analyzed model behavior separately across different regimes, which made the failure patterns visible.

---

# 3. Feature Sensitivity and Noise in Financial Data

Changing rolling window sizes sometimes led to noticeably different results, highlighting how noisy market data can be.

### How we addressed it:

We tested multiple window sizes and focused on simpler, more stable features that were easier to interpret.

**Quantifying the Markets - Machine Learning**

- This project fits naturally into the Quantifying the Markets - Machine Learning track because it focuses on understanding how markets behave, rather than simply predicting prices.

---

- We work with real historical market data and convert raw price movements into meaningful quantitative signals like **returns, volatility, drawdowns, momentum, and trends**. 
- These features are then used to study how market conditions change over time and how risk builds up, which is at the core of market quantification.

--- 

- Machine learning is used in a practical and interpretable way. Instead of treating all market days as the same, we first identify **different market regimes** and then analyze how risk and model behavior change across those regimes. 
- This helps explain why models perform well in some conditions and struggle in others, rather than just reporting a single accuracy number.

---

- The project emphasizes **interpretation, visualization, and reasoning**, using simple but effective ML techniques to make market dynamics easier to understand. 
- Overall, it aligns with the track’s goal of using machine learning as a tool to **analyze, quantify, and explain market behavior**, not just to make short-term predictions.

**The problem it solves**

- Financial literacy for kids is mostly theoretical and lacks real-world practice.
- Children rarely get a safe environment to make money decisions and learn from consequences.
- Real-life financial mistakes are risky, while existing apps focus more on lessons than experience.
- Fincity provides a risk-free, game-based simulation of real financial life.
- Kids manage a virtual monthly allowance and handle daily expenses.
- Multiplayer interactions teach lending, borrowing, saving, and trust.
- A reputation system rewards responsible behavior over wealth.
- Parental controls ensure safety while allowing independent learning.
- Makes financial education simple, engaging, practical, and effective.

**Challenges we ran into**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9ccc48b4753b478aa4688e106afc0456/2affca25-ffee-4f94-bf12-e6351b943f37.jpeg)WhatsApp Image 2026-02-02 at 23.39.20.jpeg
Balancing Visual Depth with Performance

 - One of our biggest challenges was building the city environment in a way that felt immersive without hurting performance.
- Using full 3D models looked great visually, but quickly became heavy and risky for smooth gameplay, especially on low-end devices.
- At the same time, we didn’t want to compromise the game feel or reduce player engagement.

Our Solution: Smart Visual Optimization

- We solved this by using isometric 2D images to simulate a 3D city experience.
- This approach gave us the visual depth of a 3D world while keeping rendering lightweight and fast.
- It allowed us to focus on gameplay logic, interactions, and smooth animations instead of heavy rendering costs.

Result

- The city feels alive and interactive while staying performant.
- The game runs smoothly across devices without sacrificing visual appeal.

**Financial Games & Finopoly - Game Development**

Fincity is a finance-first game that turns real-world money concepts into interactive gameplay mechanics. Instead of treating finance as theory, the game embeds budgeting, saving, lending, borrowing, trading, and trust directly into the core game loop.

Players manage a virtual monthly allowance, make daily spending decisions, and interact financially with other players in a multiplayer environment. Concepts like interest, delayed rewards, risk, and reputation are introduced naturally through in-game actions rather than instructions, aligning perfectly with the idea of learning finance through play, similar to Finopoly-style experiences.

The project strongly fits the Game Development aspect of the track by focusing on:

- Game loops and progression systems
- Social and multiplayer mechanics
- Reputation-based rewards instead of pure wealth accumulation

By combining financial abstraction with engaging game design, Fincity demonstrates how games can be used as powerful tools for financial education, making it a strong and relevant entry for the Financial Games & Finopoly track.

> Smart Financial Automation

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tesseract OCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tesseract%20OCR-333333?style=flat-square) ![Embeddings](https://img.shields.io/badge/Embeddings-333333?style=flat-square) ![Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Retrieval--Augmented%20Generation%20(RAG)-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAISS Vector Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAISS%20Vector%20Database-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vision-Language Models](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vision--Language%20Models-333333?style=flat-square) ![Local Large Language Models (LLMs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Local%20Large%20Language%20Models%20(LLMs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Faster-Whisper (Speech-to-Text)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Faster--Whisper%20(Speech--to--Text)-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Financial decision-making during disasters and climate-related events is often delayed, manual, and dependent on internet connectivity. Insurance claims, compensation payouts, and government relief funding rely on fragmented documents, images, and field reports that are difficult to analyze quickly and reliably.

This leads to delayed fund allocation, increased financial losses, lack of transparency, and unfair or inaccurate compensation decisions—especially in low-network or offline environments where cloud-based AI systems fail.

This project provides an offline-first multimodal AI system that helps stakeholders make faster, safer, and more transparent financial decisions using documents, images, and audio data.

It can be used for:
- Estimating financial damage from disaster images and reports
- Supporting insurance claim verification and fraud reduction
- Assisting governments in relief fund allocation and budgeting
- Enabling financial decisions in remote or low-connectivity regions
- Reducing manual effort in analyzing unstructured financial evidence

By working fully offline and using citation-backed AI responses, the system improves trust, reduces delays, and lowers operational costs in finance-related disaster response workflows.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges was running multimodal AI models entirely offline while maintaining reasonable performance on standard hardware. Vision-Language Models and local LLMs require high memory, which caused slow inference and occasional crashes during early testing.

Another challenge was OCR accuracy on low-quality or blurred images, which directly affected downstream financial analysis and summaries.

These issues were addressed by using lightweight, optimized models, restricting retrieval to top-relevant chunks using RAG, and applying basic preprocessing to images before OCR. This significantly improved stability, response time, and output reliability.

**Open Innovation**

Our solution fits the “Open Innovation – Redefining Finance” track because it extends finance beyond traditional banking and payments into real-world financial decision-making during disasters and climate events.

The system analyzes documents, images, and audio offline to estimate damage, verify evidence, and support faster insurance claims, compensation payouts, and government fund allocation. By enabling financial risk assessment and budget planning even in low-connectivity environments, the project directly improves how money is distributed, tracked, and utilized during critical situations.

Instead of building a conventional fintech product, we redefine finance by integrating AI-driven multimodal intelligence into insurance, governance, and climate finance workflows, making financial systems faster, fairer, and more resilient.

### Finopoly
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finopoly-17be) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/rohanchoudhary5210/Finopoly) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PayLoad'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pay-load.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> When age comes with responsiblities

![Unity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity-333333?style=flat-square) ![C#](https://img.shields.io/badge/C#-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Finance is often perceived as complex, boring, and intimidating, especially for students and first-time earners. Most people struggle to understand financial concepts like saving, spending, risk, and long-term planning because they are taught through theory-heavy explanations rather than real experiences. As a result, individuals make poor financial decisions in real life without fully understanding their consequences.

Traditional learning methods fail to show the cause-and-effect relationship between financial choices and life outcomes in an engaging way.

Finopoly solves this problem by transforming financial decision-making into a fun, interactive game, where players learn by playing, experimenting, and seeing the immediate and long-term impact of their choices. Instead of teaching finance through numbers and jargon, Finopoly allows players to experience how everyday decisions—such as spending, saving, investing, or taking risks—shape their virtual life journey. This makes financial learning intuitive, engaging, and accessible to everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

🐞 Balancing Randomness vs Player Control

One major challenge was designing the event system so that the game felt unpredictable without being unfair. Early versions relied heavily on random events, which sometimes caused players to lose progress despite making good decisions. To fix this, we introduced a risk and skill-based mitigation system, where higher skill levels unlock smarter choices and reduce the negative impact of bad events. This preserved randomness while still rewarding long-term planning.

🎮 Maintaining Clear Cause–Effect Feedback

Another challenge was ensuring players clearly understood why their stats changed after each decision. Initially, stat updates happened silently, which made the game feel confusing. We solved this by adding immediate visual feedback—such as floating stat changes and clear UI indicators—so players could instantly see the consequences of their actions.

🧠 Preventing Feature Overload

We initially planned many mechanics (loans, taxes, insurance, inflation), but this made the game feel complex and slowed development. We overcame this by deliberately simplifying financial concepts into four core stats and focusing on a tight gameplay loop. This helped us deliver a complete and playable demo instead of an unfinished feature-heavy game.

🛠️ Technical Integration Challenges

Implementing the turn-based system alongside event handling and UI updates required careful state management to avoid desynchronization bugs. We resolved this by centralizing game flow logic in a single manager and triggering UI updates only after state changes were finalized, ensuring stability and consistency throughout each turn.

**Financial Games & Finopoly - Game Development**

Finopoly fits directly into the Financial Games & Finopoly – Game Development track by transforming financial concepts into pure gameplay.
Instead of teaching finance through rules or theory, the game uses a turn-based life simulation where players learn by making decisions and experiencing their consequences. Core financial ideas such as earning, spending, saving, investing, and risk are abstracted into intuitive mechanics and visual feedback, making them easy to understand without real-world complexity. The focus is on fun, exploration, and strategy, with clear cause-and-effect outcomes that encourage experimentation and replayability. This aligns perfectly with the track’s goal of making finance engaging, accessible, and game-first.

### EchoGraph
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/skillx-6725) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Jeswanth-009/EchoGraph) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/tycmu-6GUfk) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/tycmu-6GUfk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MERGE--CONFLICT-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://mergeconflict.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Spatial Research Operating System

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Whisper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Whisper-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![langchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/langchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polars](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polars-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**🧩 The Problem: The "Data Disconnect" in Market Research**

In today's data-driven world, market research is fundamentally broken. Researchers are drowning in two disconnected oceans of data:

    The "What" (Quantitative): Massive CSVs, survey responses, and user metrics that tell us what is happening (e.g., "Retention dropped by 15%").

    The "Why" (Qualitative): Hours of audio interviews, focus group recordings, and open-ended feedback that explain why it's happening.

Current workflows are fragmented and manual:

    Researchers spend hours manually transcribing audio or copy-pasting rows from Excel.

    They struggle to link hard numbers (metrics) with soft data (human sentiment).

    The "Hallucination" Trap: Standard AI chatbots often invent facts. When an AI says "Customers hate the pricing," researchers can't easily verify who said that or where the proof is, leading to a lack of trust.

**💡 The Solution: EchoGraph - The Spatial Research Operating System**

EchoGraph replaces these fragmented tools with a single, Autonomous Research Intelligence Engine. It is not just a chatbot; it is a Spatial Knowledge Graph where AI agents actively investigate, correlate, and visualize data in real-time.
🚀 How It Makes Research Easier, Faster, & Safer:

1. Unified "Quant-Qual" Intelligence Instead of using separate tools for Excel and Audio, EchoGraph ingests both simultaneously.

    Use Case: A user uploads a survey CSV and 5 audio interviews.

    The Impact: The system automatically detects that "Low NPS scores" in the CSV correlate with specific "Pricing complaints" in the audio files. It draws a visible line connecting the metric to the quote, solving the "disconnected data" problem instantly.

2. Zero-Hallucination Traceability (Trust & Safety) Most AI tools are "Black Boxes." EchoGraph is a "Glass Box."

    The Feature: Every insight generated by our agents is a interactive node on the canvas.

    Why It's Safer: When the AI claims "Users find the UI confusing," you can click that node. The system immediately pulls up the exact source file and plays the exact audio segment (e.g., interview_04.mp3 at 12:45) or highlights the specific CSV row. This ensures 100% accountability and eliminates AI hallucinations.

3. Autonomous Agent Swarms Researchers no longer need to be prompt engineers. They simply ask a high-level question like "Why is churn increasing?"

    Automation: Our Multi-Agent System (Supervisor, Quant, Qual, and Conflict Agents) breaks down the task. They write their own Python code to analyze statistics and perform semantic searches on transcripts without human intervention.

    Efficiency: What used to take a human analyst 3 days of cross-referencing files now takes 30 seconds.

4. The "Infinite Canvas" Interface Text-based chat interfaces are linear and limiting. EchoGraph uses a Spatial UI (like Miro or Figma) that matches how researchers actually think.

    Visual reasoning: Users can see the logic flow. They can drag nodes, group insights, and visually explore the relationship between different data points.

    Conflict Detection: The system proactively identifies contradictions (e.g., "Survey data says users are happy, but audio transcripts show anger") and flags them visually with Red Conflict Nodes, preventing researchers from missing critical nuances.

**🎯 Who is this for?**

    Product Managers: To validate feature requests with real user voice evidence.

    Market Researchers: To cut report-writing time by 90% while increasing insight depth.

    Data Scientists: To effortlessly merge structured logs with unstructured human feedback.

EchoGraph transforms research from a manual chore into an interactive, visual journey of discovery.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Agent Infinite Loop Crisis** 🚨
**Problem:** The most critical issue was when our AI agents got stuck in an endless loop. The LLM would output text like "I'll analyze the data..." instead of actually executing tasks, causing the supervisor agent to repeatedly ask "What next?" and never progress.

**Root Cause:** Free LLM models (like OpenRouter's Trinity) don't reliably follow tool-calling patterns. Our code bound tools to the LLM but didn't handle cases where the model just described plans instead of calling functions.

**Solution:** We completely rewrote the agent architecture:
- **Quant Agent:** Instead of relying on LLM tool calls, we directly read CSV files using Polars and performed programmatic data analysis
- **Qual Agent:** Directly accessed transcript data from session storage instead of hoping the LLM would call search tools
- **Supervisor Agent:** Replaced LLM-based routing with hardcoded deterministic flow: Quant → Qual → Conflict → Complete

**Impact:** This transformed our system from unreliable (failing 80% of the time) to working consistently.

### 2. **WebSocket Integration Nightmare** 🔌
**Problem:** Socket.IO connections between FastAPI backend and Next.js frontend kept failing with cryptic errors like "connection closed" and "upgrade failed".

**Root Cause:** Multiple issues:
- Incorrect ASGI wrapping of FastAPI app
- Socket.IO client configuration mismatches
- CORS policy conflicts
- Session state synchronization problems

**Solution:** 
- Implemented proper `combined_app` pattern with FastAPI + Socket.IO
- Fixed CORS headers and WebSocket upgrade handling
- Added robust error handling and reconnection logic
- Created proper session state management with automatic cleanup

**Impact:** Real-time updates now work seamlessly, showing agent thoughts and node creation live.

### 3. **LLM Model Reliability & Cost Issues** 💰
**Problem:** Started with GPT-4o for development, but costs were prohibitive. Switched to free models (Trinity, then Gemma 3) which had inconsistent behavior and frequent API failures.

**Root Cause:** Free models have smaller context windows and less reliable instruction following, especially for complex multi-agent workflows.

**Solution:**
- **Model Selection:** Settled on Google Gemma 3 27B via OpenRouter (free, 131k context, good reliability)
- **Fallback Strategy:** Built graceful degradation when models fail
- **Prompt Engineering:** Restructured prompts to be more explicit and forgiving
- **Direct Data Access:** Bypassed unreliable LLM tool calls by having agents directly access data

**Impact:** Reduced costs to $0 while maintaining functionality.

### 4. **Frontend Canvas Rendering Issues** 🎨
**Problem:** Nodes were being created successfully (visible in backend logs) but not appearing on the React Flow canvas.

**Root Cause:** State synchronization issues between the graph store and session store. Nodes were created but not properly loaded into the canvas.

**Solution:**
- Fixed `loadFromSession()` to properly trigger `addNode()` calls
- Added proper state synchronization between WebSocket events and Zustand stores
- Implemented proper node positioning and layout algorithms

**Impact:** The visual canvas now accurately reflects the AI analysis results.

### 5. **Export API Method Mismatch** 📤
**Problem:** Clicking "Export Report" returned "Method Not Allowed" error.

**Root Cause:** Frontend was using `window.open()` (GET request) but backend expected POST method for export endpoints.

**Solution:**
- Modified frontend to use `fetch()` with POST method
- Implemented proper blob handling for file downloads
- Added error handling for export failures

**Impact:** Users can now successfully download Markdown and JSON reports.

### 6. **Vector Store Availability Issues** 🗄️
**Problem:** Qdrant vector database wasn't running, causing the entire system to fail during startup.

**Root Cause:** Optional dependency treated as required, no graceful fallback when database unavailable.

**Solution:**
- Made Qdrant completely optional with automatic detection
- Implemented caching for vector store availability
- Added fallback behavior when vector operations fail

**Impact:** System works with or without vector database, improving reliability.

### 7. **Audio Transcription Setup** 🎵
**Problem:** Getting local audio transcription working with faster-whisper was challenging due to model size and dependencies.

**Root Cause:** Large model files (2GB+) and complex dependency management for PyTorch/CUDA.

**Solution:**
- Used CPU-only faster-whisper with base model (smaller, faster)
- Implemented proper error handling for transcription failures
- Added fallback behavior when audio processing fails

**Impact:** Local transcription works reliably without requiring GPU resources.

### 8. **Multi-Service Docker Configuration** 🐳
**Problem:** Getting docker-compose to work with FastAPI, Next.js, and optional Qdrant services.

**Root Cause:** Port conflicts, dependency t

**Open Track**

# 🚀 Track Fit: Open Track

**EchoGraph** fits the Open Track because it is a **category-defining tool** that scores highly across all universal judging metrics—Originality, Technical Complexity, and UX. Unlike niche solutions, it solves a broad, fundamental problem (data synthesis) using a novel interface (Spatial Computing).

### 1. High Score on "Originality & Uniqueness"

* **The Status Quo:** Most hackathon submissions are standard "Text-In, Text-Out" chatbots.
* **EchoGraph's Edge:** It introduces a **Spatial Operating System** paradigm. Instead of a linear chat, it visualizes research as an **interactive Knowledge Graph**.
* **Why it fits Open Track:** The Open Track rewards projects that stand out from the crowd. Building a visual, node-based analysis tool immediately differentiates your project from the hundreds of standard RAG chatbots.

### 2. Excellence in "Technical Implementation"

The Open Track often goes to the project with the most impressive engineering under the hood. EchoGraph demonstrates a "Full-Stack" technical dominance:

* **Local ML Pipeline:** You aren't just wrapping an API. You are running **Faster-Whisper** locally for audio transcription.
* **Complex Orchestration:** You use **LangGraph** to manage stateful, multi-turn agent workflows (Supervisor → Worker → Critic), which is significantly harder than simple linear prompting.
* **Hybrid Data Processing:** The system successfully merges two incompatible data types—Structured CSVs (Quantitative) and Unstructured Audio (Qualitative)—into a single unified graph structure.

### 3. "Design & UX" Mastery (High Weightage)

The judging criteria explicitly state that "Design & UX... will have a high weightage".

* **The UX Innovation:** Research data is messy. A chat window is a poor way to explore it. EchoGraph's **Infinite Canvas** allows users to physically organize, group, and explore insights.
* **Visual Feedback:** The "Agent Activity" sidebar provides transparency, showing the user exactly what the AI is thinking ("Qual complete, moving to conflict detection"), which creates a superior user experience compared to a spinning loading icon.

### 4. "Problem Understanding & Idea Clarity"

* **Universal Utility:** The problem of "Data Disconnect" (having numbers in Excel but reasons in Zoom calls) is universal across industries—from Marketing to Healthcare to Finance.
* **Open Track Appeal:** Because the problem is broad and the solution is flexible, EchoGraph appeals to judges from *any* background. It isn't restricted to a specific niche; it is a general-purpose intelligence engine.

### 5. "Innovation & Creativity"

* **The "Conflict Node":** The creative application of an adversarial agent (The Conflict Detector) to find contradictions between datasets is a novel feature that demonstrates deep creative thinking.
* **Visual Logic:** Visualizing the "derived from" edges creatively solves the problem of "AI Hallucination" by visually proving where every insight came from.

### Summary for Submission

> "EchoGraph is submitted to the **Open Track** because it reimagines the fundamental interface of AI interaction. By moving from 'Chat' to 'Spatial Graphs' and implementing a robust, multi-agent backend that merges Quantitative and Qualitative data, it demonstrates the high level of **Originality**, **Technical Depth**, and **UX Design** required to win the Open Innovation prize."

**Agentic AI / ML**

# 🤖 Track Fit: Agentic AI / ML

**EchoGraph** is not just a passive analysis tool; it is a **Multi-Agent System (MAS)** that autonomously plans, executes, and synthesizes complex research tasks. It moves beyond simple "input-output" LLM interactions to demonstrate true **agentic behavior**.

### 1. Autonomous Multi-Agent Orchestration

The core of EchoGraph is built on **LangGraph**, enabling a team of specialized AI agents to collaborate without human intervention. This directly addresses the track's focus on "building anything incorporating AI Agents."

* **The Supervisor Agent (The Brain):** Acts as an intelligent router that breaks down high-level user queries (e.g., *"Why is retention dropping?"*) into sub-tasks and delegates them to the appropriate worker agents.
* **Stateful Execution:** Unlike standard chatbots, our agents maintain a shared state (the "Research Graph"), allowing them to build context and refine their findings iteratively over time.

### 2. Advanced Tool Use & Code Execution

A key definition of an "AI Agent" is the ability to use tools to interact with the world. EchoGraph's agents demonstrate this capability:

* **Quant Agent:** Does not hallucinate statistics. It writes and **executes real Python code** (using Polars/Pandas) to analyze CSV datasets, detecting outliers and calculating metrics deterministically.
* **Qual Agent:** Uses **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)** tools to perform semantic searches across unstructured audio transcripts, extracting evidence that humans might miss.

### 3. Local Machine Learning Pipelines

We go beyond simple API wrappers by integrating local ML models for privacy and performance:

* **Local Speech-to-Text:** We utilize **Faster-Whisper** running locally to transcribe audio, demonstrating a sophisticated, privacy-preserving ML pipeline.
* **Vector Embeddings:** The system uses vector databases (Qdrant) to map relationships between disparate data types (text vs. numbers), using embedding models to "understand" the semantic link between a metric drop and a user complaint.

### 4. Adversarial "Reasoning" Agents

True intelligence requires self-correction. EchoGraph includes a **Conflict Detector Agent** whose sole purpose is to "audit" the findings of other agents.

* It actively looks for contradictions (e.g., *"The Quant agent says NPS is up, but the Qual agent found negative sentiment"*).
* This mimics human critical thinking and elevates the system from a simple data processor to an **intelligent research partner**.

### 5. Innovation in "No Problem Statement"

The track asks participants to "build anything". We chose to tackle the **unstructured data analysis** problem by building a **Spatial Operating System**.

* Instead of a text box, we created an **Infinite Canvas** where agents "show their work" by spawning nodes.
* This visual representation of the *Agentic Workflow* (showing exactly how Agent A's finding led to Agent B's discovery) offers a level of explainability and user interaction that standard ML projects lack.

**Track Opinion**

# 🎯 Track Alignment: MDG SPACE

Our project, **EchoGraph**, was engineered specifically to solve the core challenge of the MDG SPACE track: replacing fragmented manual workflows with a single, end-to-end AI system that unifies Quantitative and Qualitative data.

Here is how EchoGraph fulfills each of the track's core technical requirements:

### 1. Unified "End-to-End" System

**The Requirement:** Build a system that ingests both qualitative (audio/text) and quantitative (CSV) data and automatically performs analysis.
**Our Solution:** EchoGraph is a **Spatial Research Operating System**. Unlike disparate tools, it ingests structured CSVs and unstructured Audio/Transcripts simultaneously. Our multi-agent backend orchestrates the entire lifecycle—from ingestion (Whisper STT) to analysis (Polars/Pandas) to synthesis—without human intervention.

### 2. Auto-Linking Quant & Qual (The Key Driver)

**The Requirement:** "Auto-linking quant findings with relevant qual evidence" (e.g., matching low satisfaction scores to negative verbatims).
**Our Solution:** This is the heart of EchoGraph. We built a specialized **Conflict Detector Agent** that actively scans for relationships between data types.

* It detects a statistical anomaly (e.g., "Churn is high in Gen Z").
* It semantic-searches transcripts for explaining factors (e.g., "Gen Z users find the UI confusing").
* It **visually draws a "derived-from" edge** on the infinite canvas connecting the metric directly to the quote, creating an explicit, explainable link.

### 3. Traceability & Hallucination Prevention

**The Requirement:** "Focus: Prevent hallucinations and ensure traceability."
**Our Solution:** We implemented a **"Glass Box" UI**. Every insight generated by our agents is rendered as an interactive node containing a specific `SOURCE_ID` and citation metadata.

* Users can click a **Quote Node** to play the exact audio segment (timestamped).
* Users can click a **Metric Node** to see the specific CSV rows used for calculation.
* This ensures that every AI claim is grounded in verifiable evidence, meeting the "Responsible AI" criteria.

### 4. Advanced "Conversational" Interface

**The Requirement:** "Design a chat UI allowing users to Drill down: Insight - Theme - Quote - Respondent."
**Our Solution:** We moved beyond a linear chat window to an **Infinite Canvas (Spatial UI)**.

* Users query the system in natural language (*"Is pricing the main issue?"*).
* The system responds not just with text, but by **spawning a knowledge graph** live.
* Users "drill down" by physically zooming into nodes, exploring connections, and interacting with the data spatially, offering a far more robust UX than a standard chatbot.

### 5. Technical Stack Alignment

We utilized the exact stack suggested in the problem statement:

* **LLMs:** Orchestrated via **LangGraph** for stateful reasoning.
* **Embeddings/Vector DB:** Used for semantic search across unstructured audio transcripts.
* **NLP Pipelines:** Local **Faster-Whisper** for privacy-preserving transcription and sentiment analysis.
* **Lightweight UI:** Built with **Next.js** and **React Flow** for a responsive, web-based experience.

**EchoGraph transforms the "fragmented manual workflow" into a collaborative, visual, and agentic experience, exactly as envisioned in the MDG SPACE objective.**

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

1. Lack of early disease detection
Farmers often identify crop diseases too late, after visible damage has already spread.
Manual inspection requires experience and is prone to human error.

2. No instant expert guidance in rural areas
Access to agricultural experts or plant pathologists is limited, especially in remote regions.
Farmers depend on guesswork or delayed advice, leading to crop loss.

3. Difficulty in identifying the correct disease
Many crop diseases look visually similar but require different treatments.
Wrong diagnosis leads to incorrect pesticide use and reduced yield.

4. Overuse or misuse of chemicals
Without proper guidance, farmers may overuse pesticides.
This increases costs, harms soil health, and affects food safety.

5. Weather impact not considered in decisions
Farmers often ignore weather factors like humidity and temperature.
Weather strongly influences disease spread and treatment effectiveness.

6. Language and technical knowledge barrier
Most existing tools are complex and not farmer-friendly.
Farmers need simple, clear, actionable advice instead of technical

**Challenges we ran into**

Image Pre-processing: Implementing a "blur detection" script before the image is uploaded.

Offline Support: Using TensorFlow Lite for edge computing.

Human-in-the-Loop: A button to "Consult a Human Expert" if the AI confidence score is below 70%.

**Agentic AI / ML**

1. Beyond Passive ML
While traditional ML only identifies a disease (e.g., "Tomato Blight"), your project acts as an Agent by reasoning through the "Why" and "How to fix it."

2. Multi-Modal Reasoning
It combines different data streams—Neural Vision (image), Geo-context (City), and Environmental data (Soil)—to formulate a specialized plan. This is "Agentic" because it uses context to change its behavior.

3. Tool Use & Orchestration
The system acts as an orchestrator that calls upon specialized tools:

The Vision Tool: For diagnostic perception.

The Knowledge Tool (LLM): For strategic advice.

The Interface: For interactive feedback loops.

4. Goal-Directed Interaction
The Advisor AI demonstrates agency by helping the farmer reach a specific goal (Crop Recovery) through a dynamic dialogue, rather than providing a static, one-time output.

> SmartHire is an AI-powered screening system

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. The Problem it Solves
In the modern recruitment landscape, HR teams are overwhelmed by two major issues: Volume and Authenticity.

How it makes tasks easier:
Massive Time Savings: Manually reading a resume takes 2-3 minutes. This system parses and scores a resume in less than 2 seconds, allowing recruiters to focus only on the top 5% of candidates.

Information Extraction: It automatically identifies and extracts contact info, education, and years of experience, saving the recruiter from "hunting" through different PDF layouts.

Skill Gap Analysis: It doesn't just look for keywords; it compares the Resume against the Job Description (JD) and explicitly lists Missing Skills, helping recruiters understand exactly what a candidate lacks.

How it makes tasks safer:
AI Detection (The Integrity Check): With the rise of ChatGPT, many candidates generate "perfect" resumes that don't reflect their actual skills. My tool uses Machine Learning (Voting Classifier) to detect AI patterns, ensuring companies hire genuine talent.

Objectivity: By using a mathematical Weighted Scoring Algorithm, it removes human fatigue and unconscious bias from the initial screening phase.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an end-to-end AI system comes with unique technical hurdles. Here are the specific challenges I faced:

A. The "Date Parsing" Nightmare (Experience Calculation)
The Hurdle: Extracting "Years of Experience" is surprisingly difficult because everyone writes dates differently (e.g., "Jan 2020 - Present", "05/19 to 08/22", or just "2 years"). Simple keyword matching wasn't enough.

The Solution: I implemented a complex Regex-based logic combined with Python's dateutil library. I built a parser that recognizes multiple date formats, converts them into a standardized datetime object, and calculates the delta (difference) between them while handling "Present" as the current date.

B. Feature Engineering for AI Detection
The Hurdle: Initially, my AI detector was giving too many "False Positives" (marking humans as AI). High-quality human writing often looks "too perfect," which confuses basic models.

The Solution: Instead of just looking at words, I shifted to Linguistic Features. I integrated textstat to calculate Perplexity (predictability) and Burstiness (variation in sentence length). Humans tend to have "bursty" writing (mixing long and short sentences), while AI is more uniform. Adding these as features to my Voting Classifier significantly improved accuracy.

C. PDF Layout Complexity
The Hurdle: Some resumes are single-column, others are double-column. Standard text extractors often mix up the text from the left and right columns, making the data nonsensical.

The Solution: I switched to PyMuPDF (fitz), which allows for better block-level text extraction. I also added a fallback mechanism to PyPDF2 and python-docx to ensure that even if one library fails to parse a specific format, the system remains functional.

D. Memory and Efficiency
The Hurdle: Loading large NLP models (like NLTK corpora) every time a page refreshed was making the Flask app slow.

The Solution: I used an _ensure_nltk() function to check for resources only once at startup and optimized the database queries using SQLAlchemy ORM to ensure the app stays lightweight and fast.

**Ethereum Track**

A. The "Date Parsing" Complexity (Experience Calculation)
The Hurdle: Extracting "Total Years of Experience" is notoriously difficult because candidates use inconsistent formats: "Jan 2020 - Present", "05/19 to 08/22", or "2015-2018". Simple keyword matching failed to calculate durations accurately.

The Solution: I built a custom parser using Regular Expressions (Regex) and the dateutil.relativedelta library. I created a logic that identifies start and end dates, handles the "Present" keyword as the current date, and calculates the total delta in months/years while accounting for overlapping roles.

B. High False Positives in AI Detection
The Hurdle: Initially, my AI detector was flagging humans who write in a very formal or professional tone as "AI."

The Solution: I moved beyond simple word-checks and implemented Linguistic Feature Engineering. I integrated textstat to measure Perplexity (predictability) and Burstiness (variation in sentence length). Humans naturally have "bursty" writing (mixing long and short sentences), while AI is very uniform. Adding these features to my Voting Classifier significantly increased the detection accuracy.

C. PDF Layout and Parsing Errors
The Hurdle: Standard PDF libraries often read two-column resumes (common in modern designs) in the wrong order, mixing text from the left column into the right.

The Solution: I implemented PyMuPDF (fitz) because it allows for block-level text extraction. I added a "Fallback Mechanism" where if one parser fails or returns low-quality text, the system automatically tries a secondary library (like PyPDF2) to ensure the data is captured correctly.

D. System Performance (Model Loading)
The Hurdle: Loading heavy NLP models and NLTK data on every request made the web application laggy.

The Solution: I implemented an _ensure_nltk() startup function and used global instances for the ML models. This ensures that heavy resources are loaded into memory once when the server starts, making the actual resume analysis near-instant for the user.

**The problem it solves**

College canteens give students almost no information before they physically reach the counter. There's no way to know how long it'll take — so students end up standing in long queues just to find out, often only to discover the item they wanted is sold out or will take too long. This wastes the limited time students have between classes and frequently results in poor, rushed food choices.

What People Can Use It For
Browse the live menu remotely — see prices, ratings, availability, and estimated wait times before leaving for the canteen, instead of queueing blind and order before itself to not wait in the line.
Filter by what actually matters — budget, veg/non-veg preference, and category, so you only see options you'd actually order.
Get instant recommendations — type a request like "Under ₹100 • Vegetarian • Filling" and get a ranked shortlist of the top matches, powered by a transparent, explainable rule-based scoring system (not a black-box AI), so you can see why an item was recommended.
Check ratings and reviews — get a sense of food quality from other students before ordering, reducing the risk of a disappointing meal.
(For canteen staff) Use the admin panel to update menu items, mark things available/unavailable, and manage estimated wait times — keeping the information students see accurate in real time.

How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier/Safer
Saves time: Decisions happen before joining the queue, not while holding up the line — directly cutting down time lost between classes.
Keeps students on budget: Clear, filterable pricing prevents the common problem of overspending or discovering a good option was outside your budget only after waiting.
Reduces crowding: Better visibility into wait times naturally spreads demand across less-busy stalls/items instead of everyone converging on the same popular choice.
Gives canteen staff useful data: Ratings and popularity trends help staff understand what students actually want, supporting better stocking and prep decisions.
Removes guesswork and reduces food waste indirectly: Since students commit to informed choices upfront rather than switching last-minute at the counter, there's less mismatch between what's prepared and what's ordered.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main hurdles we faced was getting the frontend and backend to communicate reliably. Initially, the application worked locally, but some features failed when accessed through the network, and we also encountered repeated “failed to fetch” errors. This made it difficult to determine whether the problem was in the frontend, backend, or the connection between them.

We solved it by debugging the system step by step instead of changing everything at once. We first verified that the backend was running correctly, then checked the API endpoints and frontend requests, and finally tested the application through the network URL. We also made sure that the frontend was using the correct backend address instead of relying on a localhost URL. This helped us isolate the issue and get the different parts of the application working together reliably.

> Transparent government -corruption free

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

GroundTruth solves municipal corruption, slow repair times, and contractor fraud by creating a transparent bridge between everyday citizens and government officials. 

Here is how it makes things easier and safer:
* **For Citizens:** Instead of ignoring neighborhood potholes, broken streetlights, or hazards, anyone can snap a quick photo using their phone. Our AI automatically turns a simple complaint into a formal legal notice in seconds.
* **For Municipalities & Workers:** It cuts out messy paperwork by putting all reports into a live dashboard. It automatically tracks strict repair deadlines (SLAs) so critical safety hazards get fixed fast.
* **Stopping Fraud:** It blocks fake or recycled repair photos using strict live-camera locks, GPS location checks, and AI image comparisons. If a contractor tries to fake a fix or misses a deadline, the system flags it and automatically handles legal penalties.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building GroundTruth, we ran into a few major hurdles:

* **Blocking Fake Photos:** Corrupt contractors tried to cheat by recycling old repair photos or uploading images from their gallery. We solved this by forcing live camera-only inputs (`capture="environment"`) and adding a "Ghost Vendor" duplicate check using perceptual image hashing (`dHash`).
* **Location Verification:** Making sure repair crews were actually standing at the exact defect site was tricky. We overcame this by extracting and parsing hidden EXIF GPS metadata from photos to enforce a strict on-site geofence radius.
* **Keeping Portals in Sync:** Keeping the citizen reporting side and municipal command dashboard instantly synchronized without delays was tough. We resolved this by leveraging Firebase Firestore for real-time cloud data updates and automated SLA countdown trackers.

### Triage
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/triage-2671) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ilakkiyasuresh/Triage) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wtob08nC0CI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> "Stopping malware before it even gets an answer."

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zeek/PCAP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zeek/PCAP-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Our DGA detector's rarity scoring broke when we scaled its training corpus from 150 to 10,000 domains — the original "never seen before = rare" check worked by accident on a tiny corpus but silently stopped flagging anything once the bigger corpus had seen nearly every letter pair at least once. We caught it by re-testing known-bad domains and fixed it with percentile-rank scoring plus a keyboard-adjacency signal. Separately, since the resolver, DoH server, and dashboard run as separate processes, their in-memory state can drift apart — we found a real bug where the Tunneling Radar showed a different score than the resolver actually used, caused by two copies of the same sliding-window logic disagreeing on the window size. Merging an independently-built frontend with our backend also meant fixing a mismatched API contract (wrong table names, missing env vars) before real data would render. We also learned that a fully public "everything live" deployment needs a real cloud VM, not a serverless platform, since a raw UDP DNS resolver can't run on serverless infrastructure.

**The problem it solves**

Most DNS filtering only blocks domains after a human has already flagged them — too slow for botnets that generate thousands of disposable domains algorithmically (DGAs), or for DNS tunneling, which hides data exfiltration inside traffic that looks harmless one query at a time. This project blocks known-bad domains instantly using a real ~49,600-domain threat-intel blacklist, catches previously-unseen DGA domains through character-level scoring rather than waiting for a manual blacklist update, and detects tunneling by watching per-source-IP query patterns instead of trusting any single query. It covers DNS-over-UDP, DoH, and DoDTLS, plus offline PCAP/Zeek analysis, while staying fast enough (sub-100ms, cache-backed) to actually work as a real resolver.

**The problem it solves**

Autistic adults face high unemployment (50–85%), social isolation (79%), and difficulty transferring clinic‑learned skills into real‑world contexts.
Current therapy approaches (role‑play, weekly social groups) are too safe, too low‑pressure, and not realistic enough — they don’t replicate unpredictable strangers, ambient noise, or time pressure.

NeuroPractice VR bridges this “generalization gap” by offering therapist‑controlled, repeatable, graded exposure in realistic VR scenarios (job interviews, restaurant ordering, conflict conversations).

**Challenges we ran into**

Building within a hackathon window meant balancing ambition vs. feasibility:

*NPC Dialogue Complexity: Designing branching dialogue trees that felt unscripted but still hackathon‑ready was tricky.

Therapist Dashboard Sync: Making the difficulty slider actually change NPC behavior in real time required careful state management between Unity (VR client) and React (dashboard).

WebXR Fallback: Ensuring judges without a headset could still demo the scenario meant implementing a browser‑based fallback, which introduced compatibility quirks.*

**Specific Bug / Hurdle**
*One major hurdle was real‑time difficulty adjustment:

Initially, the slider changes on the therapist dashboard weren’t reflected in the VR client — NPCs stayed “stuck” at their initial difficulty.

Root cause: Firebase session state wasn’t updating fast enough, so Unity wasn’t receiving the new difficulty tier before the dialogue advanced.*

How We Overcame It
*We implemented a lightweight WebSocket channel for instant updates, bypassing Firebase’s delay.

Added a “sync confirmation” on the dashboard so therapists could see when the VR client acknowledged the change.

This fix not only solved the bug but also made the demo feel smoother and more professional.*
