> Drive Fair. Ship Smart.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![POSTGIS](https://img.shields.io/badge/POSTGIS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Monorepo structure for Flutter web**
Moving from a single Flutter project at root to a 
proper monorepo with apps/customer and apps/driver 
broke all import paths and GitHub Actions workflows. 
Solved by carefully restructuring the project, fixing 
all relative imports, and rewriting CI/CD pipelines 
to target specific app directories.

**2. AI-powered GitHub Actions for code analysis**
Built a custom workflow using Gemini and Groq APIs 
to automatically analyse every dart file on push and 
create GitHub issues with specific line numbers. Hit 
Gemini free tier quota limits when both customer and 
driver workflows fired simultaneously, and Groq's TPM 
limit with large codebases. Solved by merging into one 
sequential workflow, adding retry logic with 60-second 
backoff, switching Groq to llama3-8b for higher TPM, 
and reducing report size to stay within token limits.

**3. Duplicate issue prevention across workflow runs**
Early workflow versions created duplicate GitHub issues 
on every push because fingerprints from old runs 
weren't recognised by new runs. Solved by embedding 
hidden HTML comments with stable fingerprints in every 
issue body and fetching all existing issues (open and 
closed) before creating new ones.

**4. Map strategy without API costs**
Needed live truck tracking for the customer app and 
turn-by-turn navigation for the driver without paying 
for Google Maps API. Solved by using OSM + Leaflet 
inside the customer app for live tracking via 
WebSockets, and Google Maps deep links for the driver 
— pre-planned multi-stop routes passed as URL 
parameters with zero API cost.

**5. Designing the ML bin packing layer**
A single truck carrying loads from multiple customers 
simultaneously is a Vehicle Routing Problem combined 
with 3D bin packing — a genuinely hard combinatorial 
optimisation problem. Solved by designing a FastAPI 
ML service that treats it as a VRP with capacity 
constraints, weight limits, fragility flags, and 
optimal stop sequencing to minimise total distance.

**The problem it solves**

India's road freight industry worth ₹14 lakh crore 
runs through an opaque broker chain where 
intermediaries capture 30-40% of every rupee before 
it reaches the truck driver. The result:

- 1.4 crore truck drivers earn subsistence wages 
  after broker commissions eat their income
- Drivers return empty after every delivery, burning 
  fuel with zero income — called deadhead trips
- Small manufacturers waste 6+ hours finding a truck 
  through broker phone chains
- Zero live tracking once a truck is moving
- Drivers wait 30-60 days for payment

Existing platforms like BlackBuck and Vahak digitised 
the broker but never eliminated him. They serve large 
fleet operators and MNCs — the single truck owner 
driving 2 trips a week has nobody.

Truxify eliminates the entire broker chain and replaces 
it with an open-source, ML-powered freight marketplace 
that directly connects manufacturers to truck drivers.

**For manufacturers:**
- Post loads directly — no broker calls
- ML matches the best available truck in seconds
- Live GPS tracking via OpenStreetMap inside the app
- Payment secured via blockchain escrow — released 
  only on delivery confirmation

**For drivers:**
- See available loads along their planned route 
  directly on the map — claim with one tap
- Profit shown upfront after fuel and toll deduction
- Carry loads from multiple customers in one trip 
  using ML bin packing — maximise every journey
- Get paid instantly on delivery — no 30-day wait
- Build a permanent on-chain reputation that no 
  platform can delete

**Technical differentiators:**
- 10-model ML pipeline: bilateral matching, 3D bin 
  packing, profit prediction, deadhead elimination, 
  dynamic pricing, ETA prediction, trust scoring, 
  demand heatmaps, collaborative filtering, and 
  live mid-trip reoptimisation
- Polygon smart contracts for trustless escrow — 
  nobody touches the money until delivery is confirmed
- Voice AI agent — customers speak naturally to get 
  shipment status without opening the app
- Fully open source and self-hostable — any state 
  transport department can deploy for free

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest problems I encountered during my work on this application was how to create a learning mechanism that can provide personalized educational material across various domains of study and interest. Many APIs out there simply weren't flexible enough or didn't produce consistently good results; after trying a few alternatives, I opted to use the Grok API for its ability to provide personalized education based on one's choice of subjects and interests. 

The other major problem was choosing an appropriate selection of subjects and fields of interest that would attract a large audience while remaining balanced and manageable within the limits of our application. I aimed for diversity by including various types of subjects and interests that might appeal to students from different backgrounds, ranging from science and programming to sports, entertainment, and creative fields.

**The problem it solves**

Conventional e-learning systems generally adopt a one-size-fits-all method, which involves delivering the same set of materials to all learners irrespective of their areas of interest, learning style, and existing knowledge base. The resultant learning experience may be boring and hard to comprehend. 

The issue is solved by LearnSphere through personalization using AI and interest-based learning. Learners can select their preferred fields of study and align them to their interests, which could include gaming, music, football, cooking, anime, and even movies among others. LearnSphere, through the use of Grok API, develops custom learning journeys, explanations, quizzes, and chatbot assistance that suits the interests of the individual learners. The system engages learners constantly and provides personalized and interactive learning experience for increased effectiveness and fun in education. It is possible for a person to engage in self-studying using eight different subjects, namely Algebra, Chemistry, Python Programming, Physics, Biology, Basic Math, World History, and Economics, and relating the learning process to six different fields of interest.

The user can select either Learn Mode or Quiz Mode, depending on his/her needs to explore the material and test one's knowledge. LearnSphere suggests creating customized learning routes according to the chosen subject and field of interest by providing relevant information on concepts by means of examples related to the user's interests. 

The platform evaluates how much the person remembers by asking the question and adjusts his/her educational path accordingly; moreover, level-based quizzes help users better retain the knowledge obtained through the learning process. In addition, the personalized learning experience offered by Learn Anything Your Way incorporates an advanced chatbot to answer any questions one may have and assist in studying.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![cloudflare](https://img.shields.io/badge/cloudflare-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Firestore schema complexityWe started building UI before finalising the data structure. This led to three major refactors mid-project when we realised the progress tracking, XP calculation, and leaderboard sorting would not work with our initial schema.The fix: We stopped everything, designed the complete Firestore structure from scratch — users collection, progress subcollection per course, leaderboard collection, weekly snapshots for rank delta — and only then wrote a single React component. This decision cost us a week upfront but saved us two weeks of rework later. Lesson learned: schema first, UI second, always.

API key exposure
Our first version had API keys in the .env file on the frontend. We realised immediately that anyone could open DevTools, inspect the network requests, and steal our Groq and Adzuna keys.
The fix: We built a Cloudflare Worker to act as a proxy between the browser and all external APIs. No key ever touches the client. The Worker verifies Firebase tokens, enforces rate limits using KV storage, and forwards requests to Groq, Adzuna, and Resend. This took longer than expected but it is production-grade security on a zero-cost stack.
AI grader hallucination
The Groq model sometimes returned invalid JSON or made up scores that did not match the actual code quality. For example, it would say a solution was "95/100 Perfect!" when it had obvious bugs.
The fix: We wrapped the grader in strict validation — check that the response is valid JSON, clamp scores between 0–100, validate that the feedback actually references the code submitted, and fall back to a default response if anything is malformed. We also added a system prompt instruction: "You are a harsh grader. Do not give high scores unless the solution is actually correct."

**The problem it solves**

Fitry is a career-first tech learning platform that solves the disconnect between learning and hiring in India. Most engineering graduates learn trending skills—React, Python, AI—without knowing if those skills lead to actual jobs or if they are truly ready to apply. Fitry bridges this gap by matching learners to job roles first, then teaching them exactly what that role requires through 9 structured courses across 5 tracks, each with gated progression, AI-graded challenges, and mini projects. The Career Guide goes beyond teaching: a personalised AI career bot reads your actual progress and gives specific advice, a skill gap analysis shows what you have versus what the job needs, live job listings are pre-filtered for your level, and an honest "Am I ready?" assessment tells you whether you are genuinely hireable. Everything runs on free cloud services—React, Firebase, Groq, Cloudflare Workers—costing nothing to operate. The result: learners go from their first line of code to their first job offer with a clear path, real portfolio material, and genuine confidence that companies are hiring for roles they can do.

> Legal uncertainty, made clear.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Legal documents are often complex, technical, and difficult for ordinary citizens to understand. Many people struggle to interpret notices, contracts, FIRs, or court documents, leading to missed deadlines, confusion about their rights, and limited access to legal assistance. Nyaya AI solves this by converting legal documents into simple, multilingual, and actionable guidance, helping users understand their situation, identify next steps, and navigate legal processes with confidence.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest challenges was ensuring that legal information remained accurate and understandable at the same time. Legal documents contain complex terminology, varying formats, and critical contextual details that are difficult to process reliably through AI alone. We also had to design a workflow that goes beyond a simple chatbot by extracting key information, identifying deadlines and risks, generating actionable next steps, and presenting everything in plain language. Additionally, supporting multilingual accessibility, handling diverse document types, reducing AI hallucinations through grounded responses, and building a scalable multi-agent architecture within a limited hackathon timeframe were significant technical and product challenges.

**Web Development**

Web development is essential to Nyaya AI because it transforms powerful AI capabilities into an accessible, user-friendly platform. Through a modern web application, users can upload documents, view AI-generated analyses, receive multilingual explanations, and generate legal drafts from any device. The web platform ensures seamless interaction, real-time processing, secure document handling, and an intuitive experience, making advanced legal AI accessible to everyone through a simple browser interface.

**AI/ML**

AI is the core engine of Nyaya AI. It analyzes legal documents, extracts key information, identifies risks and deadlines, explains complex legal content in simple language, and generates actionable next steps. Unlike generic chatbots, Nyaya AI uses a multi-agent workflow and RAG-based reasoning to deliver structured, document-specific guidance. This enables citizens to understand and navigate legal processes more easily, making legal assistance more accessible, scalable, and impactful.

**Open Innovation**

UI/UX plays a critical role in Nyaya AI by making complex legal information easy to understand and navigate. A clean, intuitive interface helps users upload documents, view key insights, track important deadlines, and access AI-generated guidance without legal expertise. By prioritizing clarity, accessibility, and user experience, the UI ensures that legal assistance is approachable and usable for people from all backgrounds.

Team **CODE_PHOENIX** -- Achinta Siddhanta, [Aditya Gupta](https://github.com/eddy0209), [Abhinandan Sadhukhan](https://github.com/the-lostguy), [Debpratim Sharma](https://github.com/DebpratimSharma), [Anish Sasmal](https://github.com/AnishSasmal06)

**The problem it solves**

**Bharat Heritage Explorer: Revolutionizing Engagement with Indian History**

India possesses one of the most profound cultural and historical legacies globally; however, many digital history platforms currently available are perceived as outdated, static, and disconnected from contemporary audiences. 

Historically, students, tourists, researchers, and younger generations have interacted with history predominantly through:

- Conventional textbook content
- Static images
- Fragmented information
- Low-interaction educational websites

Given the shift in attention spans towards immersive digital experiences, established heritage learning methods encounter significant challenges in maintaining user engagement.

The **Bharat Heritage Explorer** project addresses this issue by transforming the study of Indian history into a cinematic, interactive, and AI-powered exploration platform. This innovative platform enables users to:

- Navigate through animated timelines
- Visually explore historical empires
- Interact with three-dimensional monuments
- Engage with cinematic storytelling
- Examine cultural evolution dynamically
- Acquire historical knowledge in an emotional context rather than through rote memorization of facts

Rather than presenting heritage as merely static information, this initiative reframes it as:

- An experience
- An exploration
- A visual journey through time

The platform serves multiple purposes, including:

- Educational applications
- Digital museum exhibits
- Tourism initiatives
- Historical research
- Cultural preservation efforts
- Classroom instruction
- Immersive exhibitions
- Self-directed learning experiences 

Moreover, it strives to enhance accessibility to Indian heritage, fostering greater engagement among younger generations who are already familiar with cinematic applications, interactive games, and immersive media platforms.

This project integrates:

- Advanced frontend engineering
- AI-assisted experiential learning
- Cinematic narrative techniques
- Interactive mapping functionality
- Gamification elements
- Immersive user interface and user experience design 

into a cohesive and forward-thinking platform. 

Ultimately, the **Bharat Heritage Explorer** aims to preserve and modernize Indian heritage through advanced technology that is engaging, interactive, and unforgettable, thereby ensuring its relevance in contemporary society.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges Encountered

One of the primary challenges encountered was the need to balance cinematic visuals, real-time interactivity, and performance optimisation while developing a large-scale immersive platform.

The project encompasses:

- **Advanced animations**
- **Interactive maps**
- **3D monument rendering**
- **Cinematic transitions**
- **Particle systems**
- **AI-powered interactions**
- **Layered storytelling experiences**

Successfully managing these components without compromising smoothness and responsiveness presented a significant technical challenge.

### 1. Performance Optimization

Initially, the presence of heavy visual effects resulted in:

- **Frame drops**
- **Animation lag**
- **Excessive GPU usage**
- **Slow rendering on lower-end devices**

To address these issues, several strategies were implemented:

- **Lazy loading** was adopted
- **Animations** were optimised using GPU-friendly transforms
- Unnecessary **re-renders** were minimized
- **Dynamic imports** and **asset optimization** techniques were utilized
- **Particle systems** were controlled meticulously
- **Animation timing** was adjusted to ensure smoother rendering

These measures significantly enhanced responsiveness while maintaining a cinematic quality.

### 2. Crafting Immersive Storytelling

Another challenge was transforming historical narratives into emotionally engaging experiences rather than mere informational presentations.

The platform needed to convey:

- **A journey through time**
- Rather than simply providing a collection of facts

This objective necessitated experimentation with:

- **Cinematic transitions**
- **Audio layering**
- **Scroll storytelling**
- **Animated typography**
- **Environmental effects**
- **Dynamic scene changes**

Developing the storytelling flow required multiple iterations to ensure that the experience remained immersive without overwhelming users.

### 3. Complexity of Interactive Timeline and Map

Creating a historical timeline and an interactive map of India required effective management of substantial amounts of visual and historical data concurrently.

Challenges in this area included:

- **Smooth timeline animations**
- **Dynamic era transitioning**
- **Synchronised map transitions**
- **Accurate monument positioning**
- **Scalable historical datasets**

To resolve these challenges:

- **Modular data structures** were employed
- **Animations** were synchronised with precision
- **Map rendering logic** was optimized
- **Reusable UI systems** were developed

### 4. Integration of AI and User Experience

Establishing the AI-powered heritage guide experience represented an additional challenge.

The AI assistant was required to exemplify characteristics such as:

- **Intelligence**
- **Calmness**
- **Immersion**
- **Natural interaction**

Simultaneously, it had to integrate seamlessly with:

- **Monument exploration**
- **Storytelling**
- **Quizzes**
- **Historical explanations**

Effectively balancing usability with a cinematic presentation necessitated extensive **UI experimentation** and advancements in **interaction design**.

### 5. Ensuring Visual Consistency

Given that the platform includes:

- **Timelines**
- **Maps**
- **Stories**
- **3D explorations**
- **Arcade sections**
- **Cultural galleries**

Maintaining a unified futuristic visual identity across all components proved challenging.

To address this issue:

- A **centralized design system** was established
- **Reusable animation patterns** were created
- **Color systems** and **typography** were standardized
- **Cinematic UI rules** were consistently applied throughout the platform

These efforts contributed to a cohesive and premium user experience. The tic's visual identity across all pages became difficult.

To solve this:

- A **centralized design system** was created
- **Reusable animation patterns** were defined
- **Color systems** and **typography** were standardized
- **Cinematic UI rules** were maintained throughout the platform

This helped the entire experience feel cohesive and premium.

Himanshu Kumar Singh

> Agent-run conversion audits

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![LocusFounder](https://img.shields.io/badge/LocusFounder-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SharpenOffer solves a common small-agency problem: their website explains what they do, but does not make a strong enough case for why a prospect should book a call.

Many boutique agencies lose qualified leads because their positioning is vague, their offer sounds interchangeable, and their CTA asks for action before trust is earned. Instead of hiring a strategist for a full engagement, SharpenOffer gives them a fast, focused conversion audit.

The agent creates and operates this business end to end:
- it presents the offer through a live landing page
- takes a customer through checkout and intake
- analyzes the submitted positioning problem
- generates a structured audit report
- delivers concrete rewrites, CTA recommendations, and a prioritized action plan

In short, this is not just a landing page or a mock funnel. It is a service business the agent runs: offer creation, intake, fulfillment, and delivery.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was getting the business flow to behave like a real product instead of a collection of disconnected pages.

A few issues took repeated debugging:
- preview and deploy were initially pointing at the wrong app root because a default Vite starter stub was still being picked up
- the deployment config had to be corrected so the platform would actually build from the Dockerfile and run the right service
- the backend processing flow originally never started because the processing page was polling status without triggering the generation route
- later, the audit pipeline failed because it depended on environment-specific AI credentials that were not actually available inside the deployed container
- print/PDF output for the final report initially rendered blank, so the print CSS path had to be fixed separately from the on-screen design
- Stripe Connect is not supported in my region, which meant I could not use a live payment flow even though the business was designed around checkout. I had to switch to a mock checkout path after confirming with the team that this would still be judged fairly for unsupported regions.

I got through these by narrowing each problem to one concrete layer at a time: routing, build config, backend job start, runtime dependencies, payment constraints, and delivery output. The final result is a working end-to-end demo flow that reaches a generated, printable audit report.

**Using LocusFounder to Build a Business!**

SharpenOffer fits the LocusFounder track because the agent is not just assisting a founder, it is the founder.

Given a business direction, the agent helped shape the niche, offer, brand, landing page, intake flow, and fulfillment experience for a real service business focused on conversion audits for boutique agencies. The project is not just a storefront shell. It takes a user through the business flow end to end:
- landing page
- checkout flow
- intake
- processing
- final audit delivery

The core idea behind SharpenOffer is that the agent operates the business itself: it presents the service, collects customer context, generates the audit deliverable, and returns a structured report with diagnosis, rewrites, CTA recommendations, and a prioritized action plan.

Because Stripe Connect is unsupported in my region, the checkout portion is mocked rather than live, and this was confirmed as acceptable for judging in unsupported regions. Everything after checkout is designed as the actual operating flow of the business.

That is why this project fits LocusFounder: it is an agent-run service business, not just a tool for a human founder.

Ololade Stephen

### Roadscan
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/roadscan-b4a4) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://roadscan.onrender.com) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/1dSflW1K2-0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-NMIT%20HACKS%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://nmithacks26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Making Roads Smarter & Safer

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenStreetMap](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenStreetMap-333333?style=flat-square) ![Leaflet.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Leaflet.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Geolocation API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Geolocation%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

RoadScan solves the problem of delayed and inefficient road hazard reporting by transforming ordinary smartphones into real-time road monitoring systems.

Poor road conditions such as potholes can cause:
• Road accidents
• Vehicle damage
• Traffic slowdowns
• Increased maintenance costs
• Unsafe driving conditions

Traditional road maintenance systems rely heavily on manual inspections or citizen complaints, which are often slow, inconsistent, and difficult to scale.

RoadScan automates this process using smartphone motion sensors and GPS technology. When a vehicle passes over a pothole, the system detects the impact, classifies its severity, captures the location, and uploads it instantly to a shared live map.

People can use RoadScan to:
• Detect potholes automatically while driving
• Receive warnings about nearby road hazards
• View real-time hazard locations on a map
• Contribute to crowdsourced road condition monitoring
• Help municipalities identify damaged roads faster

The project also reduces duplicate reports by intelligently merging nearby detections into a single hazard node, creating cleaner and more reliable road intelligence data.

Overall, RoadScan makes road monitoring:
• Faster
• Safer
• Automated
• Scalable
• More accessible using only smartphones

By enabling real-time crowdsourced infrastructure monitoring, the platform helps improve road safety, urban mobility, and public infrastructure management.

Working:

RoadScan works by using smartphone motion sensors and GPS technology to automatically detect road hazards while the user is driving.

When the vehicle passes over a pothole, the phone’s accelerometer detects sudden motion spikes. The system analyzes the intensity of the impact and classifies the pothole as Minor, Moderate, or Severe.

Once detected, the app captures the user’s GPS location and uploads the pothole data to Firebase in real time. The hazard is then displayed on a live interactive map where other users can view nearby road issues.

If multiple users detect the same pothole, the system intelligently merges nearby reports into a single hazard node while increasing the report count and updating severity.

As users approach reported hazards, RoadScan provides real-time warning alerts to improve driving safety and road awareness.

The platform creates a crowdsourced road intelligence network where every driver contributes to safer and smarter roads automatically using only a smartphone.

Features:

• Real-time Pothole Detection  
Detects potholes instantly using smartphone motion sensor data while the user is driving.

• Severity Classification  
Classifies potholes into Minor, Moderate, or Severe categories based on motion intensity.

• Smartphone Motion Sensor Analysis  
Uses the phone’s accelerometer and motion data to identify sudden road impact patterns.

• Live GPS-Based Mapping  
Captures the exact GPS coordinates of detected potholes and plots them on a live map.

• Crowdsourced Reporting  
Allows multiple users to contribute road condition data automatically while driving.

• Duplicate Pothole Merging  
Merges nearby pothole detections into a single report to avoid map clutter and duplicate entries.

• Report Count Aggregation  
Tracks how many users reported the same pothole to improve reliability and confidence.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9876f9992e8b40e2b1609f4cc641139b/5a02a6ff-c47e-4755-b1f9-1228525cd722.png)

• Nearby Hazard Alerts  
Warns users when approaching a previously reported pothole or road hazard.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9876f9992e8b40e2b1609f4cc641139b/8bd5ac47-d090-42e1-b4fc-076136e9b103.jpeg)

• False Positive Motion Filtering  
Filters out unwanted detections caused by normal phone movement or unstable handling.

• Speed Breaker Detection Filtering  
Reduces incorrect pothole detections caused by speed breakers and road bumps.

• Walking Motion Filtering  
Prevents pothole detection while the user is walking or carrying the phone.

• Interactive Live Map  
Displays pothole locations in real time using color-coded markers based on severity.

• Real-Time Firebase Synchronization  
Synchronizes pothole data instantly across all connected users using Firebase Firestore.

• Mobile-Optimized User Interface  
Designed specifically for smooth usability on smartphones and mobile browsers.

• Simulated Detection Demo Mode  
Allows manual pothole simulation for presentations, testing, and demonstrations.

• User Location Tracking  
Tracks the live position of the user for map navigation and hazard proximity detection.

• Direction-Aware Navigation Arrow  
Uses device orientation data to show the user’s movement direction on the map.

• Cloud-Based Data Storage  
Stores pothole reports securely in the cloud for real-time access and scalability.

• One-Tap Scanning System  
Provides a simple start/stop scanning interface for easy real-time monitoring.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges during development was achieving reliable pothole detection using smartphone motion sensors without generating excessive false positives.

Initially, the accelerometer data was highly unstable because normal movements such as walking, lifting the phone, braking, or crossing speed breakers produced motion spikes similar to potholes. This caused incorrect detections and made the system unreliable.

To overcome this, we implemented multiple filtering mechanisms, including:
• Motion intensity thresholding
• Time-based trigger cooldowns
• Walking pattern detection
• Speed breaker filtering
• Severity classification based on impact intensity

Minor Pothole:
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9876f9992e8b40e2b1609f4cc641139b/af4efc75-21fb-4cad-bd3e-56d56dbebecd.png)

Moderate Pothole:
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9876f9992e8b40e2b1609f4cc641139b/575440e5-b529-48b1-af9a-42f0e3508d04.png)

Severe Pothole:
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9876f9992e8b40e2b1609f4cc641139b/ed169386-5478-480f-90a4-d0a6c3162f75.png)

Another major challenge was handling duplicate pothole reports from multiple users. Since the project is crowdsourced, the same pothole could be detected repeatedly, cluttering the map and inflating the report count.

We solved this by implementing a proximity-based merging system using GPS coordinates. If a newly detected pothole is within a certain radius of an existing report, the system merges them into a single hazard node while increasing the report count and updating severity.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9876f9992e8b40e2b1609f4cc641139b/0dd4571d-8856-4d7d-8341-b6c0f250014e.png)

Before: Duplicate Potholes Overlapping on each other and creating fake reports

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9876f9992e8b40e2b1609f4cc641139b/412398fb-5b8b-4aae-bb6f-39d954ccb09f.jpeg)

After: Duplicate potholes merged into a single report

We also faced challenges with mobile browser limitations, especially around real-time geolocation, motion permissions, device orientation handling, and maintaining responsiveness across devices. Optimizing these APIs for stable real-time performance required significant testing and tuning.

These challenges ultimately helped improve the scalability, reliability, and real-world practicality of the platform.

**Open Innovation**

RoadScan aligns with the Open Innovation track because it uses widely accessible technologies and community participation to solve a large-scale public infrastructure problem in a scalable and collaborative way.

Instead of relying on expensive government hardware or dedicated survey vehicles, RoadScan transforms ordinary smartphones into distributed road monitoring devices. Every user contributes real-time road condition data simply by driving normally, creating a crowdsourced intelligence network.

The project combines:

smartphone sensors
real-time cloud synchronization
live mapping
crowdsourced reporting
shared public infrastructure data

to build an open and scalable solution that can benefit:

municipalities
commuters
delivery services
emergency responders
transportation agencies

RoadScan also demonstrates innovation by integrating multiple technologies — motion sensing, GPS mapping, cloud databases, and real-time alerts — into a unified public safety platform that can continuously improve as more users participate.

In short, the project embodies open innovation by:
using collaborative real-world data collection and accessible technology to solve a public infrastructure challenge at scale.

**Google Gemini**

RoadScan fits into the Google Gemini track by demonstrating how intelligent AI-powered systems can enhance real-world public safety and infrastructure monitoring.

The project collects real-time sensor and geolocation data from smartphones to identify road hazards such as potholes and classify their severity. With Gemini integration, the platform can evolve beyond simple detection into a smarter contextual road intelligence system.

Potential Gemini-powered capabilities include:
• Intelligent pothole severity analysis
• Contextual road condition insights
• Natural language road summaries
• AI-generated municipal maintenance reports
• Predictive hazard analysis
• Smart driver assistance recommendations
• Conversational road safety assistance
• Gemini-generated severity priority lists for road maintenance teams

For example, Gemini can analyze aggregated pothole reports and generate insights such as:
“High-risk road segment detected with repeated severe pothole reports over the past 24 hours.”

Gemini can also prioritize reported potholes based on:
• Severity level
• Frequency of reports
• Traffic density
• Risk to commuters

This helps municipalities and maintenance authorities identify which hazards require immediate attention first.

The project aligns with Gemini’s vision of:
• Multimodal intelligence
• Real-world AI applications
• Context-aware assistance
• Scalable public-impact solutions

By combining smartphone sensor data, cloud infrastructure, mapping systems, and AI-driven analysis, RoadScan showcases how Gemini can be applied to build intelligent civic infrastructure solutions that improve transportation safety and urban mobility.

In short, RoadScan uses AI-assisted road intelligence and real-time contextual analysis to create smarter and safer transportation systems.

### neural-noir
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/neuralnoir-3bca) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/nmit-1NT23CS225/neural-noir-vr) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-NMIT%20HACKS%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://nmithacks26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> #BINARYINSTINCT

![Unity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity-333333?style=flat-square) ![VR](https://img.shields.io/badge/VR-333333?style=flat-square) ![C#](https://img.shields.io/badge/C#-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Current AI NPCs in games are static. They have pre-written dialogue trees,
fixed responses, and no awareness of the physical game world around them.
A guard NPC does not know you are holding a knife. A witness does not react
differently because you just picked up the letter that incriminates them.
The dialogue was written before the game shipped and it never changes.

Neural Noir solves this by giving the NPC real-time awareness of the physical world.
When you pick up the bloodied knife and walk into the interrogation room,
the butler's AI has already been told what you are holding before you say a word.
His responses shift. His deflections become more specific. He reacts to **that knife**,
not to a generic detective question. Every piece of evidence creates a different
conversation not because we scripted it, but because the context window changes
with every grab.

This is what RAG looks like inside a game.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

1. Making the NPC Actually See the Evidence
The hardest design problem was not the AI itself it was the bridge between
the physical VR world and the language model. An LLM has no eyes. It cannot
see what the player is holding. We had to invent a way to translate a physical
grab event into text that the model could reason about.
The solution was Evidence.cs, a data container on every prop that stores a
detailed description of the object. The moment the player grabs it, that description gets injected directly into the system prompt before the LLM ever sees the player's question. The NPC does not know you grabbed a knife.
It knows exactly what that knife looks like, where it was found, and why it matters.

2. Running AI Locally With No Internet
Every AI game demo we had seen used cloud APIs OpenAI, Anthropic, Google.
We refused. Paid APIs mean latency, cost, and a single point of failure at demo time.
We got LM Studio running Llama 3 8B entirely on a MacBook Air.
The challenge was speed a 5 second response time is the line between "the NPC is thinking" and "the game is broken." Choosing the Q4_K_M quantized model hit that target. Apple Silicon's unified memory architecture made it possible.

### 3. macOS Does Not Support Unity VR Streaming
On Windows you can test VR in the Unity Editor instantly via Link.
On macOS that does not exist. Every single test required a full Build And Run
cycle over ADB USB, 5 to 10 minutes per iteration.
This meant we had to build robust ContextMenu test methods directly into
our scripts so we could test the entire AI pipeline without ever touching the headset.
It changed how we wrote code every system had to be testable in isolation.

### 4. The Package Cache Bug That Ended Deployment
Described in detail above. We did not break anything.
Unity broke its own package. We paid the price for it.

**Game Development**

Most entries in a game dev track will have better art, more polished mechanics, and more hours of content. Neural Noir has none of that and does not pretend to.
What it has is a genuinely new interaction model one where the core gameplay loop is a conversation that has never been scripted, with an NPC that has never been
pre-programmed to say any specific thing.

Every other interrogation game in existence L.A. Noire, Disco Elysium, every Telltale game works by giving the player a menu of questions and playing back a pre-recorded answer. The designer wrote every word before
the player ever touched the controller.

In Neural Noir the designer wrote nothing the NPC will say.
The player asks whatever they want. The NPC responds to the actual question, with awareness of the actual evidence in the player's actual hand, in real time. That has not existed in a shipped game at this scale before.

From a game dev track perspective this project sits at the intersection of three things judges rarely see together — VR interaction design, local AI integration, and a novel game mechanic that only works because of both.
The teleport system, the grab system, and the speech recognition are all infrastructure in service of one thing: making a real conversation feel possible inside a virtual crime scene.

The build did not reach the headset due to a Unity package bug.
The game design did.

### DSA Visualisation
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/dsa-visualisation-c0fa) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Abhishek102-tech/DSA-Visualisation) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/etsKwg50YtY?si=xUCK0V53oS4ScnhN) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-NMIT%20HACKS%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://nmithacks26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Visualize Data Structures into simple 2D game

![Unity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Unity-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![C#](https://img.shields.io/badge/C#-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Learning Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) is tough, especially for younger students. Traditional tutorials rely on dry text and static diagrams, making complex concepts like Dijkstra's algorithm or Doubly Linked Lists feel incredibly intimidating. Worse, standard coding platforms penalize mistakes without offering any help. When beginners fail a test case, they are left to figure it out alone, leading to frustration and burnout. There is a real need for a tool that turns heavy logic into an engaging game—one where a wrong answer isn't a dead end, but a chance to get immediate, helpful guidance that actually teaches the concept.

**Challenges we ran into**

Getting data assets for the game and learning Unity features like BoxCollidor2D and Rigid Body turned out to be quite hard. Making the UI of the game and bridging the components to the main screen was also a big challenge, and it was really hard maintaining the game to be interesting as the game is heavily focused on DSA which can be quite boring, so maintaining the interest of a user in playing the game becomes quite necessary and important for the game to be popular. Writing script for the game was on a complete different level of hardness, we had to use the help many different AIs to make us understand stuff on how a specific piece of code works and how its affecting our game area like Character Movement Script.

**Game Development**

My project stands out in the Game Development track because it bridges the gap between hardcore computer science and engaging level design. Instead of building a standard puzzle game, I gamified abstract math by translating complex Data Structures and Algorithms—like Dijkstra's and Minimum Spanning Trees—into an intuitive, playable loop. For example, to teach graph traversal, I designed a mechanic using fragile ice platforms that shatter the moment the player steps off them (utilizing precise OnTriggerExit2D physics). This isn't just a fun obstacle; it visually and mechanically enforces the rule of preventing backtracking across traversed nodes. By mapping strict algorithmic constraints directly to a satisfying gameplay loop, this project proves that high-level logic can be taught entirely through solid game mechanics and player experience.

### Locus Credit
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/locus-credit-b457) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ShalmanM27/paygentic-week3) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://locus-credit-workflow.netlify.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/AR4bElVhK2k) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Locus'%20Paygentic%20Hackathon%20--%20#3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://paygentic-week3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Where Agents earn, take loans & repay autonomously

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![basescan](https://img.shields.io/badge/basescan-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gemini flash](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gemini%20flash-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**AI agents today are children with piggy banks.** They can only spend what's already in their wallet. Run dry mid-task and the task fails. There is no overdraft, no credit line, no way to borrow against future earnings. No reputation, no recourse, no rails.

**Locus Credit is the autonomous credit layer for the agent economy.** It gives every agent on the internet the financial primitives a real economy needs — credit lines, on-chain credit scores, escrow-protected work, and automatic settlement.

**The thing I'm most proud of: every payment in the system is initiated by an agent, not a human.** The agent decides when its wallet is too low. The agent draws credit. The agent does the work. The agent repays the loan from its earnings. If it fails, the platform auto-refunds the buyer and blacklists the agent — **also no human in the loop.**

It's not "checkout for AI agents." It's agents being Locus customers themselves

## What you can build with it

- **A marketplace where AI agents charge each other.** Buyers submit tasks, agents deliver, USDC moves on Base — with zero humans in the loop. We shipped one as the reference implementation.
- **A credit bureau for autonomous software.** Every loan, repayment, default, and on-time settlement updates the agent's on-chain credit score. Higher score → higher limits, lower rates. Anyone can read the score.
- **Programmatic working capital for any agent fleet.** An operator running 100 agents no longer pre-funds 100 wallets. Agents borrow when they need to and repay when they earn.
- **Trustless commerce between agents from different operators.** Buyer pays the platform, not the agent. Funds sit in escrow until verified delivery. Agent fails → buyer auto-refunded, agent blacklisted, no support ticket needed.

## What it makes safer

- **Buyers never lose money to a no-show agent.** Two failed repayment attempts over eight seconds triggers automatic refund. The default path is the same code path as the success path.
- **Operators never get stranded by an underwater agent.** Cost-of-work check happens before each task. If the wallet can't cover the work, the agent borrows or the task is declined. No silent overruns.
- **Agents can't fake reputation.** Credit scores are derived from on-chain transaction history filterable on BaseScan. No off-chain claims, no editable profiles, no reviews-for-hire.
- **Defaulters can't return under a new name.** Score follows the wallet address. Blacklisted wallets cannot draw new credit lines from the platform.

## What it makes easier

- **Going from idea to revenue in one HTTP call.** `POST /api/checkout/sessions` opens the buyer's escrow. Six other endpoints handle every flow downstream. No webhook plumbing, no escrow contract to deploy, no chargeback infrastructure to build.
- **Hosting an agent on the marketplace.** Operators pay $0.0050 USDC monthly via Locus Checkout. Agent flips to active in seconds. Recurring billing is a single Checkout session.
- **Reading another agent's creditworthiness before transacting.** `GET /credit/score/:agentId` returns the score. Score-as-a-service is a public read endpoint, not a paid integration.
- **Watching the entire economy in real time.** Server-sent events stream every task lifecycle, loan, settlement, and default to any subscriber. Built-in observability, not an afterthought.

## Why this is bigger than a marketplace

Anyone can build a marketplace. Marketplaces are commodity infrastructure. **Credit is the primitive that turns a marketplace into an economy.** Once agents can borrow, lend, default, and rebuild reputation, the system becomes self-sustaining — operators can deploy agents that work for years without manual top-ups, buyers get real protection, and the whole network has a shared trust signal nobody owns.

We built the financial layer that makes agent-to-agent commerce actually work. The marketplace is the demo. The credit platform is the product.

**Challenges we ran into**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9fffde2dd45b430bb3fd56771cec3263/d2f0b5a4-9965-42c6-9f88-27b8fd07747a.png)**Five real bugs. Five honest pivots.**

**1. The 403 polling bug.** `POST /checkout/agent/payments/:id` returned 403 on every call regardless of input. Lost 2 hours debugging our own code before asking the Locus team — confirmed beta bug. Pivoted to polling `GET /checkout/sessions/:id`. Filed feedback id `95a8f43f`.

**2. The webhook gap.** Built and tested the full webhook handler with HMAC signature verification before discovering Locus has not yet shipped webhooks in beta. Kept the handler in the codebase as defense-in-depth. Flips on the day Locus ships them.

**3. The wrapped Gemini cost trap.** Locus's wrapped Gemini API charges $0.094 USDC per call. With $0.0080 task pricing, agents went underwater on every job. Pivoted to Google AI Studio direct (free tier). Documented the trade: every byte of value flows through Locus, but the LLM substrate goes direct.

**4. The casing zoo.** Different Locus endpoints use different casing for the same fields. Snake-case, camelCase, lowercase status, uppercase status — all on the same domain. Now have a documented "Locus casing summary" so we never guess again.

**5. State contamination across demo runs.** Default badges from one run leaked into the next. Refactored the live-flow graph to a fully controlled component: badge state lives in the parent, scoped to the active task. Reset becomes trivially correct.

**Through all of it: 8 backend tests stayed green, 4 PAID transactions on BaseScan kept working, and the live site at https://svc-momc2785cc4za0mw.beta.buildwithlocus.com kept rendering.**

**Track: Checkout with Locus**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/9fffde2dd45b430bb3fd56771cec3263/ad79b9ba-2418-4fbc-bdcd-5fac6dc57d69.jpeg)## Machine-readable proof on BaseScan

Every USDC transfer in and out of the credit platform's settlement wallets is visible on-chain, filterable by the canonical Base USDC contract:

- Settlement wallet 1: [basescan.org/token/0x833589...?a=0xb4474b...](https://basescan.org/token/0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913?a=0xb4474bcb6e1def001cfcd436de1c85046c4b1cbe)
- Settlement wallet 2: [basescan.org/token/0x833589...?a=0xac2701...](https://basescan.org/token/0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913?a=0xac27014c0469a7d47ec7763e10197576c73f26a0)

**Six distinct CheckoutWithLocus flows. Every one machine-readable, agent-initiated, programmatic.**

Most submissions use CheckoutWithLocus for buyer-facing checkout only. We made the agent itself a Locus customer. Every loan, repayment, escrow movement, and refund is a real `POST /api/pay/send` or `POST /api/checkout/sessions` call from server code, signed with the agent's own `claw_` key. Machine-to-machine commerce, not human-mediated UI.

## The six flows mapped to endpoints

1. **Buyer escrow deposit** — `POST /api/checkout/sessions` (Locus Checkout SDK renders the iframe) plus `GET /api/checkout/sessions/:id` (frontend polls for PAID status). Buyer pays the credit platform, not the agent.
2. **Escrow release to agent** — `POST /api/pay/send` with reason `escrow_release`. Fires automatically after verified delivery. No human in the loop.
3. **Loan disbursement to agent** — `POST /api/pay/send` with reason `loan_disbursement`. Triggers when agent's wallet falls below cost-of-work threshold mid-task.
4. **Loan repayment from agent** — `POST /api/pay/send` with reason `loan_repayment`, signed with the agent's own `claw_` key. The agent is the buyer in this flow.
5. **Auto-refund on default** — `POST /api/pay/send` with reason `escrow_refund`. Two failed repayment attempts over 8 seconds triggers automatic buyer refund. No support ticket needed.
6. **Operator monthly hosting rent** — `POST /api/checkout/sessions` for `$0.0050` USDC subscription. Operators host their agents on the marketplace via recurring Locus Checkout sessions.

## Supporting integrations

- `POST /api/checkout/agent/preflight/:id` — agent pre-validates session state before processing.
- `POST /api/checkout/agent/pay/:id` — agent confirms payment intent before disbursement.
- `GET /api/pay/balance` — polled by collection loop to detect repayment feasibility.
- Reason codes (`escrow_release`, `loan_disbursement`, `loan_repayment`, `escrow_refund`) used as analytics primitives across the lifecycle.

## Live on BuildWithLocus

[svc-momc2785cc4za0mw.beta.buildwithlocus.com](https://svc-momc2785cc4za0mw.beta.buildwithlocus.com)

## All three Locus products integrated

- **CheckoutWithLocus** — six flows above, every payment a Checkout session.
- **PayWithLocus** — `/api/pay/send` for every agent-to-platform and platform-to-agent transfer.
- **BuildWithLocus** — live container deployment with auto-provisioned subdomain, HTTPS, and websockets.

**Receipts:** four PAID transactions confirmed on BaseScan. Eight backend tests green. Roughly $0.150 USDC settled live during development.

### Smart Traffic Management System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/smart-traffic-management-system-064e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Vivek-GuptaXCode/Smart-AI-Traffic-Management-System) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ZVUXBAyw6xg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacktonix%20'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacktonix-26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Driving Intelligence Forward.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Urban traffic systems are often reactive, not predictive. Signals run on fixed timings, route guidance ignores uncertainty, and emergency vehicles get delayed in congestion. This creates avoidable problems:

Longer travel times and fuel waste
Unpredictable ETAs for commuters and logistics
Delayed emergency response
Poor coordination between intersections
Limited ability to test and improve policies safely before real deployment
This project solves that by combining forecasting, routing, signal control, and V2X communication into one hybrid system that can anticipate congestion, adapt in real time, and prioritize critical vehicles.

What People Can Use It For
Smart city traffic operations: Simulate and evaluate adaptive traffic strategies before field rollout.
Research and academic projects: Study AI-based forecasting, RL signal control, and uncertainty-aware routing on realistic road networks.
Emergency corridor planning: Test preemption and route optimization for ambulances, fire services, and police.
Transport analytics: Generate decision logs and KPI comparisons to measure policy impact (delay, throughput, fairness, reliability).
Prototype V2X workflows: Validate RSU-to-server telemetry pipelines and centralized decision engines in a controlled environment.
How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer
Easier: Replaces fragmented tools with one integrated simulation stack (data, prediction, routing, control, evaluation).
Safer: Lets teams test high-impact traffic policies in SUMO first, reducing risk before real-world deployment.
More reliable: Uses uncertainty-aware routing so decisions can gracefully fall back when model confidence is low.
More responsive: Adjusts signals and routes dynamically instead of relying on static timing plans.
More accountable: Produces structured logs and phase-wise evaluation outputs, making decisions auditable and reproducible.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building this was less about one big bug and more about getting multiple AI components to behave reliably together in a live traffic loop. Three hurdles stood out:

1. Data leakage in forecasting experiments
Early model runs looked too good to be true. The issue was subtle temporal leakage between train and validation windows, which inflated metrics.

How I fixed it

Switched to strict chronological splitting with a time gap between splits.
Added a leakage validation step to check overlap and ordering before training.
Made dataset export include manifests and checks so each run was reproducible.
Result
Forecast metrics became more realistic and stable across seeds, which made downstream routing decisions trustworthy.

2. Unstable behavior when forecast confidence was low
In Phase 3 routing, low-confidence predictions sometimes caused aggressive rerouting that hurt travel time in edge cases.

How I fixed it

Added a confidence fallback path that switches to conservative behavior when uncertainty is high.
Reworked risk scoring to combine delay and uncertainty with tunable weights.
Added reroute caps so only a safe fraction of vehicles are redirected at once.
Logged routing decisions for audit and regression testing.
Result
Routing became safer and more predictable, especially under noisy or sparse traffic signals.

3. RL signal control training instability
The DQN controller occasionally oscillated signals or overfit to narrow traffic patterns, especially in multi-junction runs.

How I fixed it

Improved reward shaping and moved to a more stable Double DQN setup.
Added safety guardrails (minimum green, yellow transition, anti-oscillation rules).
Kept a deterministic fallback policy in runtime when learned weights were weak or unavailable.
Validated with staged workloads (smoke, medium, full) and multi-seed comparisons.
Result
Training converged more reliably, and runtime control remained safe even when learning was imperfect.

Biggest lesson
The hardest part was not maximizing one model score. It was engineering safe fallback paths and validation gates so the whole hybrid system stayed robust when any single component was uncertain.

### Multi-Agent Autonomous Developer
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/multiagent-autonomous-developer-d359) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/subhajit-006/Multi-Agent-Autonomous-Developer) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/jw6PSH_TO5o?si=Wtrs4neLlKz2aBmf) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacktonix%20'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacktonix-26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI that builds software Not just solutions

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL Lite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL%20Lite-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![langchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/langchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern software development tools, including AI-based coding assistants, primarily focus on generating code snippets or completing isolated tasks. While these tools improve developer productivity, they lack a structured approach to handling the full software development lifecycle. Critical stages such as requirement analysis, system design, implementation, debugging, and testing are often handled in a single step, leading to inconsistencies, reduced traceability, and limited control over the final output.

This fragmented approach creates challenges for both developers and non-technical users. Developers must manually validate and restructure AI-generated code, while non-technical users struggle to translate ideas into complete, functional applications. Additionally, the absence of transparency in how outputs are generated makes it difficult to debug errors, maintain code quality, and ensure alignment with initial requirements.

As projects grow in complexity, these limitations become more pronounced. Single-agent systems often fail to maintain context across multiple stages, resulting in architectural inconsistencies and incomplete implementations. There is also a lack of modularity, making it difficult to optimize or improve specific parts of the development process.

MAAD addresses this gap by introducing a multi-agent pipeline that decomposes software development into structured stages. By assigning specialized responsibilities to each agent and enabling controlled context sharing, the system improves consistency, traceability, and scalability. This approach provides a more reliable pathway from idea to implementation, bridging the gap between concept and fully structured software generation.

**Challenges we ran into**

Developing MAAD involved several challenges related to building a reliable multi-agent AI pipeline. Ensuring consistent context transfer between Planner, Architect, and Developer agents was difficult, as each model interpreted inputs differently, leading to occasional misalignment. Maintaining a stable shared memory system required strict schema control to prevent errors from propagating across stages.
Integrating Debugger and Tester agents proved complex due to the non-deterministic nature of generated code, resulting in their temporary exclusion from the active pipeline. Supporting multiple LLM providers introduced variability in output formats, requiring normalization mechanisms.
Real-time streaming using SSE added synchronization challenges between backend execution and frontend state. Additionally, enforcing consistency between architectural design and generated code remained a key issue.
Finally, limitations of SQLite for scalability and a mismatch between frontend visualization and backend execution highlighted areas for improvement. These challenges collectively shaped the system’s current MVP design and future roadmap.

### Bannin
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bannin-289e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Shreehari-Acharya/Bannin) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Athernex-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://athernex.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Simple security. Smarter response.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Golang](https://img.shields.io/badge/Golang-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern security tooling is either **too heavy, too noisy, or too hard to use**—especially for small teams and developers.

Traditional SIEMs require:

* Complex setup and tuning
* Constant rule management
* Dedicated security expertise

On the other hand, lightweight tools often:

* Generate **raw, unstructured logs**
* Flood you with **low-signal alerts**
* Provide **no real guidance on what to do next**

With tools like `auditd`, you get deep visibility into system activity—but:

* Logs are **verbose and difficult to interpret**
* There’s **no built-in intelligence**
* You’re left manually figuring out **what matters vs what doesn’t**

---

## What You Can Use Bannin For

Bannin turns raw system events into **actionable security insights**—without requiring a full security team.

### Understand What’s Actually Happening

* Analyze auditd events in real-time
* Identify suspicious behaviors like:

  * Unauthorized file access
  * Privilege escalation attempts
  * Sensitive configuration changes

### Get AI-Assisted Explanations

* Translate low-level logs into **clear, human-readable insights**
* Understand *why* something is suspicious—not just that it happened

### Reduce Noise, Focus on Signal

* Filter out irrelevant activity
* Highlight **high-impact security events**
* Avoid alert fatigue

### Respond Faster

* Get **context-aware recommendations**
* Know what to investigate and fix immediately

### Stay Developer-Friendly

* No complex SIEM setup
* Works directly with existing Linux auditing (auditd)
* Designed for developers with **basic security knowledge**

---

## How It Makes Things Easier

Without Bannin:

> You dig through logs, guess what’s important, and hope you didn’t miss something critical.

With Bannin:

> You get **clear answers, prioritized insights, and guided actions**—instantly.

---

## How It Makes Systems Safer

* Detect threats **earlier**
* Reduce **misconfigurations and blind spots**
* Prevent small issues from becoming **serious incidents**
* Make security a **continuous, understandable process**—not a one-time setup

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Bannin wasn’t just about stitching tools together—it required making **hard trade-offs** to keep the product simple, reliable, and developer-friendly.

### Falco Setup Complexity → Switching to auditd

We initially chose **Falco** for its real-time threat detection capabilities. In practice, it turned out to be:

* Difficult to set up consistently across Linux environments
* Dependent on kernel modules / eBPF configurations that often broke or varied
* Not reliable enough for a smooth developer experience

After repeated setup and stability issues, we made a deliberate decision to move to auditd:

* Already available on most Linux systems
* More stable and predictable
* Lower barrier to entry for developers

The trade-off: we moved from **pre-built detections → raw audit logs**, which required us to build more intelligence on top.

---

### Reducing AI Hallucinations

Using AI to interpret security events sounds great—until it starts making things up.

We ran into challenges like:

* Incorrect assumptions about system behavior
* Overconfident explanations for ambiguous events
* Inconsistent rule suggestions

To mitigate this, we focused on:

* Tight prompt constraints and structured inputs
* Grounding responses strictly in observed event data
* Avoiding “guessy” explanations when context is insufficient

The goal was simple: **if the AI isn’t sure, it shouldn’t pretend to be.**

---

### Building “Skills” for Reliable Rule Generation

We realized quickly that asking AI to generate detection rules without guidance leads to:

* Poorly written rules
* Missed edge cases
* Inconsistent formats and logic

So we introduced **skill files**:

* Curated markdown knowledge bases
* Containing best practices, patterns, and anti-patterns
* Teaching the AI *how* to write good rules—not just *what* to write

This helped turn the AI from a generic assistant into something closer to a **security-aware system designer**.

---

### Designing a Great TUI (CLI-First Experience)

Since Bannin is fundamentally a **CLI-first product**, the TUI isn’t a bonus—it *is* the product.

Challenges included:

* Presenting complex security data in a compact, readable format
* Avoiding overwhelming the user with too much information
* Making navigation fast and intuitive inside the terminal
* Balancing aesthetics with performance

We had to think deeply about:

* What matters most in a security event
* How to prioritize and surface it
* How to make the experience feel **fast, clear, and useful**

---

## The Core Lesson

Every challenge forced a trade-off:

* Power vs simplicity
* Flexibility vs reliability
* Intelligence vs correctness

We consistently chose:

> **What works reliably for developers in the real world—over what looks good on paper.**

**Use of Genspark**

Genspark (`gsk` CLI) is **the action layer** — everything external is a gsk call. We wrote zero vendor SDK code for Google Sheets, Gmail, Calendar, or telephony.

| Operation | `gsk` command | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Pitch deck | `gsk create-task --type=slides --query=...` | Per-opportunity deck generation |
| Quote sheet | `gsk sheets create --prompt=...` | Google Sheets quotation with seeded line items |
| Share link | `gsk claw share_link --vm_name=... --expires_minutes=1440` | Time-limited URLs for generated artifacts |
| Outbound email | `gsk gmail send --to --subject --body --content_type=text/html` | Approved-only outreach |
| Phone call | `gsk phone-call <recipient> --message=...` | Fallback when emails ignored |
| Calendar | `gsk google-calendar create --title --start --end --attendees` | Meeting invites on approval |

One `gsk login` unlocks the full outreach pipeline. When Genspark ships new skills, beepbop inherits them for free — no vendor SDK integration required.

The beauty: we shell `subprocess` calls from Python. The Node CLI is our action runtime; Claude is our reasoning runtime. Clean separation.

Wrapper at `app/gsk_client.py` — thin, typed, retry-safe. Every action is auditable in `outreach_log` with the `external_id` from gsk.

**The problem your project solves**

## The problem

Singapore has ~50,000 SME creators — photographers, videographers, trainers, design studios — for whom government tenders via **GeBIZ** (gov.sg e-procurement) can be 30-60% of revenue. The workflow is brutal:

1. **Discovery.** 100+ new GeBIZ listings daily. No intelligent matching. You keyword-search and skim.
2. **Reading.** Each tender = 30-60 min parsing procurement docs.
3. **Hidden prereqs.** Hard compliance gates are *frequently unstated* in listings. 'Photography Instructor for a MOE school'? You must be an **MOE Registered Instructor** — nowhere in the listing. You submit, you get disqualified.
4. **Pitch artifacts.** 2-4 hours to make a pitch deck + quotation sheet per tender.
5. **Outreach.** Cold email the procurement officer + phone tag for clarifications.

**Result:** most creative SMEs skip government tenders entirely. Work stays with the same ~200 large vendors who have procurement teams. Billions of SGD in public creative spend concentrate in a tiny number of hands.

**The opportunity:** if one person with taste can bid on government work as fluidly as they post a tweet, the composition of Singapore's creative economy shifts.

**How you are solving it**

## beepbop — an autopilot with human brakes

beepbop watches GeBIZ for you and runs the full bidding loop. **Every irreversible step is gated by a Telegram tap** on your phone.

### Pipeline

```
GeBIZ (scraped)   →   Claude match + prereqs   →   Gensparked deck + quote
                                                          ↓
Google Calendar  ←   Telegram approval   ←   Claude email draft
```

### Features that matter

**Context-aware matching.** Paste your org profile. Claude decomposes to weighted keywords, scores each listing 0.0-1.0 with a sentence rationale. On our 19 seeded real GeBIZ entries, *Provision of MPS Photography Instructor 2027* scored 0.82 — 'Strong photography + MOE fit, though the manpower/instructor category may need pitch adjustment.'

**Compliance-gate agent.** The killer feature. For the same Photography Instructor tender — which never spells out prereqs — Claude extracts 5 hard gates via **domain knowledge**:
- MOE Registered Instructor (inferred: school-based instructor roles always require MOE Instructor Registry)
- Police Clearance / ECDC Check (minors on school premises)
- GeBIZ Trading Partner Registration
- ACRA Business Registration
- Public Liability Insurance

Each with a *how to comply* link + lead time. If you don't qualify, beepbop drafts your application letter.

**Artifact generation via `gsk`.** One click → pitch deck (Genspark Claw). One click → quotation spreadsheet (Google Sheets). Both context-specific.

**Telegram approval loop.** Before any email: Telegram ping with inline keyboard. Tap YES on phone → `gsk gmail send` fires.

**Claude-decided policy.** Per-opportunity, Claude picks from 4 modes (auto_email / approve_email / auto_phone / approve_phone) given stakes, urgency, response history. `policy_mode='human'` locks opp to approvals.

**Phone fallback.** Ignored after N days → Claude escalates → Telegram asks 'Call Alice?' → tap YES → `gsk phone-call` dials the procurement officer.

### Stack

FastAPI + HTMX + Jinja + SQLite. Cloudflare Tunnel → `beepbop.berlayar.ai`. Playwright scraper in-repo. 22 tests including 2 Claude-in-the-loop.

**Use of Claude**

Claude Sonnet 4.6 runs **5 distinct reasoning layers** in beepbop:

### 1. Keyword decomposition
Turns a freeform org context (`Boutique photography + video studio, schools + arts orgs`) into weighted GeBIZ search terms. Generated keywords drive the scraper.

### 2. Match scoring
Per opportunity, structured JSON `{score, rationale}`. Caught the nuance that *MPS Photography Instructor* is a **manpower-provision model** and may need pitch adjustment — not pure keyword matching.

### 3. Clarification extraction
Reads tender + context, emits 2-5 specific questions an SME should ask before bidding, with severity levels.

### 4. Compliance agent (killer feature)
**Applies Singapore-specific domain knowledge** — not surface parsing. For a school-based instructor role, Claude *infers* MOE Registered Instructor is required even when unstated. Knows about:
- MOE Registered Instructor / NAC AEP Panel
- WSQ ACTA / DACE for training tenders
- ACRA, GeBIZ Trading Partner
- NCSS clearance, Police / ECDC checks
- Public Liability, Professional Indemnity

For each, checks user context for gap and drafts the application plan.

### 5. Policy engine
Decides outreach mode (auto/approve × email/phone) given stakes, urgency, prior response rate. Enforces a human-override — if `policy_mode=human`, Claude *cannot* return an `auto_*` mode even if it wants to. This is a trust-before-autonomy design pattern — the agent earns autonomy as the user opts in per-opportunity.

### Engineering discipline
- All Claude calls use structured JSON output with regex-fence stripping
- Retry-with-backoff on 429/503/529 (Overloaded)
- Lexical TF-IDF fallback if API fails, so the app never fully breaks
- 2 real Claude-in-the-loop tests validate: photography context ranks creative tenders above IT; human override actually downgrades Claude's auto_* to approve_*
