[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vyuha-71c6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sanchitwadehra/Vyuha) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://vyuha-ten.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Koc4LF1KrAc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Agentic Sandbox — Game Theory x LLM Agents

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Multi-agent simulations today require writing code for every scenario — new rules, new behaviors, new interactions all mean new code.
  Vyuha lets you build and control entire multi-agent worlds using just natural language.

  Type "create two rival armies and make them fight" and watch 16 autonomous LLM agents spawn, strategize, and battle on a live 2D grid.
  Mid-simulation, type "drop a mercenary in the center" or "a storm hits the battlefield" and the world changes instantly.

  Each agent thinks independently — reading the world state, reasoning about its goals, and choosing actions (move, attack, cooperate,
  trade, defend). A structured rules engine enforces consequences: agents die at 0 health, get penalized for breaking rules, and compete
  using game-theory payoffs.

  No code changes needed between scenarios. The same engine runs a war simulation, a resource economy, or a social experiment — all
  controlled through English.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge was drawing the line between engine code and God Mode responsibility. Early on, I kept hardcoding scenario-specific
   logic (auto-death at 0hp, terrain rules) into the engine. But that breaks when the scenario changes. The solution: a two-layer rule
  system — text rules that agents read and choose to follow, and structured rules that the system mechanically enforces. God Mode creates
  both.

  Agent intelligence was another battle. GPT-4o-mini agents couldn't distinguish teammates from enemies and kept attacking their own side.
  Upgrading to GPT-4o fixed it, but at 15x the cost. The prompt engineering was critical — showing agents pre-computed distances, occupied
  cells, and explicit range markers made the difference between chaos and coherent behavior.

  State management on serverless was tricky. In-memory state broke on every hot reload and couldn't survive deployment. Migrated to Upstash
   Redis (single JSON blob) which solved consistency across serverless function invocations.

**Hackathon Prizes**

Vyuha is a natural language-controlled multi-agent simulation platform. Users describe worlds in English — "create two armies and make   
  them fight" — and autonomous LLM agents spawn, think, and act on a live 2D grid. God Mode lets you reshape the world mid-simulation: add
  agents, change rules, alter the environment, all through conversation. The engine handles game-theory interactions (cooperate, defect,   
  attack, trade), structured rule enforcement, and real-time visualization. Built solo in under 4 hours — first code commit to working demo.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLAlchemy](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLAlchemy-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# 🛒 BazaarOps 

India’s retail economy is powered by over **12 million neighborhood kirana stores**, yet most of them still manage their business manually  inventory in notebooks, credit (udhar) in diaries, and orders through unstructured WhatsApp messages. This leads to stock-outs, miscalculated credit, lost revenue, and zero visibility into daily performance. Store owners operate reactively, spending mental energy managing operations instead of growing their business.

## 💡 Our Solution

**BazaarOps** is an AI-powered, event-driven retail operating system built specifically for local stores. It transforms traditional kirana shops into intelligent, data-driven micro-enterprises.

Store owners can use BazaarOps to:

- 📦 **Manage Inventory Smartly** – Real-time product tracking with automatic low-stock detection.
- 🧾 **Track Orders Systematically** – Structured order history with easy status updates.
- 💳 **Maintain Credit (Udhar) Securely** – Digital ledger with automatic balance calculation and dispute prevention.
- 📊 **View Daily Business Insights** – Revenue summaries, order counts, and top-selling products generated automatically.
- 📢 **Send Promotions Effortlessly** – Broadcast offers to customers through integrated messaging.

## 🤖 Why It’s Different

BazaarOps doesn’t just digitize retail  IT ADDS INTELLIGENCE TO IT.  
Through an event-driven architecture and AI-powered automation, the system proactively detects business events, updates records in real time, and generates actionable insights.

This reduces human error, prevents revenue leakage, lowers cognitive load, and makes local retail smarter, safer, and scalable.

---

**In one line:** BazaarOps turns reactive neighborhood retail into proactive, AI-powered commerce infrastructure for Bharat.

**Challenges we ran into**

# 🚧 Challenges We Faced & How We Overcame Them

Building BazaarOps was technically exciting BUT  definitely not smooth😭😭😭. We faced multiple real-world engineering challenges while developing an AI-powered, multi-tenant retail operating system under hackathon time pressure.

## 1️⃣ Dependency & Environment Issues

While integrating Supabase, FastAPI, and AI tooling, we ran into multiple version conflicts and dependency mismatches. Some libraries behaved differently across environments, especially during authentication and database integration.

**How we solved it:**  
We standardized versions early, isolated services properly, and documented working configurations. Once stabilized, we avoided unnecessary upgrades and focused only on core features.

---

## 2️⃣ First-Time Working with Claude Agentic Tooling

Implementing an event-driven agent system using Claude’s tool-calling capabilities was new territory. Designing structured prompts, validating AI outputs, and ensuring safe execution without hallucinated database actions required careful planning.

**How we solved it:**  
We enforced strict JSON schemas for AI responses, validated outputs before execution, and separated AI reasoning from database access through a service layer. This made the system safer and more predictable.

---

## 3️⃣ Designing a Multi-Tenant Database

Ensuring complete data isolation between stores while maintaining a shared database was a major architectural challenge. Mistakes here could lead to cross-store data leakage.

**How we solved it:**  
We implemented store-level isolation using `store_id` in every table and enforced Row-Level Security (RLS) policies in Supabase. We also double-validated store ownership at the backend level.

---

## 4️⃣ Microservice & Event-Driven Architecture

Coordinating between dashboard, bots, backend agents, and database events required careful orchestration. Debugging event chains under time pressure was challenging.

**How we solved it:**  
We clearly separated responsibilities into agents and services, and focused on building a minimal but reliable event flow before adding complexity.

---

## ⏳ Biggest Challenge: Time Crunch

Building a scalable SaaS-style architecture in a 7-HR (SERIOUSLY???!?) hackathon timeframe forced us to prioritize ruthlessly. We had to balance clean architecture with shipping a working demo.

**What we learned:**  
Scope control, modular design, and focusing on core value over perfection were critical.

---

This project pushed us technically ~~~ from AI tooling to secure multi-tenant design and strengthened our ability to build scalable, production-oriented systems under pressure.

> Learn by doing, not by watching.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

### You don't learn to ride a bike by watching YouTube.

Yet that's exactly how most people try to learn programming. They sit through hours of tutorials, copy-paste code they half-understand, and walk away feeling productive — until they try to build something from scratch and realize nothing stuck.

---

### The real problems learners face every day:

**🔁 Tutorial Hell**
You've completed 6 courses on React. You still Google "how to use useEffect" every single time. Passive learning gives you familiarity, not understanding. There's a massive gap between *recognizing* code and *writing* it — and no amount of watching bridges that gap.

**🧭 Decision Paralysis**
Before you even start learning, you spend an hour deciding *where* to learn. Udemy or YouTube? This course or that one? Free or paid? By the time you pick, your motivation is gone. Learning shouldn't require research before the research.

**🧩 The Tooling Mess**
A typical self-study session looks like this: YouTube on one tab, VS Code on another, ChatGPT in a third, documentation in a fourth, Stack Overflow in a fifth. You're not learning — you're project-managing your own education across five different tools.

**🤖 AI Gives Answers, Not Understanding**
ChatGPT is incredible — but it solves problems *for* you. You paste an error, get a fix, move on. You never learned *why* it broke. Next time the same thing happens, you paste again. It's an infinite loop of dependency, not growth.

**📉 No Feedback Until It's Too Late**
In a course, you code along and everything works. In the real world, you make a mistake on line 3 and don't find out until line 300. There's no tight feedback loop. No one telling you *in the moment* that you're going down the wrong path.

---

### How Tilper AI Solves This

**One interface. One input. Zero friction.**

You open Tilper. You type what you want to learn. That's the entire onboarding.

- **No courses to browse.** The AI builds your learning path on the fly.
- **No passive watching.** You're writing code from minute one.
- **No answer spoon-feeding.** The AI guides you with hints and questions — like a tutor sitting next to you who refuses to just give you the answer.
- **No tab-switching chaos.** The IDE, the challenges, the AI mentor, the visual explanations — all in one place.
- **No wondering "did I actually learn that?"** You run tests. They pass or they don't. You know exactly where you stand.

---

### What people use it for:

- **"I need to learn Python for my exam next week"** → Type it in. Get a roadmap. Start solving challenges immediately.
- **"I keep forgetting how linked lists work"** → The AI generates a hands-on challenge. You build one. Now you remember.
- **"I want to learn React but every course is 40 hours"** → Tilper gives you focused, bite-sized challenges. Learn the hard parts by building, not watching.
- **"I understand the theory but can't write code on my own"** → That's literally the problem Tilper was built to fix. Every session forces you to write, think, and debug — with support, but without shortcuts.
- **"I'm preparing for coding interviews"** → Generate challenges at the right difficulty. Practice with real-time feedback. See visual breakdowns of algorithms you're struggling with.

---

### The bottom line:

Tilper AI doesn't teach you more. **It makes you learn more** — by putting you in the driver's seat from the very first second and making sure you never fall back into passive consumption.

**Stop watching. Start building. Actually remember what you learned.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Making the AI Actually Teach Instead of Just Give Answers

This was the hardest problem by far. The whole point of Tilper is **learning by doing** — but LLMs naturally want to be helpful. Ask it a coding question and it hands you the full solution on a silver platter. That's the opposite of what we needed.

**The struggle:** Getting the AI to guide without spoiling. It needed to act like a great teacher — give hints, ask leading questions, nudge you toward the answer — not just dump code.

**How I solved it:** A lot of prompt engineering iteration. I built a layered hint system where the AI starts vague and only gets more specific if the student keeps struggling. It took dozens of iterations to get the tone right — helpful but not hand-holding. I also added guardrails that detect when a response contains a full solution and forces the AI to restructure it into a guided explanation instead.

---

### 2. Real-Time Code Execution in the Browser

Building an in-browser IDE that actually **runs code and executes tests** is deceptively complex. It's not just a text editor — it needs to compile, run, catch errors, and return meaningful output, all without a heavy backend round-trip for every keystroke.

**The struggle:** Latency. Early versions had a noticeable delay between clicking "Run" and seeing output. For a learning platform where you're running code dozens of times per session, even a 2-second delay kills the flow.

**How I solved it:** I optimized the execution pipeline and leaned into client-side execution where possible. For languages that couldn't run in the browser, I built a lightweight sandboxed execution layer that minimized cold starts. It's still not instant for every language, but it's fast enough that the feedback loop feels tight.

---

### 3. Generating Challenges That Are Actually Good

Anyone can ask an LLM to "generate a coding challenge." The problem is that most of them are either **too vague, too easy, or completely untestable**.

**The struggle:** I needed challenges that were:
- Clearly defined with specific inputs/outputs
- Appropriately difficult for the student's level
- Actually verifiable with automated tests
- Genuinely educational, not just busy work

Getting all four consistently was brutal. Early versions would generate challenges with ambiguous requirements or edge cases that made the auto-generated tests fail on correct solutions.

**How I solved it:** I built a structured challenge generation pipeline — the AI doesn't just generate a description. It generates the challenge, the test cases, the expected solution, and then **validates them against each other** before presenting anything to the student. If the tests don't pass against the expected solution, the challenge gets regenerated. It added a bit of latency to challenge creation but made the experience 10x more reliable.

---

### 4. Visual Animations That Actually Help

The "Visual" tab was supposed to be a killer feature — watch sorting algorithms sort, see recursion trees branch, understand data structures visually. In practice, generating **meaningful, accurate, and well-timed** animations from AI output was a nightmare.

**The struggle:** The AI would describe a concept, but translating that into a smooth, step-by-step animation required a bridge between natural language explanation and actual visual rendering logic. Static diagrams were easy. Animated, interactive visualizations that **sync with the concept being taught** were a completely different beast.

**How I solved it:** I built a library of animation templates for common concepts and patterns. Instead of generating animations from scratch every time, the AI maps concepts to the closest template and populates it with the relevant data. It's not infinitely flexible yet, but it covers the most common use cases well — and it's a foundation I can keep expanding.

---

### 5. Keeping the UX Dead Simple

This sounds like a non-technical challenge, but it almost derailed the project. I kept adding features — different modes, settings, customization options, dashboards — and the interface started looking like a cockpit.

**The struggle:** The whole promise of Tilper is "just type what you want to learn." Every additional button, menu, or option contradicted that promise.

**How I solved it:** I ruthlessly cut features. If it couldn't be triggered naturally through the chat interface, it probably didn't need a dedicated button. I reduced the entry point to a single input field and two clear actions — **Plan** or **Learn**. Everything else reveals itself only when it's relevant. It was painful to remove things I'd spent time building, but the product got dramatically better every time I deleted something.

**The problem it solves**

TruthTag ,basically, helps us to spot biasing done in the news articles. as we know, nowadays, most of the news articles contains more of the biased statements rather than the actual news and the audience get emotionally triggered and believe those news articles. So to provide the filtered and original news to the readers we have made this project which figure out how much biasing has been done in the news.

As a team of freshers, one of our biggest challenges was translating our idea into a working prototype with limited technical experience.

**The problem it solves**

SkillMap AI helps students and beginners identify their skill gaps and provides a personalized learning roadmap.

Many learners feel confused about what to study next or which skills they are lacking for a specific career role. They often waste time jumping between random tutorials without clear direction.

SkillMap AI solves this by:

• Allowing users to select a career role (Frontend, Backend, AI, Data Science, etc.)
• Conducting a short MCQ-based assessment
• Analyzing their performance using visual charts
• Detecting weak skill areas automatically
• Generating a daily improvement routine
• Recommending free learning resources and courses
• Tracking consistency with a streak heatmap

This makes learning structured, personalized, and goal-oriented instead of random.

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, I faced multiple challenges:

• Handling multi-page navigation using pure JavaScript without frameworks
• Fixing issues where the login page duplicated or did not redirect correctly
• Managing dynamic question generation for different roles
• Integrating Chart.js for performance visualization
• Ensuring state persistence like streak tracking using localStorage
• Connecting frontend with Flask backend for saving scores and leaderboard

I solved these by restructuring page routing logic, debugging event handlers, simplifying the codebase into single files, and testing each feature independently before integration.

These optimizations made the application stable, faster, and easier to maintain.

[![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AMUHACKS%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://amuhacks-5.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> "Your Voice, Your Safety in campus, Our Priority."

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. The "Silence" of Victims (Safety & Discrimination)
Traditional reporting often forces students to reveal their identity, leading to fear of retaliation from peers or faculty.

The Solution: By using Device ID Hashing, students can report issues like institutional discrimination (caste, religion, or financial status) and harassment with 100% anonymity.

Women's Safety: It addresses the lack of immediate response during threats through a one-tap SOS button that bypasses bureaucracy to alert security instantly.

2. Outdated Academic Frameworks
Decision-makers are often unaware that lab equipment is broken or that the curriculum has fallen behind industry standards.

The Solution: The portal allows students to report poor laboratory conditions and a lack of teaching exposure. This "Collective Intelligence" provides administrators with real-time data on where the academic infrastructure is failing.

3. Invisible Infrastructure Failures
Issues like frequent electricity disruptions, poor water supply, and unhygienic restrooms often go ignored until they become a crisis.

The Solution: The Campus Heatmap feature visualizes "high-complaint zones." If multiple students report a water leak in "Block B," the map glows red in that area, forcing the administration to prioritize that specific repair.

4. Absence of Mental Health Support
High-pressure environments often lack full-time counselors, and students may feel stigmatized seeking help in person.

The Solution: The portal provides a discreet, non-intimidating digital channel to request mental health support or report stress-related challenges without public exposure.

5. Misleading Transparency (The "Placement" Gap)
Colleges often advertise 100% placement rates that don't reflect reality.

The Solution: Through the Reviews and Trust Score section, students can provide honest, anonymous feedback on career prospects and placement quality, creating a "Trust Score" that accurately reflects the campus value.

6. Slow Administrative Response
Standard grievance letters often sit on desks for weeks.

The Solution: The Live Tracking System (similar to a delivery app) keeps the administration accountable. Students can see when a complaint moves from "Submitted" to "In Progress" to "Resolved," eliminating the "black hole" of administrative silence.

**Challenges we ran into**

Real Issues:

IP address logging

Browser fingerprinting

Firebase auth tracking

Metadata inside uploaded images (EXIF data)

GPS precision revealing identity

 Solution:

Strip image metadata before storing

Don’t log IPs (or hash them)

Use session hashing instead of login for anonymous mode

Separate complaint DB from identity DB

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/park-conscious-6b25) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.parkconscious.in/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> find, reserve, and pay

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Urban parking is highly unorganized, time-consuming, and inefficient. Drivers often spend 15–25 minutes searching for parking, which increases traffic congestion, fuel wastage, and daily stress. At the same time, many parking spaces remain underutilized because there is no unified digital system connecting drivers with available parking providers.

Park Conscious makes parking easier by helping users quickly find nearby parking spaces, view pricing and details, and move toward digital booking and payments. For parking owners, it simplifies operations by providing tools to digitally manage spaces, track usage, and monitor revenue instead of relying on manual registers or cash handling.

In the long term, the platform aims to make parking safer and smarter using technologies like automated vehicle entry/exit logging, data-driven insights, and integration with smart city systems.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was handling location-based data and map integration reliably. While building the “Find Nearby Parking” feature, I had to work with Google Maps APIs, browser geolocation, and large JSON datasets of parking locations. Initially, issues like inconsistent coordinate formats, slow data loading, and map marker performance caused bugs and incorrect results.

I solved this by cleaning and standardising parking data using Python (BeautifulSoup + Pandas), converting fields like latitude, longitude, and pricing into consistent numeric formats, and optimising how parking data is loaded and filtered on the frontend.

**Open Innovation**

Park Conscious fits into Open Innovation because it solves a real-world urban problem that spans multiple sectors, including mobility, smart cities, infrastructure, and digital payments. The solution is not limited to a single industry; it can be integrated with government smart city initiatives, private parking operators, commercial buildings, EV infrastructure providers, and urban mobility platforms.

**The problem it solves**

# Bharat Mat  
### A Secure, Verifiable & Interactive Platform for Voter Awareness and Misinformation Control

**Bharat Mat** is a next-generation civic technology platform designed to combat political misinformation, improve voter awareness, and help citizens clearly understand complex democratic reforms such as **One Nation One Election (ONOE)** through interactive simulations, AI-powered fact-checking, and official-source verification.

Built by **Team Tensor Troops**, Bharat Mat bridges the gap between voters and trustworthy political information in an era of deepfakes, AI-generated propaganda, and fragmented civic knowledge.

---

## Problem Statement

Modern democracies face a growing crisis of trust and information overload:

- Political misinformation spreads faster than verified truth  
- AI-generated deepfakes mislead voters at scale  
- Reforms like **ONOE** are poorly understood due to lack of visual and interactive explanation  
- Existing tools are fragmented, text-heavy, and non-interactive  
- Voters lack a single, trusted source to verify claims and understand real-world impact  

**Bharat Mat** addresses these challenges by combining **AI, visualization, verification, and privacy-preserving identity systems** into one unified platform.

---

## Purpose & Vision

The goal of Bharat Mat is to:

- Empower voters with **clear, verifiable, and explainable information**
- Reduce the spread and impact of political misinformation
- Make democratic reforms understandable through **visual simulations**
- Provide a **single source of truth** backed by official documents
- Restore trust using **transparent AI + human verification**

---

## Key Features

### AI-Powered Misinformation Detection
- Detects **text, image, audio, and video** misinformation
- Classifies content as **Fake / Manipulated / Misleading**
- Displays **deepfake forensic heatmaps** as visual proof
- Links directly to **original documents or raw footage**
- Blockchain-logged verdicts ensure immutability

---

### Democracy & ONOE Impact Simulator
- Interactive **India Map–based Digital Twin**
- Visualizes state-wise tenure extension 🟢 and curtailment 🔴
- Sliders simulate governance efficiency vs accountability
- Shows required constitutional amendments
- Clear pros & cons instead of political narratives

---

### ECI Situation Room
- Real-time fetching of **official Election Commission of India (ECI)** circulars
- AI-generated summaries grounded only in official sources
- Interactive election timelines
- One-tap access to original ECI PDFs
- Calendar sync for critical election dates

---

### Campaign & Policy Intelligence Hub
- Source-backed verification of party claims
- Downloadable manifestos and policy documents
- PM / CM candidate comparisons
- No opinionated ranking — only verified data

---

### Secure & Private Voter Access
- DigiLocker / Aadhaar-based voter login
- **Zero-Knowledge Proofs** for privacy protection
- Prevents bots, fake users, and coordinated manipulation
- No tracking or profiling of voter behavior

---

### Smart Voter Assistance
- Interactive polling booth mapping
- Automated voter support center
- Real-time alerts and personalized reminders
- Works on mobile-first, low-bandwidth environments

---

### WhatsApp & SMS Verification (Planned)
- Forward suspicious messages to a national WhatsApp number
- Instant reply with:
  - Fake / Real verdict
  - Official source link
  - Simple explanation
- Designed for rural users and senior citizens

---

## Technical Architecture

- **Frontend:** React Native (Expo), TypeScript  
- **Backend:** FastAPI / Node.js (Express)  
- **AI Stack:**  
  - LLaMA-3, Mixtral  
  - Sentence Transformers  
  - LangChain + FAISS (RAG)  
  - Vision-Language Models (VLMs)  
- **Databases:** PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Pinecone  
- **Messaging & Alerts:** Twilio (SMS & WhatsApp APIs)  
- **Security:** Blockchain-based verdict logging, Zero-Knowledge Proofs  
- **Architecture:** Modular microservices + agentic AI  

Scalable from **1 citizen to 1 million citizens**.

---

## Impact

- Reduced misinformation exposure  
- Improved civic understanding  
- Higher informed voter participation  
- Transparent, proof-based political awareness  
- Stronger trust between citizens and democratic institutions  

---

## Future Scope

- Regional language expansion (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, etc.)
- Integration with India’s Digital Public Infrastructure:
  - DigiLocker
  - UMANG
- State-wise journalist & fact-checker verification network
- Nationwide WhatsApp & SMS misinformation gateway
- Deeper government and civil society partnerships

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I ran into

Building trust in AI fact-checks was difficult, as simple true/false labels felt unreliable for political content.  
We solved this by adding explainable evidence like deepfake heatmaps and direct links to official ECI sources.

Handling misinformation across text, images, and videos increased complexity.  
This was addressed using a modular AI pipeline with NLP, vision-language models, and RAG grounded in verified data.

Real-time performance and voter privacy were critical concerns.  
We improved scalability using async microservices and ensured privacy through DigiLocker-based verification with Zero-Knowledge Proofs.

Explaining ONOE clearly was challenging, so we built an interactive map-based simulator instead of long text.

**Open Innovation**

This project addresses a real-world civic problem: misinformation and voter awareness using emerging technologies like AI, blockchain, and interactive simulations.  

It combines public data, official government sources, and modern AI systems in a novel, user-facing way.  

The platform is designed to be extensible, allowing integration with existing digital public infrastructure and third-party services.  

By enabling transparency, explainability, and citizen participation, it creates a scalable foundation others can build upon.  

The solution is not limited to elections and can be adapted to multiple governance and public-information use cases.

### AquaRisk
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aquarisk-532c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/codemuggle09/AquaRisk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Predicting Safety for 60M Indians.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Folium](https://img.shields.io/badge/Folium-333333?style=flat-square) ![Plotly](https://img.shields.io/badge/Plotly-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Fluoride contamination is a 'silent killer' affecting over 60 million people in India. Because it is colorless and odorless, rural communities often realize their water is toxic only after developing irreversible dental or skeletal fluorosis.

AquaRisk bridges this critical information gap by:

Predicting Risk at Scale: Using chemical markers like pH and Calcium to predict fluoride levels where laboratory testing is unavailable.

Human-Centric Communication: Translating complex hydrogeochemical data into intuitive Fuzzy Risk Labels (Low, Medium, High) for non-technical users.

Community Connectivity: Automatically linking high-risk Pincodes to the nearest safe water sources and mapped NGOs like WaterAid India for immediate intervention.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major hurdle was Data Imbalance. Our dataset of 16,776 samples was heavily skewed toward 'Safe' readings, which caused initial ML models to overlook high-risk 'Red Zones'.

The Solution: We implemented SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) to balance our classes, ensuring our Random Forest Classifier achieved 93% accuracy even for the rarest, most dangerous contamination levels.

Technically, we also faced a 'Cluttered UI' challenge. Judges initially found the raw data overwhelming. We overcame this by redesigning the interface using a Two-Stage Workflow: a simple community safety portal for citizens and a Technical Dashboard for experts, separating noise from insight.

**Sustainable Development Goals**

AquaRisk is a system designed to provide climate and health resilience through advanced monitoring and governance of freshwater resources. It specifically aligns with the following goals:
+3


SDG 6.3 (Water Quality & Pollution): Our platform addresses the critical need for detecting geogenic pollution like fluoride, which poses a severe ecological and health risk. By using a 93% accurate Random Forest model, we provide a scalable alternative to expensive lab testing, enabling immediate intervention in "data-dark" rural areas.
+4


SDG 6.B (Community Participation): AquaRisk democratizes water intelligence. By translating complex hydrogeochemical data into an intuitive Fuzzy Risk Score, we empower local communities and non-technical health workers to make informed decisions about water safety.
+4


SDG 11.5 & 11.B (Disaster Resilience): Since groundwater quality is under growing stress due to climate change, our Regional Trends map acts as an early-warning system. It identifies contamination corridors before long-term health damage occurs, allowing governments to prioritize infrastructure like defluoridation plants.

> Bridging people in need with NGOs that care

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Finding help during times of need is often harder than it should be.

People facing issues like food insecurity, medical needs, shelter, or safety usually don’t know:

Which NGOs operate near them

What kind of help those NGOs actually provide

How to contact them quickly and safely

Existing information is:

scattered across different websites

outdated or hard to verify

not location-specific

overwhelming during stressful moments

As a result, people either delay seeking help or give up entirely.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building this project, I faced issues with state management and data flow across pages. Category selection worked visually, but selected data was not being passed correctly during navigation, causing NGO results not to display.

I resolved this by restructuring how state was handled, explicitly passing selected filters between pages and maintaining a clear separation between original and filtered NGO data. I also avoided over-engineering early by focusing on a frontend-first MVP, which helped me stabilize the core user flow before adding polish.

Through this, I learned the importance of clear data flow, proper state management, and debugging existing logic instead of continuously adding new code.

**Sustainable Development Goals**

This project supports multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals by improving access to nearby NGOs that provide essential services such as food, healthcare, education, and social support. By making local help easier to discover and contact, the platform contributes to No Poverty (SDG 1), Zero Hunger (SDG 2), Good Health and Well-being (SDG 3), Quality Education (SDG 4), and Reduced Inequalities (SDG 10). Overall, it strengthens community-level support systems, aligning with Sustainable Cities and Communities (SDG 11).

### Civic-saarthi
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/civicsaarthi-fcfe) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://GitHub.com/jagritiuppal158/civic-saarthii) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> 3R's Report Resolve Rewards

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Urban civic issues like garbage overflow, potholes, water leakage, and broken streetlights are common in cities, but the process to report them is complicated and inefficient. Citizens often do not know which department to contact, and government portals are fragmented across multiple platforms with confusing procedures.
Because of this:
Complaints get misrouted or ignored
Citizens lose trust and stop reporting issues
Authorities receive unstructured data, making prioritization difficult
Small issues escalate into larger environmental and infrastructure problems
There is no intelligent system that helps citizens identify the correct authority, understand issue urgency, or get guidance on whether the problem can be resolved locally. At the same time, governments lack real-time, structured civic data to make sustainable urban planning decisions.
Our project solves this gap by creating an AI-powered civic intelligence platform that simplifies reporting for citizens while converting complaints into actionable insights for authorities.
It makes existing tasks:
Easier — single platform, voice/text/image reporting
Faster — automatic issue classification and authority routing
Smarter — predictive analysis of recurring civic problems
More sustainable — tracks waste, water, and infrastructure stress trends
This transforms isolated complaints into a connected civic intelligence system that benefits both citizens and city administrations.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an AI-powered civic intelligence platform involved both technical and real-world challenges:
1. Multimodal Data Processing
Handling text, voice, and image inputs together was complex. We had to ensure accurate speech-to-text conversion and reliable image recognition for civic issues like potholes, garbage, and water leakage.
2. Issue Classification Accuracy
Civic complaints often use informal language. Training the system to correctly classify issues and detect urgency from varied descriptions required fine-tuning NLP models.
3. Authority Mapping
Different cities and regions have different departments and jurisdictions. Mapping issues to the correct authority dynamically was challenging due to lack of standardized public data.
4. Realistic Status Tracking
Government systems are not always integrated via APIs, making automated status updates difficult. We designed a hybrid tracking approach to handle this limitation.
5. Balancing AI Guidance vs. Misinformation
Providing citizen self-resolution guidance needed careful validation to avoid unsafe or incorrect suggestions.
6. Scalability & Real-Time Processing
Ensuring the system remains fast and responsive while processing AI models and storing large civic datasets required backend optimization.
7. Data Privacy & Security
Handling location-based civic complaints required secure authentication, user data protection, and safe data storage practices.

### ECNS Systemic Risk Engine
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ecns-systemic-risk-engine-0e04) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/CYCLOP5/lowertaperfade-datahack-2026) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://frontend-rosy-phi-35.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/FHIbY6sQ-_8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DATATHON-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://datathon-9.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Architecture of Collapse

![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deep Neural Networks](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Neural%20Networks-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The **ENCS Systemic Risk Engine** is designed to solve the challenge of identifying and mitigating systemic financial risks that arise from the complex interdependencies within global banking networks. It addresses several critical problems identified in the provided documentation:

### 1. Mapping Invisible Fault-Lines and Cascading Failures

The system models the "Architecture of Collapse" by mapping the hidden connections (credit exposures and settlement obligations) between over **4,500 financial institutions**. It solves the problem of predicting how a local failure at one bank can trigger a chain reaction of defaults across the entire network through **Eisenberg-Noe clearing physics**.

### 2. Strategic Coordination Failures (Bank Runs)

Unlike static models, ENCS accounts for **strategic behavior under incomplete information**. It models "coordination failures" where banks may withdraw credit or "run" on a counterparty not because the counterparty is insolvent, but because they fear other banks will withdraw first. This helps identify "self-fulfilling panics" that can collapse a system even when fundamentals are relatively strong.

### 3. Information Asymmetry and Transparency

The engine evaluates the impact of **Opaque vs. Transparent regimes**. It demonstrates how a lack of public information (Opaque regime) forces banks to rely on noisy private signals, leading to prisoner's dilemma dynamics and systemic instability. Conversely, it shows how Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can provide accurate "public signals" to anchor beliefs and prevent coordination failure.

### 4. Self-Reinforcing Liquidity and Margin Spirals

The engine simulates complex feedback loops where:

* **Fire-sale losses** degrade asset values, triggering further liquidations.
* **Margin spirals** occur when variation margin calls force banks to liquidate assets, driving prices down further.
* **Dynamic risk aversion** causes distressed banks to become increasingly conservative and prone to hoarding liquidity, which accelerates the system-wide collapse.

### 5. Green Swan Climate Risks

It addresses the emerging problem of **climate transition risk**. The model simulates how sudden regulatory shifts, such as a **carbon tax**, create shocks that propagate through the network. It specifically demonstrates that even "green" banks (e.g., in the EU) can default if their "brown" counterparties (e.g., in the US) are hit by climate shocks.

### 6. Regulatory Policy and Infrastructure Design

The system provides a sandbox for testing the effectiveness of financial infrastructure and regulations, such as:

* **Central Clearing Counterparty (CCP) Default Funds**: Modeling how pre-pledged member capital affects systemic resilience without creating "fictional equity".
* **Circuit Breakers (Trading Halts)**: Quantifying how much systemic damage is prevented by halting liquidations when prices drop below a certain threshold.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Fragmented and Missing Interbank Data

The team had to reconstruct a trillion-scale global banking network from fragmented regulatory filings, such as US FFIEC Call Reports and EU EBA Transparency Exercises. A major challenge was that interbank bilateral data is often missing or not publicly reported. To solve this, the engine uses a **Gravity Model** calibrated to BIS statistics and the **Sinkhorn-Knopp (RAS) algorithm** to impute missing connections while satisfying balance sheet constraints.

### 2. Computational Scale and Complexity

Modeling over 4,500 banks creates an  network complexity that is computationally expensive for standard simulation. The developers addressed this by:

* Using **sparse matrix construction** (`scipy.sparse.csr_matrix`) for memory-efficient storage of millions of interbank edges.
* Offloading the heavy simulation logic to a high-performance **Rust core** via PyO3 to handle massive Monte Carlo runs.

### 3. Underestimation of Risk in Standard Models

A core challenge was that standard industry models (like the "Max-Entropy" or "Uniform" models) often underestimate systemic risk by assuming interbank connections are spread out thinly and uniformly. This "artificial dilution" absorbs shocks that should realistically trigger a cascade. The ENCS team had to implement a **"Smart" Core-Periphery topology** to correctly capture the high interconnectivity of major systemic banks (SIFIs).

### 4. Modeling Nonlinear "Cliff-Edge" Dynamics

The engine had to account for complex, self-reinforcing feedback loops that create sudden, catastrophic failures rather than linear declines:

* **Liquidity and Margin Spirals:** Modeling how variation margin calls force banks to liquidate assets, which further drives down prices and triggers more calls.
* **Exponential Fire-Sales:** Implementing non-linear price impacts where asset prices decay exponentially based on the volume of liquidated assets.

### 5. Transitioning from Mechanical to Strategic Behavior

Moving beyond simple mechanical defaults (where a bank only fails if it is insolvent) required modeling **strategic coordination failures**. This involved assigning "Edge-level agents" to every interbank exposure to decide whether to "Roll Over" or "Withdraw" based on Bayesian beliefs and expected utility. A key challenge here was implementing **Dynamic Risk Aversion**, where a bank's internal behavior changes as its equity is depleted, making it twice as likely to hoard liquidity and accelerate a run.

### 6. Ensuring Conservation of Money

In complex simulations involving Central Counterparties (CCPs) and margin shortfalls, there is a risk of "conjuring capital" or violating basic accounting principles. The developers had to ensure the **Conservation of Money** by:

* Funding CCP Default Funds through pro-rata deductions from bank equity.
* Tracking margin shortfalls as systemic credit losses rather than phantom liquidation pressure.

### LoopKart
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/loopkart-af11) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://janisha-10.github.io/LoopKart/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackTU%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacktu7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> "Don't dump it- Loop it!"

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

LoopKart helps businesses transform surplus and waste into valuable resources, creating a win-win for industries and startups.

- Maximizes resource utilization: Industries often discard usable materials; LoopKart connects these businesses directly with buyers who need them, reducing wasted resources.

- Cost-effective sourcing: Startups, NGOs, and small manufacturers can purchase surplus materials at lower costs, saving money and reducing dependency on raw production.

- Simplified supply chain: LoopKart streamlines the process of listing, discovering, and purchasing surplus materials, eliminating manual negotiation and reducing administrative overhead.

- Sustainability & compliance: By diverting usable waste from landfills, companies not only cut disposal costs but also strengthen their environmental compliance and corporate social responsibility (CSR) efforts.

- Safer transactions: Verified business accounts and transparent listings ensure that transactions are reliable, secure, and professional, reducing the risk of fraud or miscommunication.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building LoopKart, we faced several challenges on the backend: 

- Integrating AI tools: Incorporating Gemini AI for smart recommendations and material matching. We needed to improve data flow and API calls to keep the system fast and reliable. 

- Smooth UI: We aimed to create an easy-to-navigate user interface. These challenges drove us to improve our backend structure, making LoopKart faster, smarter, and more secure.

**Google Gemini**

We integrated Google Gemini into our platform to enable intelligent material searching and content discovery. It processes user queries, understands context, and delivers accurate, relevant results in real time.

The integration uses secure API communication through our backend, ensuring fast performance and data privacy. This allows users to quickly find study materials, documents, and resources without manual searching.

By using Gemini, our system improves search efficiency, reduces time spent browsing, and enhances overall user productivity.

> DETECT - SUPPORT - INCLUDE

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Millions of students with learning differences such as dyslexia, dyscalculia, and comprehension challenges remain undetected, especially in large classrooms where teachers lack time and specialized tools to identify early warning signs. Traditional assessments focus only on marks and written responses, missing how a child actually thinks, perceives, and learns. As a result, many children are mislabeled as weak or inattentive instead of receiving timely support. Parents also lack clear insights into their child’s learning patterns, and schools struggle to provide personalized intervention at scale. SwarSetu addresses this gap by enabling early, accessible, and intelligent learning assessments that go beyond right-or-wrong answers. It helps educators and parents understand each child’s cognitive and learning behavior early, allowing timely support and more inclusive classrooms.

**Challenges we ran into**

Balancing speed vs intelligence: Real-time AI (image, voice, perception analysis) increased latency, so I had to design caching and pre-generation strategies to keep the platform responsive.

Designing meaningful assessments: Creating tests that evaluate perception and cognition (not just right/wrong answers) while keeping them age-appropriate and non-diagnostic was complex.

Multilingual implementation: Ensuring the platform works across multiple Indian languages required handling UI translation, voice inputs, and consistency across dashboards.

Role-based data flow: Linking student, teacher, parent, and principal dashboards into one synchronized analytics system without data conflicts took careful architecture planning.

AI integration reliability: Integrating models for voice, image, and text while maintaining accuracy and stability across devices required multiple iterations and fallback logic.

User experience vs feature depth: Keeping the interface simple and engaging while supporting advanced analytics and reports was a constant design challenge.

Deployment & scaling: Managing real-time deployments, caching, and performance on Vercel while maintaining a smooth demo-ready experience required optimization.

**Google Gemini**

SwarSetu uses Google Gemini to power intelligent perception-based learning assessments and real-time insight generation. Gemini enables dynamic creation of contextual test content, including scenario-based questions and adaptive learning prompts tailored to different grade levels and learning patterns. Through Gemini’s multimodal capabilities, the platform analyzes student responses from voice, text, and perception-based interactions to generate meaningful, non-diagnostic insights for teachers and parents. It also supports real-time generation of visual scenarios for cognitive and emotional interpretation tests, making assessments more engaging and personalized. By integrating Gemini’s advanced reasoning and content generation capabilities, SwarSetu transforms traditional assessments into adaptive, multilingual, and insight-driven learning experiences that scale across diverse classrooms.

**ElevenLabs**

SwarSetu leverages voice as the primary interface to make learning assessments more accessible and natural for children. Using speech-based interaction, the platform evaluates reading fluency, pronunciation, response confidence, and comprehension patterns across multiple Indian languages. Voice input enables students especially those with early learning difficulties to respond comfortably without relying only on written tests. These spoken responses are analyzed to generate insights for teachers and parents, helping identify learning gaps and provide timely support. By integrating advanced voice technologies, SwarSetu transforms traditional assessments into interactive, inclusive, and scalable voice-first learning experiences aligned with the ElevenLabs vision of powerful, real-world voice applications.

> Advance UAV detection software

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

****The Rising Threat of Malicious Drones****

**Malicious Use:** There is a rapid rise in the use of small , low-cost drones for malicious activities like surveillance and smuggling.

**Detection Gap**:Traditional radar and GPS systems fail to detect these low-altitude and micro-drones.

**High Security Risk:** This creates significant security risks for defense installations, borders, airports, and critical infrastructure.

**Cost Barrier:** Existing counter-drone systems are often prohibitively expensive and heavily dependent on specialized hardware.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1.⁠ ⁠Lack of Specialized Data (Thermal & RF)**
The Problem: While standard drone images are easy to find, Thermal (Infrared) drone footage and Raw RF Drone Signals are extremely rare in open-source datasets.
Our Struggle: We couldn't just download a "ready-to-use" dataset for the night-vision and signal models.
How we solved it: We had to manually curate a small custom dataset and use Data Augmentation (flipping, rotating, changing brightness) to artificially increase our training data size.
**2. Challenge :** Converting raw high-frequency radio signals into 2D Spectrogram images requires heavy mathematical computation (Fast Fourier Transform), which initially caused a 300ms lag in our system.
Why it mattered: This delay meant the "Alert" would pop up after the drone had already moved, making the tracking feel unresponsive.

**MongoDB Atlas**

We Used Mongo DB atlas to store the Json Histories of the dections and runs

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Unsafe or Uncertain Drone Landings**

Existing systems often provide only binary “safe/unsafe” decisions.

AegisNet evaluates landing safety in a nuanced way, scoring candidate zones and highlighting risk levels.

**Lack of Visual Feedback for Decision-Making**

Pilots or autonomous systems may not know which areas are safer at a glance.

Your gradient heatmap gives an intuitive visual representation from unsafe (red) to safe (green) zones.

**Difficulty Identifying the Optimal Landing Spot**

Choosing a landing spot manually or blindly can be risky near obstacles like forests, water, vehicles, or buildings.

AegisNet automatically calculates the safest landing coordinates based on obstacle proximity and open terrain.

**Inability to Quickly Prototype on Small Datasets**

Many AI-based landing systems require large datasets to train.

AegisNet can train a prototype with fewer images, enabling fast testing and iterative development during hackathons.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Training the YOLO / CNN Model**

Collecting and preprocessing sufficient data for accurate predictions was time-consuming.

Balancing model complexity with real-time performance required careful optimization.

**Integrating Python Backend with JavaScript Frontend**

Connecting model inference (Python) to a responsive web interface (JS/HTML/CSS) involved setting up API endpoints and ensuring smooth data transfer.

Handling image uploads, heatmap generation, and real-time display added additional integration complexity.

**Dataset Research and Annotation**

Identifying high-quality images representing varied landing scenarios was challenging.

Manual annotation of candidate landing zones, obstacles, and safe areas was labor-intensive but crucial for training accuracy.

**MongoDB Atlas**

Data-Centric Architecture:

AegisNet relies on storing drone images, heatmaps, confidence scores, and recommended landing coordinates for real-time analysis and historical tracking.

MongoDB, as a flexible NoSQL document database, is ideal for handling this heterogeneous data (images metadata, JSON-based safety scores, and history logs).

Scalable History Management:

The History tab feature tracks past analyses. MongoDB can efficiently store and query large numbers of records with variable data structures, enabling quick retrieval of prior landing assessments.

Rapid Prototyping & Flexibility:

MongoDB allows storing dynamic data structures, making it easy to integrate new data types (e.g., additional sensors or annotations) without redesigning the database.

Real-Time Querying:

Confidence scores and heatmap metadata can be queried in real-time for visualization on the web app, supporting immediate decision-making for drone operations.

Integration with AI Pipelines:

MongoDB can store model predictions alongside images, providing a centralized repository for analysis, training data updates, and future model improvements.

### HawkEye
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/market-regime-interpretation-and-insights-ae5a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ishanvianand-lol/quantitative-research-1) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://quantitative-research-hawkes.streamlit.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PayLoad'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pay-load.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Advanced Market Microstructure Analytics

![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Jupyter Notebook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jupyter%20Notebook-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional technical analysis treats all price moves as equal, but markets don't work that way. 
A 1% move during calm conditions is fundamentally different from a 1% move during a crisis. 
Most retail traders and even professional analysts miss the **hidden structure** beneath price movements:

1. **Shock Clustering** - Volatility begets more volatility, but when will the next shock hit?
2. **Jump vs Diffusion** - Is this a temporary noise or a fundamental regime shift?
3. **Information Asymmetry** - Are informed traders active right now, or is it just noise?

**VolatilityLens solves this by:**
- Identifying **self-exciting shock patterns** using Hawkes processes (borrowed from earthquake prediction)
- Detecting **statistical jumps** (discontinuous price moves from news/large orders) vs normal diffusion
- Providing **actionable intelligence**: probability of next shock, jump contribution to volatility, regime identification

Instead of just saying "RSI is 70, market is overbought," it tells you:
- "RSI is 70 AND Hawkes intensity is elevated → High probability reversal in next 10-30 minutes"
- "Jump detected with 42% branching ratio → Expect 0.42 additional shocks from this event"

**Challenges we ran into**

### **1. VPIN Implementation Hell**
**Problem**: Initial VPIN (Volume-synchronized Probability of Informed Trading) was stuck at 1.0 
(100% toxic flow) - clearly wrong!

**Root Cause**: 
- Used simple tick rule (price up = buy, down = sell) → Too binary
- Didn't account for zero price changes → Forward fill issues
- Volume bucket logic had off-by-one errors

**Solution**: 
- Switched to **Bulk Volume Classification (BVC)** with Z-score methodology
- V_buy = V × Φ((ΔP)/σ) where Φ is normal CDF
- This gave realistic 50/50 buy/sell split instead of 100/0

**Lesson**: Read the actual academic papers (Easley et al. 2012), don't just implement 
from blog posts!

---

### **2. Hawkes Process Optimization Instability**
**Problem**: MLE optimization would randomly fail or return nonsensical parameters 
(α/β > 10, persistence > 1.5)

**Root Cause**:
- Poor initial parameter guesses
- Log-likelihood function has local minima
- Compensator integral was numerically unstable for large T

**Solution**:
- Used L-BFGS-B with strict bounds: α, β, μ > 1e-6, α/β < 0.99
- Better initialization: μ = N/T (empirical rate), α = 0.05, β = 0.2
- Vectorized intensity calculation (avoided Python loops)

**Code snippet that saved me:**
```python
# Compensator term - use numpy broadcasting
compensator = mu * T + (alpha/beta) * np.sum(1 - np.exp(-beta * (T - events)))
```

---

### **3. mplfinance Integration with Custom Indicators**
**Problem**: mplfinance is powerful but opinionated - couldn't overlay Hawkes intensity 
on candlestick charts

**Challenges**:
- `make_addplot()` expects same index as OHLCV data
- Can't mix scatter + line plots easily
- No built-in support for dual y-axes (price vs intensity)

**Solution**:
- Create shock points as separate series with NaN for non-shocks
- Use `type='scatter'` in addplot for event markers
- For complex layouts (RSI + Volume + Custom), fell back to matplotlib subplots

**Workaround:**
```python
shock_points = chart_data['Close'].copy()
shock_points[chart_data['Hawkes_Shock'] == 0] = np.nan  # Hide non-shocks
apds.append(mpf.make_addplot(shock_points, type='scatter', marker='v', color='red'))
```

**Quantifying the Markets - Machine Learning**

### **The Core Philosophy:**

Markets are **NOT** random walks. They have **structure**, **memory**, and **regime-dependent behavior**. 
Traditional finance assumes Gaussian returns and constant volatility - this project REJECTS that.

**VolatilityLens quantifies three hidden market properties:**

---

### **1. Self-Excitation (Hawkes Process)**

**The Quant Insight**: 
- Each shock increases probability of future shocks (α > 0)
- Shocks cluster in time (not independent like coin flips)
- **Branching ratio α/β** = expected number of aftershocks

**Real Example from Demo:**
```
μ = 0.0012 (baseline rate)
α = 0.0089 (excitation)
β = 0.0211 (decay)
Branching ratio = 0.42

Translation: Each shock triggers 0.42 additional shocks on average.
The market has MEMORY - it's a self-exciting point process, not white noise.
```

**Why This Matters**: 
- VaR models assume independence → underestimate tail risk
- Our Hawkes model QUANTIFIES the cascade effect
- If branching ratio → 1.0, market enters critical state (2008-style cascades)

---

### **2. Jump-Diffusion Decomposition (Lee-Mykland)**

**The Quant Insight**:
Price evolution = Continuous diffusion + Rare jumps

Returns = σ·dW (Brownian motion) + J·dN (Jump process)

**Real Example:**
```
Total price variation: 100%
Jump contribution: 47.3%
Diffusion contribution: 52.7%

Translation: Despite jumps being only 2.1% of observations,
they account for HALF of total volatility!
```

**Why This Matters**:
- Traditional volatility models (GARCH) assume continuity → fail during crises
- Jump-robust volatility (Bipower Variation) gives TRUE continuous risk
- Position sizing should account for jump risk separately

---

### **3. Information-Driven Volatility (Technical + Microstructure)**

**The Quant Insight**:
Not all volatility is equal:
- **Uninformed volatility** (noise traders, liquidity shocks) → Mean-reverting
- **Informed volatility** (jumps, Hawkes cascades) → Directional

**Framework:**
```
IF Hawkes_intensity > threshold AND RSI > 70:
    → Informed selling pressure (smart money exiting)
    
IF Jump_detected AND Bollinger_squeeze:
    → Information asymmetry resolved (breakout confirmed)
```

**Why This Matters**:
- **Quantifies** the difference between "price moved" and "price moved for a reason"
- Combines classical TA (RSI, Bollinger) with modern microstructure (Hawkes, Jumps)
- Gives probabilistic trading signals, not binary "buy/sell"

---

### **The "Quantifying the Market" Thesis:**

**Traditional Approach:**
"Market is at resistance, RSI is 70, so sell."

**VolatilityLens Approach:**
"Market is at resistance (price), RSI is 70 (momentum), Hawkes intensity is 3.2σ above baseline 
(shock clustering), and 3 jumps detected in last 50 bars (informed activity). 

→ Probability of 5% move in next 2 hours: 68%
→ Recommended stop: 2.1 ATR = $4.50
→ Expected cascade: 0.42 additional shocks (10-30 min)

**This is quantification.**"

---

### **Mathematical Rigor:**

1. **Hawkes MLE**: Maximizes log-likelihood of observed event times
```
   L(μ,α,β|events) = Σ log λ(tᵢ) - ∫₀ᵀ λ(t)dt
```
2. **Technical Indicators**: Classic formulas (RSI, BB, ATR) with volatility normalization

**All combined** → A probabilistic framework for market analysis, not guesswork.

---

### **Impact on "Quantifying the Market":**

- **Democratizes** institutional-grade analytics (Hawkes, VPIN, jump detection)
- **Open-source** implementation for educational purposes
- **Real-time** dashboard replacing static historical analysis
- **Bridges gap** between academic research (Lee-Mykland 2008, Hawkes 1971) and retail trading

**This project proves:** You CAN quantify market chaos. You CAN measure shock cascades. 
You CAN distinguish signal from noise. 

**And now, anyone can.**

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
1. Hostel students often struggle with:
2. Running out of money before month‑end
3. Confusion in splitting shared expenses fairly
4. Hidden wastage from skipped mess meals vs outside food orders
5. Roommate mismatches and unresolved hostel complaints
6. Lack of transparency in utilities and safety management

How People Can Use It
1. Our app makes hostel life easier and safer by:
2. Budgeting & Tracking: Students can plan monthly expenses, track spending categories, and avoid shortages.
3. Survival Predictor: Alerts when funds are running low, with actionable suggestions to stretch money.
4. Mess & Food Intelligence: Compares mess usage with outside food orders to highlight wastage.
5. Shared Expense Automation: Auto‑splits bills, assigns payers, and sends polite reminders.
6. Roommate Intelligence: Matches compatible roommates and ensures fairness in contributions.
7. Complaint Governance: Transparent system for submitting and tracking hostel issues.
8. Safety Management: Digital leave requests, entry‑exit logs, and parent dashboards for accountability.
9. Utility Heatmaps: Divides costs based on actual usage, reducing disputes.

Impact
By combining money, utilities, food, roommates, and complaints into one platform, the app transforms hostel living into a fair, transparent, and stress‑free experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building the project in Figma, our team faced a few hurdles:
1. Consistency Across Screens:  
Initially, different team members designed separate pages, which led to slight variations in buttons, cards, and layouts.
Solution: We created a shared component library in Figma and applied auto‑layout. This ensured that any change updated everywhere automatically.
2. Visualizing Complex Features:  
Features like bill splitting and roommate fairness index were difficult to represent in a simple, student‑friendly way.
Solution: We decided to use icons + minimal text instead of long explanations, which made the UI cleaner and easier to understand.

**Hostel Life Utility Manager - UI/UX Beginner Track (Freshers Only)**

Our project directly addresses the challenges faced by hostel students in managing their daily life and finances. The Hostel Life Utility Manager track is about creating tools that simplify hostel living, and our solution fits perfectly because:
1. It helps students plan, track, and control monthly expenses so they don’t run out of money.
2. It manages shared utilities and expenses fairly with auto-split bills and polite reminders.
3. It provides mess vs outside food intelligence, highlighting hidden wastage and improving food budgeting.
4. It introduces roommate compatibility and fairness systems, reducing conflicts and improving hostel harmony.
5. It integrates complaint governance, safety management, and lifestyle tracking into one platform.

In short, our project is not just a budgeting app — it is a complete hostel life simulator and manager that combines money, utilities, food, roommates, and complaints into one student-friendly system. This makes it a perfect fit for the Hostel Life Utility Manager track.

The Problem It Solves

Hostel students often struggle to track daily expenses and manage shared bills, leading to confusion, forgotten payments, and awkward money discussions. Most finance apps are complex and fail to keep users consistent.

SpendSmart simplifies expense management by enabling easy daily tracking, automatic bill splitting, and clear visibility of pending dues. It uses gamification through XP, levels, and badges
to maintain consistency and encourage healthier spending habits, making budgeting simple and engaging for hostel life.

**Challenges we ran into**

A key challenge while building SpendSmart was keeping the budget status and visual indicators (Safe / Caution / Overspent, savings jar, progress bar) in sync when users edited or deleted expenses. 

Initially, the spending total updated correctly, but some UI elements did not refresh instantly, leading to inconsistent feedback.

How I solved it:
- Centralized all budget and expense calculations into a single logic flow  
- Updated UI states only after recalculations were completed  
- Tested edge cases like deleting or modifying the only expense of the day

Result:
All visual indicators now update accurately in real time, improving user trust and overall app reliability.

### FrozenGround
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/frozenground-a6e8) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.notion.so/Off-road-semantic-segmentation-2f7527ed7aee8004a8bce9012868054f?source=copy_link) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PayLoad'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pay-load.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> When frozen foundations learn to see the desert.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

Autonomous off-road navigation requires accurate understanding of unstructured terrain, where roads, lanes, and standardized cues do not exist. Misclassifying terrain types (e.g., drivable ground vs rocks or vegetation) can lead to unsafe navigation decisions, vehicle damage, or mission failure.

Our project solves this by providing robust pixel-level semantic scene segmentation for off-road environments. It enables machines to reliably identify terrain, obstacles, and environmental features even when operating in previously unseen desert conditions.

## What it can be used for

Autonomous off-road vehicles: Improve path planning and obstacle avoidance in deserts, forests, or construction sites

Robotics & exploration: Support ground robots used in search-and-rescue, mining, or planetary exploration

Simulation-to-real transfer: Reduce reliance on expensive real-world data by training on synthetic environments

Safety & reliability: Enable safer decision-making by distinguishing drivable terrain from hazardous regions

## Why it makes existing tasks easier

Eliminates the need for large, manually annotated real-world datasets

Improves generalization across environments through data-centric optimization

Produces interpretable, pixel-level outputs that can directly feed downstream navigation and planning systems

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into

### Dataset structure and label interpretation
One of the initial challenges was understanding the structure of the Falcon-generated dataset and how segmentation labels were encoded as pixel values rather than simple class indices. This required careful inspection and a custom mask conversion step to correctly map raw pixel values to semantic class IDs before training.

### Training efficiency under time and resource constraints
Training a ViT-based segmentation model on Colab’s free-tier GPU was computationally expensive, with long epoch times. This was addressed by freezing the backbone, tuning batch size for the available GPU memory, and focusing on high-impact changes (data augmentation and loss design) rather than costly architectural modifications.

### Improving generalization without overfitting
Since the evaluation environment was unseen, overfitting to the synthetic training data was a real risk. This was mitigated by introducing realistic, on-the-fly data augmentations and switching to an overlap-aware loss (Cross-Entropy + Dice), which improved region-level segmentation quality and robustness.

### Colab environment and path issues
Running the project on Google Colab introduced challenges around file paths, execution context, and script consistency (e.g., __file__ not being available in notebooks, relative paths breaking across runs). This was resolved by switching to explicit absolute paths and treating the notebook as a controller that executes standalone training and evaluation scripts.

**Offroad Semantic Scene Segmentation Challenge - LLMs and AI**

Our project directly targets the challenge of off-road semantic scene segmentation under domain shift. We train a pixel-level segmentation model using synthetic desert imagery generated with Duality AI’s Falcon platform and evaluate it on a previously unseen desert environment, strictly avoiding any test-set leakage.

The approach focuses on generalization and robustness, combining a frozen foundation vision model (DINOv2) with a lightweight segmentation head, realistic data augmentations, and an overlap-aware loss (Cross-Entropy + Dice). This design improves segmentation quality across diverse terrain and object classes, aligning closely with the track’s goal of enabling reliable scene understanding for autonomous off-road navigation.
