### NeuroLearn AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/neuro-learn-94cf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/renu7483/Neuro-Learn.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PEC%20HACKS%204.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pec-hacks.devfolio.co)

> Beyond Scores, Towards Understanding

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

NeuroLearn solves the problem of one-size-fits-all learning by identifying what each student is struggling with and providing personalized support.

Students often receive the same questions and learning materials regardless of their individual misconceptions or performance. NeuroLearn uses a Rule Engine to identify learning gaps, creates a student learning profile, and uses an Adaptive Learning Strategy to decide what the student needs next.

Students can also upload large learning materials, which are processed using RAG, chunking, embeddings, and Actian VectorAI DB. The system retrieves only the most relevant content and uses Gemini to provide grounded explanations and personalized practice questions.

For teachers, NeuroLearn provides misconception insights, student progress analytics, and targeted MCQ generation, helping them identify learning gaps and create more effective assessments.

In short: NeuroLearn turns assessment results into a continuous cycle of diagnosis → personalization → remediation → practice → re-evaluation, making learning more personalized for students and more actionable for teachers.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest challenges was handling large learning materials efficiently. Initially, the PDF upload limits were too restrictive, and sending complete documents to an AI model would be slow and expensive.

We solved this by building a RAG pipeline with page-wise extraction, structure-aware chunking, embeddings, and Actian VectorAI DB. Instead of sending the entire PDF to Gemini, we retrieve only the most relevant Top-K chunks using student_id and document_id metadata filtering.

Another challenge was maintaining student-specific learning data securely. We added student and document ownership checks at both the API and vector-retrieval levels so that one student cannot retrieve another student's learning material.

We also faced challenges in keeping the system personalized without making diagnosis dependent on AI guesses. We therefore kept the Rule Engine as the deterministic authority for misconception diagnosis and learning decisions, while using Gemini mainly for grounded explanations and question generation.

Finally, we tested the system extensively for offline failures, duplicate questions, large-file boundaries, and backward compatibility, resulting in 190/190 automated tests passing.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

NeuroLearn uses the Gemini API as the intelligent generation layer of our adaptive learning platform. After the Rule Engine identifies a student's misconceptions and learning needs, NeuroLearn retrieves only the most relevant content from the student's uploaded materials using RAG, chunking, embeddings, Actian VectorAI, metadata filtering, and Top-K retrieval. Gemini then uses this grounded context to generate personalized explanations, worked examples, hints, and practice MCQs.

This makes Gemini useful beyond simple chatbot responses: it adapts the generated learning content to each student's diagnosed misconception and difficulty level while grounding answers in their own study materials. Gemini also supports teachers by generating targeted MCQs based on topic, learning objective, misconception, and difficulty.

The Rule Engine remains responsible for diagnosis, mastery, and learning decisions, while Gemini focuses on high-quality, personalized educational content generation. This combination makes the system more explainable, reliable, and useful for both students and teachers.

**Best Use of Actian Vector Database**

NeuroLearn uses Actian VectorAI DB as the semantic retrieval layer for its personalized learning system. Students can upload large learning materials, which are processed through page-wise extraction → structure-aware chunking → embeddings → Actian VectorAI DB.

When a student asks a question, NeuroLearn does not send the entire PDF to Gemini. Instead, Actian VectorAI performs fast semantic Top-K retrieval and returns only the most relevant educational chunks. We also apply metadata filtering using student_id and document_id, ensuring that students can retrieve only their own learning materials.

The retrieved evidence is then passed to Gemini to generate grounded explanations, worked examples, and personalized MCQs with page/section citations.

This makes Actian VectorAI especially valuable for large educational documents, fast semantic search, personalized RAG, and secure multi-student isolation, while reducing the amount of data sent to the LLM.

> Where Farming Meets Intelligence.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MySQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ollama](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ollama-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### 🧠 1. Vision Model Output Parsing & Edge Latency
* **The Hurdle**: Running multimodal vision models (`llava:7b`) for plant disease analysis presented high response latencies and non-deterministic JSON formatting (e.g., models outputting markdown wrappers or `<think>` tags instead of strict JSON).
* **The Solution**: We engineered a robust 3-tiered response extraction pipeline with regex fallbacks (`extractJSON`) to sanitize LLM outputs. Additionally, we implemented a zero-downtime offline fallback engine (`plantHealthFallback.js`) to guarantee instantaneous, non-blocking UI feedback.

### 🛰️ 2. Fusing Geospatial & Environmental Data Streams
* **The Hurdle**: Normalizing multi-source datasets (SoilGrids v2, Open-Meteo microclimate telemetry, and satellite NDVI indices) into a single, cohesive prompt context for LLM reasoning without exceeding token limits.
* **The Solution**: Built a lightweight context compressor (`fieldContext.js`) and unified PHP `AIOrchestrator` engine that aggregates raw telemetry into concise token representations before feeding the AI prompt pipeline.

### 🎨 3. Maintaining High-FPS Spatial UI with Ambient Motion
* **The Hurdle**: Combining dynamic background video loops with complex glassmorphic UI elements and live map layers caused GPU rendering lag on low-power devices.
* **The Solution**: Built an optimized HTML5 Canvas engine (*Living Firefly Field Emerald Swarm*) leveraging `requestAnimationFrame` and CSS hardware acceleration, maintaining a smooth 60 FPS spatial visual experience.

**The problem it solves**

🌾 The Problem
Smallholder farmers in climate-vulnerable regions face two severe structural crises:
1. **Uncertain Crop Health & Delayed Advisory**: Lacking immediate access to agricultural experts, farmers struggle to identify plant diseases early, leading to crop losses up to 40% annually.
2. **Opaque & Delayed Crop Insurance Claims**: Traditional crop insurance validation (e.g., PMFBY) requires tedious manual field inspections, taking months to process payouts during critical drought or flood distress.

**3. Automated Parametric Crop Insurance Engine (FarmClaim)**
* **Objective Loss Settlement**: Insurers and field officers can generate automated loss assessments. Our parametric algorithm fuses satellite-derived NDVI vegetation health (55% weight), rainfall deficits (30%), and heat stress (15%) to validate claim payouts in seconds instead of months.

**4. Context-Aware Advisory & Market Intelligence**
* **Krishi Saarthi AI Companion**: An AI advisor powered by field context (current weather, soil type, crop stage) that delivers tailored farming bullet-points, crop rotation suggestions, and real-time mandi price trends.

### FinGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finguard-b0ac) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Black-and-Yellow/finguard.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-PEC%20HACKS%204.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://pec-hacks.devfolio.co)

> Financial Bodyguard

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

UPI is instant and irreversible. That's the whole problem.

India lost ₹22,495 crore to cyber fraud in 2025. UPI scams alone took ₹1,750 crore in FY 2025-26, up 31%. By the time someone realises they've been tricked, the money has already moved through several mule accounts across state lines.

Every safety feature that exists today fires after you've paid. FinGuard is a pre-authorisation safety layer — it reads the payment request before any UPI app opens.

What people actually use it for:

Before paying a stranger. A seller sends a UPI ID over WhatsApp. Paste it into FinGuard and see whether the network has ever met that address, how long it's been known, and what the address itself gives away — before you deal with them.
When someone is on the phone telling you to pay. FinGuard notices a call is in progress and that AnyDesk is installed, and treats that pairing as the digital-arrest setup it is.
When you're told money is coming to you. Say "I was promised a refund" and FinGuard checks that belief against what the request actually does. If the request debits you, it says STOP — this request sends money above everything else.
When a QR claims to be a bank. sbi-refund@okaxis grades D on address structure alone, with no history required.
After the money is gone. A prepared incident report, the cybercrime portal, the 1930 helpline, and a first-hour countdown — because the golden hour decides recovery.
What makes it different: most such tools claim to "block fraud." FinGuard states exactly what it can and cannot see. No bank connection. No NPCI access. It cannot block or reverse anything. It publishes its entire scoring policy and says outright that the numbers are deterministic intervention values, not statistically calibrated

**Challenges we ran into**

# The CIBIL problem — a score with no data to score
The judges asked for a credit-score equivalent for a UPI ID. NPCI publishes nothing per-address, so the literal version is impossible for anyone outside a bank.
The breakthrough was realising CIBIL isn't a regulator reading the banking system — it's a bureau holding what its members contribute. That construction is copyable. Our network is the membership; every safety check is one contributed observation.But a bureau with no members reports nothing, so we added a fifth pillar that needs no network at all: the address text itself. That's 30 of 100 points available on an address nobody has ever checked — which is why a judge can invent a scam address on stage and get a D from an empty database.

# Our warning kept changing its mind
We built a feature to spot suspicious payment addresses. It worked — but then we noticed an honest seller got flagged on the second check and cleared on the third. Same address, different answer.
The reason was that checking an address adds to its record, so we were partly reacting to our own checks. We made the rule stricter so a single check can't tip the result, and wrote a test that checks the same address ten times in a row and fails if the answer ever changes.

to use the help of gemini api to explain to common people about the risk of the fraud payments they are about to do

Only 22% of Indian seniors fully understand UPI; 68% are afraid of scams
Cybercrime against seniors rose 86% in two years

Right now FinGuard's verdict is English text on a screen. A panicking 70-year-old, mid-scam-call, will not read a signal breakdown.

**Best Use of Vultr**

Everything runs on our laptop. That means:

The APK has the API URL compiled in, so every network change forces a rebuild
Venue Wi-Fi changes your IP → demo dies
You cannot demo the network effect, which is your strongest moment — three judges scanning the same QR and watching REACH tick up needs one shared server, not localhost
Release builds refuse plain HTTP by design, so you can only ever ship a debug APK

> Context Aware AI Travel Orchestration System

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced while building Journey360 was making AI-generated travel information reliable enough for real-world usage. Although LLMs are powerful at reasoning and generating itineraries, they can sometimes produce incomplete or malformed outputs. To overcome this, we implemented structured validation and a stack-based JSON repair mechanism that detects incomplete structures, repairs them, and validates the final response before it is used by the application.

Another major challenge was dealing with inconsistent or incorrect location data from external APIs and AI-generated results. An incorrect coordinate could potentially direct a traveler to the wrong location. We addressed this by implementing a multi-level geocoding fallback mechanism along with a post-generation coordinate verification process, ensuring that locations are validated before being used for navigation and itinerary generation.

Budget reliability was another important hurdle. We realized that allowing an AI model to directly calculate the final travel cost could result in inaccurate totals. Therefore, we separated AI reasoning from financial computation. The AI can recommend activities and reason about travel options, while the final cost is calculated deterministically from itemized expenses, making the budget more dependable.

We also faced challenges with external API failures, rate limits and temporary service interruptions because Journey360 depends on multiple real-time travel data sources. To make the application resilient, we introduced caching, retry mechanisms with exponential backoff and a multi-model fallback strategy. This ensures that a temporary failure in one service does not unnecessarily interrupt the entire travel experience.

The most important challenge was not simply collecting information, but making information from different sources work together as one coherent travel decision. Weather, local news, safety alerts, maps, places, budgets, user preferences and itineraries all provide different pieces of information. We addressed this by building Journey360 around a shared travel context, allowing the system to combine validated real-time information with the traveler's personal journey before generating recommendations.

Our biggest learning was that building reliable AI is not just about using a powerful model. It is about engineering everything around the model—validation, grounding, deterministic computation, error recovery and intelligent fallbacks—so that AI can be trusted in real-world situations.

**The problem it solves**

Travelers today have access to countless apps for navigation, weather, news, budgeting, translation and trip planning, but these services are often fragmented. When conditions change, travelers must manually connect information from different sources and decide what to do next—creating confusion, wasted time and avoidable safety risks, especially in unfamiliar cities.

Journey360, aligned with SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities, addresses this gap by creating an intelligent, context-aware travel companion that brings critical travel information together and helps travelers make better decisions throughout their journey.

The platform combines AI-powered itinerary planning, real-time safety alerts, local news and alerts, weather conditions, route and navigation assistance, budget awareness, local recommendations, multilingual assistance and adaptive itinerary management. Instead of simply displaying information, Journey360 uses the traveler's location, itinerary, preferences, budget and real-world conditions to understand how a change may affect the journey and recommend an appropriate action.

Its Journey Impact Analyzer further enables travelers to ask “What if?” before changing their plans—such as “What if I leave two hours late?”, “What if I add another destination?” or “What if the weather changes?” The system evaluates the potential impact on time, cost, route, safety and existing activities, helping users understand trade-offs before making a decision.

By bringing these capabilities together, Journey360 aims to make urban travel safer, more accessible, better informed and more resilient, while reducing the need for travelers to constantly switch between disconnected applications.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/af0bf0a781f04be093b572fa14545f54/974ef6d5-a24c-428a-abac-4297926c84a2.png)

**Best Use of Actian Vector Database**

Journey360 uses Actian VectorAI DB as a core intelligence layer rather than as a secondary data store. We use 384-dimensional vector embeddings and cosine similarity to transform unstructured travel intent into meaningful semantic results. User queries such as “misty tea estates with hiking and serene lakes” are converted into embeddings and matched against our indexed destination data to power semantic discovery. More importantly, every AI-generated itinerary can be embedded and indexed in our trips_index and itinerary_places collections, allowing Journey360's RAG-based travel assistant to retrieve relevant past itineraries, places and local context when making recommendations. We also apply vector similarity to our Scam Radar, where submitted fare feedback is semantically matched with existing transit routes to support local price calibration. Thus, Actian VectorAI DB is not simply storing vectors—it connects semantic search, RAG, personalization and community intelligence into a unified travel intelligence layer. This enables Journey360 to move beyond keyword-based travel search toward context-aware, continuously improving travel recommendations.

Problem It Solves

Nizhali addresses the dual challenge of menstrual hygiene accessibility and plastic waste management in rural communities. Many women face difficulties accessing sanitary pads due to limited availability, distance, affordability, and social stigma. At the same time, plastic waste is often improperly discarded and remains underutilized.

Our solution creates an integrated ecosystem where plastic bottles are collected and intelligently detected using AI-based technology, while the system provides access to sanitary pads through automated dispensing machines. The collected plastic can further support sustainable, women-led reuse and recycling initiatives, helping create a circular and potentially self-sustaining model.

Nizhali ultimately aims to improve menstrual hygiene accessibility, promote responsible plastic waste management, and empower rural women through technology and sustainable livelihood opportunities.

**Best Use of Actian Vector Database**

Actian VectorAI aligns directly with the Nizhali Reverse Vending Machine (RVM) architecture by acting as a high-speed, local-first "memory bank" for real-time visual classification. Instead of relying on static, monolithic object-detection models that require hours of GPU retraining whenever new product packaging or bottle brands are introduced, Nizhali offloads semantic recognition directly to Actian VectorAI. Raw camera frames are converted on the fly into 512-dimensional OpenAI CLIP embeddings, allowing Actian to execute Cosine Nearest-Neighbor ($K$-NN) similarity searches over gRPC in under 20 milliseconds. Operating as a lightweight Docker container, Actian VectorAI enables instant multi-modal retrieval across normalized image and text space directly on edge hardware. This empowers Nizhali to ingest new waste items dynamically without model retraining, validating waste types and triggering automated eco-token dispense actions with minimal latency.

> Your goals. Your plan. Smarter investing.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

Building the platform involved several technical challenges as we evolved it from a basic fund-listing application into a **data-driven, goal-based recommendation system**.

### 1. From Alphabetical to Meaningful Recommendations

The initial system returned funds alphabetically. We introduced a **peer-relative scoring engine** that ranks funds using measurable performance and risk metrics.

### 2. Building a Reliable Scoring System

Fund quality is evaluated using multiple metrics, including **CAGR, volatility, maximum drawdown, Sharpe, Sortino, benchmark performance, and consistency**. Missing data is handled through dynamic weight adjustment.

### 3. Separating Score from Data Confidence

We separated **recommendation score** from **data confidence**, ensuring funds with insufficient or unreliable data do not receive misleading recommendations.

### 4. Benchmark Integration

Implementing **Alpha, Beta, R², and rolling consistency** required integrating benchmark data, category mappings, historical observations, and date alignment.

### 5. Tax-Aware Planning

Tax considerations were integrated without allowing tax benefits to distort fund-quality rankings. The system considers factors such as **ELSS, Section 80C, investment horizon, liquidity, and risk**.

### 6. Making Recommendations Interactive

Instead of immediately producing a final allocation, the system is designed to let users **review their strategy and consider alternatives** such as increasing investment, extending the horizon, or adjusting risk.

### 7. Reliable Data Synchronization

We implemented **scheduled data refreshes, database-backed locking, and sync-status tracking** to prevent duplicate synchronization and monitor ingestion failures.

### 8. Testing and Stability

We encountered test-isolation issues caused by shared refresh state. These were resolved with explicit state-reset mechanisms and test fixtures.

### 9. Preserving Existing Functionality

The new recommendation, scoring, tax, and strategy layers were added **modularly without breaking the existing application**, with the full test suite passing after integration.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Choosing the right mutual fund is often confusing because a fund with high historical returns is not necessarily the right choice for a particular financial goal. Users need to consider their goal, investment horizon, risk tolerance, required investment, tax considerations, and the quality of the underlying fund data—all at the same time.

Our platform solves this by turning mutual fund selection into a goal-based, data-driven, and personalized investment planning process.

Users can:

Define a financial goal and target amount.
Specify their investment horizon, risk level, and investment capacity.
Check whether their goal is realistically achievable.
Explore suitable investment strategies and asset allocations.
Understand potential tax-optimization opportunities before finalizing the strategy.
Compare mutual funds using quantitative metrics such as CAGR, volatility, maximum drawdown, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, and benchmark-relative metrics.
Receive funds ranked using a deterministic recommendation score, rather than alphabetical or arbitrary ordering.
See a separate data-confidence level so they understand how reliable the analysis is.
Incorporate personal investment preferences without changing the underlying fund-quality assessment.
Understand why a particular fund or strategy was recommended.

The platform is designed to make the process more transparent:

Financial Goal → Feasibility → Strategy → Tax Review → Preferences → Fund Analysis → Confidence Assessment → Ranking → Personalized Recommendation

The project also includes a mobile application version, allowing users to access the same goal-based investment experience from a mobile device. The APK will be provided through a Google Drive link.
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1O0oQl23zT3-AHnbejrjePueXfSDUqC5w/view?usp=sharing](url)

In short: the platform helps users answer not just "Which mutual funds are available?", but "Which funds are most suitable for my goal, how reliable is that recommendation, and why?"

**Best Use of Render**

Our project is a goal-based mutual fund investment planning platform that combines financial goals, risk profiling, tax awareness, real-time fund data, quantitative analytics, and deterministic fund recommendations.

Render is the production backend layer of the application. We deploy our FastAPI backend on Render and expose the APIs consumed by both our web application and mobile application. The backend handles goal creation, strategy generation, mutual-fund discovery, NAV data ingestion, performance analytics, recommendation scoring, data-confidence evaluation, and tax-aware planning.

A key part of the system is keeping the mutual-fund universe and NAV information updated. We designed a synchronization pipeline with database-backed locking, sync-status tracking, failure handling, and automated scheduled refreshes. Our GitHub Actions workflow can trigger the deployed Render API for scheduled data synchronization, allowing us to keep the data pipeline automated without requiring a continuously running worker.

Render therefore serves as the bridge between our development code and a publicly accessible, continuously usable investment-planning service. It allows the same backend logic to power our web experience and Android mobile application while keeping the architecture modular and scalable.

**Best Use of n8n**

**n8n acts as the automation and intelligence layer of our investment platform.** Instead of putting every notification and AI-related task inside the FastAPI backend, we use n8n to orchestrate these processes independently.

The workflow starts with a **Schedule Trigger**, which periodically initiates the process. n8n then sends an **HTTP request to our FastAPI server**, which provides the latest goal information such as the user's email, goal name, target amount, current amount, and progress. The data is passed to an **AI Agent**, which interprets the goal progress and generates a personalized notification. n8n then checks its **Data Table** to determine whether that milestone has already been notified, preventing duplicate emails. If it is a new milestone, another **AI Agent** prepares the final email content, and **Gmail sends the notification to the user**. Finally, n8n stores the notified milestone in the Data Table.

### In simple terms:

**FastAPI → provides the data**
**n8n → manages the workflow**
**AI Agents → add intelligence and personalization**
**Gmail → communicates with the user**
**Data Table → prevents duplicate notifications**

This approach keeps the main application clean while allowing us to **automate, personalize, and extend notification workflows without changing the core FastAPI application every time.**

**Best Use of Gemini API**

Our project uses the Gemini API as an intelligent decision and communication layer rather than just a chatbot. Gemini analyzes users’ financial goals and progress data, identifies meaningful milestone events, and generates personalized, motivating notifications based on each user’s situation. It is integrated into our n8n automation workflow, where Gemini processes the data received from our FastAPI backend and produces structured email content such as the subject and message. This allows our application to automatically transform raw financial data into human-friendly, personalized guidance, demonstrating a practical use of generative AI in financial goal management.

> From where do I start to we are ready to demo

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Students often struggle to find the right teammates for hackathons and projects because they don't know who has complementary skills, interests, or roles. Elevora solves this by intelligently matching students based on their skills, interests, preferred roles, and project/hackathon interests, using a swipe-based interface to make team formation quick and intuitive.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into
Frontend–backend connectivity: Initially, the deployed frontend was trying to connect to localhost, which only works on the developer's computer and caused network errors for the deployed website.
Backend deployment: We had to deploy the FastAPI backend separately so the frontend could communicate with a publicly accessible API.
Authentication integration: Connecting the login/signup flow with the FastAPI authentication endpoints and JWT-based authentication required careful handling of tokens and user IDs.
Database integration: We integrated the real student database with the team-matching system instead of relying on mock student data.
Matching algorithm: Designing a deterministic compatibility algorithm required combining shared skills, interests, hackathon interests, complementary roles, complementary skills, and college information.
Swipe persistence: We initially had swipe actions only on the frontend, then implemented backend persistence so Interested/Pass actions are stored and previously swiped students are excluded.
Pagination: The matching system had to support loading recommendations continuously instead of being limited to the first 10 students.
Authentication & authorization: We added checks to prevent users from accessing another student's recommendations or submitting swipes on behalf of another user.
Testing and deployment: Backend tests passed successfully, while frontend deployment required additional debugging because the local and deployed environments behaved differently.
Time constraints: Integrating and testing the complete system close to the submission deadline required prioritizing the core login, dashboard, database, and student-team matching functionality.

### trevo
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trevo-59a1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/arneshb07/trevo) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co)

> Smarter Cash Flow Decisions

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was making the frontend, backend, database, and decision engine work together as one system.
Initially, the frontend could display simulated information, but connecting it to the actual backend meant that the application had to deal with real API responses, database state, and decisions generated by the optimization engine.
1. Connecting the frontend to the real decision engine
The frontend was originally designed around mock data. We had to replace that approach with calls to the actual FastAPI backend.
This required making sure that the data returned by the backend matched what the frontend expected.
We solved this by introducing adapters between the backend responses and the frontend's view models. This allowed us to keep the frontend structure while connecting it to the real decision engine.
2. Database initialization problem
We encountered a particularly important issue with the SQLite database.
The backend was running correctly and the health endpoint returned:
200 OK
However, requesting the actual business state returned:
500 Internal Server Error
The reason was that the SQLite database file existed, but it was empty or did not contain the required tables.
The backend then tried to access the business_state table, which did not exist.
We diagnosed this by inspecting the database itself rather than assuming that the API code was broken.
The solution was to restore the valid baseline database and add database initialization safeguards so that the backend can create the required tables and seed the baseline data when necessary.
3. Making the application reproducible
This database issue exposed a larger problem.
If the application depends on a local trevo.db file, simply cloning the GitHub repository on another computer may not be enough to run the application correctly.
We therefore started moving toward an environment based architecture where configuration and database connections are controlled through environment variables.
This is important for eventual deployment because the production application should not depend on a database file sitting inside the GitHub repository.
4. Running the backend and frontend together
We also encountered issues with development servers already occupying ports.
For example, when another Vite process was already running, starting the frontend again caused Vite to automatically move from port 5173 to 5174.
Similarly, Uvicorn sometimes reported:
[WinError 10048]
Only one usage of each socket address is normally permitted
This happened because another backend process was already using port 8000.
We diagnosed these issues using Windows networking commands such as netstat and process inspection, then managed the running processes before starting the server again.
5. Dependency and environment problems
The backend initially failed because a required Python package was not installed in the active environment.
The error was:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dotenv'
The important lesson was that having Python installed is not enough. The project needs a clearly defined environment containing all of its dependencies.
We addressed this by using a project virtual environment and maintaining dependency files so that the backend can be installed consistently.
6. Making the financial decisions reliable
The most important technical challenge is not simply calculating a cash balance. TREVO needs to consider multiple financial decisions at the same time.
For example, delaying one payment may preserve cash today but create another problem later. Borrowing money may solve an immediate shortage but introduce financing costs.
The decision engine therefore evaluates these competing possibilities and generates a joint decision plan rather than treating every payment as an isolated problem.
This is where the optimization engine becomes important. It allows TREVO to search through possible decisions and select a plan that balances cash availability, obligations, financing, and the consequences of different actions.
7. Testing the complete system
Another challenge was that a successful backend startup does not necessarily mean that the application works.
We therefore moved toward testing the system endpoint by endpoint.

**The problem it solves**

Small businesses often have enough money to operate, but the timing of when money comes in and goes out creates problems. An invoice may be delayed, a supplier payment may be due earlier than expected, or an important expense may suddenly appear. In these situations, simply looking at the current bank balance is not enough.

TREVO helps businesses decide what to do with their money before a cash flow problem becomes a crisis.
It looks at the business's available cash, upcoming payments, expected customer payments, financial obligations, and available financing options. It then evaluates possible actions and recommends a practical decision.
Instead of asking:
"Do we have enough money today?"

TREVO helps answer:
"Given everything that is expected to happen, what should we do now to keep the business financially safe?"

People can use TREVO to:
- Plan upcoming cash flow: See how current decisions may affect the business over the coming days.
- Prioritize payments: Identify which payments should be made first when available cash is limited.
- Handle delayed customer payments: Understand how a late invoice can affect the rest of the business.
- Compare financing options: Determine when using available financing may be better than delaying an important payment.
- Respond to unexpected events: Simulate situations such as a customer payment being delayed and immediately see how the recommended plan changes.
- Understand why a decision was made: TREVO does not just provide a recommendation. It shows the reasoning behind the decision, making the system easier to trust and verify.
- Explore alternative decisions: Users can examine what would happen if a different action were taken instead of simply accepting the first recommendation.
- Keep a history of decisions: Previous decisions and events can be recorded so that users can understand how the financial situation evolved.
- Use voice explanations: The system can explain financial decisions through voice, making the information easier to consume for users who may not want to read a detailed financial analysis.
The main idea is to turn a complicated cash flow planning problem into something a business owner or financial manager can understand, simulate, and act on.

TREVO is therefore not simply a dashboard showing financial numbers. It is designed as a decision support system that connects the numbers to an actual recommended action.

### AssestFlowAI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/assestflowai-548c) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://agent-6a91dfba3a09cc283964ba98--assetflow-ai.netlify.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Er5Saq2ekd8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co)

> Smarter Financing. Every Stage. Every Asset.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Supply-chain businesses often create economic value long before they receive cash, but traditional working-capital financing is usually tied to specific milestones such as purchase orders, invoices, or receivables. This creates a financing gap while goods are being produced, stored, transported, and delivered.

AssetFlow AI solves this by creating a financial layer that travels with the physical asset throughout its entire supply-chain lifecycle — from Purchase Order → Raw Material → Production → Finished Goods → Shipment → Warehouse → Delivery → Invoice → Receivable → Cash Realisation.

Instead of treating financing as a one-time decision, the platform continuously:

Tracks the asset's physical, financial, and contractual state
Combines data from ERP, warehouse, logistics, invoices, telemetry, and financial sources
Detects and reconciles conflicting information
Evaluates the asset's value and risk
Determines whether financing is needed and how much can safely be provided
Selects the most suitable financing instrument
Reassesses financing automatically when events such as shipment delays, inventory deterioration, or buyer-risk changes occur
Tracks existing exposure to prevent duplicate financing and over-leverage
Transitions, reduces, refinances, or settles financing as the asset progresses
Provides explainable decisions, alerts, evidence, and an audit trail
What people can use it for

For suppliers/businesses:
Get working-capital financing aligned with the actual stage and value of goods, rather than waiting until an invoice or receivable exists.

For lenders/financing providers:
See the underlying asset, its current condition, existing financing exposure, risk, and supporting evidence before making a financing decision.

For supply-chain operators:
Identify delays, conflicts, and exceptions early and understand how they affect financing.

For risk/credit teams:
Automatically reassess exposure when the underlying asset or supply-chain conditions change.

Why it makes the process safer

The platform does not simply increase financing when an asset has value. Low data confidence, conflicting sources, high risk, or excessive existing exposure can reduce financing capacity or trigger review.

For example, if a shipment is delayed, the system can detect the event, update the asset state, reassess risk and value, and automatically change the financing recommendation rather than continuing with an outdated decision.

In one sentence:

AssetFlow AI turns supply-chain assets into continuously monitored, financeable economic objects, enabling working-capital decisions to evolve safely as the physical asset moves toward cash realisation.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest challenges was **keeping the asset lifecycle, data reconciliation, risk assessment, and financing decisions synchronized**. A change in one part of the supply chain could affect the asset's value, risk, financing capacity, and recommended financing instrument.

We also faced difficulties when **different simulated data sources disagreed**. For example, ERP, warehouse, and telemetry data could report different production or inventory states. Simply choosing one source could lead to an unsafe financing decision.

We addressed this by building a **reconciliation layer** that preserves the original source evidence, detects conflicts, assigns confidence, and produces a canonical state. Material conflicts then trigger a reassessment of risk and financing.

Another hurdle was ensuring that AI-generated decisions remained **consistent and explainable**. Instead of allowing the AI to directly calculate financial amounts, we kept critical financing and risk calculations deterministic and used AI primarily for orchestration and explanation.

Finally, integrating multiple modules in a hackathon environment was challenging. We solved this with a **contract-first approach**, keeping the API, lifecycle states, database entities, and event definitions consistent across the team. This allowed the frontend, backend, AI, and data components to be developed in parallel without breaking each other's work.

The result is a prototype where a single event—such as a shipment delay or data conflict—can flow through the system, update the asset state, reassess risk, recalculate financing, generate an alert, and record the decision for audit.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ares-autonomous-risk-and-execution-security-c615) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/SRIKUMARAN2008/ARES---AUTONOMOUS-RISK-EXECUTION-SECURITY-) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Afh7p1I4H4k) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co)

> ARES -  Where AI Acts, Security Decides 🔥

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Modern AI agents can independently browse the web, execute commands, access APIs, and interact with sensitive systems—but this autonomy also creates new security risks. ARES - Autonomous Risk & Execution Security provides a security layer that evaluates AI-generated actions before they are executed , identifying dangerous, suspicious, or policy-violating behavior.

People can use ARES to safely deploy and test autonomous AI agents without giving them unrestricted access to systems. It analyzes proposed actions, detects risks such as malicious commands, unauthorized access, data exfiltration, destructive operations, and prompt-injection-driven behavior, then assigns a risk level and can block or allow the execution.

ARES makes existing AI-agent workflows safer, more transparent, and easier to control by providing real-time risk assessment, explainable security decisions, execution monitoring, and replay capabilities. Instead of blindly trusting an AI agent, developers and organizations can see what the agent wants to do, why it may be dangerous, and whether it should be allowed to proceed.

In short, ARES acts as a security checkpoint between autonomous AI decisions and real-world execution, helping organizations harness AI autonomy without sacrificing control or safety.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

One of our biggest challenges was designing ARES to make security decisions in real time without slowing down autonomous AI agents. The system needed to analyze an AI-generated action, identify potential threats, assign a risk score, and decide whether to allow or block it while keeping the execution flow fast and reliable.

Another major hurdle was handling ambiguous or context-dependent actions. A command that is harmless in one situation can be dangerous in another—for example, modifying a file may be legitimate during development but risky when performed on a protected system. We solved this by combining action analysis, contextual risk scoring, policy checks, and execution monitoring rather than relying on simple keyword-based detection.

We also encountered challenges around prompt injection and malicious instructions hidden inside seemingly legitimate tasks. To address this, ARES separates the agent's intent from the actual action being executed and evaluates the action independently before allowing it to reach the execution layer.

Finally, building a useful replay and audit mechanism required us to capture enough information about each decision without overwhelming the system with unnecessary data. We designed a structured event trail that records the action, risk assessment, security decision, and execution outcome, making incidents easier to understand, debug, and reproduce.

These challenges helped shape ARES into more than just a threat detector—it became a real-time security control layer for autonomous AI execution.

Team **Obsidian** -- Ravishankar K K, Harihaarasudan S, SRIKUMARAN V

### Intent-Mesh
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/intentmesh-4dfd) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mohamed-anas-j/intent-mesh) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co)

> Stop crossing bridges. Start stating intents.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional cross-chain swaps force users to rely on bridges, which act as centralized honeypots and are highly vulnerable to hacks-accounting for roughly 69% of all stolen crypto value in 2022. Furthermore, the current model places the entire execution burden on the user: they must research bridges, select specific liquidity pools, manage slippage, and pay upfront gas fees. Bridges also lack competitive pressure, executing trades at whatever price they prefer.  

**Intent-Mesh** solves this by completely replacing the bridge model with a competitive marketplace for execution. Instead of specifying how to route a trade, users simply sign a gasless "intent" stating their desired outcome and minimum acceptable floor. Independent bots (solvers) then compete in a sealed-bid auction to fulfill that order using their own capital across chains. You get better prices through actual market competition, and your money never sits in a vulnerable bridge vault.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our core philosophy was that every trust assumption had to be converted into a mathematical or economic bond. This presented a few major technical hurdles:

* **Closing the "Free Option":** A major challenge in intent systems is solvers winning an auction but walking away if market conditions turn against them. We overcame this by implementing a strict bonded system with micro-timeouts (T_fill). If a solver ghosts, the smart contract automatically slashes their bond and routes the penalty directly to the user as compensation.

* **On-Chain Scoring Complexity:** We wanted to rank solvers not just on price, but on execution speed, reliability, and route toxicity (Loss-Versus-Rebalancing). Because this formula had to be independently verifiable on-chain during a dispute, we couldn't use standard floats. We had to build a custom ScoreLib using strict integer fixed-point math (WAD = 1e18) that mirrors exactly between our TypeScript backend and Solidity contracts.

* **The Trusted Coordinator Problem:** Running an off-chain auction usually requires trusting the coordinator to pick the actual winner. We solved this by forcing the coordinator to publish a fully signed, recomputable transcript containing every bid's commitment hash. If the coordinator drops a bid or rigs the math, anyone can prove it on-chain and slash the coordinator's bond.

Team **IGNITE** -- Piraveen G, Arunmozhivarman AR

### Finova
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finova-4195) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/srisaidhakshini/csi-origins) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co)

> Autonomous Financial Intelligence for the Variable

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Multi-Channel Deduplication & Asynchronous Transaction Collision
The Challenge: When a user pays an invoice, the event is emitted almost simultaneously across multiple channels—an instant transactional SMS from the bank, a payment confirmation email via Gmail OAuth, and later a scanned paper receipt.
How We Solved It: We engineered a deterministic Fuzzy Fingerprinting Engine

2. Preventing LLM Hallucinations in Financial Balance Calculations
The Challenge: Early prototypes attempted to pass the user's raw transaction history to an LLM to "calculate" if upcoming bills would bounce. 
How We Solved It: We decoupled financial computation from natural language explanation. All cashflow dependencies and cascade traversals are modeled as a Causal State DAG in PostgreSQL.

**The problem it solves**

Modern personal finance applications are designed around a predictable 30-day corporate paycheck cycle. However, freelancers, gig workers, creators, and independent contractors experience asymmetrical, irregular cashflows. Their financial signals are heavily fragmented across:

- Transactional bank SMS alerts
- Client payment emails and PDF invoices
- Platform payout notifications (Upwork, Stripe, Razorpay)
- Physical utility bills and rent slips

The Limitations of Existing Tools
Traditional budgeting tools operate in the rearview mirror—they log transactions after they occur and visualize historical spending pie charts. They fail to answer three mission-critical questions for variable-income earners:

Cascade Risks: “If Client A delays their payment by 8 days, which specific bills or loan EMIs will bounce next week?”
Deficit Foresight: “What will be my exact cash shortfall on the 15th of the month?”
Proactive Mitigation: “What concrete, prioritized action should I take right now to prevent default?”

2. What People Can Use It For
Finova is an Autonomous Financial Intelligence Platform that maps income dependencies and predicts liquidity shortfalls before they happen. Users can use Finova for:

Automated Multi-Channel Financial Syncing:

- Ingest bank SMS notifications, Gmail invoices/receipts via OAuth, and physical bills/receipts via real-time Gemini Vision Camera OCR.

- Eliminates manual bookkeeping and duplicate transaction tracking.
Causal Dependency Mapping & Simulation:

Visualizes finances as a Causal State Graph (Inflows → Liquid Buffers → Outflows like Rent, EMIs, and SIPs).
Simulates "what-if" scenarios (e.g., invoice payment delays or emergency expenses) to observe downstream effects.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/autochain-automated-multi-agent-market-system-1b83) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Amirtha655/BUGCREW) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zcdRNfdL3bE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co)

> Automated Multi - Agent Market System

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSOC](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSOC-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLAlchemy](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLAlchemy-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI is good at deciding but hard to trust with consequences — especially
money. Rule-based trading bots can't adapt when conditions change;
LLM-driven ones can't be audited or constrained. Meridian is an autonomous
trading desk built on one rule: The AI proposes, deterministic code
decides. It watches equities, currencies and commodities, forms its own
view and executes without being told to — but every trade must first clear
an independent risk check written in plain code the AI cannot argue with or
bypass. It grades its own results and measurably reins itself in after a
losing run, and explains each decision in plain English rather than jargon.
The result is automation you can actually verify, tested safely against
simulated markets with no real money at risk.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our biggest bug was one that looked like it was working. The system is meant
to learn from its results, but it grew relentlessly more timid until it
stopped trading entirely — because we were marking "HOLD" decisions, where
no trade was ever placed, as completed trades worth ₹0. The learning layer
counted every one as a loss, so the system punished itself for correctly
deciding not to trade, and the tighter it got, the more HOLDs it produced: a
loop it could never escape, since recovering needed winning trades it was no
longer allowed to place. Marking non-executed decisions `SKIPPED` instead
fixed it. We also lost time to timestamps that disagreed across pages by
exactly 5.5 hours (naive UTC serialised without an offset, so browsers read
it as local time), and to our Risk Guardian's "reduce" verdict rarely
firing in demos. That last one was tempting to fix by tuning the scoring
until it looked better — we didn't, since untouched numbers are the whole
claim, and instead wrote a scenario that hits the concentration limit
honestly. The through-line: three of these produced perfectly reasonable
looking output, so "it ran without errors" proved almost nothing.

### Trace(Autonomous AI Task Exchange)
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/traceautonomous-ai-transfer-exchange-abe4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/souravgowdilyan/trace.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Origins-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://origins.devfolio.co)

> A marketplace where AI agents hire each other.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## AI agents can work. They can't get paid.

Autonomous agents already do real digital work — summarising, translating,
labelling, benchmarking, refactoring code. What they can't do is **transact**.

A human still has to hand out the task, judge whether the work is good
enough, and release the money. That human is the bottleneck stopping agents
from being genuine economic participants rather than tools waiting on
approval.

And the hard part isn't payments. It's **trust**. In an agent-to-agent
transaction, neither side can be assumed honest:

- Was the work actually done correctly?
- How do you compare competing submissions fairly?
- What discourages an agent from submitting rubbish?
- What happens when there's a genuine disagreement?

## What TRACE does

A marketplace where agents hire each other and settle payments
automatically — with the amount of verification scaling to how risky each
task is.

An agent posts a task and the payment locks into escrow immediately. Other
agents discover it by capability, and claim it by putting down a **stake** —
their own money at risk. They submit the work, and other agents act as
judges, each writing an actual explanation of its verdict rather than
returning a score.

Pass, and escrow releases automatically. Fail, and the stake is slashed and
reputation drops — which locks that agent out of higher-value tasks. Nobody
bans anyone; the economics do it.

## The idea we're most proud of

**Verification effort isn't a fixed rule — it's a consequence.**

The system scores each task on the money at stake, the worker's track
record, and how ambiguous the criteria are. That score decides how many
independent opinions to gather.

| Task | Bounty | Risk | Judges called |
|---|---|---|---|
| Summarise an investor call | $120 | low | 1 |
| Refactor an auth module | $400 | medium | 2 |
| Localise a manual, 3 languages | $900 | high | 4 |

Nobody wrote a rule saying "expensive tasks get four judges." It falls out
of the scoring.

We also model every task as a small graph, which means **competition and
collaboration are the same mechanism** — several agents against one node is
a race, one agent per node is a split job. Not two features. One structure.

And when the judges genuinely can't agree, that single piece of work freezes
for human review. Only that piece. Everything else settles and the
marketplace keeps running.

> Autonomy with Financial Guardrails

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Dynamic Database Hash-Chain Integrity: Maintaining a sequential SHA-256 chain in a SQLite database was challenging when dealing with dynamic sandbox simulations. Simulating transaction tampering or resetting data could easily corrupt live database logs. We overcame this by separating the simulation audit verification checks—running tamper checks on isolated in-memory copies of the ledger state—and implementing strict database locks to prevent race conditions during block updates.
LLM Safety Pipeline Robustness: Depending purely on cloud LLMs (like Groq) for prompt analysis risks complete gateway failure during API rate-limits or network timeouts. We engineered a dual-pipeline approach using Groq server-side for detailed JSON-schema validated analysis combined with a robust local deterministic regex fallback engine. If the external API key is missing or fails, the gateway gracefully falls back to local parsing without failing open.
Deterministic Anomaly Baselines: Dynamic transactions would naturally shift the baseline payment averages, making sandbox tests like Scenario B (Amount Anomaly) non-deterministic over time. We solved this by establishing a rigid historical average baseline of ₹1,800 via seeded data, ensuring simulations evaluate consistently against historical limits.

**The problem it solves**

In a world powered by autonomous AI agents, standard API keys and cryptographic credentials are no longer enough. An agent might initiate a transaction that is technically valid and correctly signed, but contextually catastrophic—such as transfer limits being exceeded, capital sent to unverified external protocols, or the agent falling victim to prompt injection or behavioral overrides.

AgentShield acts as a risk-aware security gateway and control dashboard sitting directly between your autonomous financial agents and your actual assets.

Key Use Cases & Safety Features:

Contextual Risk Engine: Automatically scores proposed transactions based on agent roles, historical transaction baselines, daily spend velocity, and asset exposure limits.
Prompt Injection Protection: Scans natural-language instructions dynamically for urgency manipulation, secrecy, policy-bypass keywords, or conflicting developer roles before they are sent to the execution layer.
Tamper-Evident Ledgering: Stores all gateway decisions and security assessments in an immutable local SHA-256 cryptographic hash-chain. Any backend database tampering is immediately caught by the dashboard.
Policy Version Control: Permits granular configuration of per-agent allowances. Updating policy limits preserves previous policy versions and registers the change in the audit chain.
Web3 Security Anchoring: Optionally anchors audit hash chains to EVM-compatible testnets via Solidity smart contracts, ensuring public verifiability of high-risk actions.

> An intent-aware security control plane that preven

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLAlchemy](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLAlchemy-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem: When an AI Agent Is Compromised, Who Stops the Transaction?

Autonomous financial agents can now interpret instructions and initiate real-world actions. But traditional security systems mostly answer one question:

**“Is this agent allowed to act?”**

FluxLedger asks the more important question:

**“Is this specific action actually consistent with what the agent was authorized to do?”**

An agent can have valid credentials, access to a legitimate payment tool, and still be manipulated into sending money to the wrong recipient, exceeding its spending authority, bypassing policy, or following a malicious prompt injection.

This creates a critical security gap between **agent authorization and actual execution**.

### Our Solution

**FluxLedger is an Intent-Aware Runtime Control Plane for Autonomous Financial Agents.**

Instead of blindly trusting an agent's proposed transaction, FluxLedger places a security decision layer between the agent and the financial execution system.

Every proposed action is evaluated against:

- **Identity** — Who is the agent?
- **Authorization** — What tools and spending limits does it have?
- **Intent** — Does the action match its pre-authorized intent contract?
- **Behavior** — Does it deviate from expected behavior?
- **Context** — Is the execution environment normal?
- **Counterparty** — Who is receiving the money?
- **Threat** — Is the action showing prompt injection or goal hijacking?
- **Policy** — Does it violate enterprise rules?

These signals are combined into an explainable risk decision:

**APPROVE → CONSTRAIN → BLOCK**

The result is a security model where autonomous agents can move fast when they are behaving normally, while high-risk or adversarial actions lose their autonomy before financial execution.

**We are not securing the AI after the transaction. We are controlling the transaction before it happens.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Faced

### 1. The hardest problem: defining what “safe” actually means

A financial action cannot be judged by a single security signal.

An agent may be authenticated but use the wrong tool.  
It may use the correct tool but exceed its authorized amount.  
It may stay within the amount but redirect the payment to an unknown counterparty.  
It may satisfy the technical permissions while being triggered by a malicious instruction.

We therefore designed FluxLedger as **eight independent security evaluators** rather than one monolithic risk check.

### 2. Turning human intent into machine-verifiable boundaries

Natural-language authorization is too ambiguous for high-impact financial actions.

We introduced **Intent Contracts** that convert authorization into explicit constraints: purpose, approved counterparties, maximum amount, currency, allowed tools, validity window and approval threshold.

The proposed transaction is then compared against these constraints before execution.

### 3. Detecting attacks that look legitimate at the infrastructure layer

The most interesting attacks are not necessarily unauthorized logins.

Our Attack Lab tests cases where the agent itself is manipulated:

**Legitimate payment → APPROVE**

**High-value payment → CONSTRAIN**

**Prompt injection + amount escalation + counterparty substitution → BLOCK**

This forced us to build consequence-aware threat detection rather than relying only on authentication.

### 4. Making security decisions explainable

A simple “BLOCKED” message is not sufficient for an enterprise security system.

FluxLedger produces a decision record containing the risk score, intent alignment, evaluator breakdown, violated policies, detected threats and the reasoning behind the final decision.

This makes the system auditable rather than a black-box security filter.

### 5. Making the prototype survive real deployment

We validated the system beyond localhost.

The backend was deployed as a FastAPI service and the control-plane UI as a Next.js application. We encountered and resolved production environment/CORS issues during deployment, then verified the deployed health endpoint and end-to-end frontend/backend communication.

The final repository was validated with **29 automated tests, a red-team audit, and a successful production frontend build.**

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an autonomous financial decision system for SMEs within a 24-hour hackathon came with several challenges:

**Balancing multiple financial factors**: A payment decision cannot depend only on available cash. We had to consider payment deadlines, discounts, penalties, future obligations, receivables and financing costs together, as required by the problem statement.

**Handling uncertain future payments**: Customer payments may be delayed, so our system needed to support what-if scenarios instead of assuming every expected payment arrives on time.

**Making complex financial decisions understandable**: We designed the recommendations in simple language so that an SME owner without a finance background can understand what to do and why.

**Re-optimizing when conditions change**: A major challenge was making the simulator respond when variables such as customer delays or emergency expenses change. The system recalculates the projected cash balance and reserve buffer rather than relying on a fixed recommendation.

**The problem it solves**

Small and medium-sized businesses often have limited cash but many competing financial needs—supplier payments, customer receivables, salaries, emergencies, discounts, penalties, and financing. It is difficult for an SME owner to know whether to pay now, wait, borrow, or keep cash for future needs.

FlowGuard AI solves this by acting as an AI financial co-pilot for SMEs. It analyzes current cash, upcoming payments, expected customer receipts, supplier deadlines, discounts, penalties, financing costs, and future obligations to recommend the best use of available money.

It also lets businesses simulate “what-if” situations, such as delayed customer payments or unexpected expenses, and see how their future cash position and recommended strategy would change.

> Sense the Market. Think Ahead. Decide Autonomously

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sketch](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sketch-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![SPRINGBOOT](https://img.shields.io/badge/SPRINGBOOT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Eleven Labs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Eleven%20Labs-333333?style=flat-square) ![Stich](https://img.shields.io/badge/Stich-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Financial markets generate enormous amounts of information every second, making it difficult for traders to analyze everything, react quickly, and manage risk consistently.
Most existing automated trading systems focus heavily on  speed or prediction, while many AI-based solutions simply provide recommendations without having a robust mechanism to control what happens after the recommendation is made.

This creates three major problems:
Information overload: Market data, technical indicators, news, and sentiment are difficult to evaluate simultaneously.
Slow and inconsistent decisions: Human traders can miss opportunities or make emotionally driven decisions during volatile conditions.
Unsafe automation: Giving a single AI model direct control over financial actions can create unacceptable risks when predictions are wrong.

CORTEX addresses this by separating intelligence from authority. Multiple specialized agents analyze the market and reach a consensus, but an independent risk layer has the final power to approve or veto the proposed action.

This allows us to move toward  controlled autonomous trading rather than blindly automated trading.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest challenges was figuring out  how to make multiple AI agents work together reliably instead of simply having several models generate independent answers. We had to design a clear communication and consensus mechanism so that every agent contributed meaningful information to the final decision.

Another challenge was  risk management. We didn't want the same AI system that generates a trading decision to also have unlimited authority to execute it. This led us to design the Risk-Veto Circuit Breaker, creating a separate safety layer between AI reasoning and execution.

We also had to deal with the challenge of latency. In financial systems, a good decision that arrives too late can be useless. We therefore focused on keeping the decision pipeline lightweight and efficient, from data ingestion through consensus, risk validation, allocation, and execution.

Finally, integrating different technologies — including AI models, backend services, real-time data, voice interaction, and the execution layer — required us to think carefully about how the components communicate and remain synchronized.

These challenges helped shape CORTEX into more than an AI prototype. They pushed us toward building a system where intelligence, autonomy, speed, and safety have to work together.

> “Detect. Defend. Protect Every Payment.”

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL server](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL%20server-333333?style=flat-square) ![swagger](https://img.shields.io/badge/swagger-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was designing the system for **real-time detection and response** rather than performing fraud analysis after transactions were completed.

We had to coordinate multiple components: event ingestion, AI-based risk scoring, behavioral signals, graph analysis, response decisions, and the live security dashboard. Keeping these components synchronized while maintaining a fast response path required careful separation between the detection engine and response orchestration layer.

Another challenge was detecting **mule-transfer behavior**, where individual transactions may appear legitimate when viewed independently but become suspicious when the relationships between multiple accounts and transactions are considered. We addressed this using graph-based analysis to identify suspicious transaction relationships and patterns.

We also faced the challenge of balancing **security sensitivity with false positives**. A system that blocks every unusual transaction would create a poor user experience. Instead, CashGuard uses graded risk responses so lower-risk anomalies can trigger additional verification while higher-risk activity can be escalated or temporarily held.

Finally, integrating AI outputs into an actionable security workflow was challenging. We focused on making the AI a decision-support component of a larger real-time defense pipeline rather than treating a model prediction as the final decision.

**The problem it solves**

CashGuard is an AI-powered real-time financial security platform designed to detect and respond to suspicious digital-payment activity before it becomes a major financial loss.

Traditional fraud detection often relies heavily on static rules such as transaction amount, location, or frequency. These approaches can miss coordinated attacks and evolving fraud patterns such as account takeover, mule-account transfers, and abnormal transaction chains.

CashGuard addresses this by combining multiple signals in real time:

* **Behavioral analysis** to identify unusual login and transaction patterns.
* **Device and session intelligence** to detect suspicious changes in user behavior and devices.
* **AI-based anomaly detection** to identify transactions that deviate from normal activity.
* **Graph-based analysis** to uncover suspicious relationships and money-flow patterns between accounts.
* **Real-time risk scoring** to prioritize potentially fraudulent activity.
* **Automated response orchestration** to trigger appropriate actions based on risk, such as step-up verification, temporary transaction holds, or security alerts.
* **Live case monitoring and audit trails** so security teams can understand what happened and why a response was triggered.

The goal is not simply to flag fraud after it happens, but to move toward **real-time, explainable, adaptive financial defense** where suspicious activity can be detected and acted upon within the same user session.
