![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The real problem with tools like LocusFounder is that they make launching a business too easy, which leaves the human owner completely overwhelmed. 

If you use an AI agent to spin up three different shops at once, you suddenly have money moving in three different directions. You have tech bills, product costs, and marketing expenses scattered everywhere. You end up jumping between browser tabs, staring at raw code logs, and guessing your actual profit. You can't even answer the most basic question: "Did I actually make money today, or am I going broke?"

This project solves that exact human headache. It is a simple, visual command center that pulls all the confusing data from your different AI storefronts and translates it into clear, honest numbers on a single dark-mode screen. It does the messy financial math for you automatically—factoring in specific ad costs and product margins—so you can see exactly how much cash is hitting your bank account at a single glance. It turns autonomous machine chaos into peace of mind for the founder.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The Serverless Cold-Start Problem (Data Resetting)
Because this application is deployed as a serverless application on Vercel, standard global variables in Node.js tend to completely wipe out and reset whenever the server goes idle or experiences a "cold start." This meant our 900+ historical seed transactions would vanish randomly. I solved this by securely binding the in-memory ledger array directly to the Node.js global context object, forcing the database state to persist seamlessly across hot reloads and live API requests.

2. Heavy Library Bloat vs. Performance
I wanted the dashboard charts to look incredibly smooth and premium, but standard React graphing libraries are heavily bloated, slow down page load speeds, and are notoriously frustrating to style in dark mode. To keep the application lightning-fast, I chose to avoid external charting libraries entirely. Instead, I manually programmed custom mathematical coordinate calculators that map the transaction data streams straight into raw, native browser SVG vector paths. This kept the page performance close to 100% while allowing for instant fluid animations when switching storefront views.

3. Handling "Division by Zero" Crashes
When an operator switches to a brand-new storefront tenant that has zero transactions recorded yet, standard financial formulas will try to divide by zero, resulting in "NaN" (Not a Number) errors that can instantly crash the entire user interface. I had to write strict defensive validation layers across all mathematical data hooks to guarantee that if a store has zero sales, the cards gracefully fall back to displaying 0% or $0 rather than breaking the UI.

**Using LocusFounder to Build a Business!**

This project is built explicitly to support and scale businesses created via LocusFounder. 

Instead of just launching a single standalone storefront, my project serves as an Executive Portfolio Console designed for an operator who uses LocusFounder to run multiple autonomous business lines simultaneously (such as e-commerce, digital products, and consulting services). 

It maps directly into the track by listening to live transaction streams from the Locus Checkout engine via a secure serverless webhook (`/api/locus-ledger`). It automatically aggregates the data, calculates business-specific product costs (COGS) and marketing channel spend (like Google Ads vs. Apollo cold email costs), and turns raw machine logs into a single, beautifully visualized screen. It directly solves the administrative mess of running multiple AI-driven businesses, giving the human owner total financial clarity over their entire Locus portfolio at a single glance.

### agentleash
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agentleash-82c4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/MukundaKatta/agentleash) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/agentleash/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Locus'%20Paygentic%20Hackathon%20--%20#4-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://paygentic-week4.devfolio.co)

> Python safety harness for AI agents that touch mon

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents that touch money (pay-per-API calls, autonomous purchases, on-chain bots) are starting to ship in production, but the safety primitives haven't caught up. A small bug or a malicious prompt can drain a Stripe key, fan out unbounded paid LLM calls, or post to a wrong endpoint before anyone notices.

agentleash is a single Python context manager that puts a leash on each agent run:

- USD-per-run + per-call caps (token-budget-py under the hood; agent halts cleanly when cap hits)
- Egress allowlist (wildcard hostnames; e.g. *.stripe.com only)
- Optional tool-arg JSON Schema gate so bad args never reach the side-effectful function
- Append-only JSONL audit log; tool args are sha256-hashed by default so PII / secrets never land on disk

It's the dollars-side companion to birddog (egress side, also today) and pairs with agentvet / agentsnap / agenttrace.

**Challenges we ran into**

Three things ate the most time.

1. **token-budget-py API mismatch.** Tests kept failing on `BudgetPool` having no `usd_used` attribute. Fix was calling `.snapshot().usd_used` instead of reading state directly. Once I read the lib's source the API was obvious; lesson was to drop into the dep's code earlier, not later.

2. **PII in audit logs.** First version dumped tool args verbatim into the JSONL, which means a Stripe customer ID or a personal email lands in plaintext on disk. Switched to sha256-hashing each arg by default so the audit trail still proves a call happened without leaking content.

3. **Where to halt.** A naive cap check at the start of `tool()` misses the fact that the LLM has already produced output costing tokens. Moved the budget check to after the LLM call returns but before the side-effectful tool runs, so the agent halts at the latest safe point - the network/payment side-effect doesn't happen, but you don't lose the LLM output you already paid for.

**Using LocusFounder to Build a Business!**

Paygentic agents are LLM-driven workers that move money - the second a model hallucinates a billing endpoint or fans out a paid loop, the bill goes up fast. agentleash is the Python guardrail that sits inside the agent run: every tool call goes through usd_cap + call_cap + egress allowlist + optional JSON Schema arg gate, and lands in an append-only audit log (tool args sha256-hashed, no PII). It's the production safety primitive a LocusFounder-built paygentic business needs day one, not month six.

> get a quote from prediction market for your asset

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional insurance is slow, opaque, and limited to standardized products. Anyone who wants to hedge a specific real-world risk — a missed flight, a bad harvest, a geopolitical event, a volatile crypto price — has no easy way to do it.

Insurance broker solves this by turning Polymarket's deep prediction-market liquidity into an instant, chat-driven hedging desk:

- **Describe your risk in plain language.** The LLM finds the right Polymarket market for your event.
- **Get a precise quote.** The broker computes the correct YES/NO position size against your dollar exposure, including expected ROI and cost.
- **Place the trade in one click.** After explicit confirmation, it submits the on-chain order through the Polymarket CLOB — no trading UI, no manual position sizing.

In short: it converts any insurable event into an executed, on-chain hedge in seconds.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Mapping free-text risk descriptions to Polymarket markets**
Users describe risks in natural language (e.g. "I'm worried about a Bitcoin crash"). The hardest part was building a reliable routing layer that maps these descriptions to actual Polymarket market slugs across categories — weather, politics, crypto, sports, entertainment — and gracefully tells the user when no matching market exists.

**2. Correct hedge sizing math**
Computing the right YES/NO share quantity to fully offset a user's dollar exposure (not just buy an arbitrary amount) required careful `computeHedge` / `quoteFromMarket` logic accounting for current market prices and implied probabilities.

**3. Safe on-chain trading flow**
The trading flow spans wallet creation, USDC + MATIC funding, one-time CLOB approvals on Polygon, and finally order placement — all while never placing an order without explicit user confirmation in chat. Getting the state machine right and recovering gracefully from partial states (e.g. wallet funded but approvals not run) was tricky.

**4. Streaming tool calls with real-time UI state**
Integrating the AI SDK's streaming responses with live wallet/trade state updates in the Next.js UI — keeping the chat reactive while tool calls run asynchronously — required careful coordination between server actions and client components.

**The problem it solves**

# 🛡️ The Problem It Solves

Demo: https://share.descript.com/view/pnsbObRikUV

### The Challenge: Information Chaos & Adversarial Markets
Traders and participants in futarchic decision markets (such as **Umia**, **MetaDAO**, and **Polymarket**) operate in a high-stakes, high-noise environment. Currently, making an informed decision requires manually tracking scattered signals across Telegram, X (Twitter), Discord, GitHub activity, and on-chain movements. 

This fragmented landscape leads to critical failures:
* **High Cognitive Load:** Participants spend hours cross-referencing data, leading to slow and inefficient decision-making.
* **Vulnerability to Manipulation:** Markets are often swayed by coordinated misinformation and "pump-and-dump" schemes disguised as community consensus.
* **Inefficient Capital Allocation:** Poor information quality results in mispriced risks in high-stakes governance and prediction markets.

---

### The Solution: Umia Analyst Agent
The **Umia Analyst Agent** is an autonomous AI research analyst designed to turn chaotic data into actionable, auditable intelligence. It operates as a continuous intelligence layer that:

* **Smart Ingestion & Weighting:** Automatically classifies signals from multiple sources using a credibility-weighted model (**Verifiable** / **Partial** / **Manipulable**).
* **Adversarial Synthesis:** Generates structured Bull and Bear cases with direct citations, ensuring every claim is backed by evidence.
* **Anti-Manipulation Shield:** Actively flags coordinated manipulation attempts by cross-referencing social hype with on-chain reality.
* **Skin in the Game:** Beyond mere reporting, the agent publishes structured trading memos, takes its own positions, and maintains a public, transparent PnL track record.

---

### 🚀 Key Benefits
| **For Traders** | **For Protocols** | **For the Ecosystem** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Reduces research time from hours to seconds. | Improves the quality of governance decisions. | Enhances market efficiency and liquidity. |
| Minimizes exposure to social engineering. | Attracts informed capital via clear reporting. | Reduces the success rate of malicious actors. |
| Provides an auditable trail of logic for every trade. | Hardens the futarchy mechanism against "noise." | Sets a new standard for AI-driven financial transparency. |

**The Umia Analyst Agent doesn't just provide data—it provides the "Signal" necessary to navigate the "Noise" of decentralized governance.**

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges WE Ran Into

Building the **Umia Analyst Agent** presented several unique technical and conceptual hurdles. Our goal was to move beyond simple "AI wrappers" and build a resilient, institutional-grade engineering system.

### 1. Adversarial Information Filtering
The biggest challenge was creating a system that doesn't just aggregate data but actively resists manipulation. In futarchic markets, we found that social signals (Telegram/X) are often heavily manipulated by proposal authors to create "fake consensus."
* **The Solution:** We implemented a **Source Classification Layer**. We assigned deterministic weights to data: verifiable sources (on-chain transactions, GitHub commits) are weighted at `1.0`, while manipulable social channels are strictly capped at `0.3`.

### 2. Ensuring Agentic Reliability
Standard LLM prompts often suffer from "hallucinations" or "groupthink." In a financial context, we couldn't risk the agent making biased or "hallucinated" trading recommendations.
* **The Solution:** We utilized a **LangGraph-based multi-node architecture**. By separating the pipeline into distinct stages—Source Classification, Synthesis, and Position-taking—and adding an autonomous **Self-Reviewer** node (the "Advocatus Diaboli"), we forced the agent to argue against its own conclusions before finalizing a memo.

### 3. Domain Shift & Architecture Repurposing
We started with a robust pipeline designed for corporate credit underwriting and had to transform it into a DeFi intelligence tool within 48 hours. Mapping "banking risk" to "governance risk" required a total overhaul of the business logic.
* **The Solution:** We maintained the underlying "plumbing" (deterministic logic gates, audit trails, and versioned skills) while completely swapping the domain layers. This allowed us to preserve institutional-grade reliability while moving at hackathon speed.

### 4. Data Ingestion Latency
Scraping decentralized forums and GitHub activity in real-time is computationally expensive and prone to rate limits.
* **The Solution:** We developed a dual-mode ingestion system. For the demo, we use a high-fidelity mock-market layer based on historical MetaDAO proposals, while the production environment is designed to utilize Apify actors for fresh signal ingestion.

### 5. Ecosystem Early-Stage Adaptation (The MetaDAO Bridge)
Since Umia’s native decision markets are currently in their earliest stages, we faced a "cold start" problem regarding live data for testing our agent's predictive accuracy.
* **The Solution:** We chose to stress-test our agent on **MetaDAO** (the pioneer of futarchy). This is a strategic advantage: by proving our agent can navigate the most adversarial and "noisy" established market in the space, we ensure it will be the most robust and battle-tested analyst the moment Umia’s mainnet markets go live. We aren't just building for a sandbox; we are building for the open ocean.

**Network Economy**

We built Mochifi — an autonomous research analyst that makes futarchic decision markets function the way they were designed to. Today, governance markets suffer from thin liquidity and uninformed traders: social signals are manipulated, on-chain data is unread, and most token holders vote blind. Our agent ingests every signal — GitHub commits, on-chain wallet flows, Telegram, X — classifies each source by verifiability, and publishes an institutional-grade trading memo with a YES/NO/ABSTAIN position scaled by confidence. It then tracks its own realized PnL as markets resolve. We're not building another DAO dashboard. We're building the Bloomberg Terminal that makes decentralized governance economically rational.

**Future Society**

Futarchy only works if the people trading in governance markets actually understand what they're trading. We built the infrastructure that makes this possible. Our agent implements adversarial information filtering — verifiable on-chain data is weighted at 1.0, manipulable social signals are capped at 0.3 — and forces itself to argue against its own conclusions through an autonomous Self-Reviewer node before publishing any memo. The result is a system where governance decisions get priced on facts, not coordinated shilling. We believe this is what the next generation of community-driven organizations needs: not just a voting mechanism, but an intelligence layer that makes every vote worth casting.

**Best Agentic Venture**

# 🤖 Why Umia Analyst Agent is the Ultimate Agentic Venture

Our project is a perfect embodiment of an **Agentic Venture** on Umia. We haven't just built a tool; we have launched an autonomous economic entity that operates, earns, and scales natively within the Umia ecosystem.

### 🧠 Autonomous Intelligence Layer
The core of our venture is an **AI Agent** that acts as a real-time intelligence layer for traders in Umia’s resolution markets. 
* **Continuous Monitoring:** The agent autonomously tracks all open proposals, aggregating data from Discord, Telegram, X (Twitter), and on-chain activity (with a focus on Uniswap V4 pools).
* **Actionable Output:** It delivers structured “Memos” that help traders bypass information asymmetry, making the entire Umia ecosystem more efficient and liquid.

### 💎 Economic Alignment & Tokenomics
We have designed a sustainable, deflationary business model that directly benefits the Umia community and token holders:
* **Revenue Loop:** Our subscription and pay-per-memo services run natively on Umia’s token rails.
* **Deflationary Pressure:** **20% of all revenue generated by the agent is automatically burned**, creating a powerful feedback loop that increases scarcity and drives long-term value for token holders.

### 🏛️ A True On-Chain Organization
We operate as a fully sovereign digital entity. By utilizing the **MetaLex BORG** legal wrapper, we transform from a "project" into a **True Agentic Venture**:
* **Autonomous Governance:** We are an autonomous economic entity governed by our own token and resolution markets.
* **Native Infrastructure:** From treasury management to service delivery, every part of our business model is built to leverage Umia’s non-custodial vaults and settlement layers.

---

> **The Bottom Line:** We don’t just participate in Umia — we enhance the entire protocol. By turning chaotic information into a monetizable, deflationary service layer, we provide the essential "Signal" that allows Agentic Ventures on Umia to thrive.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/swarmtree-c724) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gepng/swarmtree) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://swarmtree.eth.limo/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ckdE4dmh4io) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHPrague%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethprague2026.devfolio.co)

> decentralize your bio

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Swarm](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swarm-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most link-in-bio platforms and personal profile pages rely on centralized cloud infrastructure. When providers like AWS experienced outages in 2025, thousands of applications and websites became temporarily inaccessible, showing how fragile centralized systems can be.

Users currently depend on third parties to host and maintain their online identity. If a provider goes offline, changes policies, removes content, or shuts down services, users lose control over their profiles and links.

Swarm + ENS domains provides a decentralized alternative.

People can use it for:
- Creating decentralized Linktree-style profile pages
- Sharing wallets, social links, portfolios, and Web3 identities
- Publishing permanent profiles that are not tied to a single company
- Building censorship-resistant personal websites

It makes existing tasks safer and more resilient by:
- Removing single points of failure
- Distributing content across the Swarm network instead of one server
- Allowing users to fully own their profile through swarm
- Allowing users to easily share their profiles using ENS domain
- Preventing dependency on centralized hosting providers
- Keeping profiles accessible even during infrastructure outages

By combining Swarm’s decentralized storage with ENS human-readable domains, the project creates a more sovereign and durable way for users to manage their online presence in Web3.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Running swarm node ourselves to use as an endpoint to upload

**Network Economy**

## Why Swarmtree fits the “Network Economy” track

Swarmtree aligns with the **Network Economy** track by giving users ownership over their digital identity, online presence, and personal data through decentralized infrastructure.

Today, most creator profiles, and identity hubs depend on centralized providers that control hosting, availability, and access. This creates single points of failure and limits user autonomy. Events such as major cloud outages in 2025 demonstrated how centralized infrastructure can make thousands of applications temporarily inaccessible.

Swarmtree solves this by combining:
- **Swarm decentralized storage**
- **ENS human-readable identities**
- **User-owned content and hosting**

This creates a censorship-resistant and self-sovereign identity layer for Web3 users.

### How it fits the track

#### User-controlled digital identity
Swarmtree allows users to create decentralized profile pages tied directly to ENS domains, enabling portable and verifiable Web3 identities without relying on centralized platforms.

#### Elimination of central points of failure
Unlike traditional Linktree-style services hosted on centralized infrastructure, Swarmtree distributes content across the Swarm network, improving resilience against outages, censorship, and service shutdowns.

#### Privacy and ownership first
Users fully control their profiles, links, and associated identities without depending on a platform intermediary to manage or monetize their data.

#### Building real-world decentralized infrastructure
The project demonstrates how everyday internet tools such as personal profile pages and identity hubs can be rebuilt using decentralized technologies while maintaining usability for mainstream users.

By replacing centralized hosting with decentralized storage and human-readable ENS identities, Swarmtree contributes to a more resilient, user-owned, and privacy-preserving network economy.

**A Simple Key-Value Store on Swarm**

Swarmtree upload all link tree websites that were generated from the app to swarm. 

While Swarmtree is not a traditional key-value database product, it demonstrates a practical and user-friendly adoption of Swarm’s storage primitives in a real-world application.

Swarmtree uses Swarm as the persistence layer for decentralized profile data. 

The project showcases how Swarm can power familiar Web2-style user experiences while preserving decentralization, ownership, and censorship resistance.

We believe this is a strong example of Swarm adoption because it abstracts away protocol complexity and exposes decentralized storage through a simple, consumer-facing experience that mainstream users can immediately understand and use.

**Most Creative Use of ENS**

## Why Swarmtree fits the category

Swarmtree uses ENS as more than a simple wallet resolver, it turns ENS into a decentralized identity, hosting, and discovery layer for Web3-native profile pages.

Instead of using ENS only for "name → address" resolution, Swarmtree combines:
- ENS identities
- ENS contenthash
- ENS text records
- Swarm decentralized storage

to create fully decentralized Linktree-style profiles that users permanently own and control.

### How ENS meaningfully improves the product

#### ENS as a decentralized website router
Swarmtree uses ENS "content hash" records to point directly to decentralized profile pages hosted on Swarm. This removes dependence on centralized hosting providers and enables censorship-resistant personal websites accessible through human-readable ENS domains.

Instead of:
`username.linktree.com`

users own:
`username.eth`

with the ENS record resolving directly to decentralized content.

#### ENS as a portable identity layer
Each Swarmtree profile is tied to a user-owned ENS identity, allowing profiles to become portable across wallets, apps, DAOs, and Web3 ecosystems.

This creates:
- Persistent creator identities
- Wallet-linked public profiles
- Human-readable Web3 presence

#### ENS text records for social and identity metadata
Swarmtree leverages ENS text records to store:
- Social handles
- Profile references
- Web3 identity information

This allows profiles and identity data to remain interoperable across applications without depending on centralized databases.

#### Decentralized hosting through ENS + Swarm
Traditional link-in-bio platforms rely on centralized cloud infrastructure. During major cloud outages in 2025, many applications became inaccessible because users had no ownership over hosting infrastructure.

Swarmtree uses ENS + Swarm to eliminate this dependency:
- ENS routes users to content
- Swarm distributes and persists content across the network
- Users maintain ownership of both identity and hosting

This creates a resilient and censorship-resistant alternative to centralized profile platforms.

### Nyayasarthi
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nyayasarthi-c45a) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://law-and-justicehackolution-11.onrender.com) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/IuHuiOMJ5o8?si=pmJuuobd3uyswIBv) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hackolution%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackolution2k26.devfolio.co)

> The digital bridge for India's legal system.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem:** A Disconnected Justice System
The legal system is crippled by over 50 million pending cases. Currently, Citizens, Police, Lawyers, and Judges operate in isolated silos, causing massive delays.

For the common citizen, seeking justice is terrifying due to complex legal jargon (especially with the new BNS laws), language barriers, and zero transparency. Meanwhile, police forces drown in administrative paperwork instead of focusing on active investigations. Justice is not just delayed; it is disconnected.

**The Solution: Nyayasarthi**
Nyayasarthi is an AI-driven Universal Justice ecosystem that connects all four pillars of the legal system on a single, transparent digital platform.

Breaks the Legal Literacy Barrier: A Multilingual AI Chatbot lets citizens speak or type in their native language. The AI instantly acts as a legal assistant, educating them on applicable BNS sections before they even file a report.

Automates Police Administration: The AI automatically extracts the citizen's chat to generate a structured, Draft Digital FIR, cutting police administrative work down to a single verification click.

Unifies the Network: A secure, role-based 4-Way Chat allows direct, permission-controlled communication between citizens, lawyers, police, and judges, drastically reducing the time between physical court dates.

Guarantees Transparency: A live Case Progress Tracker and an Immutable Transparency Log ensure citizens are never left in the dark and case files cannot be tampered with.

**Real-World Impact:**

- A non-English speaker easily drafts a legally sound police report via voice.
- Police precincts clear documentation backlogs using AI-generated drafts.
- Citizens track their case live on low-end mobile devices without traveling to a courthouse

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Taming the AI for Legal Structuring**
The Hurdle: When building the chatbot, the AI was initially too conversational. We needed it to extract specific incident details and map them strictly to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) sections for the Draft FIR, rather than just offering generic advice.

- The Fix:

 We overhauled our Gemini API integration using strict system instructions and few-shot prompting. We enforced a JSON-only response format and built a custom parsing layer to feed the structured legal data directly into our database securely.

**2. The 4-Way Communication State Management**
The Hurdle: Connecting four distinct roles (Citizen, Police, Lawyer, Judge) on a single platform created a massive headache for real-time state management and data privacy. For example, a citizen cannot see internal police remarks, but both need to be interacting with the same active case file.

- The Fix:

 We implemented a rigorous custom Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) middleware. Every API route and live chat room is strictly scoped—not just by the user's role, but by their specific authorization level tied to the unique Case ID.

**3. Handling Multilingual Asynchronous Data**
The Hurdle: Processing non-English inputs and translating them into accurate legal English for the police dashboard caused significant latency, resulting in a poor user experience on the citizen side.

- The Fix: 

We decoupled the translation and FIR generation logic into background asynchronous tasks. The user gets an immediate success response, while the heavy lifting happens server-side, updating the front-end via live progress trackers once completed.

![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![NetworkX](https://img.shields.io/badge/NetworkX-333333?style=flat-square) ![Plotly](https://img.shields.io/badge/Plotly-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

CyberTwin AI addresses the growing problem of cyber insecurity caused by phishing attacks, weak passwords, password reuse, and lack of cybersecurity awareness.

Most users today manage multiple online accounts across email and social media platforms but do not understand how vulnerable they are to cyber threats. Existing tools are often reactive and only respond after an attack has already occurred.

Cyber AI Dashboard solves this by providing:
• AI-based cyber risk prediction
• Multi-platform security analysis
• Phishing and spam awareness
• Attack propagation visualization
• Password strength evaluation
• Preventive cybersecurity recommendations

The platform helps users understand and visualize how a single compromised account can lead to wider digital exposure and account takeovers.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was integrating multiple cybersecurity functionalities into a single lightweight dashboard while maintaining smooth performance and usability.

We faced challenges in:
• Designing realistic cyber risk simulation logic
• Training and comparing multiple machine learning models
• Visualizing attack propagation dynamically using graphs
• Integrating real email fetching securely using IMAP
• Handling inconsistent email formats during spam analysis
• Creating an interactive UI that remains simple for non-technical users

Another challenge was balancing cybersecurity realism with hackathon-level implementation speed while ensuring the platform remained visually engaging and functional.

Bug / Hurdle Faced

While building my project (Skill Matchmaker Collective
), one major challenge I encountered was handling real-time skill matching and data flow between components.

The issue was that user inputs (skills, preferences, etc.) were not consistently syncing with the matching logic, which led to incorrect or delayed results being displayed on the UI. Implemented input validation and preprocessing before sending data to the matching system
Broke down the matching logic into smaller, testable functions
Used debugging and logging to trace where mismatches were happening

After these improvements, the system became more accurate, responsive, and reliable.

### Sprouts-Lands
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sproutslands-3bf0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ANAMASGARD/Sprout-Lands) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://sprout-lands.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Devlynix%20Buildathon%201.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devlynix-buildathon.devfolio.co)

> Turn your secret message into an adventure games

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Phaser.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/Phaser.io-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest architectural challenge was designing the reward reveal flow so the secret message stays hidden until the player genuinely completes the game — not just skippable or URL-extractable. Since Next.js NEXT_PUBLIC_* environment variables are client-visible by default, we had to architect a solution where the reward payload is never exposed in the page source or network tab until the win condition is verified client-side. The final design uses the game's own puzzle state as the gate — mystery:solved only emits after all four charm conditions pass inside Phaser, and the reveal overlay only mounts after that event fires.

The second challenge was keeping the game loop alive across Phaser scene transitions. When players enter sub-scenes (the Library rune puzzle or the Caverns platformer), Phaser's main IslandScene goes to sleep. Any game state living purely in Phaser would freeze. We solved this by moving shared state — the countdown timer, the HP economy, the win/lose overlay logic — entirely into React, communicating through a typed gameBus event bridge. This meant the experience stays coherent regardless of which scene the player is in.

Making the game feel personal to each recipient without requiring the sender to build anything custom was the core product design challenge. The solution was keeping the island, puzzles, and characters fixed — but making the final chest reveal fully dynamic based on the sender's input. The journey is the same for everyone; the destination is unique every time. This balance between a consistent game experience and a personalized emotional payoff was the hardest design constraint to satisfy, and the one we are most proud of.

**The problem it solves**

Sharing something personal — a confession, a surprise, a secret message — over text feels flat and forgettable. SproutLands turns that moment into an experience worth remembering.

SproutLands is a gamified secret message platform disguised as a pixel-art puzzle adventure. Here is how it works: the sender logs in, customizes their secret reward (a message, a confession, a surprise reveal — anything they want), and gets a shareable link. The recipient clicks the link, plays through a charming island mystery, solves four puzzles, and only then — when they open the final chest — does the secret reveal itself. The message becomes a reward that was earned, not just received.

This solves a real emotional problem: how do you make someone feel something when you send them a message? A text saying "I like you" is easy to dismiss. Solving four puzzles on a mystery island to unlock those same words is unforgettable. SproutLands transforms personal communication into a shared story — the recipient does not just read the message, they experience the journey to it.

Use cases range from romantic confessions and friendship surprises to birthday reveals, scavenger hunt endings, and team announcements. Anyone who wants to make a moment feel special can build a SproutLands link in under a minute and send it to anyone in the world .

[Gaurav Chaudhary](https://github.com/ANAMASGARD)

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most agent workflows break at the exact point where money, trust, and delivery need to meet.

Today, teams often stitch this together manually:

one tool to publish a service,
another channel to negotiate requirements,
a separate payment flow,
and ad-hoc messages to prove what was delivered.
That creates friction and risk:

unclear service scope and SLA,
weak proof of payment status,
no clean audit trail for buyer/seller handoff,
more manual coordination between humans and agents.
What People Can Use A2M For
A2M is a lightweight marketplace layer for agent-to-agent services.
People can use it to:

publish agent services with structured metadata and pricing,
let buyer agents discover and order those services,
initiate checkout sessions for paid execution,
track order lifecycle (PENDING → PAID/EXPIRED/etc.),
exchange materials and delivery artifacts in one order thread,
monitor agent presence (heartbeat) for operational readiness.
How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer
Single workflow, fewer handoffs: listing, order, payment session, and delivery stay in one system.
Clear state transitions: standardized order/payment statuses reduce ambiguity.
Better accountability: each order keeps payment proof and message history.
Agent-native integration: skill.md gives external agents a concrete contract to follow.
Operational visibility: dashboard/account views surface active agents and latest proof.
Safer demo-to-production path: you can run end-to-end flows without improvising custom glue code each time.
In One Line
A2M turns fragmented “agent does work, trust me” interactions into a structured, traceable, payment-aware service workflow.

**Challenges we ran into**

1) External-agent onboarding vs. UI ownership model mismatch
Another hurdle was expectation mismatch: skill.md guides external agent behavior, but does not itself “magically” register ownership in the UI unless the registration step is done via the authenticated app flow.

**How I got over it**

- Clarified the lifecycle: operator registration establishes ownership, then external agent uses API key for automation.
- Updated demo narrative to explicitly include pre-created seller/buyer agents before runtime tasks.

**Track: Checkout with Locus**

1) Order creation creates a Locus checkout session
When buyer calls POST /api/orders:

- Authenticates buyer agent (requireAgent), validates -listing, blocks self-purchase.
- Creates local orders row with PENDING.
- Calls createLocusSession(...) with:
    - amount/description
    - successUrl and cancelUrl
    - webhookUrl (/api/webhooks/locus)
    - metadata (orderId, buyer/seller IDs)
- Saves returned Locus session into checkout_sessions:
    - sessionId, checkoutUrl, status, expiresAt, webhookSecret

2) Buyer can trigger agent-side payment API
POST /api/checkout/agent/pay/:sessionId:

- Authenticates agent and ensures caller is that order’s buyer.
- Requires x-locus-api-key (buyer’s key; rejects shared server key).
- Calls Locus POST /checkout/agent/pay/:sessionId.
- Returns “payment request submitted” (not final state yet).

### Souq
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/souq-4480) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/andreasstudents/souqlocus) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://souqlocus.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Locus'%20Paygentic%20Hackathon%20--%20#3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://paygentic-week3.devfolio.co)

> A Marketplace for AI Agents. powered by Locus

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem:

  AI agents are becoming increasingly capable—able to write code, analyze data, create content, and perform complex
  tasks—but there's no trusted marketplace where they can economically transact with each other or with humans. Current
  payment systems (Stripe, PayPal, credit cards) are designed exclusively for humans, requiring GUIs, CAPTCHAs, and
  manual bank connections. This creates a deadlock: humans want to hire AI agents but have no quality guarantee (what if
   the agent does a bad job?), and AI agents want to earn money but have no trusted platform to find work or ensure
  they'll actually get paid. There's also no escrow system for agent-to-agent commerce, no dispute resolution when work
  quality is contested, and no way to verify that services were delivered as promised.

  What Souq Solves:

  Souq creates an agent-to-agent marketplace with built-in escrow and quality control, enabling both humans and AI
  agents to transact with confidence. The platform uses a three-party system (Client, Provider, Evaluator) where
  payments are held in escrow until an independent evaluator approves the work—protecting clients from bad work and
  providers from non-payment. The Locus checkout integration makes this work for both humans (who get a Stripe-style
  checkout URL) and AI agents (who can programmatically discover and pay for jobs via MCP tools). The escrow ensures
  fairness: if the evaluator rejects the work, the client gets automatically refunded; if approved, the provider
  receives 90% of the payment, the evaluator gets 5%, and the platform gets 5%.

  Use Cases:

  - Humans hiring AI agents: Post a job ("Research AI trends in healthcare," "Debug this React component," "Write
  marketing copy") → AI agents discover it via MCP tools → Fund via Locus checkout → Evaluator reviews quality → Payment
   released only when satisfied
  - AI agents hiring AI agents: One agent specializes in data scraping but needs analysis → Posts job on Souq → Another
  AI agent (analysis specialist) completes it → Escrow ensures both parties are protected
  - Service discovery: AI agents can list their capabilities (code review, testing, content generation, data enrichment)
   and humans/agents can browse and hire them through the same platform
  - Quality assurance: The three-party model (Client-Provider-Evaluator) means agents can't just take money and deliver
  garbage—independent evaluators provide accountability
  - Autonomous agent economy: Agents can earn USDC on Base by completing jobs, then use those earnings to hire other
  agents, creating a self-sustaining agent economy

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into:

  The biggest technical hurdle was Locus's rate limiting (5 requests/IP/hour) which made development and testing
  extremely slow—every registration attempt consumed quota, so I had to implement strict double-submit protection on all
   forms to prevent accidental re-submissions. Another challenge was managing two types of wallets in the auth system:
  Locus wallets (where addresses are fetched real-time from the API) and manual fallback wallets (where static addresses
   live in Firestore). I solved this by adding a walletManuallyAdded flag that tells the auth context which method to
  use, preventing unnecessary API calls. The private key security problem was tricky too—Locus only shows the private
  key once during registration, so I had to build a copy-gated flow that won't let users proceed until they've saved it,
   balancing security with good UX.

  On the build and architecture side, I hit TypeScript errors from redundant conditional logic (checking status ===
  "loading" inside a block that only renders when status === "idle"), which I fixed by removing unnecessary type checks.
   The Firebase + Locus authentication timing was complex—registration requires creating a Firebase user, calling Locus
  self-registration, polling 30-45 seconds for wallet deployment, then saving to Firestore—all while keeping the user
  informed with loading states. Finally, the project went through a major architecture migration from WDK smart
  contracts to Locus checkout abstraction, which meant ripping out all direct blockchain interaction code and replacing
  it with checkout URL-based payments. The key insight was maintaining the same API surface layer (jobs, status, bids)
  so the frontend and MCP server didn't need major changes—just the underlying payment mechanism swapped out.

**Track: Checkout with Locus**

Souq is an agent-to-agent marketplace that exemplifies the "Checkout with Locus" track by creating a platform where AI
   agents can autonomously list services, discover jobs, and transact via Locus Checkout. The project implements the
  exact use case described in the track examples: an escrow-based job marketplace where agents act as clients (posting
  jobs with budgets), providers (bidding on and completing work), and evaluators (reviewing deliverables)—all payments
  flow through Locus checkout sessions. What makes Souq unique is its dual interface architecture: the same Locus
  checkout integration powers both a human-facing Next.js web app (where users browse jobs and fund via checkout URLs)
  and an MCP server for AI agents (where tools like fund_job autonomously discover and pay for jobs programmatically).
  By leveraging Locus's machine-readable checkout pages, Souq enables agents to participate in commerce just as easily
  as humans—agents can list services via create_job, discover opportunities via list_jobs, and complete payments through
   checkout sessions that both humans and agents can interact with. The project turns Locus wallets into revenue streams
   for AI agents who can earn USDC by completing jobs, while humans can post tasks and pay agents, all unified through a
   single Locus checkout integration that handles wallet connections, on-chain USDC settlements on Base, and webhook
  notifications for job status updates.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/blink-9cbf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Sampurnasit/blink.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://blink-five-delta.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacktonix%20'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacktonix-26.devfolio.co)

> When voices fade, emergencies go unheard

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Shaders](https://img.shields.io/badge/Shaders-333333?style=flat-square) ![Speech API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Speech%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Router-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

For individuals suffering from severe motor neuron diseases like ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis), locked-in syndrome, or varying degrees of quadriplegia, interacting with the digital world is a massive friction point. Traditional physical input devices are unusable, and existing accessibility hardware often requires expensive, proprietary eye-tracking rigs.

BLINK solves this by providing a highly accessible, zero-cost, hands-free Communication and Navigation System (AAC). By leveraging standard consumer webcams, the application dynamically translates the user's micro-facial expressions, blink-driven Morse code, and continuous eye-gaze tracking into tangible actions. It empowers users to trigger emergency SOS messages, type through predictive text, perform external searches, and navigate interactive 3D interfaces completely hands-free.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a reliable, accessible computer-vision system entirely within a web browser presented some incredibly stubborn math and optimization hurdles.

1. The Horizontal Eye Tracking "Cancellation" Bug

The Hurdle: When we built the continuous gaze-tracking logic for the 3D Cube control, we noticed that vertical tracking (UP/DOWN) worked flawlessly, but horizontal tracking (LEFT/RIGHT) registered almost zero movement!
How we got over it: After deep mathematical debugging, we realized the projection vectors for the left eye (outer-to-inner corner) and the righteye (inner-to-outer corner) were physically inverted. When a user looked left, the pupil distance increased on one eye but decreased on the other—averaging out to 0. We resolved this by explicitly defining a standardized Left-to-Right Cartesian axis for both eyes globally, bypassing the "inner/outer" corner ambiguity.
2. Head Motion Drift and Tracking Jitter

The Hurdle: Natural micromovements of the human head, turning, or tilting would violently skew the location of the pupil, causing the cursor or cube to snap uncontrollably even when the user was staring dead center.
How we got over it: We engineered aHead Pose Compensation Algorithm that calculated the geometric roll, pitch, and yaw of the entire face-mesh. By subtracting this rotational angle from the raw pupil ratios, the gaze-tracker suddenly became head-independent. To solve the remaining high-frequency twitching, we implemented a custom mathematical One-Euro Filter (a dynamic low-pass filter) to stabilize and smooth out jitter without sacrificing high-speed responsiveness.
3. Complex Calibration Thresholds

The Hurdle: Every human's Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) is completely different, making a "one-size-fits-all" blink detection impossible.
How we got over it: We crafted a dynamic two-step auto-calibration script that quietly records an array of the user's neutral eye states during the first 2 seconds of initialization, algorithmically calculating Interquartile Ranges (IQR) to establish a personalized deadzone and blink threshold in real-time.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sjsj-a177) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/luo-yongzheng/AutoOptimize.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://3000-ii1m99gkefnhlhk7q012p-82b888ba.sandbox.novita.ai/Autoor%20Chat.html) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Push%20to%20Prod%20Hackathon%20with%20Genspark%20&%20Claude-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://push-to-prod.devfolio.co)

> Optimization AI Harness for Everyone

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![LLM](https://img.shields.io/badge/LLM-333333?style=flat-square) ![Optimization](https://img.shields.io/badge/Optimization-333333?style=flat-square)

**Use of Genspark**

GenSpark is what makes this tool deployable as an internal tool without us having to stand up our own VPC, CI/CD, sandbox, and email ingestion. The whole pipeline runs on GenSpark hosted infrastructure with GitHub-integrated CI/CD, every push auto-builds and deploys to the sandbox, so the live endpoint always reflects the latest code. GenSpark hosts the FastAPI WebSocket backend (port 8000) and the React/JSX frontend (port 3000), and provides the isolated runtime sandbox where Gurobi solvers execute safely against user data. For the second internal workflow, the one many of our engineers actually prefer, we use GenSpark Claw as an email-driven entry point: an engineer emails a problem description with data attachments to Claw, which parses the email, uploads files into the GenSpark sandbox via API, triggers the same Autoor pipeline, and emails the outputs (Excel, solver code, solution JSON, HTML dashboard) back as reply attachments. Zero UI, zero logins, fits the way operations teams already coordinate work today. GenSpark compressed what would normally be weeks of infra setup into minutes, letting us focus 100% of the hackathon time on the AI product and the real workflow problem.

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://3000-ii1m99gkefnhlhk7q012p-82b888ba.sandbox.novita.ai/Autoor%20Chat.html

**The problem your project solves**

This is a real, recurring internal workflow pain at our own company (a major airline). Every week our operations research team gets inbound requests from internal business units Crew Scheduling, Aircraft Maintenance, Ground Ops, Cargo, Network Planning to solve optimization problems (crew rostering, check rotations, gate assignment, spare-parts allocation, route planning). The workflow is painfully manual and identical every time: a business unit writes a requirements doc and drops Excel/CSV data on the OR team → a specialist spends 2–6 weeks interpreting the spec, cleaning data, hand-coding a Gurobi model, debugging infeasibility, validating outputs, and authoring a report → business stakeholders wait weeks for a first answer and cannot self-serve when assumptions change. Scarce OR experts become the permanent bottleneck; we turn down a large share of inbound requests for lack of bandwidth. Knowledge from finished projects stays trapped in scattered notebooks and tribal memory, so every new request starts from zero. The same pattern repeats at every enterprise with an OR or analytics function  it's expensive, slow, and structurally under-delivers the value optimization could provide internally.

**Use of Claude**

Claude is the reasoning engine of every stage, orchestrated through the Claude Agent SDK. We mirror how a real OR team delegates work internally, one coordinator plus three specialists, each with scoped tools and skills:
 
Root agent - reads files, classifies the problem, and uses AskUserQuestion to confirm assumptions with the business user before anything irreversible runs. This is the "analyst intake" step done manually by an expert today.
formula-builder, produces the LaTeX mathematical formulation (objective + constraints) as structured JSON.
solver — generates Gurobi Python code, executes it in the sandbox, and exports Excel + solution.json.
visualizer — analyzes the solution and builds an interactive Chart.js dashboard for business stakeholders.
Enterprise OR expertise is encoded once as auto-discovered Claude Agent Skills  (problem-classifier, problem-decomposer, assignment-scheduling, routing-logistics, inventory-resource-allocation, visualize) — new problem types slot in by adding a skill, not by rewriting the agents, so the internal playbook compounds over time. The frontend streams Claude's thinking, tool calls, and results in real time over a WebSocket, with mid-run clarifying questions rendered as option cards so non-technical business users can drive the pipeline themselves. Default model is Claude Sonnet via the Agent SDK, with an upgrade path to Opus for harder problems.

**How you are solving it**

We’re essentially compressing a traditionally multi-week Operations Research workflow into a deterministic, production-grade pipeline that executes in minutes. A business user provides raw operational data (e.g., fleet schedules, crew rosters, maintenance constraints), and a Claude-powered multi-agent system translates this into a formally defined optimization problem, generates a mathematically valid LaTeX model, compiles and executes a Gurobi solver, and returns an optimized allocation with full auditability (Excel/JSON outputs + KPI dashboards). The system also handles infeasibility via IIS diagnostics and iterative self-repair, ensuring robustness without human intervention. By modularizing domain expertise into reusable agent skills (e.g., scheduling, routing, resource allocation), we eliminate repeated modeling effort and create a continuously improving internal optimization layer. In practical terms, this shifts OR teams from manual model development to high-leverage validation, enabling business users to self-serve ~70–80% of use cases. For an airline-scale operation, even a conservative 0.5–1% improvement in aircraft utilization, crew efficiency, or maintenance scheduling can translate to **$500K–$2M+ annual savings per optimization domain**, with SIA easily unlocking **$5M–$20M+ total yearly impact** across multiple workflows—while also reducing turnaround time from weeks to minutes and significantly lowering coordination overhead across engineering, operations, and planning teams.

Core theme fit "real internal workflow problem, solved with AI"

Claude is not a bolt-on — it is the core intelligence layer of Clarion. We use 13 distinct Claude platform features in a single cohesive product:

Agent SDK: The Claude Agent SDK powers the core agent loop, orchestrating email tools, MCP servers, and subagents into a unified reasoning pipeline.

MCP (Model Context Protocol): We run two MCP servers — the official Gmail MCP for live email ingestion, and a custom Node.js MCP server implementing domain-specific tools (mark_done, snooze, split_invoice). MCP gives the agent structured, tool-based access to external data rather than brittle prompt injection.

Subagents: Three persona subagents (Developer, Manager, Finance) sit behind a router. The same inbox data is analyzed through entirely different lenses depending on who you are — a finance persona prioritizes bills and expense deadlines, a developer persona flags CI failures and expiring tokens, a manager persona surfaces unreplied threads and team blockers.

Skills: Two Claude Code skills — invoice-splitter (vision + math) and digest-formatter (structured rendering) — are built as proper SKILL.md modules, composable and testable independently.

Hooks: A SessionStart hook auto-runs the daily digest when you open Claude Code — proactive intelligence without the user having to ask.

Extended Thinking: Digest generation uses extended thinking for deeper reasoning about urgency, deadline proximity, and cross-message dependencies.

Structured Output: The digest returns a strict ActionItem[] schema via Zod-validated tool calls — not string parsing, but typed, reliable structured data.

Citations: Every chat answer cites the exact source message (subject line + quoted snippet) so users can verify in one click.

Vision: The invoice splitter reads line items directly from receipt images — no OCR preprocessing, no manual data entry.

Prompt Caching: System prompts and message indices are cached across turns, with visible cache-hit metrics in the UI for efficiency.

Streaming: Chat responses stream via SSE for a real-time conversational feel.

Slash Commands: A /digest command provides quick access to the daily briefing inside Claude Code.

LLM-Powered To-Do Derivation: The universal push interface feeds raw message text from any source into Claude, which extracts structured action items (title, due date, urgency, category) and writes them to the database. This is what makes Clarion channel-agnostic from day one — Claude does the hard parsing work, not hand-written extractors.

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://pushtoprod-theta.vercel.app

**The problem your project solves**

The modern knowledge worker doesn't have one inbox — they have five: email, Slack, Teams, project trackers, and calendar notifications. Buried across all of them are unpaid invoices, expiring contracts, forgotten threads, missed deadlines, and action items that nobody wrote down.

McKinsey estimates professionals spend 28% of their workweek — 11 hours — just managing messages. Not doing work. Deciding what work to do. Scanning, triaging, remembering, following up — across multiple disconnected tools, every single day.

The result is predictable: things fall through the cracks. An SSL cert expires because the renewal email was buried. A client escalation sits unanswered because it came through Teams while you were triaging email. A teammate's action item from a Slack thread is forgotten the moment it scrolls off-screen. No one needs another notification tool. They need an AI that reads everything for them, reasons about what's urgent, and delivers a single prioritized briefing every morning.

**How you are solving it**

Clarion is a unified AI chief-of-staff that ingests messages from across all your communication channels — email, Teams, Slack — and converts them into structured, prioritized action items. One secretary. Every channel. Every to-do surfaced.

Each morning, Clarion delivers a proactive digest: not a summary of everything, but a prioritized list of what requires action — bills due, expiring licenses, unreplied threads, hard deadlines, and team action items — color-coded by urgency and grouped by category. One glance replaces thirty minutes of inbox-and-channel scanning.

Beyond the digest, users can chat with their messages in plain English ("What invoices are due this week?", "What haven't I replied to?") and get cited answers across every channel. For channels without native connectors yet, our universal push interface lets users feed any message — Teams, WhatsApp, a voice memo transcript — into the secretary, where an LLM automatically derives structured action items. No connector needed.

The architecture is channel-agnostic by design: email is the launch connector, but adding a new source is an adapter change, not a rewrite. The problem is universal (every employee has an inbox), the cost is massive (130 hours per person per year lost to triage), and the solution is immediate.

**Use of Genspark**

GenSpark powers Clarion's multi-channel expansion layer. Our architecture is deliberately channel-agnostic — email is the launch connector, but every other communication tool (Slack, Teams, WhatsApp) needs an adapter to feed messages into our unified action-item database. GenSpark Claw acts as that adapter layer.

A GenSpark workflow connects to a team's Slack workspace using its native integration — no custom OAuth or bot setup required. The workflow triggers on a schedule (e.g., every morning before the digest runs) or on new-message events in designated channels, forwarding message content to Clarion's universal intake API endpoint (/api/push). From there, Clarion's LLM derivation engine parses the Slack messages into structured ActionItem objects — the same pipeline that already handles manually pushed messages.

The key advantage: zero connector code on our side. GenSpark handles Slack auth, pagination, rate limits, and message formatting. The same workflow pattern extends to Teams, WhatsApp, and Notion without building separate adapters for each. This means Clarion scales to new communication channels by configuring a GenSpark workflow, not by writing and maintaining integration code. GenSpark is the bridge between "works with email today" and "works with everything tomorrow."

## CFO Copilot — Three Integrated Components

### Component 1 — Consolidated Variance Report
A Group-level P&L with drill-down by entity showing:
- Budget vs. Actual vs. Prior Period for each line item
- Variance flagged automatically by configurable materiality threshold (e.g. >5% or >$10K)
- Entity-level detail accessible on demand — one click from the Group view

### Component 2 — AI Narrative Layer
For each flagged variance, Claude AI auto-drafts a plain-English explanation:
> *"Singapore headcount costs exceeded budget by 18%, driven by 2 hires pulled forward from Q3. This was a planned acceleration approved in the August board meeting."*

- Finance Director reviews, approves, edits, or overrides each narrative inline
- Country heads can add their own commentary per entity
- Approved narratives are locked and timestamped — creating an audit trail of management explanations

### Component 3 — Cost Structure Scorecard
A live panel benchmarked against Series B SaaS/cybersecurity investor norms across three buckets:

| Bucket | What It Covers |
|--------|----------------|
| Sales & Marketing | S&M headcount, campaigns, events, commissions |
| Service Delivery | SOC operations, delivery headcount, delivery tooling |
| Administrative | Finance, Legal, People/HR, Internal technology |

Each bucket shows actual % vs. budget %, trend vs. prior period, benchmark band, and a flag if outside range.

### Why This Matters for Series B
Cost structure is one of the first things Series B investors scrutinise. This tool lets you walk into any investor conversation and immediately answer: Are you spending on the right things? Is delivery scalable? Is overhead lean?

Management asks **"why?"** and the current process requires manual digging, reformatting, and explaining across 4–6 entities with data spread across accounting software and spreadsheets.

- No single place where variance, context, and commentary live together
- No quick way to benchmark cost structure against investor expectations

**Use of Genspark**

Leveraged GenSpark AI’s deep‑learning content generation to accelerate intensive research, close domain-knowledge gaps, and produce integrated slide decks and presentation assets.

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://github.com/ngohanping/tr-devfolio-2026

**How you are solving it**

Graph model: stores Project, Service, Team nodes and relationships (OWNS, DEPLOYED_ON, CALLS, EXPOSED_BY) so topology, ownership and dependency queries are simple and fast.
Analysis layer: exposes ready Cypher queries to answer ownership, dependency, impact and path queries; complex analysis comes from combining MATCH, shortestPath, and aggregation.
UI & visualization: Angular frontend (dashboards, ecosystem and squad views) visualizes nodes/edges and lets users drill into services, projects, and teams.
Exports & integrations: CSV/JSON exports, API endpoints, and optional connectors to other tools for reporting and change workflows.

**Use of Claude**

Claude served as the project's primary AI collaborator across research, content generation, code assistance, validation, and presentation production. Its contributions were integrated into development workflows using repeatable prompt templates and human-in-the-loop checkpoints to ensure accuracy, provenance, and safe exposure of outputs.

Research & synthesis: Claude performed deep-topic research, consolidating technical references, best practices, and architectural patterns into concise briefs. It summarized papers, API docs, and platform notes, identified domain gaps, and produced prioritized research agendas so engineers could focus on high-value verification work rather than exploratory reading.

Code generation & review: Claude generated Cypher query drafts, scaffolding for ingestion scripts, and small TypeScript/Angular snippets. Each suggestion was emitted alongside rationale and example inputs/outputs. Generated code always passed through a human reviewer and automated linters/tests; Claude’s outputs were used as an accelerant rather than an authoritative source.

Ontology & modelling: Claude helped design the graph ontology (node/label choices, relationship semantics, properties) by proposing normalized schemas and migration-safe MERGE patterns. It produced examples showing how to represent ownership, deployment topology, and API exposure to maximize queryability and reduce ambiguity.

Analysis & validation: Claude authored and iterated on Cypher queries used for impact analysis, shortest-path discovery, and safety previews. For destructive operations, Claude-produced patterns followed a preview-first workflow (RETURN the target nodes → review → DETACH DELETE), and the project enforced manual confirmation and backups before apply.

Content & product assets: Claude generated README copy, UI microcopy, onboarding guides, and full slide decks. Slide creation included speaker notes and suggested visual layouts; outputs were exported into presentation templates and hand-curated by the team for brand alignment and factual checks.

Prompt engineering & templates: We captured effective prompts as reusable templates with fixed context blocks (ontology, constraints, style guide) and variable slots (task, examples). This ensured consistent outputs and made human review faster because Claude’s responses followed predictable structure.

Measurable benefits: Claude reduced initial draft time for research briefs and query prototypes by an order of magnitude, accelerated slide production, and increased the throughput of exploratory queries so engineers could iterate faster on modeling decisions.

**The problem your project solves**

This project provides an architecture/portfolio tool that discovers, models, and visualizes an organization’s software landscape—projects, services, teams, and their relationships—so engineers and architects can query ownership, dependencies, and deployment topology, spot risks, and coordinate changes. It includes Cypher queries for Neo4j and an Angular-based UI (dashboards, ecosystem and squad views, AI-chat helper) to explore and export architectural data.

> You take care of crisis, we take care of DevOps

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![BuildWithLocus](https://img.shields.io/badge/BuildWithLocus-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Human Latency in DevOps: In traditional environments, deploying a coordination hub requires a human team to navigate cloud consoles, write Dockerfiles, and manage SSL certificates, a process that can take 15–60 minutes. By using BuildWithLocus, the agent eliminates this delay, deploying full-stack containerized services via API in under 120 seconds.

2. Infrastructure Overload: Communication networks and routing systems often collapse during unpredictable spikes in demand. The "Overwatch" agent solves this by autonomously scaling container replicas to match real-time traffic surges, preventing system downtime during peak emergency periods.

3. Financial Bottlenecks: Traditional budget approval and procurement cycles for additional compute power are too slow for high-stakes crises. Through PayWithLocus, the agent acts as an autonomous economic actor, instantly funding its own scaling needs with a USDC wallet rather than waiting for human financial intervention.

4. Alert Fatigue: Emergency response centers frequently struggle to triage massive volumes of low-fidelity alerts. The agent acts as a high-speed aggregation layer, processing thousands of geographic SOS flags to detect and respond to localized crises before human operators can even identify the pattern.

5. Cost Inefficiency and Waste: Organizations often over-provision "hot" standby servers to handle potential emergencies, leading to wasted budget. The Crisis Grid maintains a "minimal footprint" under normal conditions and automatically liquidates redundant services once a crisis abates, recovering unspent credits into a master wallet.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Open Checkbook" & Recursive Loop RiskThe most significant hurdle was the risk of runaway inference and transaction costs. Because the Overwatch agent operates at machine speed, a simple logic error or a "retry loop" during an infrastructure deployment could potentially deplete the USDC wallet in minutes $$.The Fix: I moved away from assuming "human-speed" oversight and instead implemented Spending Policies at the protocol level using the Locus dashboard. This included strict per-transaction caps and daily allowances that return a 403 Forbidden error if the agent attempts to exceed them, regardless of its internal logic $$.
2. Wallet Synchronization LatencyA frequent bug occurred where the agent attempted to fund BuildWithLocus deployments immediately after registration, resulting in failed transactions. This happened because the agent's wallet was still being provisioned on the Base network $$.The Fix: I implemented a robust Status Polling Loop. The agent is now programmed to poll the GET /api/status endpoint and must receive a walletStatus: "deployed" confirmation before it is permitted to trigger any financial or infrastructure actions $[1]$.
3. API "Hallucinations" in Multi-Step WorkflowsDuring the transition from "detecting a crisis" to "deploying microservices," the agent occasionally "hallucinated" the required JSON schema for the BuildWithLocus API, leading to failed builds or deployment errors $$.The Fix: To ensure the agent didn't rely on potentially outdated training data, I integrated Runtime Skill Discovery. The agent is required to read the SKILL.md file (provided at registration) at the start of every crisis event to ingest the current API reference for deployments and wrapped tools $[1, 2]$.
4. Handling Multi-Step Failure CascadesIn early testing, if one microservice failed to deploy (e.g., a triage routing API), the entire "Crisis Grid" would halt, leaving the coordination hub isolated $$.The Fix: I decomposed the monolithic deployment into Specialized Sub-Agents. Instead of one "brain" doing everything, the system now uses a supervisor that routes tasks to specific "coder" and "deployer" sub-agents. If one service fails, the supervisor can trigger a specific retry or fallback to a "safe mode" minimal hub without crashing the entire response grid $$.

**Track: Using BuildWithLocus to leverage our suite.**

I deployed my backend and DevOps stuff to Build With Locus so that it can be scaled proeprly and that too without any manual intervention.
Check it out at https://svc-mo9tnetizgij5tdx.buildwithlocus.com
