### ARZIS-Adaptive-Root-Zone-Intelligence-System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/arzisadaptiverootzoneintelligencesystem-9b8e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/anshgupta110805/ARZIS-Adaptive-Root-Zone-Intelligence-System) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://anshgupta110805.github.io/ARZIS-Adaptive-Root-Zone-Intelligence-System/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> From field decisions to plant decisions.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern agriculture still applies fertilizer at the field or zone level, assuming that soil nutrients are evenly distributed. In reality, nutrient levels vary significantly from plant to plant due to soil composition, moisture variation, and root competition.
Because of this, farmers often apply fertilizer uniformly across large areas. This leads to fertilizer waste, increased costs, environmental damage, and inconsistent crop health.
Current precision agriculture platforms improve efficiency but still operate at hectare or zone resolution, meaning thousands of plants receive the same treatment even though their nutrient needs differ.
ARZIS solves this problem by introducing plant-level decision making.
Instead of optimizing fertilizer at the field level, ARZIS simulates a root-zone digital twin where AI evaluates nutrient conditions for every individual plant. The system dynamically recommends targeted fertilization only where it is needed.
By shifting agriculture from field-level optimization to plant-level intelligence, ARZIS reduces fertilizer waste, improves crop health, and enables a new generation of highly precise and sustainable farming.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was designing a system that could simulate plant-level nutrient optimization without using physical sensors. Most real-world precision agriculture platforms rely on hardware soil sensors, but our goal was to create a software-only solution that could still demonstrate root-level intelligence.
Another challenge was building a realistic farm simulation within the limited time of a hackathon. Modeling soil nutrients, plant health, and fertilizer impact accurately is complex. To solve this, we simplified the system by creating a virtual farm grid where each plant has simulated NPK values, and plant health follows the principle of Liebig’s Law of the Minimum.
We also initially considered using reinforcement learning, but training an RL model within a hackathon time limit proved difficult. Instead, we implemented a faster adaptive decision engine that still demonstrates how AI could optimize fertilizer distribution across thousands of plants.
Finally, making the results visually clear for judges was another challenge. We solved this by building an interactive dashboard that shows a plant-level heatmap and compares traditional fertilization with the ARZIS adaptive system.
These challenges helped us focus on building a simple but powerful prototype that clearly demonstrates the concept of plant-level agricultural intelligence.

**Requestly – Creative Use Challenge**

AI / Machine Learning
Sustainability / Climate Tech
Agriculture Technology (AgriTech)
Smart Farming / Precision Agriculture

> Care Today, Protect Tommorow

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many people do not regularly monitor their health due to lack of easy tools and quick access to medical assistance. In emergency situations, sharing important health information with hospitals or support organizations can also take valuable time. CareTrack solves this problem by providing a simple platform where users can store their health details, track basic health parameters, and generate instant health reports. In case of an emergency, the app can quickly share the user's health information with nearby NGOs or government hospitals, helping ensure faster medical response and better care.

**Challenges we ran into**

One challenge we faced while building CareTrack was saving and retrieving the user's profile data correctly. Initially, when users entered their details and refreshed the page, all the information was lost because the data was not being stored permanently.

To solve this problem, we implemented LocalStorage in JavaScript. This allowed the application to store the user's information directly in the browser so that the data remains available even after refreshing the page. We also added proper functions to save and retrieve the data automatically.

By using LocalStorage, we were able to ensure that user details such as name, age, blood group, and emergency contact remain saved, which is essential for generating health reports and enabling the emergency SOS feature.

### FastCred.UPI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fastcredupi-2e00) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ankit1morecode/Team-Aegis5IEGE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Instant Payment Smart Credit

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL server](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL%20server-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Router-333333?style=flat-square) ![Auth0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth0-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FlexCred.UPI solves the problem of failed digital payments due to insufficient balance in UPI transactions. In real life, people often need to make urgent payments even when their bank balance is temporarily low, and many users do not have access to credit cards or formal credit. When a UPI payment fails, users may be forced to delay the purchase or turn to high-interest lending apps, while merchants lose potential sales. FlexCred.UPI introduces an instant micro-credit layer during the payment process, allowing the system to offer small credit automatically when the user’s balance is insufficient so the transaction can still complete. This makes everyday payments like groceries, transportation, medical purchases, or small bills easier and more reliable, while also improving payment success rates for merchants and expanding financial access for users who lack traditional credit options.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was designing a system that could provide instant micro-credit without overcomplicating the architecture within the limited hackathon time. Since real UPI systems are highly regulated and controlled by banking infrastructure, we had to simulate the payment environment while still making the concept technically realistic. Another challenge was deciding how to calculate credit limits and risk quickly, so we implemented a simple rule-based credit scoring model instead of a complex AI system. We also had to balance between building a working prototype and explaining the financial infrastructure clearly, ensuring that the solution demonstrates how such a middleware credit layer could realistically operate within existing digital payment ecosystems.

### MANASSAATHI AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/manassaathi-ai-6c6c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/amank9115/Ai-Enabled-Autism-Screening-Platform.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> AI Powered Early Autism Screening

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Autism is a developmental condition that often goes undetected during the early stages of childhood. Early identification is critical because timely intervention can significantly improve a child’s cognitive, social, and communication development. However, many parents struggle to recognize early behavioral signs, and access to specialists is often limited or delayed, especially in remote or underserved areas.

Our platform ManasSaathi AI addresses this problem by providing an AI-assisted behavioral screening system that allows parents to perform an initial assessment using a simple camera-based interface. The system analyzes behavioral indicators such as eye contact, attention patterns, facial expressions, and interaction behavior.

The platform helps in:

- Early behavioral screening: Parents can identify potential developmental concerns earlier than traditional diagnosis timelines.

- Doctor-assisted review: Recorded sessions and AI-generated insights can be shared with doctors for professional evaluation.

- Accessible screening: Families in areas with limited access to specialists can still perform preliminary assessments.

- Continuous monitoring: Parents can track behavioral patterns across multiple sessions.

- Faster clinical support: Doctors receive structured behavioral data before consultation, helping them make informed decisions.


By combining artificial intelligence with accessible digital tools, the platform aims to bridge the gap between early behavioral observation and professional medical consultation, making early autism screening more accessible, efficient, and supportive for both parents and healthcare professionals.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building ManasSaathi AI, we encountered several technical and design challenges during the development process.

One of the main challenges was integrating real-time camera-based behavior analysis with a web application. Processing live video data while maintaining smooth performance on the frontend required careful optimization. To handle this, we separated the system into a frontend interface and an AI processing module, allowing the camera stream to be analyzed independently without affecting the user interface.

Another challenge was designing a reliable behavioral indicator system. Autism screening is a sensitive domain, and it is important not to present AI outputs as medical diagnoses. We addressed this by designing the platform to provide behavioral indicators such as eye contact, attention level, and emotional signals, rather than making medical conclusions. This ensures the system acts as a screening support tool for doctors and parents, not a replacement for professional diagnosis.

We also faced challenges in managing user experience for different roles, such as parents and doctors. To solve this, we implemented separate dashboards and workflows that allow parents to perform screenings and doctors to review recorded sessions and behavioral insights.

Finally, coordinating frontend development with backend integration required careful planning to avoid conflicts in the codebase. We organized the project structure into modular components and APIs, which allowed both parts of the system to be developed and integrated smoothly.

These challenges helped us design a more robust and scalable system that can evolve into a practical AI-assisted screening platform.

**Requestly – Creative Use Challenge**

Our project involves multiple components such as frontend interfaces, backend APIs, and AI-based behavioral analysis modules. During development and testing, tools like Requestly can be highly useful for debugging and modifying network requests in real time.

In a system like ManasSaathi AI, where the frontend communicates with backend services and AI processing APIs, Requestly can help developers:

Inspect and modify API requests between the frontend and backend during development.

Simulate different server responses to test various behavioral analysis outputs without modifying backend code.

Debug network issues and ensure that AI analysis results and user data are transferred correctly.

Test edge cases such as delayed responses, error handling, or unexpected API results.

Using tools like Requestly improves the development workflow, debugging efficiency, and reliability of the system, especially when working with real-time video processing and API-based AI analysis.

### Agriloop Marketplace
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agriloop-marketplace-4756) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AlokGond/AgriLoop) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://agri-loop-eight.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Stop Burning!! Start Earning.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

After harvesting paddy/Many Different Types of other seeds in regions like Punjab and Haryana and Bihar & Many More States. farmers have a very short window of about 14–21 days to prepare their fields for the next wheat. Removing crop residue (stubble or parali) using machines is expensive, while burning it is cheap and fast. Because of this time pressure and cost difference, many farmers choose to burn the residue. This practice releases large amounts of PM 2.5  ( microscopic airborne particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres—about 30 times smaller than a human hair—that pose severe health risks by penetrating deep into the lungs and bloodstream) and carbon emissions, causing severe air pollution and increasing respiratory health problems in nearby cities and villages.
Also Soil Fertilizer Problem Due To Stubble Burnning. 

1. Short Time Window
After paddy harvesting, farmers have only 14–21 days to clear fields before wheat sowing.
2. High Cost of Machines
Removing stubble with machines costs ₹3000–₹4000 per acre, which many farmers cannot afford.
3. Burning is Cheaper
Burning crop residue costs only ₹500, so farmers choose this option.
4. Severe Air Pollution
Burning releases PM2.5 and CO₂, causing major air pollution and respiratory diseases.
5. Supply Chain Gap
Industries like biomass plants and paper mills need crop residue, but there is no platform connecting farmers, machine operators, and buyers.

At the same time, this crop residue is not actually waste — it can be used as raw material for- 
1. biomass energy plants,
2. paper industries,
3. And other bio based products.

However, there is currently no efficient system that connects farmers who have residue, machine operators who can collect it, and industries that need it. This gap in the supply chain leads to wasted resources and environmental damage. 

It helps:
•	Farmers clear fields quickly
•	Farmers earn money from crop residue
•	Operators get optimized work routes
•	Industries get biomass supply
Instead of burning waste → it becomes a resource.

**Challenges we ran into**

While developing the Agri-Loop application, we encountered various challenges. One of the key challenges we encountered while developing the application was to create a system that links three different types of users, i.e., farmers, machine operators, and industrial buyers. To do this in a simple manner, we had to plan the database accordingly.

Another challenge we encountered while developing the application was to create a system that allows users to see updates in real time. For instance, the farmers create a pickup request, and the operators need to see the request in real time. To do this, we used Firebase Cloud Firestore to create a system that allows users to see updates in real time.

Another challenge we encountered while developing the application was to create a system that links the map services to the application. To do this, we used the Leaflet Maps service to create a system that allows users to see the pickup locations on the dashboard.

### RAT(REMOTE ACCESS TROJAN)
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ratremote-access-trojan-26de) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> MAlWARE ANALAYSIS

![Request Network](https://img.shields.io/badge/Request%20Network-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket Programming](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket%20Programming-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Pillow](https://img.shields.io/badge/Pillow-333333?style=flat-square) ![Robot Operating System](https://img.shields.io/badge/Robot%20Operating%20System-333333?style=flat-square) ![WireGuard](https://img.shields.io/badge/WireGuard-333333?style=flat-square) ![Subprocess](https://img.shields.io/badge/Subprocess-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV / cv2](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV%20/%20cv2-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

a RAT is built on a genuine, critical IT need: how do you manage, monitor, or control a computer you're not physically sitting at?
This is one of the most fundamental challenges in all of IT:

Servers live in data centers thousands of miles away
Employees work from home or travel
IT teams support hundreds/thousands of machines
Critical systems need 24/7 monitoring without human presence

The underlying technology (remote access + persistent connection + stealth/efficiency) is completely legitimate. The "trojan" part is what makes it malicious — it's installed without consent and hides its presence.
The Real Problem It Solves
Before remote access tools existed, if a server crashed at 3am you had to physically drive to the data center. If an employee's laptop had an issue, IT had to walk over. If you ran 500 machines, you needed 500 people or constant physical rounds.
RATs (and their legitimate cousins) solved:

Distance — manage anything from anywhere
Scale — one admin managing thousands of endpoints
Speed — instant response to incidents without travel
Persistence — survive reboots, maintain always-on monitoring
Low overhead — run silently in the background without disrupting the user
Legitimate Real-World Use Cases
1.  Enterprise IT & Help Desk
Tools like TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Microsoft SCCM let IT support staff remotely take over an employee's screen to fix issues. Massive companies run entire support desks this way — no one flies to fix your Excel problem.
2.  Server & Infrastructure Management
SSH, RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol), Bastion Hosts — sysadmins manage Linux/Windows servers this way. AWS, Azure, GCP — every cloud server you manage is accessed via remote access protocols that share DNA with RAT architecture.
3.  Security Operations (SOC / IR)
Security teams deploy EDR agents (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Carbon Black) that sit silently on every endpoint, sending telemetry, and allowing analysts to remotely kill processes, pull files, or isolate machines — this is architecturally very similar to a RAT.
4.  MDM — Mobile Device Management
Jamf, Intune, VMware Workspace ONE — corporations remotely manage, wipe, lock, or push software to thousands of phones and laptops. Same concept: persistent agent, remote command execution.
5.  Critical Infrastructure Monitoring
Power plants, hospitals, and factories use SCADA/ICS remote monitoring — sensors and control systems that allow engineers to read data and send commands to equipment remotely. A misconfigured or hijacked version of this is one of the scariest attack scenarios in cybersecurity.
6.  Game / Application Anti-Cheat & Telemetry
Many games and enterprise apps run kernel-level agents (Valorant's Vanguard, etc.) that monitor system state persistently — controversial precisely because they resemble RAT behavior.
7. 

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/520e51e48ead4b22b5ecbfdecf5729cc/69893638-ebc5-472c-b407-4ed8ba0cd7cc.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/520e51e48ead4b22b5ecbfdecf5729cc/7c3fe659-4a16-4944-8734-d11f18785d5b.jpeg)

Security professionals use tools like Cobalt Strike, Metasploit, Havoc C2 — which are essentially controlled RATs — to simulate real attacker behavior so organizations can test their defenses. Completely legal when authorized.

The Key Distinction (Critical for Malware Analysis)
FeatureLegitimate ToolMalicious RATConsentUser/org knows & approvesInstalled secretlyVisibilityShows in task manager, add/remove programsHides from OSControlControlled by the ownerControlled by attackerPurposeProductivity / securityData theft, espionage, botnetC2 channelKnown, documented serverHidden, encrypted, bulletproof hosting

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
Making the Agent Run Silently in the Background
The biggest hurdle I faced was getting the monitoring agent to run persistently in the background without showing a visible console window or being easily spotted by the user.
Initially, every time the script executed, Python would spawn a terminal window — which completely defeats the purpose of a monitoring tool. My first instinct was to just rename the script or bundle it, but that didn't solve the underlying problem.
What I tried first (that didn't work):
python# This still flashes a console window on Windows
subprocess.Popen(["python", "agent.py"])
The fix — using pythonw.exe and CREATE_NO_WINDOW flag:
On Windows, switching from python.exe to pythonw.exe suppresses the console entirely. For subprocess calls, I had to pass the CREATE_NO_WINDOW flag explicitly:
pythonimport subprocess

CREATE_NO_WINDOW = 0x08000000
subprocess.Popen(
    ["python", "agent.py"],
    creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW
)
For persistence across reboots, I ran into a second layer of the same problem — startup registry entries and Task Scheduler would re-launch the script visibly. Getting the flags right there took significant debugging and reading through Windows API docs.
On Linux, the equivalent challenge was daemonizing the process properly — a naive & background job would die when the terminal session closed. The proper fix was using a double-fork pattern:
pythonimport os, sys

def daemonize():
    if os.fork() > 0:
        sys.exit(0)       # kill parent
    os.setsid()           # new session
    if os.fork() > 0:
        sys.exit(0)       # kill second parent
    # now fully detached

What I Learned
This challenge taught me a lot about how the OS manages processes and sessions — something that's easy to take for granted. It also gave me direct insight into why real-world malware uses these exact same techniques, and how defenders can detect them by watching for pythonw.exe spawns, suspicious registry run keys, or orphaned processes with no parent terminal. Building the "wrong" thing first made the right solution stick.

**Requestly – Creative Use Challenge**

our monitoring app deals heavily with network requests (sending IP data, location logs, screenshots remotely). Requestly fits naturally:

Use it to intercept and inspect the HTTP requests your agent sends
Mock server responses to test how your agent behaves when the C2 server is down
Modify headers to simulate different network environments

### JobGuardAI

> NLP + Crowdsourcing: The End of Fake Job Offers

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In 2026, fake job postings and recruitment scams have become a major global problem, especially for students, fresh graduates, and job seekers. With the growth of online job portals, social media recruitment, and messaging platforms, scammers are increasingly posting fraudulent job offers that look legitimate but are designed to steal money, personal information, or sensitive documents.

Many job seekers receive offers promising high salaries, easy work-from-home opportunities, or immediate hiring. These postings often use generic greetings, suspicious email domains, unrealistic salary packages, and AI-generated descriptions to appear professional. Unsuspecting candidates are then asked to pay registration fees, training charges, or provide personal information such as bank details, identification documents, or passwords.

The problem is made worse because most job platforms do not have strong automated systems to verify job authenticity. As a result, thousands of fake postings circulate online daily. Students and fresh graduates—who may lack experience in identifying scams—are particularly vulnerable.

These scams cause several serious issues:

Financial Loss: Victims often pay fake application or training fees.

Identity Theft: Personal documents like Aadhaar, passports, or bank details can be stolen.

Wasted Time and Effort: Candidates spend time applying and preparing for jobs that do not exist.

Loss of Trust: Genuine companies and job platforms lose credibility because of fake listings.

Psychological Stress: Victims may experience anxiety, embarrassment, or loss of confidence.

Currently, identifying fake jobs requires manual verification, which is slow, unreliable, and difficult for individuals. There is no widely accessible intelligent system that can instantly analyze and flag suspicious job postings.

Solution: JobGuard AI

JobGuardAI aims to solve this problem by creating an AI-powered verification system that analyzes job postings using Natural Language Processing (NLP), machine learning, and crowdsourced reporting. The platform evaluates job descriptions, salary claims, recruiter emai

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges we faced while developing JobGuardAI was accurately detecting fake job postings using Natural Language Processing (NLP). Initially, our AI model struggled to correctly classify job descriptions because many fake job postings were written in a very professional and convincing way, making them appear legitimate to the system.

The Problem

At the beginning of the project, our machine learning model was trained on a small dataset of job postings. Because of this:

The model misclassified many fake jobs as legitimate.

Some genuine job posts were incorrectly flagged as scams (false positives).

The accuracy was below our target, which made the system unreliable for users.

Another hurdle was that fake job postings often used slightly modified wording to bypass detection. For example, scammers changed phrases like “registration fee” to “processing charge” or “training deposit”, which confused the model.

### Eduvibe
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/eduvibe-73ba) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Vasu-gera/EduVibe) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Learn Anything, Teach Anything

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

While the internet has democratized information, it has failed to democratize mentorship. Learning complex skills (like React, Day Trading, or UI Design) via pre-recorded videos or tutorials often leaves learners stuck, frustrated, and unable to ask specific questions when they hit a wall.

Access to a real 1-on-1 human mentor is currently constrained by two massive hurdles: you either need to be lucky enough to have a personal connection in the industry, or wealthy enough to afford a $10,000+ bootcamp.

The Solution: EduVibe is a peer-to-peer live learning ecosystem that turns anyone into a student today, and a teacher tomorrow. It solves the mentorship gap by:

1. Smart AI Matching: Learners don't have to endlessly scroll. They simply type their learning goal, and our integration of the Gemini 2.0 instantly breaks down the required skills and matches them with the perfect expert.
2. Frictionless Economics: By natively integrating Stripe, users can securely pay for premium 1-on-1 sessions, while community-driven "Free Sessions" trigger a fast-path zero-click enrollment.
3. Native Video Classrooms: We eliminated the friction of hunting for Zoom links by building a Jitsi Meet infrastructure directly into the browser. The entire classroom experience happens inside the platform.
4. AI-Powered Roadmaps: After a live call, the AI generates a structured, actionable summary of the topics covered, giving the learner a concrete set of next steps.
5. EduVibe makes skill acquisition faster, highly interactive, and community-driven.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a seamless, live peer-to-peer marketplace within the hackathon timeframe presented several distinct technical hurdles:

1. Creating a Frictionless Video Experience

- The Hurdle: We initially looked at using standard WebRTC or relying on external Zoom/Google Meet links, but this created massive drop-off friction for users who had to leave our platform to join a class.
- The Solution: We pivoted to implementing the Jitsi Meet API. By embedding Jitsi directly into our React frontend via an iframe, we dynamically generate unique video rooms based on the sessionTopic slug. This kept users 100% engaged inside the EduVibe dashboard without requiring them to install third-party apps.

2. Handling Asynchronous Payment Flows

- The Hurdle: Managing the state between a user clicking "Book", leaving our site to pay on a hosted Stripe Checkout page, and returning safely to confirm the booking in our MongoDB database was highly prone to race conditions and lost data.
- The Solution: We decoupled the payment from the session creation. We pass critical metadata (like mentorId, time, and topic) directly into the Stripe success_url as encoded query parameters. When Stripe redirects the user back to our PaymentSuccess React component, the frontend reads those parameters and makes a final secure API call to fulfill the booking in MongoDB.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/focus-flow-a0ed) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/chaitanya-1106/Focus-Flow) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://focusflowhierarchy.netlify.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> The Deep Work Guardian

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In the modern digital landscape, the primary obstacle to success isn't a lack of effort, but the prevalence of "Pseudo-Productivity."
Fragmentation of Attention: The average student fragments their focus every 5 to 10 minutes by checking social media or notifications. Because of the "Cognitive Switching Penalty," it takes the human brain an average of 23 minutes to return to a state of deep focus after a single interruption.
The "Passive Timer" Flaw: Most existing productivity tools (like basic Pomodoro timers) are passive; they measure time spent at a desk but do not actively prevent a user from opening distracting applications.
Quality vs. Quantity Gap: There is often a massive disconnect between "hours sat at a laptop" and "actual deep work performed." Without a specialized scoring system, users cannot accurately quantify their efficiency or identify their "productivity killers."
Lack of Verifiable Integrity: In an era of remote learning and high-stakes assignments, students lack a tamper-proof way to certify their genuine focus and hard work to mentors or institutions

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a comprehensive "Deep Work Guardian" required overcoming several significant hurdles:
Real-Time Interception Logic: Developing a system that monitors active processes and triggers instant warnings or auto-close sequences for blacklisted apps within a seamless React state-management environment was a primary technical challenge.
Context-Aware Architecture: Creating a modular "Category" system (Coding, Research, Assignment) that dynamically swaps whitelists and blacklists without system lag or crashes required complex architectural planning.
Quantifying the "Flow State": Designing a "Deep Work Algorithm" was a major strategic challenge. We had to move beyond simple time-tracking to create a weighted score (A+ to D grade) based on distraction frequency, session length, and focus consistency.
Ensuring Data Immunity: To make session reports viable for academic integrity, we had to implement a concept for AES-256 encrypted logs. This ensures that a user cannot manually edit their focus data to "pad" their study hours.
Minimizing Interface Friction: A significant design challenge was building a high-density dashboard (containing heatmaps and analytics) that provides all necessary data at a glance without becoming a distraction itself.

> TrustBuy – Shop Smart, Trust Real Reviews.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TextBlob](https://img.shields.io/badge/TextBlob-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Fake and Manipulated Online Reviews**:-

-A significant portion of reviews on e-commerce platforms are fake, paid, or generated by bots.

-Studies estimate that 20–30% of online reviews are fabricated on major marketplaces.

-These fake reviews mislead consumers, making low-quality products appear trustworthy.

-Honest businesses suffer, because competitors can artificially boost ratings.

-Current platforms rely heavily on unverified community feedback, which can easily be manipulated.

**Why This Matters**

-Consumers waste money on poor products.

-Marketplaces lose credibility and user trust.

-The rise of AI-generated reviews and bot networks makes the problem even harder to detect manually.

-What TrustBuy Addresses

**TrustBuy solves this by analyzing review data using NLP and statistical techniques to detect suspicious patterns and generate a reliable Trust Score, helping users quickly understand whether product reviews are genuine or manipulated.**

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Detecting Subtle Fake Reviews**
Fake reviews are becoming increasingly sophisticated. Many are written to look natural, making it difficult to distinguish them from genuine feedback using simple keyword checks.

**2. Text Similarity Detection at Scale**
Identifying duplicated or highly similar reviews across large datasets required efficient text comparison techniques and optimization to avoid slow processing.

**3. Sentiment Analysis Accuracy**
Not all positive reviews are fake. Designing a system that flags unnatural sentiment patterns without falsely accusing genuine reviews was a key challenge.

**4. Data Quality Issues**
Real-world review datasets often contain missing fields, inconsistent formatting, or duplicate entries, which required preprocessing and cleaning before analysis.

**5. Converting Complex Analysis into a Simple Score**
We needed to transform multiple detection signals (similarity, sentiment, user duplication) into a single understandable Trust Score (0–100) that users could interpret easily.

**6. Building a Fast and Scalable Pipeline**
Ensuring the system could analyze uploaded datasets quickly while maintaining accuracy required balancing performance between the React frontend and FastAPI backend.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agrosync-8700) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Satyamsharma990/AgroSync) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ALE3cfqT-aU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Where Farms and Intelligence Stay in Sync.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square) ![API3](https://img.shields.io/badge/API3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Agriculture often depends on experience, assumptions, and scattered information rather than clear, data-driven insights. Many farmers do not have quick access to reliable guidance about crop selection, soil health, disease identification, irrigation planning, or market trends. As a result, important decisions are sometimes made with incomplete knowledge, which can lead to lower crop yields, higher costs, and increased risk of crop failure.

Another challenge is that agricultural information is usually spread across multiple sources such as government portals, research papers, weather platforms, and agricultural experts. Accessing and interpreting this information requires time, technical knowledge, and sometimes internet literacy that many farmers may not have. This gap makes it difficult to convert raw data into practical actions at the field level.

AgroSync addresses this issue by providing a unified AI-powered system that converts agricultural data into simple, actionable insights. Instead of searching through multiple platforms or relying only on traditional guesswork, users can input their farming conditions—such as soil details, crop type, weather conditions, or observed symptoms—and receive intelligent recommendations in real time.

What People Can Use It For

AgroSync helps farmers and agricultural stakeholders perform several tasks more efficiently:

Crop Planning: Suggests suitable crops based on soil properties, climate conditions, and seasonal factors.

Soil Health Analysis: Evaluates nutrient levels and recommends fertilizers or soil improvements.

Disease Identification: Assists in identifying potential crop diseases using observed symptoms and environmental conditions.

Irrigation Guidance: Recommends optimal watering schedules and methods to conserve water and improve crop growth.

Market Awareness: Provides insights about potential price trends and selling strategies.

Multilingual Interaction: Allows farmers to interact with the system in their preferred language, making the platform more accessible.

How It Makes Tasks Easier and Safer

By combining AI analysis with structured agricultural knowledge, AgroSync simplifies complex decision-making. Farmers no longer need to interpret raw datasets or consult multiple sources manually. Instead, the system transforms agricultural inputs into clear recommendations, helping users make informed decisions faster.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building AgroSync involved several technical and practical challenges during development. One of the major hurdles was integrating AI-powered responses while keeping the system reliable and cost-efficient.

1. Managing AI API Costs

A key feature of AgroSync is the use of AI to generate insights for crop recommendations, soil analysis, irrigation advice, and disease identification. Initially, the system relied heavily on AI API calls for every feature request. However, this quickly revealed a challenge: frequent API requests can increase operational costs, especially when using large language models for real-time analysis.

For a platform intended to support farmers at scale, uncontrolled API usage could make the system expensive to maintain. To address this issue, the system was redesigned to optimize how and when AI calls are made. Instead of sending unnecessary or repeated requests, the application now structures inputs carefully and sends only essential data to the AI model. This reduces the number of API calls while still producing meaningful insights.

Additionally, a lightweight model configuration was used for faster and more cost-efficient responses, ensuring that the application remains practical for demonstration and potential real-world deployment.

2. Structuring AI Responses

Another challenge was ensuring that the AI consistently returned information in a structured format that the frontend could display. Early responses from the model were sometimes inconsistent, which made it difficult to render results properly in the user interface.

This was solved by designing strict prompts and structured response formats so that the AI always returns data in a predictable structure. This allowed the frontend components to display recommendations, analysis, and advice without additional manual processing.

3. Integrating Multiple Features into One System

AgroSync includes several modules—such as crop recommendations, soil analysis, irrigation guidance, and disease detection. Combining these features into a single platform required careful design so that the system could process different types of agricultural inputs without creating conflicts or redundant logic.

The solution was to build a centralized AI interaction layer that routes different feature requests to the AI engine while maintaining a consistent output format.

Outcome

By addressing these challenges, the platform became more stable, scalable, and efficient. The system now generates realistic agricultural insights while controlling resource usage and maintaining a smooth user experience.

Calculate accurate shoe size

Display a 3D shoe overlay on the user's foot

Allow users to see how the shoe looks before buying

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Faced During Development

While building FootView AI, we faced several technical challenges related to integrating Augmented Reality, real-time camera input, and 3D rendering in a web environment.

One of the main challenges was setting up the AR overlay using Three.js and React Three Fiber. Aligning the 3D shoe model correctly with the user's foot position was difficult because real-time camera coordinates needed to be mapped to the 3D scene. We experimented with different coordinate scaling and positioning techniques to ensure that the shoe appeared naturally over the detected foot area.

Another challenge was handling camera access and real-time video rendering in the browser. Browser security restrictions and device compatibility issues sometimes prevented the camera from initializing correctly. We solved this by properly configuring the camera permissions and optimizing the video stream handling.

We also encountered issues with project structure and dependency management, especially when integrating multiple libraries like Vite, React Three Fiber, and MediaPipe. Some conflicts occurred due to mixing JavaScript and TypeScript files. We resolved this by standardizing the project structure and cleaning unnecessary files.

Finally, achieving a smooth and intuitive user interface was important for the overall experience. We improved the UI by implementing a modern, futuristic design that makes the AR try-on system feel interactive and user-friendly.

Through debugging, experimentation, and collaboration, we successfully overcame these challenges and built a working prototype of the AR-based virtual shoe try-on system.

### AI Decision Intelligent System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-decision-intelligent-system-ecc2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Krish-codex/AI-Decision-Engine) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/5W2P1VHL8pg) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Turn decisions into simulations.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Organizations make critical strategic decisions every day, such as acquisitions, layoffs, market expansion, and product launches. These decisions usually involve multiple departments like finance, HR, and operations, and gathering insights from each of them can take significant time.

As a result, leaders often make decisions with fragmented information or rely heavily on intuition, which increases the risk of costly mistakes. Many strategic decisions fail because potential risks, unintended consequences, or alternative strategies are not fully explored beforehand.

This project solves that problem by providing a platform that simulates a boardroom-style analysis using multiple AI agents.

Users can enter a decision, and the system analyzes it from different perspectives such as financial impact, employee effects, hidden consequences, and strategic risks. The platform then generates a structured decision report with risk scores, scenario projections, and recommendations.

By doing this, the system helps users:

Identify risks before implementing a decision

Consider multiple perspectives quickly

Explore alternative strategies

Make more informed and structured decisions

In short, the platform makes complex decision-making faster, more transparent, and less prone to oversight.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. LLM Output Inconsistency

One major challenge was that Large Language Models sometimes return responses that do not strictly follow the expected JSON format. This caused parsing errors when the backend tried to extract fields like risk levels or scenario analysis.

Solution:
I implemented a robust parsing layer that:

Uses structured prompts requesting strict JSON output.

Adds fallback regex-based extraction when JSON parsing fails.

Includes validation checks to ensure all required fields are present before aggregation.

This significantly improved the reliability of the system.

2. Running Multiple AI Agents in Parallel

The system uses four specialized AI agents that must analyze the same decision simultaneously. Initially, running them sequentially made the analysis slow (10–15 seconds).

Solution:
I used Python’s ThreadPoolExecutor to execute all four agents in parallel. This reduced the total analysis time to about 4–5 seconds, making the system feel much more responsive.

3. Converting Qualitative AI Responses into Numerical Risk Scores

AI agents return qualitative labels such as Low, Moderate, or High. However, the platform needed a numerical risk score to generate recommendations.

Solution:
I built a risk scoring engine that maps qualitative labels to numerical values and computes a weighted average across agents. This allowed the system to produce a consistent 0–10 risk score and structured recommendations.

4. API Rate Limits

Using free AI APIs introduced rate limits that sometimes caused agents to fail.

Solution:
I implemented:

Multiple API keys (one per agent)

Retry logic

Provider fallback support

This ensured the system continues working even if one API request fails.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Nodemailer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Nodemailer-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Sheild is a proactive, AI-driven safety ecosystem designed to protect tourists through real-time predictive intelligence. By leveraging live GPS tracking and behavioral anomaly detection, it warns users before they enter high-risk zones, transforming traditional reactive alerts into a preventative safety shield. Our mission is to empower authorities with a data-driven dashboard that visualizes tourist clusters and incident heatmaps, ensuring rapid, precision-targeted assistance.

**Challenges we ran into**

Hurdle: Dynamic Risk Visualization

Problem: Map libraries natively only support single-color navigation paths. We needed the route to change color (Red/Yellow/Green) in real-time as it entered or exited risk zones.
Solution: Developed a custom Polyline Segmentation Algorithm using the Haversine formula to "cut" the navigation path into separate, color-coded fragments whenever it intersects with crime heatmaps.
Hurdle: Reliable Emergency Triggers

Problem: The Twilio SDK would occasionally fail to initialize during rapid backend restarts, creating a risk of missed emergency alerts.
Solution: Implemented "Lazy Initialization" and Auto-Retry logic in the backend controller to ensure the SMS/Call client triggers reliably the moment an emergency is activated.

### Memory Search
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/memory-search-engine-ea69) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ravish706/Memory-Search) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Search your mind, not just your files.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square) ![chromadb](https://img.shields.io/badge/chromadb-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ollama](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ollama-333333?style=flat-square) ![pypdf](https://img.shields.io/badge/pypdf-333333?style=flat-square) ![watchdog](https://img.shields.io/badge/watchdog-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

You have years of knowledge trapped in files you cannot find.

Keyword search fails because you never remember the exact words you used. Cloud AI tools solve it but read your private data. Manual organization systems work for two weeks then collapse.
This solves three problems simultaneously:
Retrieval failure — you wrote something important, you know it exists, you cannot find it. This makes everything you have ever written permanently accessible by what you meant, not what you typed.
Privacy sacrifice — every tool that searches by meaning requires sending your data to an external server. This is the only one that does not.
Capture friction — every personal knowledge system dies because feeding it requires new habits. This feeds itself passively from folders you already use, apps you already have, habits you already follow.

**Challenges we ran into**

1.The very first hurdle. Installing chromadb on Windows failed immediately because it depends on hnswlib — a C++ library for vector search. pip tried to compile it from source, found no Microsoft Visual C++ compiler, and threw a wall of errors.

2.Pydantic Version Conflict

3. Models were running painfully slowly — 15 to 30 seconds per response. Running ollama ps showed 100% CPU despite having an NVIDIA RTX 2050 installed.

How we got over it: The diagnosis came from understanding the VRAM constraint. The RTX 2050 has exactly 4GB VRAM. llama3.1:8b requires 5GB. Ollama silently falls back to CPU when the model does not fit — no warning, no error message, just slow responses. Switched to gemma3:4b which needs only 2.5GB VRAM, fits comfortably, and runs on GPU. Response time dropped from 25 seconds to 2 seconds.

Team **Nava_Sankalp** -- Sahil Ahmad, Ayush Kumar, Raghav Dadwal, Ravish Raj

**The problem it solves**

University Placement Cells:
To manage large-scale student databases and corporate drive schedules.
To automate mass communication without hiring a dedicated calling team.
Students:
To receive personalized job alerts that actually match their skills.
To get 24/7 support through the AI Chatbot for placement-related queries (deadlines, eligibility, etc.).
Corporate Relations Teams:
To quickly identify the "Top 10%" or most relevant candidates for a specific company role using the AI Matcher.
⚡ How it makes existing tasks easier?
From Manual Screening to AI Insights:
Old Way: Coordinators read hundreds of resumes to find a "Java Developer".
Placentra Way: The AI analyzes resumes the moment they are uploaded and tags students automatically. Searching for a specific role is now as simple as a database query.
From Calling Chains to Automated IVR:
Old Way: Calling 100 students takes 4-5 hours of manual labor.
Placentra Way: "Reverse Match" triggers automated calls instantly. You can notify an entire batch in the time it takes to sip a cup of coffee.
Centralized "No-Code" Management:
Coordinators don't need to be tech-savvy. They can update Twilio details, coordinator info, and company links directly from the Settings panel without touching a single line of code.
🛡️ How it makes tasks safer & more reliable?
Data Privacy (On-Premise AI):
Most AI tools send student resumes to the cloud (OpenAI/Google). Placentra uses Local LLMs (Llama 3.2 via Ollama). This means student resumes never leave your local server, ensuring 100% data privacy and compliance.
Secure Authentication:
Student Portal: Uses OTP-based login. This eliminates the risk of weak passwords and ensures only students with registered emails can access sensitive placement data.
Admin Security: The portal is protected by a dedicated admin credentials system, allowing you to change passwords frequently to prevent unauthorized access.
Credential Masking:
Sensitive information like Twilio Auth Tokens and SMTP passwords are stored in Environment Variables (

.env
), keeping them hidden from the source code and protected from potential leaks on GitHub.
Verified Communication:
The Voice Bot verifies the student’s identity ("Is this [Name] speaking?") before providing information, ensuring that sensitive drive details are only shared with the intended recipient.

**The problem it solves**

Lack of Financial Literacy: Many women do not receive formal education about:
•	Budgeting
•	Investing
•	Financial planning

Complex Financial Platforms: Most financial platforms are designed for experienced investors and are too complicated for beginners.

Lack of Accessible Guidance: Women often lack trusted financial guidance or mentorship.

Fragmented Financial Tools: Budgeting, learning, investment tracking, and financial assistance information exist on separate platforms.

Limited Awareness of Government Schemes: Many beneficial government schemes remain unknown to women due to poor accessibility.

**Challenges we ran into**

While developing the Aarvika platform, several challenges were encountered during both the technical implementation and feature integration stages. One major problem was managing data persistence for financial records, especially ensuring that expenses entered by users were correctly stored and retrieved after login. Designing a user-friendly interface for financial tools such as expense tracking, savings monitoring, and investment simulation was also challenging because the platform needed to remain simple enough for beginners while still offering useful functionality. Finally, coordinating multiple technologies in the tech stack—including React, backend services, database integration, and external APIs—required debugging compatibility issues and ensuring smooth communication between all components of the system.

**The problem it solves**

This food delivery platform is designed to make ordering food easier, faster, and more convenient for users. People can use the website to browse different food items from restaurants, view images of dishes, add items to their cart, and place an order online without needing to visit the restaurant physically. The platform simplifies the entire process by allowing users to select food, review their order, enter their delivery address, and choose a payment method all in one place. This reduces the time and effort required compared to traditional ordering methods such as calling restaurants or waiting in long queues.

The platform also improves safety and convenience by enabling contactless ordering and digital payments. Users can clearly see the food items, prices, and order details before confirming their purchase, which helps reduce mistakes and confusion. By bringing multiple restaurant options together on a single website, the platform allows customers to quickly compare choices and order their favorite meals in just a few clicks. Overall, the system makes food ordering more efficient, user-friendly, and accessible for people with busy schedules who want a quick and reliable way to get food delivered.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building this project, one of the main hurdles we faced was making the cart and checkout system work properly across different pages of the website. Initially, when a user added food items to the cart and clicked the checkout button, the cart information would disappear when the next page opened. This happened because the cart data was not being stored anywhere once the page changed. As a result, the selected items could not be displayed on the checkout or payment page. To solve this problem, we used the browser’s localStorage feature in JavaScript, which allows data to be saved temporarily in the user’s browser. By storing the cart items in localStorage before moving to the checkout page and retrieving the same data on the next page, we were able to keep the cart information throughout the ordering process. This solution helped us fix the issue and ensured that users could smoothly move from adding items to the cart to completing their order.

### ParcelGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/parcelguard-f746) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Satvik-creator/ParcelGuard.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/o56r6K6gQL0) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/o56r6K6gQL0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Every parcel. Every checkpoint. Zero fraud.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLAlchemy](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLAlchemy-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

India's e-commerce industry loses over ₹10,000 crore annually to supply chain fraud — 
empty boxes, switched products, tampered parcels, and fake deliveries. Existing systems 
have no way to detect fraud mid-transit. By the time a customer complains, the evidence 
is gone and accountability is impossible.

**ParcelGuard solves this with AI-powered verification at every checkpoint:**

- **Sellers** upload an X-ray scan, packing photo, and product photo when the parcel 
  is packed at the warehouse
- **Couriers** scan the parcel at every handoff point — pickup, sorting hub, and delivery
- **AI compares** each checkpoint photo against the original packing photo using 
  ResNet50 image similarity, and also checks weight, RFID tag, and dimensions
- **Fraud is scored 0–100** in real time. Anything above 70 auto-creates an investigation 
  case with full evidence trail
- **Trust scores** track every seller and courier over time — repeat offenders get 
  flagged and suspended automatically

The result: end-to-end accountability from warehouse to doorstep, with zero manual 
investigation overhead for clean parcels.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Real-time AI scoring without a GPU server**
Integrating ResNet50 image similarity in a hackathon environment meant we couldn't 
rely on a cloud GPU. We optimised the pipeline to run inference on CPU using 
TorchVision's pretrained weights and cosine similarity, keeping response time under 2 
seconds per checkpoint scan.

**2. Designing a weighted fraud formula from scratch**
There was no existing dataset to train on. We researched real e-commerce fraud patterns 
and designed a weighted scoring engine: Image Δ (40%) + Weight Δ (25%) + RFID (20%) + 
Dimensions (15%). Calibrating thresholds so legitimate parcels weren't falsely flagged 
took multiple iterations.

**3. Multi-image evidence chain**
Linking three separate images (packing photo, checkpoint photo, customer photo) to the 
same parcel across different actors required careful database schema design and a 
stateful audit trail that couldn't be tampered with retroactively.

**4. Trust score decay system**
Building a fair trust scoring system that penalises fraud but rewards clean streaks — 
without being too harsh on new sellers — required careful tuning of the penalty and 
recovery weights.

**5. Full-stack integration under time pressure**
Connecting a FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL database, two React frontends (Ops Portal + 
Customer Portal), and an AI service layer — all within a hackathon timeline — required 
strict API contract discipline and modular architecture from day one.

Team **Byte_Coders** -- [Devansh Bansal](https://github.com/DevanshBansal08), [Satvik Kapoor](https://github.com/Satvik-creator), Apoorva Dixit, RaviRanjan Bhardwaj

> "Fikar not, Karigar on the spot"

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![v0](https://img.shields.io/badge/v0-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

KarigarHub

Problem

Finding reliable local service workers such as electricians, plumbers, carpenters, or repair technicians can be difficult. People often rely on word-of-mouth recommendations or random contacts, which may lead to unreliable service, unclear pricing, and lack of accountability. At the same time, many skilled workers struggle to gain visibility and find consistent job opportunities.

Solution

KarigarHub connects customers with nearby skilled workers through a simple platform. Users can browse worker profiles, view ratings and previous work, and book services through an organized scheduling system. This provides a transparent and reliable way to discover and hire local professionals.

Key Features

- Discover nearby workers based on location and service category  
- View worker profiles including experience, pricing, and ratings  
- Portfolio gallery showing previous work  
- Service booking with selectable date and time slots  
- Booking status tracking from request to completion  
- Customer reviews and ratings

Tech Stack

Frontend: React with TypeScript  
Backend and Database: Supabase  
Authentication: Supabase Auth  
Storage: Supabase Storage  
UI: Tailwind CSS with custom components

How It Helps

KarigarHub simplifies the process of hiring local services by making it faster and more transparent. Customers can easily find trusted workers, while skilled professionals gain a platform to showcase their work and reach more potential clients.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major challenges we faced was designing a reliable booking system that prevents multiple customers from booking the same time slot for a worker. Initially, the booking interface displayed static time slots without verifying whether they had already been reserved by another user. This created a risk of overlapping bookings. To resolve this, we implemented a dynamic slot filtering mechanism that queries existing bookings for the selected worker and date from the database before rendering available slots. The system then removes already reserved slots from the selectable list, ensuring that users only see valid booking options.

Another significant challenge involved authentication and session management. Since the platform supports two different roles (customers and workers), it was important to maintain a consistent authentication state across the application and ensure that role-specific data was loaded correctly after login. During development we occasionally encountered issues where simultaneous login attempts from multiple users caused session synchronization problems, which sometimes resulted in unexpected 404 responses or incomplete user state initialization. This happened because the application attempted to access protected resources before the authentication session had fully propagated. We resolved this by restructuring the authentication flow, adding proper session checks, and ensuring that user data is only fetched after the authentication state has been confirmed.

We also encountered difficulties while implementing portfolio image uploads for workers. Each worker can upload multiple images showcasing their previous work, which required handling file uploads through Supabase Storage and linking the uploaded files to the correct worker profile in the database. Managing multiple asynchronous upload operations while ensuring database consistency required careful handling. We addressed this by uploading files sequentially, retrieving their public URLs, and then inserting the metadata into the database only after successful uploads.

Another technical hurdle involved managing asynchronous data fetching throughout the application. Many components depend on data retrieved from the backend, such as worker profiles, bookings, and reviews. Early in development, some components attempted to render before the necessary data had finished loading, which caused UI errors and inconsistent states. We solved this by implementing proper loading states, conditional rendering, and defensive checks to ensure components only render once the required data has been successfully retrieved.

Finally, maintaining consistent UI behavior across different pages presented its own challenges. Since the application includes multiple interconnected views such as worker profiles, booking interfaces, and dashboards, ensuring a consistent design system while integrating dynamic data required several iterations of component refactoring and state management improvements.

> Smart Cheating Detection System is an AI-powered e

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyAudio](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyAudio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In recent years, the rapid growth of online education and remote examinations has created new challenges in maintaining academic integrity. Traditional examination systems rely heavily on physical invigilation to prevent cheating, but in online environments it becomes difficult for instructors to effectively monitor students. This often leads to issues such as impersonation, use of unauthorized materials, multiple persons appearing in front of the camera, or students looking away from the screen to access external help.

Manual monitoring of a large number of students during online examinations is inefficient and prone to human error. Existing solutions often require continuous human supervision, which increases the workload for educators and does not guarantee accurate detection of suspicious activities.

To address these challenges, there is a need for an automated and intelligent system that can monitor students during online examinations and detect potential cheating behaviors in real time.

The Smart Cheating Detection System aims to solve this problem by using computer vision and face recognition technologies to automatically monitor students through their webcams. The system verifies the identity of students, tracks their facial movements, detects anomalies such as multiple faces or absence of a face, and records suspicious events. All detected activities are stored in a MySQL database for later review by instructors.

By automating the monitoring process, the system helps ensure fairness, transparency, and integrity in online examinations, while reducing the burden on human invigilators.

**Challenges we ran into**

We faced several technical challenges during the development of our project. One of the main issues was establishing a stable connection between the MySQL database and the main project, which took a considerable amount of time to debug and configure properly.

In addition, we encountered compatibility issues while installing required libraries. Some libraries showed version conflicts, and the face recognition library in particular was difficult to install in our development environment. Due to these issues, we had to spend extra time researching and testing alternative libraries that could provide similar functionality.

Despite these challenges, we were able to resolve the problems by troubleshooting the database configuration and identifying suitable alternatives for the required libraries, which allowed us to successfully complete the implementation of our project.

**Challenges we ran into**

challenges helped us improve the system architecture and make the platform more scalable.

Influencers

Brands

How we solved it

We implemented role-based authentication in the backend using Node.js and Express.js.

Each user role gets separate access and UI components in the frontend built with React.

The platform needs to store multiple types of data such as:

Gamer profiles

How we solved it

We implemented token-based authentication using JSON Web Token.

This allows secure login sessions and protects user data.

**The problem it solves**

Problem CampusCart Solves
1️⃣ The Current Situation in Campuses

In most universities, students frequently need to buy or sell second-hand items such as:

textbooks

calculators

bikes

electronics

hostel furniture

lab equipment

These needs happen every semester.

But currently students rely on inefficient methods, such as:

WhatsApp groups

Telegram channels

notice boards

asking friends

These systems create several problems.

2️⃣ Problem 1 – No Central Marketplace

There is no single platform where students can see all available items.

Example:

A student wants to buy a second-hand calculator.

They must:

ask friends

check multiple WhatsApp groups

wait for replies

Sometimes they never find a seller, even if someone nearby is selling.

So the first problem is lack of visibility and discovery.

3️⃣ Problem 2 – Messy Communication

WhatsApp groups quickly become chaotic.

Messages like:

“Selling book”

“Is this available?”

“Price?”

get buried under hundreds of messages.

This makes finding items very difficult.

4️⃣ Problem 3 – Lack of Trust

General marketplaces like OLX connect you with strangers.

Students may feel unsafe meeting unknown people.

But within a campus, students prefer to trade with other verified students.

So there is a trust gap in current systems.

5️⃣ Problem 4 – Location Confusion

Even if someone is selling something, buyers don't know:

which block they are in

which hostel they live in

how far the item is

This makes transactions slow and inconvenient.

6️⃣ Problem 5 – Lost Items

Students frequently lose items like:

ID cards

calculators

lab equipment

headphones

Currently there is no organized system to report and find lost items.

How CampusCart Solves These Problems

CampusCart provides a centralized digital marketplace for the campus.

Step 1 – Organized Listings

Students can post items with:

image

price

condition

category

location (block/hostel)

This makes listings clear and searchable.

Step 2 – Easy Discovery

Buyers can browse items by:

categories

price

hostel/block location

Instead of asking people, they can instantly find what they need.

Step 3 – Direct Communication

CampusCart includes chat between buyers and sellers, so they can quickly coordinate.

Step 4 – Hyper-Local Transactions

Because listings include exact campus locations, buyers can meet sellers quickly.

Example:

Boys Hostel 1 → Room 134
Block C → Lab 2

Transactions happen within minutes.

Step 5 – Community Trust

CampusCart is designed specifically for students within the same campus, creating a trusted community marketplace.

Step 6 – Lost & Found System

Students can post lost items, helping others find and return them easily.

Final Impact

CampusCart transforms the campus into a connected student marketplace where students can:

save money

reuse resources

trade safely

find items quickly.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building CampusCart, one of the main challenges was designing a smooth and visually appealing user interface while keeping the website responsive and organized. Since the project uses modern animation libraries like Framer Motion and GSAP, balancing animations with performance was sometimes tricky. Some animations initially caused layout shifts or slowed down the interface.

Another challenge was structuring the component architecture in React. The application has multiple pages such as Explore, Item Details, Chat, Wishlist, and Profile, so organizing reusable components like ItemCard, Navbar, and CategoryCard required careful planning to keep the code clean and scalable.

I also faced minor issues while integrating React Router navigation with animated page transitions, where certain animations were triggering at the wrong time. I solved this by properly managing component lifecycles and separating animation logic into dedicated components.

To overcome these challenges, I spent time debugging, restructuring components, and optimizing animations, which helped me improve both the performance and maintainability of the project.

Overall, these challenges helped me gain a deeper understanding of frontend architecture, animation performance, and scalable UI design.
