### AI Security System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ai-security-system-b5b7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/armanCANTcode/security-system) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--N--Win%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknwin-3.devfolio.co)

> Smart surveillance that understands conflict.

![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Object Detection](https://img.shields.io/badge/Object%20Detection-333333?style=flat-square) ![DeepSpeech](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSpeech-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Violence in places like schools, hostels, public areas, and campuses often starts suddenly. Security cameras are everywhere, but they usually just record video passively. Someone has to watch hours of footage later to understand what happened.

That means two big problems:

First, incidents are detected too late. By the time someone reviews the footage, the fight is already over.

Second, humans cannot monitor dozens of cameras continuously. Attention drops quickly, and important events get missed.

Our system tries to solve that gap. It creates a surveillance layer that can see body movement and hear aggressive sound patterns at the same time. When fast arm motion happens near another person and shouting is detected, the system flags a potential violent situation and records it automatically. In simple terms, the camera stops being a passive recorder and becomes an active observer.

The goal is faster awareness, automatic incident capture, and reduced dependence on human monitoring.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the first challenges is detecting real aggression vs normal movement. People wave their hands, play sports, or gesture while talking. The system must avoid constantly triggering false alarms. That’s why combining pose motion with audio shouting helps; two signals together are more reliable than one.

Another challenge is tracking body motion accurately. Pose detection models like YOLO pose output keypoints, but those points can jump or jitter between frames. Measuring wrist speed across frames requires careful comparison with previous positions.

Audio detection is also tricky. Real environments contain background noise, music, talking, and echoes. A model like YAMNet classifies many sounds, but mapping those predictions to “shouting” reliably requires experimentation with class ranges.

Performance becomes another obstacle. Running computer vision, pose detection, audio classification, and UI rendering in real time can slow the system down. Maintaining usable FPS while processing multiple models at once requires optimization and sometimes multithreading.

Integrating different technologies is its own puzzle. The project combines OpenCV, YOLO pose estimation, TensorFlow Hub audio models, and real-time threading. Each system has its own behavior, dependencies, and latency.

Finally, designing a useful interface becomes important. Raw detections are hard to interpret quickly, so the challenge becomes turning model outputs into clear visual information for a human operator.

PromptGuard protects AI agents from prompt injection attacks by detecting and blocking hidden malicious instructions inside external inputs before they reach the model. > Honest product reviewer

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Review Overload — Shoppers can't read 500+ reviews per product, so they guess instead of deciding.

Fake Reviews — 30-40% of online reviews are fake or paid, and shoppers have no way to filter them out.

Useless Star Ratings — A 4.2-star average hides whether the battery is terrible and the camera is amazing.

Contradictory Reviews — "Best product ever" and "Worst purchase of my life" sit side by side with zero context.

Comparison Paralysis — Choosing between two similar products means mentally juggling hundreds of reviews across both.

No Reliability Indicator — No existing platform tells you whether a conclusion is backed by 3 reviews or 300.

**Challenges we ran into**

JSON Output Truncation — The LLM kept cutting off mid-JSON response, returning invalid data that broke our parser.

API Rate Limits — Hit the 15 requests/minute quota ceiling during rapid testing, forcing unexpected downtime.

Large Input Handling — Feeding 50+ reviews (50K characters) caused slow responses and output corruption; had to optimize review selection.

Prompt Engineering — Getting the AI to return consistently structured, concise, and honest analysis instead of vague or overly positive summaries took multiple iterations.

Fake Review Detection Accuracy — Balancing between flagging genuinely suspicious reviews and not over-flagging legitimate short positive reviews.

Response Time vs Quality Tradeoff — Larger prompts gave better analysis but slower responses; had to find the sweet spot for a live demo experience.

**AI / ML**

Natural Language Processing (NLP) — The core engine processes unstructured, messy human-written text and extracts structured, meaningful insights from it.

Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis — Goes beyond basic positive/negative classification to identify specific product features and evaluate sentiment per aspect individually.

Large Language Model (LLM) Integration — Uses state-of-the-art generative AI (Grok/Gemini) via API for zero-shot analysis without requiring any custom-trained model.

Prompt Engineering — Demonstrates advanced prompt design with structured JSON output, role-based instructions, and constraint enforcement to control LLM behavior.

Anomaly Detection — The fake review flagging system identifies outlier patterns in review text, acting as a lightweight text-based anomaly detector.

Confidence Scoring — Implements a statistical reliability measure based on review volume and opinion consistency, a core ML concept applied to real-world decision-making.

Intelligent Data Preprocessing — Smart review selection filters noisy, short, or redundant inputs before analysis, mirroring standard ML data cleaning pipelines.

AI for Decision Support — The entire application is an AI-driven decision support system that augments human judgment rather than replacing it — a key principle in responsible AI.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/speakharvest-274f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ANTHELIS/XIBIT-2k26) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://speak-harvestxibit.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://res.cloudinary.com/dmf25bc5a/video/upload/v1773229837/SpeakHarvest_n1o2um.mp4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-The%20XiBit-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://the-xibit.devfolio.co)

> Just Speak. The Market Listens.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cloudinary](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloudinary-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![TailWindCSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/TailWindCSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## 🚨 The Invisible Crisis in Indian Agriculture

Imagine being a potato farmer in rural Bihar. You've harvested 2 tonnes of produce. You *know* buyers in Mumbai will pay ₹40/kg — but the local middleman offers ₹15. You can't access online mandis because they're in English. You can't type because you never learned. You can't negotiate because the buyer speaks Marathi and you speak Bhojpuri.

**This is the daily reality for 100 million+ Indian farmers.**

Existing platforms like eNAM assume literacy, English fluency, and smartphone expertise — alienating the very people they were built to serve.

## 💡 Enter SpeakHarvest — *Just Speak. The Market Listens.*

We built an **AI-native agricultural marketplace** where **your voice is the only interface**. No typing. No forms. No language barriers.

🎙️ **Talk to sell** — A farmer says *"100 kilo aloo post karo, Nashik mein, ₹25 per kilo"* and the listing goes live instantly — in any of **6 Indian languages**.

🌐 **Trade across languages** — A Bengali-speaking farmer and a Tamil-speaking buyer negotiate seamlessly. Every message is **auto-translated in real-time** by Gemini AI.

📊 **Never sell cheap again** — Before listing, farmers receive **AI-powered price recommendations** and trend analysis, ensuring they always know the fair market rate.

🔍 **Buyers find anything by voice** — *"Show me fresh wheat under ₹50/kg in Punjab"* — instant results, zero clicks.

💬 **AI-powered negotiation** — The voice assistant reads chat history, summarizes offers, and lets both parties reply by speaking — acting as a **real-time multilingual mediator**.

**SpeakHarvest doesn't just digitize agriculture. It democratizes it — making fair trade accessible to every farmer, regardless of language, literacy, or tech skills.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## 🔥 Wrestling with Real-Time AI Voice

The biggest beast? **Bidirectional audio streaming with Gemini 2.0 Flash Live.** We're not just sending text prompts — we're streaming raw microphone audio over WebSockets, receiving AI-generated speech back, *and* executing structured tool calls (create listing, search market, send message) — all simultaneously. Getting this pipeline stable without audio dropouts or race conditions took days of debugging.

## 🌍 Making AI Understand 6 Languages × 10 Tools

When a farmer says *"प्याज़ का दाम ₹30 कर दो"* (Hindi for "change onion price to ₹30"), the AI must parse intent, extract parameters, and call [updateListing()](cci:1://file:///d:/Works%20Only/Hacathons/XIBIT-2k26/frontend/src/api.ts:129:4-143:5) with the right data. Now multiply that by 6 languages, each with different grammar structures. Crafting a system prompt that handles this reliably — without hallucinating tool calls — was an exercise in prompt engineering at its hardest.

## 🔄 Real-Time Cross-Language Chat

Building a chat system where messages are *stored in the original language* but *displayed in the reader's language* — without losing conversational nuance or context — was architecturally tricky. We had to track per-user language preferences and translate on-the-fly while keeping the chat feeling natural, not robotic.

## 🎨 That Dark Mode Animation

We wanted the theme toggle to feel *cinematic* — an expanding circle reveal (like Android 13's Material You). Achieving this with pure CSS `clip-path` animations that perform at 60fps on mobile — without triggering layout reflows — took more iterations than we'd like to admit.

## 🛡️ Security vs Speed

Voice-first apps demand sub-second response times. But we also needed DDoS protection, NoSQL injection scrubbing, and strict payload limits. Balancing `express-rate-limit` + `helmet` + `mongo-sanitize` without adding noticeable latency to the voice pipeline required careful middleware orchestration.

**Open Innovation**

## SpeakHarvest — Redefining Agricultural Commerce Through Voice AI

SpeakHarvest is a radical reimagination of how agricultural trade should work in India. Instead of forcing 100M+ farmers to adapt to text-heavy, English-first digital platforms, we flipped the paradigm — **the platform adapts to the farmer**.

**What makes this truly innovative:**

🎙️ **Voice-as-the-entire-interface** — SpeakHarvest is not a marketplace with a voice feature bolted on. Voice IS the interface. Farmers list crops, negotiate prices, read messages, and manage inventory — all by speaking naturally in their mother tongue. Zero typing, zero forms, zero digital literacy required.

🧠 **AI-Native Architecture** — We leverage Google Gemini 2.0 Flash Live to enable real-time bidirectional audio streaming with tool execution. The AI doesn't just answer questions — it performs actions: creating listings, filtering markets, sending messages — all triggered by natural voice commands in 6 Indian languages.

🌐 **Breaking the Language Wall** — India has 22 official languages, yet digital commerce operates in English. SpeakHarvest's real-time translation engine lets a Bengali farmer negotiate with a Tamil buyer as if they spoke the same language — every message auto-translates to the reader's preferred language.

📊 **AI-Powered Fair Pricing** — Before a farmer posts a crop, our AI analyzes market trends and recommends optimal pricing — combating the information asymmetry that middlemen have exploited for decades.

**SpeakHarvest sits at the intersection of AI, accessibility, and social impact — proving that the most powerful technology is the kind that disappears, leaving only empowerment behind.**

**The problem it solves**

When people buy products online from platforms like Amazon or Flipkart, they face information overload.
Products often have hundreds or thousands of reviews, many of which are repetitive, misleading, or even fake. Users must spend significant time reading through reviews and comparing multiple tabs before making a decision. This makes the buying process slow, confusing, and sometimes unreliable.
Our Solution
We built an AI-powered shopping assistant that analyzes product reviews and provides a clear, data-driven summary. Instead of manually reading large numbers of reviews, users receive an instant breakdown of the most important insights.
The system automatically:
Extracts the most common pros and cons from reviews
Calculates a trust score to identify suspicious or low-quality reviews
Allows comparison of up to three products at the same time
Provides a personalized recommendation based on user preferences
What Makes It Different
Most e-commerce platforms only show star ratings and raw reviews. Our system goes further by interpreting review data and presenting structured insights.
Key differentiators include:
AI review intelligence: converts unstructured reviews into clear pros, cons, and insights.
Fake review detection: identifies suspicious review patterns and assigns a trust score.
Multi-product comparison: users can paste multiple product links and compare them in a single view.
Personalized recommendations: the system suggests the best product based on budget, use case, and priorities.
How It Improves Existing Workflows
Traditionally, users must open several product pages, read many reviews, and manually compare features. This process can take 30–60 minutes.
With our system, users simply paste product links and receive a complete analysis and comparison within seconds.
Impact
The platform simplifies online shopping by turning large volumes of unstructured reviews into clear, trustworthy insights. It helps users make faster, safer, and more informed purchasing decisions.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges Faced While Building the Project**

1. **Scraping and extracting review data**
   E-commerce sites often have complex page structures and dynamic content, making it challenging to reliably extract product details and reviews from links.

2. **Handling unstructured review text**
   Customer reviews are written in different styles, lengths, and languages, so converting them into meaningful pros, cons, and insights required careful text processing.

3. **Detecting fake or low-quality reviews**
   Identifying suspicious patterns such as duplicate reviews, very short comments, or rating-text mismatches was challenging and required creating heuristic rules.

4. **Comparing different products fairly**
   Products from different pages may describe features differently, so normalizing information to enable meaningful comparison was difficult.

5. **Designing a clear and professional UI**
   Presenting large amounts of analysis (pros, cons, ratings, trust scores, comparisons) in a clean, easy-to-understand interface required thoughtful layout and prioritization of information.

6. **Performance and response time**
   Processing multiple product links and large numbers of reviews quickly while maintaining a smooth user experience was a key technical challenge.

**Web3**

Web3 track because it aims to improve transparency and trust in online product reviews. On many traditional e-commerce platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart, review data is managed by centralized systems, which can sometimes lead to concerns about manipulation or authenticity.
A Web3-based approach focuses on creating a more open and verifiable ecosystem. By leveraging decentralized technologies, product reviews and ratings can be stored in a way that is tamper-resistant and transparent, making it easier for users to trust the information they see.
In this context, the project contributes to the Web3 vision by promoting data integrity, transparency, and user trust in the online shopping experience while helping users make more informed purchasing decisions.

> Your smartest AI partner

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Modern Student's Dilemma
Students today are overwhelmed by "information overload." A single semester results in hundreds of pages of PDFs, disorganized lecture slides, and messy handwritten notes. When cramming for an exam, finding a specific concept or explanation across all these different formats is like finding a needle in a haystack.

Furthermore, while students try to use standard AI tools to study, those models frequently hallucinate—making up facts or providing generic explanations that don't match the professor's specific curriculum.

How Our AI Study Assistant Solves This
Our RAG-based AI Study Assistant acts as a highly personalized, Socratic tutor that is strictly bounded by the user's actual study materials. It makes studying faster, safer, and infinitely more interactive:

Universal Digitization (OCR): Students aren't limited to clean digital files. By integrating Tesseract OCR, they can snap a photo of their messy handwritten notebook and instantly make it searchable and queryable by the AI.

Zero-Hallucination Q&A: When a student asks a question to clear up a doubt, the backend retrieves the exact relevant chunk of text from their uploaded notes and feeds it to the Gemini API. The AI answers using only that context, guaranteeing 100% syllabus-accurate answers.

Instant Summarization: Turns a dense, 50-page lecture PDF into a digestible executive summary in seconds, drastically reducing reading time.

Active Recall Testing: Instead of passive reading, students can click a button to have the system read their notes and instantly generate a 5-question Multiple Choice Quiz to test their knowledge retention, complete with explanations for the correct answers.

By bridging the gap between raw, messy data and intelligent, contextual retrieval, we transform passive studying into an active, highly efficient learning loop.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building the RAG data pipeline presented a few specific technical hurdles that we had to debug on the fly:

1. Multi-Modal File Upload Crashes (500 Internal Server Errors): While setting up our FastAPI backend to accept both PDFs and images of handwritten notes, our /upload-notes endpoint kept throwing 500 Internal Server Errors. We realized FastAPI couldn't process the incoming file streams out-of-the-box. We overcame this by integrating the python-multipart dependency to handle raw form data, and then restructured our main.py to securely save the UploadFile to a temporary directory before passing it to our PyMuPDF and Tesseract ingestion modules.

2. Forcing Strict JSON Output for Quizzes:
When prompting the LLM to generate 5 Multiple Choice Questions based on the uploaded notes, it naturally wanted to output conversational text. This unpredictability would break our frontend UI. We solved this by implementing LangChain's PydanticOutputParser. We created a strict Pydantic BaseModel schema and paired it with a RetryWithErrorOutputParser. If the AI hallucinates a malformed JSON string, our backend automatically catches the exception and forces the AI to correct its formatting before passing the data to the frontend.

3. API & Context Window Pivots:
We initially faced context limits and API constraints when trying to feed heavily chunked PDF data into our models. We quickly pivoted our architecture to use the Gemini 1.5 Flash API, taking advantage of its massive context window to process full lecture materials seamlessly without losing semantic meaning.

**Open Innovation**

Our project perfectly aligns with the Open Innovation track because we identified a universal, real-world problem—student information overload and the struggle to extract targeted knowledge from messy, fragmented notes—and built a highly creative, technology-driven solution from scratch.

Instead of conforming to a predefined problem statement, we engineered a custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) AI Study Assistant. We moved beyond standard chatbots by incorporating multi-modal OCR (Pytesseract) to process actual handwritten notes alongside digital PDFs. By pairing this with smart semantic chunking and the Gemini API, our platform provides instant, context-aware summaries, doubt resolution, and automated MCQ generation based strictly on the student's uploaded materials, eliminating AI hallucinations.

By combining advanced LLMs with practical data ingestion pipelines, we have created an innovative, open-ended tool that directly improves the modern educational experience.

**The problem it solves**

This project addresses the complexity and security risks associated with unmonitored mobile data. Here is how it improves the current landscape:

Visibility into Hidden Traffic: Most users have no idea which background processes are communicating with external servers; this tool provides real-time transparency.

Security Auditing: It helps identify suspicious connections or unauthorized data exfiltration by documenting every IP and port being accessed.

Performance Optimization: By pinpointing data-heavy applications, users can manage bandwidth more effectively and reduce data costs.

Simplified Monitoring: It replaces complex command-line tools with a mobile-native interface, making network diagnostics accessible to developers and power users alike.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a bridge between a high-level mobile frontend and a low-level network backend presented several hurdles:

Asynchronous Data Flow: Managing the real-time stream of traffic data from the Node.js backend to the Flutter frontend without causing UI lag.

Solution: Implemented Redis as a message broker to handle high-throughput data and ensured the Flutter app used optimized stream controllers.

Cross-Platform Architecture: Coordinating a backend built with Express with an Android-specific network environment.

Solution: Standardized the communication layer using a structured RESTful API and ensured the repository was strictly organized into separate frontend and backend directories for better dependency management.

State Management in Flutter: Keeping the network logs updated in the UI without rebuilding the entire widget tree every second.

Solution: Utilized efficient state management patterns to ensure only the log list updated when new packets were detected.

![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20Studio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gson](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gson-333333?style=flat-square) ![Room Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Room%20Database-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem SafeDial Solves
India loses thousands of crores every year to SMS phishing, KYC fraud, OTP theft, and scam calls — and most victims never see it coming because the attack arrives as an ordinary-looking message or phone call.
Existing solutions fall short in two critical ways:

They only understand English — a scammer writing in Hindi, Tamil, or Bengali slips right through
They're reactive — they warn you after you've already read the message, or worse, after you've already clicked the link

SafeDial fixes this
For everyday users, SafeDial works silently in the background and instantly flags suspicious SMS messages and calls the moment they arrive — before you even open them. No manual action needed.
For users in regional India, SafeDial is the first fraud detector that understands scam messages written in Hindi, Hinglish, Tamil, Telugu, and Bengali — covering the languages that scammers actively exploit because no app was watching.
Against bot attacks, if a scammer or automated system floods your phone with multiple messages in rapid succession, SafeDial detects the burst pattern and auto-blocks the sender within 60 seconds — no other app does this at the device level.
For the community, SafeDial lets users report scam numbers directly to a shared Firebase database, building a crowdsourced blocklist of known Indian fraud numbers that protects everyone.
In short, SafeDial makes your phone:

- Safer against phishing, KYC fraud, OTP theft and fake government messages
-Smarter in 5 Indian languages, not just English
-Faster at blocking bot attacks before they overwhelm you
-More trustworthy — because you know who's really calling

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into
**MIUI Killed Everything** — The Hardest Problem
The biggest challenge of the entire build was getting live SMS detection to work on a Redmi 9 Power running MIUI Android 12.
On stock Android, receiving an SMS broadcast is straightforward. On MIUI, it is not. No matter what we tried, the app simply would not receive incoming messages. The SMS_RECEIVED broadcast was being silently killed by MIUI's aggressive battery and background process management before it could reach the app.
We went through multiple failed approaches before landing on a solution:

Attempt 1 — Standard BroadcastReceiver with SMS_RECEIVED. MIUI blocked it silently. No error, no log, just nothing.
Attempt 2 — Added a ContentObserver on content://sms. Worked occasionally, but MIUI killed the background service within minutes.
Attempt 3 — Registered the app as the default SMS app, which forces Android to deliver SMS_DELIVER broadcasts exclusively to us. This finally worked — but required implementing all four mandatory components: SmsReceiver, SmsDeliverReceiver, MmsReceiver, HeadlessSmsSendService, and a SmsComposeActivity.
Final solution — Combined the default SMS app registration with a foreground SmsMonitorService (START_STICKY), a 60-second AlarmManager poller as a fallback, and a BootReceiver to restart everything after reboot. Three layers of redundancy just to reliably receive a text message.

Even after all that, MIUI required manual steps — Autostart had to be enabled and battery restrictions set to "No Restrictions" from the MIUI settings — because no API can do this programmatically on MIUI.

** Call Overlay Arriving Too Late**
The real-time call warning overlay was designed to appear the moment a suspicious call arrives. The first implementation routed the analysis through WorkManager — which introduced a 2–5 second delay. By the time the overlay appeared, the user had already seen the call screen with no warning.
The fix was to move fraud analysis directly into goAsync() inside the CallReceiver, cutting analysis time to under 100ms and making the overlay appear almost instantly.

**MIUI's Double RINGING Broadcast**
MIUI sends two PHONE_STATE RINGING broadcasts for every incoming call — the first with a null number, the second with the actual number. Our duplicate-call guard was checking state == lastState, which blocked the second broadcast entirely, meaning the overlay never showed because the number was always null.
The fix was changing the guard to caller == lastProcessedNumber instead, so the second broadcast with the real number always gets through.

**Vernacular Keyword Matching at Scale**
Building fraud keyword banks across 5 languages — Hindi (Devanagari), Tamil, Telugu, Bengali and Hinglish — without any external NLP library was a research and engineering challenge. Each language required understanding the cultural context of how scammers phrase their messages, not just direct translations of English fraud terms. For example, a UPI scam in Hindi uses completely different phrasing than its English equivalent, and a government impersonation scam in Tamil has its own set of trigger words.

**Room Database Migration**
Every major feature addition — India Spam Shield and Trusted Contacts — required a new Room database schema. Managing incremental migrations (v1 → v2 → v3) without wiping user data on upgrade required careful migration scripts and testing, especially since a failed migration crashes the app on launch.

**Special Track**

Smart SMS/Call Fraud Detector
Challenge:

Modern mobiles are flooded with spam messages, phishing SMS, and fraudulent calls. Build a mobile solution that monitors incoming SMS and call metadata to detect potential fraud using rule-based + lightweight ML techniques.

Key Features to Implement:

Parse and classify SMS/call logs.
Detect phishing/scam patterns (keyword matching, sender anomalies).
Provide user warnings and safe action suggestions.
Expected Outcome:

An Android proof-of-concept app that flags scam messages/calls with category labels (e.g., "Phishing", "Spam", "Unknown") and history logging.

> Guardrails for your Mobile

![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![API3](https://img.shields.io/badge/API3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Mobile operating systems today prioritize battery life and smooth user experience, which means users rarely receive aggressive update notifications.

Because of this:

• People run outdated apps with known vulnerabilities for weeks or months
• Hackers exploit these using patch-diffing techniques
• Users suffer from “Temporal Blindness” — they don't know when sensors like microphone or camera are accessed in the background
• Permission managers lack contextual intelligence — a calculator using GPS is treated the same as Google Maps using GPS

Even worse, third-party SDKs embedded inside apps often contain hidden vulnerabilities that users cannot detect.

**Challenges we ran into**

● The Update Deadlock: Because app stores suppress aggressive update notifications to 
prevent "alert fatigue," users unknowingly run outdated, vulnerable applications for 
weeks or months. 
● The Binary-Only SDK Blind Spot: Over 60% of top Android third-party components are 
shipped as precompiled binaries, hiding outdated, vulnerable code deep within the app's 
supply chain. 
● Contextual & Temporal Blindness: Users are entirely blind to "Shadow 
Access"—situations where an app triggers a sensor (like the microphone or camera) 
while the screen is off or the app is minimized. 
● Action Paralysis: Standard vulnerability scanners output highly technical data, and 
built-in OS alerts lack actionable guidance, leaving users without the technical 
knowledge to effectively audit and revoke complex permissions.

**Special Track**

Privacy Guardian for Mobile Sensor & App Usage

![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Room Database](https://img.shields.io/badge/Room%20Database-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

KageMei is a purpose-built Android security application that continuously monitors how installed apps access sensitive device sensors — the camera, microphone, and GPS — and alerts users in real time when unexpected or potentially malicious access occurs. Modern smartphones are treasure troves of personal data. Camera access can expose visual surroundings; microphone access can capture conversations; GPS access can reveal precise location history. Most users have no visibility into when these sensors are active or which apps are accessing them in the background. KageMei closes this gap by providing a SOC-style (Security Operations Center) monitoring dashboard directly on the user's device.

**Challenges we ran into**

The following challenges were faced by us:
Android telemetry limits: Modern Android restricts cross-app sensor visibility, so we used a hybrid confirmed + inferred telemetry model.

False positives: Normal apps using camera/mic looked suspicious, so we added app-category based rules.

System vs user apps: System components have special permissions, so we downgraded anomaly rules for trusted system apps.

App categorization issues: Some apps are hard to classify, so we used confidence scoring with a GENERAL fallback.

User-friendly explanations: Raw Android permissions are technical, so we created human-readable PII mappings with AI explanations.

Severity vs confidence: We separated alert severity from evidence confidence to avoid overstating risks.

Dashboard usability: Designed a SOC-style dashboard showing alerts, privacy posture, rules, and drill-down analysis.

Actionable alerts: Added direct fix actions like opening system settings from alerts.

LLM integration: Handling emulator vs physical device networking for AI explanations required different configurations.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/smartshield-e24c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Abhikumar199/SmartShield) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1DB_2jgnSLivQt_xt62p-Z6klgb2cv1lY/view?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co)

> Protecting Users from SMS Fraud

![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![ANN](https://img.shields.io/badge/ANN-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Smartphones are increasingly targeted by SMS phishing (smishing), OTP fraud, and scam campaigns. Traditional keyword-based filters fail to detect evolving and zero-day attacks, while cloud-based deep learning solutions introduce latency, privacy risks, and higher energy consumption. This project aims to develop a lightweight, privacy-preserving, fully on-device fraud de- tection system that combines rule-based filtering with a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) for real-time, energy-efficient inference. The core challenge is enabling adaptive, zero-network- latency fraud detection on smartphones using event-driven neuromorphic intelligence

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was integrating the trained fraud detection model into the Android application within the limited hackathon time. While we successfully developed and tested the SMS fraud detection pipeline using ANN and energy-efficient SNN models, replicating the preprocessing steps (vectorization and rule-based fraud checks) on the mobile side required additional adjustments.

Due to time constraints, we focused on validating the core AI detection engine and evaluating computational and energy efficiency. Our experiments showed that the SNN model significantly reduces computational operations compared to a traditional ANN, demonstrating its potential for energy-efficient on-device fraud detection in future mobile security applications.

**Special Track**

The proposed system presents an energy-efficient, neuromorphic-inspired fraud detection framework tailored for mobile environments. By leveraging latency-encoded 1D Convolu- tional Spiking Neural Networks alongside lightweight preprocessing mechanisms, the solution achieves low-latency and privacy-preserving on-device inference. The hybrid dataset strategy, combining benchmark UCI data with contemporary real- world phishing samples, enhances robustness against evolving fraud tactics. Compared to conventional ANN-based approaches, the proposed SNN architecture aims to provide com- petitive detection performance while reducing computational overhead and energy consump- tion. Overall, this work demonstrates the feasibility of deploying adaptive, secure, and resource- aware spiking neural network models for real-time telecom fraud detection in low-resource and privacy-sensitive settings.

### RansomWare
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ransomware-490e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sahu-virendra-1908/secure_f) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HACKSECURE'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacksecure-1461.devfolio.co)

> Country First

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebRTC](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebRTC-333333?style=flat-square) ![AES](https://img.shields.io/badge/AES-333333?style=flat-square) ![Redis](https://img.shields.io/badge/Redis-333333?style=flat-square) ![LibSodium](https://img.shields.io/badge/LibSodium-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLCipher](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLCipher-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Challenge: NAT Traversal & WebRTC Signaling
In a pure P2P environment, establishing a direct connection between two devices behind different firewalls (NATs) is notoriously difficult. Initially, our peer discovery was failing 40% of the time.

The Solution:
We implemented a Double-Blind Signaling Layer. We built a custom signaling server using Node.js and Redis that acts as a "blind matchmaker." It uses STUN/TURN protocols to facilitate the "handshake" without ever seeing the content. To keep this anonymous, we nested Onion Routing principles into the signaling phase so the server doesn't even know the IP addresses of the two peers it is connecting.

The Challenge: Hardware Key Management
Integrating the libsodium library with the Android Keystore/iOS Secure Enclave was a hurdle because these hardware modules don't always support the specific curves required by the Signal Protocol (Double Ratchet).

The Solution:
We created a Hybrid Key Wrapper. We use the hardware enclave to protect a "Master Key," which then derives the ephemeral session keys in the application's secure memory space using SecureZeroMemory to ensure no traces are left in the RAM after the session ends.

Tracks Applied
Security & Privacy: For implementing E2EE, Double-Blind Routing, and Hardware Key Storage.

Web3/Decentralized: For removing central server dependency and using cryptographic identities.

Communication/Social: For building a high-performance, real-time messaging protoco

> An AI-Powered Personalized Travel Planning App

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Planning a trip today often requires using multiple apps and websites — searching for destinations, checking maps, finding restaurants, building itineraries, and figuring out what to pack. This process can be time-consuming, overwhelming, and confusing, especially for people who are traveling to a new place or planning on a tight schedule.

Our project solves this by creating a single AI-powered travel planning platform that simplifies the entire process.

With just a few inputs like destination, mood, budget, and number of days, the platform automatically generates a personalized travel itinerary. It also integrates helpful tools in one place, such as:

* Smart route maps to visualize travel paths between places
* Nearby recommendations for restaurants, temples, and shopping spots
* Weather-based outfit suggestions
* Packing checklist guidance
*Travel music playlists to enhance the journey

Instead of manually planning every detail, users can instantly get a structured travel plan powered by AI.

This makes travel planning:

- Faster – generates itineraries in seconds
- Simpler – everything in one platform
- Personalized – based on mood, preferences, and trip duration

Ultimately, the goal is to transform travel planning from a complex, multi-step task into a seamless and enjoyable experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

One of the biggest challenges we faced was handling component crashes and dependency errors while integrating multiple UI modules in React. Our Results page was designed to show several dynamic components such as the itinerary map, outfit suggestions, weather-based packing tips, playlists, and nearby place recommendations.

While building this page, we encountered multiple issues:

Import resolution errors in Vite (e.g., `Failed to resolve import "../components/PackingChecklist"`).
Runtime crashes caused by undefined props, especially when mapping over arrays like `places.map()` before data was available.
Map rendering errors in the `SmartRouteMap` component when the itinerary data had not yet loaded.

These errors caused the Results page to fail completely and display a blank screen.

To solve this, we implemented several fixes:

1. Created placeholder components for modules that were still under development so that the app wouldn't crash due to missing imports.
2. Added defensive programming techniques such as default props (`places = []`) and optional chaining (`places?.map(...)`) to prevent runtime errors when data is undefined.
3. Structured our components to gracefully render loading or empty states until AI-generated itinerary data becomes available.

By isolating errors component-by-component and ensuring safe rendering conditions, we stabilized the entire Results page and ensured the travel itinerary UI loads reliably.

> Safety before it happens.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**1. Lack of Safety Awareness in Unfamiliar Areas**
People often travel through unfamiliar locations without knowing the safety risks associated with those areas.

**2. Navigation Systems Ignore Safety Factors**
Most navigation applications focus only on the fastest or shortest routes and do not consider safety issues such as harassment incidents or suspicious activities.

**3. Incidents Often Go Unreported**
Many unsafe situations remain unreported because victims hesitate to file complaints or find the reporting process difficult.

**4. Authorities Remain Unaware of Local Safety Issues**
Since complaints are not always registered, police and city authorities may not be aware of location-based harassment or safety problems.

**5. Complex Reporting Process**
In many cases, people must visit police stations multiple times to file complaints, which discourages them from reporting incidents.

**6. Need for an Easy and Smart Reporting Platform**
A digital platform is needed where citizens can easily report incidents, share location-based information, and help authorities respond quickly.

**7. Improving Public Safety Through Technology**
By combining incident reporting, safety heatmaps, SOS alerts, and community feedback, the platform helps identify unsafe areas and prevent repeated incidents.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Real-Time Complaint Sync**
Ensuring that citizen complaints instantly appear in the authority dashboard was challenging. This was solved by using a centralized real-time database.

**2. Safety Score Calculation**
Designing a fair safety score for each location was difficult. We solved it by combining incident reports, citizen feedback, and actions taken by authorities.

**3. Preventing Fake Reports**
Open reporting may lead to false complaints. We addressed this with verification methods and optional evidence submission.

**4. Privacy Protection**
Users may hesitate to report incidents due to privacy concerns. We implemented anonymous reporting and secure data handling.

**5. Authority Accountability**
A challenge was ensuring authorities respond to complaints. We added an escalation system where if no action is taken within 3–5 days, the complaint can move to higher authorities, and citizens can track the status digitally.

**6. Easy-to-Use Interface**
The platform needed to be simple to use during emergencies. We simplified the reporting process and added SOS and chatbot assistance.

### Offline Survival Companion
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/offline-survival-companion-32f4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Pushkar-prog/offline-Survival) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ThsbxsC53I4?feature=shared) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Safety that works even without signal bars

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In many emergency situations, people rely heavily on their smartphones for help. However, most modern safety and emergency applications depend entirely on internet connectivity, mobile networks, or external infrastructure. This creates a serious gap in safety because emergencies often occur in places where network connectivity is weak, unavailable, or disrupted.

Situations such as natural disasters, remote travel, trekking, accidents, or unsafe environments frequently leave individuals without internet access. In these moments, traditional safety apps fail to function because they require active data connections, cloud services, or continuous network availability to send alerts, share locations, or access guidance.

This problem becomes even more critical in countries like India and other developing regions where network coverage in rural areas, highways, forests, mountains, and disaster-affected zones is often unreliable. A person facing danger may have a smartphone in their hand but still have no practical way to communicate distress or access survival guidance.

The Offline Survival Companion (OSC) addresses this gap by providing a reliable emergency support system that works even without internet connectivity. The application is designed to ensure that a user can still trigger emergency alerts, access survival information, and share essential details with trusted contacts using minimal or alternative communication methods such as SMS or locally stored emergency tools.

By functioning independently of internet connectivity, OSC ensures that critical safety features remain accessible when they are needed the most. The app transforms a regular smartphone into a self-contained emergency support tool, enabling individuals to respond to dangerous situations even in offline environments.

What People Can Use It For

People can use the Offline Survival Companion in a variety of real-world scenarios where safety and communication become difficult:

1. Emergency Alerts Without Internet
Users can trigger emergency alerts that notify pre-saved contacts even when internet services are unavailable, ensuring that someone is informed about their situation.

2. Safety During Travel or Outdoor Activities
Trekkers, hikers, travelers, and adventure enthusiasts often visit remote areas where mobile networks are unreliable. OSC provides them with an additional layer of safety by allowing them to access emergency tools offline.

3. Disaster Situations
During earthquakes, floods, or other disasters, communication networks may collapse. The application allows users to still access survival information and emergency communication methods.

4. Personal Safety and Women’s Safety
Individuals can quickly trigger distress signals in unsafe situations. The offline functionality ensures that the safety mechanism does not fail simply due to lack of internet.

5. Guidance in Critical Situations
The app can store essential survival information and emergency instructions locally on the device, allowing users to access them even when they cannot reach online resources.

How It Improves Existing Solutions

Most existing safety applications assume that internet connectivity will always be available, which is not always realistic. OSC improves upon these systems by focusing on offline reliability and resilience.

Instead of relying entirely on servers or cloud infrastructure, the application keeps essential safety functions locally available on the device. This ensures that emergency features remain accessible regardless of network conditions.

By prioritizing offline accessibility, fast emergency triggers, and locally stored safety resources, the Offline Survival Companion ensures that a smartphone can still serve as a dependable survival tool when conventional communication systems fail.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building the Offline Survival Companion (OSC) came with several technical and practical challenges. Since the goal of the project was to create a safety application that continues to function even without internet connectivity, many conventional development approaches could not be used. Most modern mobile applications rely heavily on cloud services, APIs, and real-time data access, so designing a system that remains functional offline and during emergencies required solving multiple hurdles.

1. Implementing Reliable Emergency Triggers

One of the early challenges was designing a fast and reliable way for users to trigger an SOS alert during dangerous situations. In real-life emergencies, a person may not have the time or ability to unlock the phone and navigate through multiple screens.

Initially, the SOS system relied on a manual button trigger, but this approach was not always practical. During discussions with judges and mentors during the hackathon, Judge Keshav Bhatt suggested implementing a gesture-based emergency trigger that could activate the SOS quickly.

Based on this recommendation, we implemented a “Shake to SOS” feature, where the application detects rapid device motion using the phone’s accelerometer sensors. When a predefined shake pattern is detected, the app automatically triggers the SOS protocol. This allows users to send alerts even when they cannot interact with the screen properly.

The challenge here was avoiding false triggers, since normal phone movements could accidentally activate the SOS. To solve this, we implemented a threshold-based motion detection algorithm that recognizes only strong and repeated shaking patterns before activating the emergency alert.

2. Designing an Offline-First System

Another major challenge was ensuring that the application could still operate when internet connectivity is unavailable. Many features commonly used in safety applications—such as live location sharing, server authentication, and cloud-based alerts—depend heavily on network infrastructure.

To overcome this limitation, we designed OSC with an offline-first architecture, where critical emergency functionalities are stored and executed directly on the device rather than relying on remote servers. This included:

Locally stored emergency contacts

Offline survival guides

SMS-based alert systems instead of internet messaging

Device-based sensor triggers for emergencies

This design ensures that even when users are in remote locations, disaster zones, or areas with no network signal, the application can still perform essential safety operations.

3. Integrating an Offline Agentic AI System

Another challenge we explored was how the application could assist users more intelligently during emergencies without relying on cloud AI services.

Most AI-powered systems require continuous internet connectivity because they process requests on remote servers. However, this would contradict the core philosophy of OSC, which focuses on offline reliability.

To address this, we began integrating a lightweight offline Agentic AI system capable of performing certain autonomous tasks during emergency situations. The goal of this AI component is to help the application make context-aware decisions such as:

Automatically triggering emergency protocols

Providing survival guidance during crises

Assisting the user in stressful situations without requiring internet access

Implementing this required experimenting with lightweight AI models and optimized local processing, ensuring that the system can operate within the limitations of a smartphone’s processing power.

4. Balancing Performance and Battery Usage

Another technical hurdle was managing battery consumption, since emergency applications must remain reliable even when the phone’s battery is low.

Continuous sensor monitoring (such as accelerometer data for shake detection) and background processes can drain battery quickly if not optimized. To solve this, we optimized the system by:

Running sensor monitoring at controlled intervals

Activating certain modules only when needed

Using efficient background processing techniques

This helped maintain a balance between responsiveness and energy efficiency.

Key Learning

These challenges helped us improve the project significantly. Feedback from mentors and judges played an important role in shaping the system. Features like Shake to SOS and the development of an offline Agentic AI assistant made the application more practical and responsive for real-world emergencies.

Overall, overcoming these challenges strengthened the core idea of the project: creating a reliable safety companion that continues to function when conventional systems fail.

> When AI Meets Plant Care

![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Plant diseases and improper plant care are major challenges for both farmers and home gardeners. Identifying plant health issues often requires expert knowledge, which is not always easily accessible. Many plant enthusiasts struggle to diagnose diseases, understand treatment methods, or find reliable plant care information.

As a result, plants may suffer from delayed treatment, incorrect remedies, or poor maintenance, leading to reduced crop yields or plant loss.

PlantCare addresses this problem by providing an AI-powered plant care assistant that helps users quickly identify plant problems and receive actionable guidance.

How People Can Use It

PlantCare simplifies plant care by combining AI detection, intelligent guidance, and location-based services into one mobile platform.

Users can:

Scan plant images to detect possible diseases or health issues.

Receive treatment recommendations and prevention tips for plant diseases.

Listen to plant care guidance in multiple languages using voice output.

Find nearby nurseries and fertilizer stores using integrated map services.

Store detection history for future reference.

How It Improves Existing Tasks

PlantCare makes plant care simpler, faster, and more accessible.

Instead of relying on manual research or expert consultation, users can:

Diagnose plant problems instantly using AI

Get clear and easy-to-understand plant care advice

Access reliable plant information anytime

Discover nearby plant supply stores quickly

Receive guidance in audio format for better accessibility

By combining AI technology, cloud services, and voice assistance, the app helps users protect plant health and improve agricultural productivity.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we Ran Into:

One of the main challenges during the development of PlantCare was related to dataset availability and limited time for training the plant disease detection model.

Limited Dataset Availability

Training an accurate plant disease detection system requires a large and diverse dataset of plant images that includes different crops, disease types, and environmental conditions. However, during the development of PlantCare, there was insufficient access to a large and well-labeled dataset.

Many publicly available datasets contain only a limited number of plant species or disease categories. In addition, real-world images vary significantly due to factors such as lighting conditions, camera quality, background noise, and different stages of plant growth. This made it challenging for the model to generalize well across all scenarios.

Limited Time for Model Training

Another major hurdle was the limited time available to properly train and fine-tune the machine learning model. Achieving high accuracy in image-based disease detection typically requires:

Large training datasets

Multiple training iterations

Hyperparameter tuning

Continuous model evaluation and improvement

Due to project time constraints, it was not possible to perform extensive training and optimization. As a result, the current model may have lower accuracy in certain cases, especially when dealing with unfamiliar plant species or unclear images.

How the Challenge Was Addressed

To address these limitations, the PlantCare system was designed with a hybrid approach:

Firebase cloud storage allows plant images and detection results to be stored, enabling the possibility of building a larger dataset over time.

The system architecture was designed to be scalable, making it easier to retrain and improve the detection model in future updates.

This approach ensured that PlantCare remains useful and functional, while leaving room for improving detection accuracy as more training data becomes available.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

How Our Project Fits the “Best Use of ElevenLabs” Track

PlantCare leverages the capabilities of ElevenLabs’ advanced text-to-speech technology to make plant disease information and care guidance more accessible, understandable, and user-friendly, especially for farmers and plant enthusiasts who may face literacy or language barriers.

1. Voice-Based Plant Care Guidance

After the AI system analyzes a plant image and identifies a possible disease, the results are not only displayed as text but are also converted into natural-sounding speech using ElevenLabs.
This allows users to listen to the diagnosis and treatment suggestions, making the experience easier and more interactive.

2. Multi-Language Accessibility

Many farmers and plant growers are more comfortable listening in their native language rather than reading technical plant care information.
Using ElevenLabs, PlantCare can generate spoken explanations in different languages, helping users clearly understand:

Plant disease diagnosis

Treatment recommendations

Preventive care steps

This significantly improves accessibility for rural farmers and non-English speakers.

3. Improving Accessibility for Low-Literacy Users

In many agricultural communities, reading long instructions on a screen can be difficult. By integrating high-quality AI voice output, PlantCare ensures that users can simply listen to the guidance instead of reading it, making the platform more inclusive.

4. Creating a More Natural User Experience

ElevenLabs provides human-like voice synthesis, which allows the application to deliver plant care advice in a clear, natural, and conversational tone. This creates a more engaging user experience compared to robotic or basic text-to-speech systems.

**The problem it solves**

**Healthcare AI systems require large volumes of medical data to train reliable machine learning models. However, real-world healthcare datasets contain highly sensitive patient information such as ECG records, cholesterol levels, blood pressure history, and other clinical parameters.**

*Because of strict privacy regulations, hospitals and research institutions cannot freely share patient datasets. This creates a major challenge for developers and researchers who want to build AI systems for healthcare.*

**How can we train accurate medical AI models without exposing sensitive patient data?**

Our project, NeuroCardio AI, addresses this challenge by combining predictive machine learning with privacy-preserving concepts.

The system analyzes cardiovascular health parameters such as age, blood pressure, cholesterol levels, chest pain type, ECG results, and heart rate to predict the risk of heart disease.

**Key benefits of the system include:**

- Early prediction of heart attack risk using AI

- Privacy-aware learning approaches inspired by federated learning

- Explainable AI techniques that show which medical features influenced the prediction

- A web-based platform that allows users to instantly check heart health risk

In addition, the project explores synthetic healthcare data generation, which allows developers to create high-quality artificial datasets that maintain the statistical properties of real medical data without exposing personally identifiable information.

**This approach enables researchers to train AI models safely while maintaining strict patient privacy.**

**Challenges we ran into**

**Building an AI-powered healthcare prediction system involved several technical and conceptual challenges.**

One major challenge was working with healthcare data that contains sensitive patient information. Designing a system that could potentially train models without exposing raw medical records required exploring privacy-preserving machine learning approaches and federated learning concepts.

Another challenge was achieving strong prediction performance on a relatively small tabular dataset. We experimented with multiple machine learning models including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, KNN, and XGBoost.

To improve model performance, we implemented advanced hyperparameter optimization techniques such as RandomizedSearchCV, GridSearchCV, and Optuna.

Integrating explainable AI was another important hurdle. Since healthcare predictions must be interpretable, we used SHAP and LIME to analyze how different clinical parameters influence the model's predictions.

**Finally, building a complete end-to-end system—from data preprocessing and model training to deploying a web application using Flask—required integrating multiple technologies into a single working pipeline.**

**Despite these challenges, the project successfully demonstrates how machine learning, explainable AI, and privacy-first approaches can work together to build reliable healthcare prediction systems.**

**Best Use of Gemini API**

**NeuroCardio AI predicts heart attack risk using machine learning models trained on clinical health parameters such as age, cholesterol, blood pressure, ECG results, and heart rate.**

Gemini API is used to convert complex model predictions into easy-to-understand medical insights. Instead of only showing a risk probability, Gemini can generate natural language explanations describing the possible factors influencing the prediction.

This helps doctors and users better understand the AI decision and improves transparency in healthcare analytics. Gemini can also assist in analyzing synthetic healthcare datasets, ensuring that generated data maintains realistic patterns without exposing sensitive patient information.

**Best Hack Built with Google Antigravity**

**Our project NeuroCardio AI uses advanced machine learning techniques to analyze cardiovascular health data and predict heart attack risk. The system processes medical parameters such as age, cholesterol levels, blood pressure, ECG results, and heart rate to detect potential risk patterns.**

Using Google’s AI ecosystem and tools, the platform focuses on building an intelligent, interactive healthcare application that combines predictive analytics with explainable AI. The system not only predicts the risk but also helps interpret the results in a more understandable way for users.

**This approach demonstrates how modern AI technologies can be applied to build innovative healthcare solutions that are intelligent, scalable, and user-friendly.**

> A decentralized, automated flight insurance.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

When a flight is delayed, getting compensated means filing a claim, submitting proof, and waiting weeks for a human to approve it — if they do at all. Insurance companies are slow by design, and self-interested by nature. TravelGuard replaces that process with a smart contract. The rules are in code, not a policy document. If a delay is confirmed, the payout happens — automatically, instantly, no one to argue with.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the key challenges we faced was a type mismatch between our frontend and the smart contract. When calling a contract function on Algorand, the app generates a fingerprint based on the function name and its argument types. We had defined one argument as a boolean, but the contract expected a number. The fingerprints didn't match, so the contract couldn't identify the function and threw a cryptic bytecode error with no clear description of what went wrong. We had to manually compare our code against the compiled contract's ABI output line by line to catch a single word difference.

**Algorand Bharat**

TravelGuard qualifies for the Algorand partner track on every core criterion:

Built natively on Algorand. The smart contract is deployed on Algorand TestNet, written in Puya-TS and compiled for the AVM. The entire policy lifecycle — registration, booking, status updates, refunds — happens through Algorand transactions.

Uses Algorand primitives directly. It leverages ABI method calls, Atomic Transaction Composer, Box Storage for scalable on-chain state, and inner transactions for automated payouts. These are not surface-level integrations — they are central to how the product works.

Demonstrates real utility on Algorand. It shows that Algorand is fast and cheap enough to make microtransactions (small insurance premiums, instant refunds) practical — something that would be unusable on chains with high gas fees.

Integrates the Algorand wallet ecosystem. It uses Pera Wallet Connect, the primary wallet for the Algorand ecosystem, giving users a native, familiar experience.

In short: the product would not work on any other chain in this form. It is an Algorand-first application solving a real problem.

> Hisaab se paise settle karo

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![MySQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/MySQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Spring](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spring-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Manual Expense Entry is Painful**

After a trip, someone has to sit down, open Splitwise, manually type every expense one by one — amount, who paid, who was there. Takes 20-30 minutes and people make mistakes.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenge 1: Gemini Returning Dirty JSON
**The Bug:**
> We asked Gemini to return pure JSON for expense parsing, but it kept wrapping the response in markdown code blocks like:
> ````json
> ```json
> { "amount": 800 ... }
> ```
> ````
> This caused `JSON.parse()` to crash the entire API.

**How we fixed it:**
```javascript
// Added a cleaning step before parsing
const raw = result.response.text();
const cleaned = raw.replace(/```json|```/g, "").trim();
const parsed = JSON.parse(cleaned);
```
> Lesson learned: Never trust raw LLM output — always sanitize before parsing.

### Challenge 2: CORS Errors When Calling APIs from Frontend
**The Bug:**
> When the frontend tried to call ElevenLabs and OpenRouter APIs directly from the browser, we got:
> ```
> Access to fetch blocked by CORS policy
> ```

**How we fixed it:**
> Moved all API calls to **Next.js backend API routes** (`/pages/api/`). The browser never calls external APIs directly anymore — it only calls our own backend, which then calls ElevenLabs/OpenRouter/Gemini safely from the server side.



### Challenge 3: Voice Recording Not Working on Chrome
**The Bug:**
> `MediaRecorder` was capturing audio but the Blob format (`audio/webm`) wasn't being accepted by the speech-to-text API. The transcription was returning empty strings.

**How we fixed it:**
> Switched to the **Web Speech API** (browser native) as fallback:
```javascript
const recognition = new window.webkitSpeechRecognition();
recognition.lang = "en-IN"; // Indian English
recognition.onresult = (e) => {
  const text = e.results[0][0].transcript;
  // send to parse-expense
};
```
> This was actually more reliable AND required zero backend infrastructure.


### Challenge 4: Algorand Transaction Failing on Testnet
**The Bug:**
> Algorand payments were throwing:
> ```
> overspend: account balance too low
> ```
> Even though we were on testnet, our wallet had zero ALGO.

**How we fixed it:**
> Used the **Algorand Testnet Dispenser** at `dispenser.testnet.algoexplorer.io` to fund test wallets. Also added a balance check before every transaction:
```javascript
const accountInfo = await algodClient.accountInformation(sender).do();
if (accountInfo.amount < amount + 1000) {
  return res.status(400).json({ error: "Insufficient balance" });
}
```


### Challenge 5: Hindi/Hinglish Parsing Giving Wrong Results
**The Bug:**
> When users typed *"Rahul ne 500 rupaye diye sab ke liye"*, OpenRouter's Mixtral model parsed `paid_by` as `null` and `amount` as `0`. It simply didn't understand Hinglish.

**How we fixed it:**
> Switched Hinglish input specifically to **Gemini** which handles Indian languages natively. We added language detection first:
```javascript
// If text contains Hindi characters or common Hinglish words
const isHinglish = /[अ-ह]|(\bne\b|\bke liye\b|\bdiye\b)/i.test(text);
const endpoint = isHinglish ? "/api/parse-expense-gemini" : "/api/parse-expense";
```



### Challenge 6: Environment Variables Not Loading on Vercel
**The Bug:**
> Everything worked perfectly on localhost but after deploying to Vercel, all API calls failed with:
> ```
> Error: API key is undefined
> ```

**How we fixed it:**
> We had forgotten to add the `.env.local` keys to **Vercel's dashboard**. Vercel doesn't read your local `.env.local` file — you have to manually add each key in:
> `Vercel Dashboard → Project → Settings → Environment Variables`


### Challenge 7: Receipt Image Too Large for Gemini API
**The Bug:**
> When users uploaded a photo of a receipt directly from their phone camera, it was 4-8MB. Gemini's API was timing out and throwing size errors.

**How we fixed it:**
> Added client-side image compression before sending:
```javascript
const compressImage = (file) => {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
    const img = new Image();
    img.onload = () => {
      canvas.width = 800; // max width
      canvas.height = (img.height / img.width) * 800;
      canvas.getContext("2d").drawImage(img, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
      resolve(canvas.toDataURL("image/jpeg", 0.7).split(",")[1]); // base64
    };
    img.src = URL.createObjectURL(file);
  });
};

**Algorand Bharat**

## How Algorand is Used


Algorand is the **payment layer** of the app. Instead of just tracking who owes whom (like Splitwise), your app actually **settles debts on blockchain** with real transactions.



### Where It's Used

**1. Wallet Connection**
Every user connects their Algorand wallet when joining a group. Their wallet address acts as their payment identity inside the app.

**2. One-Click Payment Settlement**
When the app shows *"Rahul owes Ritika ₹200"*, Rahul clicks **"Pay"** → Algorand transaction executes instantly → debt is automatically marked settled.

```javascript
const txn = algosdk.makePaymentTxnWithSuggestedParamsFromObject({
  from: senderWallet,
  to: receiverWallet,
  amount: amountInMicroAlgos, // 1 ALGO = 1,000,000 microAlgos
  suggestedParams: await algodClient.getTransactionParams().do(),
});
```

**3. Permanent Transaction Proof**
Every payment is recorded on Algorand blockchain permanently. Anyone in the group can verify *"yes this payment happened"* — no disputes, no trust issues.

**4. Optimized Settlements**
AI first minimizes the number of transactions needed, then Algorand executes only those optimized payments — saving time and transaction fees.


### Why Algorand Specifically
- ⚡ Transactions confirm in **under 4 seconds**
- 💰 Fees are extremely low (**0.001 ALGO** per transaction)
- 🌱 Carbon negative — environmentally friendly
- 🇮🇳 Works without traditional banking infrastructure.

### Simple Flow
```
AI calculates who owes whom
        ↓
User clicks "Settle Up"
        ↓
Algorand transaction fires
        ↓
Blockchain confirms in 4 seconds
        ↓
Debt marked as settled in app
```
