### Safe-route
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/saferoute-a087) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Yashwardhan2/safe-route/tree/main) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/XApeItXeMVI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AceHack%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://acehack5.devfolio.co)

> Navigate smarter. Avoid danger. Arrive safe.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most navigation apps like Google Maps route you based purely on distance or time — they have no awareness of crime hotspots, dangerous neighbourhoods, or how safety changes after dark.
Safe-route solves this by:

Ingesting 600,000+ real crime incidents from Chicago's open data portal (2025 year)
Clustering them into danger hotspots using HDBSCAN
Embedding danger scores directly onto every street edge in an OSMnx graph
Running a custom A* algorithm with three safety modes — Fastest, Balanced, and Safest

Who needs this:

A woman walking home alone at 2 AM
A tourist unfamiliar with which neighbourhoods to avoid
A delivery worker choosing between two routes at night

The app shows all three routes simultaneously on a live map with safety scores out of 100, danger cluster overlays, and a time-of-day slider that dynamically recalculates risk — because a street that's safe at noon can be a danger zone at midnight.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Balanced and Safest routes were identical
The original cost function used a flat additive penalty (+500 × danger). With safety_weight=0.2, balanced barely differed from safest — on a 40km route, balanced was taking 66km just like safest. The fix was switching to a proportional formula (length × (1 + danger^1.5 × time_mult × weight)) so penalties scale with edge length, not overpower it.
2. Safest route was cutting straight through danger clusters
Even with penalties, the green route passed directly through the largest crime hotspot. The issue was the penalty coefficient wasn't strong enough to make a 500m safe detour cheaper than a 50m dangerous shortcut. Raising the coefficient and adding hard physical distance caps (A* prunes any path exceeding fastest × 1.80) fixed this.
3. Night-time routing produced runaway detours
At 3 AM (time_multiplier = 10×), the safest route was adding +147 minutes and scoring lower than balanced — it was taking such a massive southern detour that it passed through entirely different crime clusters. The fix was capping time_mult independently for each mode rather than letting it multiply unchecked.
4. HDBSCAN on 680,000 crime points was computationally infeasible
Running haversine-metric HDBSCAN on the full dataset would have taken hours. We stratified-sampled down to 80,000 points while preserving the severity distribution, bringing runtime to under 5 minutes without losing meaningful cluster structure.

**Challenges we ran into**

🔥 Challenge 1 — Google Sign-In Was Completely Broken
Every login attempt hit a blank error screen. The OAuth redirect URI wasn't registered in Google Cloud Console and Firebase was initializing multiple times due to Next.js hot reload.
Fix: Added the Firebase auth handler URL to Google Cloud's authorized redirect URIs. Wrapped Firebase init with a getApps().length === 0 guard to prevent duplicate instances.

🗺️ Challenge 2 — Google Maps Showed a Grey Error Box
API key was correct but the map refused to load. Turns out having an API key isn't enough — each Google API needs to be individually enabled in Cloud Console.
Fix: Manually enabled Maps JavaScript API, Geocoding API and Places API separately in the Cloud Library. Created an unrestricted dev key for localhost testing.

⚙️ Challenge 3 — Dev Server Refused to Start
After a crash, npm run dev threw a lock file conflict error and the server wouldn't launch at all.
Fix: Force-killed all Node processes, deleted .next/dev/lock manually, restarted. One command, two minutes, never forgotten.

🔐 Challenge 4 — Firestore Silently Blocked Everything
After enabling production security rules, the entire app went blank. No listings, no data, no errors — just silence. Missing or insufficient permissions hiding in the console.
Fix: Rewrote rules with proper role-based logic. Tested every rule in the Firestore Simulator before deploying.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major hurdle we faced was related to deployment and routing issues after authentication.

The Problem
After deploying the project, the home page loaded correctly, but when a user logged in or navigated to protected pages, the application returned a 404 error. This happened because the hosting platform did not recognize the client-side routes used in our single-page application.

Why It Happened
Our frontend used client-side routing, but the server was trying to find actual files for routes like `/dashboard` or `/profile`, which do not physically exist.

How We Solved It
We fixed this by configuring the deployment platform to redirect all routes to the main `index.html` file, allowing the frontend router to handle navigation.

For example, we added a configuration file to rewrite routes so that every request loads the SPA entry point.

Result
After applying the fix:
- Authentication redirects worked correctly
- All routes loaded without 404 errors
- The application behaved correctly in production

This experience helped us understand the importance of proper deployment configuration for single-page applications.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: Most e-commerce platforms are text-heavy, require complex form-filling, and operate primarily in English. This alienates roughly 60% of rural artisans who are not tech-savvy or comfortable typing out detailed product descriptions in English. The Solution ("Voice-First Commerce"): BharatKart allows artisans to simply tap a microphone and speak about their product in their native dialect (supporting 11 Indian languages). Instead of filling out 20 complex form fields, the artisan just describes the item naturally.

2. Time-Consuming Digital Onboarding
The Problem: Creating a professional digital listing usually takes a lot of time and technical know-how. The Solution: The platform uses AI (Google's Gemini 1.5 Flash) to analyze the artisan's voice recording and automatically extract structured data like the product's name, material, region, and price. This auto-fills the product form, reducing the time it takes to create a listing from 20 minutes to just 2 minutes.

3. Middlemen Exploitation
The Problem: Because artisans lack market access and digital skills, they rely on middlemen to sell their goods, who often take massive cuts (up to 40% margins). The Solution: By making it effortless for artisans to list products online, BharatKart empowers them to sell directly to buyers (like a customer in London wanting authentic Indian decor), ensuring the artisan receives the full payment and the buyer gets an authentic, verified product.

In short, it is an inclusive, AI-powered platform designed to bring millions of offline, non-tech-savvy artisans into the digital economy effortlessly through the power of voice.

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**

FarmToFabric bridges the gap between raw textile producers and fabric manufacturers, streamlining the supply chain from farm to finished fabric.

**Key Challenges Addressed:**

Lack of transparency: Farmers, suppliers, and manufacturers often have no real-time visibility into raw material quality and availability.

Inefficient sourcing: Manufacturers spend excessive time finding reliable suppliers and verifying fabric quality.

Quality inconsistency: Variations in fabric type, texture, and grade lead to production delays and waste.

Manual record-keeping: Tracking orders, inspections, and shipments is often paper-based or fragmented, leading to errors.

**How FarmToFabric Helps:**

Real-time tracking: Users can monitor raw material quality, location, and supplier reliability through a unified platform.

Smart quality analysis: AI-powered prediction of fabric type, grade, and defects reduces manual inspection effort.

Simplified sourcing: Manufacturers can quickly find verified suppliers, compare products, and make informed purchasing decisions.

Transparency & accountability: Every batch is traceable from farm to factory, reducing disputes and improving trust.

**Use Cases:**

Farmers can showcase their produce to multiple manufacturers without intermediaries.

Fabric manufacturers can streamline procurement and reduce defective material.

Apparel brands can ensure consistent quality and sustainability in their supply chain.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

Integrating real-time AI for fabric quality prediction was challenging because processing large images slowed the system. I solved this by optimizing the model, resizing images, and batching predictions.

Ensuring supplier data consistency was another hurdle, which I addressed by adding validation checks and standardized input fields.

Keeping the React.js UI synchronized with backend updates caused flickering, fixed by implementing WebSockets and React Query for smooth real-time updates.

Balancing prediction speed and accuracy was tricky, so I added progressive loading with confidence thresholds to provide instant results while final analysis completed.

**The problem it solves**

1. Build an application that helps students set savings goals and track their progress using Algorand. Users can create multiple savings goals (like "New Laptop," "Trip Fund," "Emergency Fund") and the app tracks deposits made toward each goal using ASAs or ALGO.
2. Build a crowdfunding platform specifically for campus projects, clubs, and student initiatives. Students can create campaigns, set funding goals, and accept contributions in ALGO or stablecoins. All transactions are transparent and recorded on Algorand.

Savings Goals App
Getting started was trickier than expected — every new savings goal needs an ASA opt-in, which costs real ALGO. Students with near-empty wallets hit a wall immediately. Mapping multiple goals to a single wallet without mixing up balances was also messier than it looks on paper.
Crowdfunding Platform
The hardest part was handling failed campaigns — returning funds to contributors automatically using smart contracts required more logic than I anticipated. Stablecoin support added another layer since each one (USDC, etc.) is a separate ASA with its own opt-in requirement. Campus Wallet

And since this is student-facing, I had to abstract away almost all the blockchain complexity while keeping it actually functional.
Across all three
Testnet ALGO availability was a constant friction point during development. Algorand's documentation is solid but scattered — piecing together the SDK, indexer, and node calls from different sources slowed things down noticeably.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wikipedia Api](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wikipedia%20Api-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gemini API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gemini%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

HalluciScan — AI Hallucination Auditor
Project Overview
HalluciScan is an AI-powered system designed to detect hallucinations in AI-generated text.
The platform verifies factual claims produced by large language models and checks them against trusted external knowledge sources.
It helps improve the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-generated reports, articles, and summaries.
Problem Statement
Generative AI models sometimes produce incorrect or fabricated information, known as hallucinations.
These inaccuracies reduce the reliability of AI systems in professional and enterprise environments.
HalluciScan solves this problem by introducing a validation layer that fact-checks AI outputs in real time.
Core Idea
Extract factual claims from AI-generated text.
Search trusted knowledge sources for supporting evidence.
Compare the claims with retrieved information.
Calculate a confidence score indicating how reliable the claim is.
Key Features
Claim Extraction – Automatically identifies factual statements in AI-generated text.
Evidence Retrieval – Searches external knowledge sources such as Wikipedia to find relevant information.
Fact Verification – Compares extracted claims with retrieved evidence.
Hallucination Detection – Flags claims that are likely incorrect or unsupported.
Confidence Score – Generates a reliability score for each claim.
Sentence-Level Highlighting – Visually highlights factual, uncertain, and hallucinated statements.
Evidence Viewer – Displays sources used for verification.
Interactive Dashboard – Presents analysis results in a clear and structured interface.
System Workflow
User inputs AI-generated text.
The system extracts factual claims from the text.
External knowledge sources are queried to retrieve evidence.
Claims are compared with the retrieved information.
A confidence score is generated for each claim.
The results are displayed on the dashboard.
Technology Stack
Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, CSS
Backend: Node.js API routes
AI Integration: Google Gemini API
Knowledge Sources: Wikipedia API and external search APIs
Use Cases
Verifying AI-generated reports and articles.
Fact-checking AI outputs before publishing content.
Improving reliability of enterprise AI systems.
Supporting researchers, analysts, and journalists in validating information.
Impact
Reduces misinformation in AI-generated content.
Helps users identify unreliable or hallucinated statements.
Enables safer and more trustworthy use of generative AI systems.

**Challenges we ran into**

Problem Description
Modern generative AI models are widely used to generate reports, summaries, research notes, and answers to complex questions.
However, these models sometimes produce incorrect, fabricated, or misleading information, a phenomenon commonly known as AI hallucination.
Hallucinations occur when a language model generates statements that appear convincing but are not supported by real-world facts or reliable sources.
Why This Is a Problem
AI-generated content is increasingly used in business reports, research work, journalism, and decision-making processes.
If incorrect information is included in these outputs, it can lead to:
Misleading conclusions
Incorrect decision-making
Spread of misinformation
Loss of trust in AI systems
Current Limitation
Most generative AI tools do not automatically verify the factual correctness of the information they produce.
Users must manually fact-check AI outputs, which is time-consuming and inefficient, especially for long documents or complex reports.
Problem the Project Solves
There is a need for a system that can automatically validate AI-generated text and determine whether the claims are factual or potentially hallucinated.
The system should analyze the content, retrieve evidence from trusted knowledge sources, and provide a confidence score indicating the reliability of each claim.
Goal
Build a real-time AI validation layer that checks AI outputs against reliable information sources and helps users quickly identify factual inaccuracies.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

HalluciScan is an AI-powered browser extension that detects hallucinations in responses generated by AI platforms. Our project integrates the **Gemini API** to analyze AI-generated text and evaluate the probability of hallucinated or misleading information.

When a user interacts with AI platforms such as ChatGPT or other LLM-based tools, the extension captures the response text and sends it to our analysis system powered by Gemini. Gemini processes the content, evaluates factual consistency, and returns a hallucination risk score along with highlighted suspicious sentences.

The extension then displays a floating panel directly on the page showing the hallucination score, risk level, and highlighted lines that may contain incorrect or unsupported information. This helps users instantly verify AI responses and avoid relying on potentially misleading content.

By using the Gemini API for intelligent text analysis, HalluciScan transforms AI usage into a safer and more trustworthy experience for students, developers, and researchers.

**Best Use of Vultr**

HalluciScan is an AI-powered browser extension designed to detect hallucinations in responses generated by large language models. Our project combines intelligent text analysis with scalable cloud infrastructure to help users identify potentially misleading AI-generated information.

The extension captures AI responses from supported platforms and sends the text to our backend analysis service. This backend is deployed on **Vultr Cloud**, where our API processes the data and communicates with the Gemini API to analyze the factual reliability of the response. The system calculates a hallucination probability score and identifies sentences that may contain unsupported or inaccurate claims.

Using Vultr’s cloud infrastructure allows our application to run a fast and scalable analysis service that can handle multiple requests from users in real time. The results are returned to the extension, which displays a floating panel on the page showing the hallucination score, risk level, and highlighted suspicious statements.

By combining Vultr’s reliable cloud platform with AI-powered analysis, HalluciScan provides a scalable and practical solution for improving trust in AI-generated information.

> Every child noticed. Every mother heard.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

NeuroNurture — What It Does
 ARM 1 — For Mothers

The problem it solves: Most mothers don't realise they're slipping into postpartum depression until they're already deep in it. And when they do, they have no one to talk to at 3am and no easy way to get help.

- Daily mood check-ins catch declining patterns before they become a crisis
- The AI chatbot is available when no one else is — no judgment, no wait time
- SafeCircle connects you anonymously with mothers having the exact same week as you
- When you need real help, booking a specialist is two taps away — not a phone call and a two-week wait
🟢 ARM 2 — For Parents of Young Children

The problem it solves: Parents often sense something is off with their child's development before any doctor does — but have no structured way to act on that instinct, and no idea what to look for.

- A general quiz (no medical knowledge needed) figures out the area of concern on its own — you just answer questions about your child
- Tracks behaviour across multiple sessions, not just one snapshot
- Adaptive therapy games work at home, on a phone, at the child's own pace
- Generates a report you can actually bring to a doctor — instead of just saying "I'm worried"

**Challenges we ran into**

The Quiz Branching Problem
The trickiest part of building ARM 2 was the adaptive quiz flow.
Our original design had separate quizzes for each condition — ASD, Dyslexia, Dyscalculia. The problem was immediately obvious when we tested it: parents had to choose which condition to screen for. Most parents have no idea what they're looking for. A parent noticing their child struggles with reading doesn't know whether that points to Dyslexia, an attention issue, or just a confidence problem. Asking them to pick a category upfront was the wrong starting point entirely.

What We Did
We restructured the entire quiz into a staged branching system — inspired by how MBTI works. Stage 1 asks completely general questions about the child. No labels, no conditions mentioned. Based on the pattern of answers, the quiz silently identifies which domain to explore and branches into Stage 2 automatically.
The parent just sees a flowing set of questions. The routing logic happens entirely in the background.

What We Learned
Designing for someone who doesn't know what they don't know is genuinely hard. The instinct when building a tool is to give users options and control. But sometimes the right UX decision is to remove choices entirely — and let the system figure it out for them.
That one restructure made the whole ARM 2 experience feel less like a medical test and more like a conversation.

### PrivGuard - sandbox
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/privguard-sandbox-c0a2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aashlesh-lokesh/PrivGuard---Sandbox) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> Leave no digital footprint behind.

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chrome Extension](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome%20Extension-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3​](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3​-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In today’s digital age, we are constantly entering sensitive information into web platforms, often without realizing how much we are oversharing. PrivGuard acts as a proactive, intelligent filter between your keyboard and the internet.

1. Prevention of "The Oops Paste."
We’ve all done it: accidentally pasting a password, an AWS API key, or a private note into a public chat or a search engine.

The Solution: PrivGuard monitors your input in real-time. If you paste something sensitive, the Shield Active UI blurs it instantly, requiring a conscious "Unblur" or "Redact" action before you accidentally hit enter.

2. Safeguarding AI Conversations
Platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are powerful, but they store your prompts to train their models. Sending PII (Personally Identifiable Information) to these LLMs is a major security risk for both individuals and companies.

The Solution: Our specialized LLM Shield detects PII like phone numbers, emails, and Aadhaar/SSN numbers within chat interfaces. It prompts you to Auto-Redact your data before it ever reaches the AI’s servers.

3. Secure Screenshot Sharing
Sharing a screenshot of a conversation or a bug often leads to accidental leaks of email addresses or internal IDs visible in the background.

The Solution: Our Screenshot Masking feature isn't just a filter—it’s a post-processor. It identifies sensitive text on your screen and physically burns solid black redaction bars into the image file. This makes the redaction permanent and irreversible, unlike simple drawing tools.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Divergent Branch" Git Crisis
During a critical phase of the hackathon, my local environment and the remote GitHub repository diverged. A simple git pull failed, stalling our progress just as we were trying to integrate the NVIDIA Nemotron API.

The Solution: To ensure we were working on the most stable version of the project, I used:

git fetch origin

git reset --hard origin/main

git clean -fd
This wiped the local "mess" and synced my MacBook Air exactly to my partner's latest stable code, allowing us to resume building immediately.

2. The [object Object] Serialization Bug
The Hurdle: One of the most frustrating bugs was seeing [object Object] appear in the UI instead of the blocked sensitive data. This happened because the background script was sending raw JavaScript objects to the popup, but the UI was expecting a simple string.

The Solution: I overhauled the Data Bridge. I implemented a strict Integration Protocol in background.js and popup.js that forced all data into clean strings using String(payload) and JSON.parse() only when necessary. This ensured that the Recent Blocked Data list displayed readable text while keeping the underlying data secure.

3. Asynchronous AI Latency
The Hurdle: Integrating NVIDIA Nemotron meant moving from near-instant regex checks to asynchronous API calls. If the user typed faster than the AI could respond, the blurring would lag, creating a "privacy window" where data was briefly visible.

The Solution: I implemented Contextual Debouncing. I modified the content_llms.js script to wait for a 400ms pause in typing before hitting the AI engine. To bridge the gap, I kept a local regex "fast-pass" for obvious patterns (like 10-digit numbers) that triggers a blur instantly, while the Nemotron AI runs in the background to provide the "smart" final verdict.

4. Manifest V3 Service Worker Dormancy
The Hurdle: In Manifest V3, background scripts (Service Workers) go to sleep after a period of inactivity. This meant our Image Security Audit would sometimes fail to trigger because the "brain" of the extension was essentially offline.

The Solution: I moved the core detection state into chrome.storage.local. By making the extension "stateless," the background script could wake up, read the current risk level from storage, perform the scan, and go back to sleep without losing the user's session data.

### AIGuardian
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aiguardian-eb58) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/No-Reed/AIGuardian) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1bEJC6uQBdk3OnRGG6fKiKSvwmAmUVNRjaSECgBbFAVw/edit?usp=sharing) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/GFQr4XTZPkE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> C++ Runtime guard for AI Agent tool calls.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![CMake](https://img.shields.io/badge/CMake-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents are dangerous in a specific, underappreciated way — not because they go rogue, but because they're given real tools with real consequences and nobody's watching the sequence.

Every major agent framework (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI) makes it trivially easy to give a model access to databases, email, file systems, APIs, and code execution. What none of them give you is any runtime guarantee about what the model does with that access.

Here's what that looks like in practice:

An agent reads a customer database, finds a relevant record, and emails it to an external address. Both tool calls are individually "correct" — the agent was just being helpful. No one defined that you can't chain read_db → send_email without a sanitization step in between. Data just left the building.

An agent is given access to a CI/CD pipeline and decides a bug fix is safe to deploy. It skips the request_approval step because the model reasoned it wasn't necessary. The fix breaks prod. The model was not malicious — it was confident.

A reasoning agent gets stuck in a loop and hammers an internal search service 4,000 times before the on-call engineer wakes up. No quota, no circuit breaker, no guard — just an agent that got confused.

The existing mitigations work at the wrong layer. Prompt engineering changes what the model wants to do. Model fine-tuning changes what it's likely to do. Output filters catch what it says. None of them intercept what it executes.

AIGuardian sits directly in the tool dispatch path. You declare a policy: which tools exist, which transitions between them are allowed, which nodes touch sensitive data. Every tool call the agent makes is checked against that graph before it reaches the executor. If the transition isn't in the policy, the call is blocked — regardless of why the model decided to make it.

Who actually needs this:

Teams running agentic pipelines on production data (finance, healthcare, legal)
Developers building multi-agent systems where a planner spawns subagents with broad access
Security engineers who need an audit trail of every tool call an AI made, in sequence, with the reason each was allowed or denied
Any org that needs to tell a regulator "here is proof our AI cannot exfiltrate patient data" — and have that proof be a live enforcement mechanism, not a slide deck
The decision runs in C++, takes ~5 microseconds, and the model has no path to reason around it. The policy is owned by your security team, lives in git, and goes through PR review like infrastructure code.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest bug: SSE events were firing but the browser never received them

The SOC dashboard uses Server-Sent Events to stream policy decisions to the frontend in real time. I had the /events endpoint working — curl could connect and receive the stream — but the browser dashboard showed nothing. Sat on this for longer than I'd like to admit.

The issue turned out to be CORS. The SSE endpoint was responding correctly, but the browser was silently blocking the stream because the CORS preflight didn't include the right headers for text/event-stream responses. The fix was adding Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Cache-Control: no-cache on the SSE response specifically, not just on the normal JSON endpoints. Once I saw it I couldn't unsee it — but finding it required actually reading what the browser's network tab was saying about the options request, not the GET.

Building the policy graph session state correctly

The PolicyGraph isn't just a static graph — it needs to track where each session currently is in the graph, so consecutive calls build on each other. My first implementation stored the "current node" per session correctly, but I hadn't thought through what happens when a session tries an invalid transition. I was mutating the state before validating the edge, which meant a failed call would corrupt the session state and subsequent valid calls would be blocked. The fix was to validate the full transition first, then commit the state update — classic check-then-act. Obvious in hindsight, invisible in the moment.

The scenario animations in the dashboard weren't sequencing

The demo has three pre-built incident scenarios that animate through a sequence of tool calls — each step lights up green or red with a short delay. My first implementation called a backend /demo/run/:scenario endpoint that ran the whole sequence server-side and returned a result. That meant the animation had to be driven from a single response, which meant I had to reconstruct the sequence client-side anyway from a response I'd already thrown away.

The fix was to ditch the server-side scenario runner entirely and drive the sequence directly from JavaScript — each step calls /session, then the individual /intercept calls in order, with async/await and deliberate delays between them. The frontend owns the animation state. The backend is just the enforcement engine. That's actually the correct architecture — I just had to get the wrong one working first to see why.

Getting RapidCheck (property-based testing) to behave on Windows

RapidCheck is a C++ property-based testing library, and integrating it as a CMake FetchContent dependency on Windows with MSYS2 was not the smooth experience the docs implied. The library was building fine but the test runner was linking against the wrong runtime, producing cryptic __imp___acrt_iob_func errors at link time. The fix was explicitly setting -DCMAKE_MSYSTEM=UCRT64 and making sure the RapidCheck build picked up the same compiler flags as the rest of the project. Two hours of CMake archaeology for three lines of fix.

Writing a policy that was interesting enough to demo but simple enough to explain in 60 seconds

This sounds soft but it was genuinely tricky. A policy that blocks everything is safe but boring. A policy that's too permissive makes the demo unconvincing. I went through about five iterations before landing on the current 9-edge graph — it's small enough to visualize on a screen, but covers all three failure modes (exfiltration, unauthorized deploy, loop detection) with distinct paths for each demo scenario. The constraint of "a judge has to understand this graph at a glance" was actually a useful forcing function for keeping the API surface clean too.

> Your price left the server.It arrives the same way

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Core ProblemAny e-commerce site that builds its own checkout flow has a hidden vulnerability the server trusts the price the browser sends.
A customer adds ₹1,499 tea to their cart. The browser sends total: 1499.00 to the server. The server charges that amount. Simple.But an attacker opens Burp Suite, intercepts that request mid-flight, changes total: 1499.00 to total: 1, and forwards it. The server charges 1 rs. The order goes through. The shop loses money and never knows why.This is not theoretical. It happens to small Indian startups, freelancer-built shops, and anyone using custom UPI or COD checkout flows instead of a fully managed payment gateway.

**Challenges we ran into**

One challenge we faced was making sure the HMAC cart signature stayed valid across the entire checkout flow. During testing, when we intercepted the request in Burp Suite and modified the price, sometimes the server still accepted the request because the signature was not being recomputed correctly during verification.

We solved this by ensuring that the server recreates the HMAC signature using the exact same cart data and secret key during checkout and compares it with the original signature. If even a single value (like the price) is changed, the signatures no longer match and the request is rejected. This fix allowed us to reliably detect and block price-tampering attacks

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![NetworkX](https://img.shields.io/badge/NetworkX-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem Statement

Finite State Machines (FSMs) are a core component of digital hardware systems and are widely used by RTL designers to implement control logic in processors, communication controllers, security modules, and embedded systems. These FSMs define how a system transitions between different operational states based on inputs and internal conditions.

However, designing secure and reliable FSMs is challenging for RTL engineers. As designs grow more complex, FSMs can contain **dozens or even hundreds of states and transitions**, making it extremely difficult to manually verify every possible execution path.

RTL designers commonly face several challenges:

* **Hidden illegal transitions** that may unintentionally allow the system to enter unsafe states.
*Dead or unreachable states caused by incomplete transition logic.
* Missing guard conditions on transitions, allowing unexpected inputs to alter control flow.
* Improper reset handling, which can push the FSM into undefined states during power-up or recovery.
* Security vulnerabilities* where attackers could manipulate input signals to force the system into privileged or unintended states.

Traditional verification tools such as simulation and basic formal checks primarily focus on **functional correctness**, ensuring that the design behaves as intended under normal conditions. However, they rarely provide automated methods to **detect security weaknesses within FSM structures or recommend fixes**.

Because of this, RTL designers often have to manually inspect FSM logic, analyze large `case` statements, and reason about complex transition paths—an error-prone and time-consuming process.

FSMGuard AI addresses this gap by providing an **automated analysis and repair framework**. It extracts FSM structures from Verilog designs, models them as graphs, detects vulnerable states using graph neural networks, and applies reinforcement learning to generate secure fixes. The system then formally verifies the patched design to ensure both **functional correctness and improved security**, significantly reducing the burden on RTL designers.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges Encountered

One of the main challenges during the development of FSMGuard AI was evolving the project from a simple prototype into a more structured, industry-style pipeline.

Initially, the system relied on basic FSM extraction and simple rule-based analysis. However, real-world RTL designs are far more complex, with FSM logic spread across multiple blocks, conditional transitions, and reset behaviors. This required improving the parsing and FSM reconstruction process to make the analysis more reliable.

Another challenge was **designing a pipeline where multiple components—static analysis, graph representation, machine learning, reinforcement learning, and formal verification—could work together seamlessly**. Ensuring that each stage produced consistent and usable outputs for the next stage required careful structuring of the workflow.

Finally, creating an RL environment that could modify FSM transitions while preserving functional correctness required defining meaningful constraints and rewards.

Addressing these challenges helped transform FSMGuard AI from a basic analysis tool into a more scalable and structured framework closer to industry-grade hardware security analysis workflows.

### CodeGuardian
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/codeguardian-0b34) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Aryan-jaiswa/codeGuardianFinal-Project.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Aegis%20SandBox%20v2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://aegis-sandbox-v.devfolio.co)

> Scan, trace, and patch vulnerabilities automatic

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern software projects often contain hidden security vulnerabilities such as SQL injections, hardcoded secrets, insecure API usage, and command injection, which are usually introduced unintentionally during development and can remain unnoticed until they lead to serious security breaches. While existing security tools can detect these vulnerabilities, they typically only show what is vulnerable without explaining when or where the issue was introduced, forcing developers to manually investigate the origin of the problem and implement fixes themselves through time-consuming code changes and pull requests. This slows development workflows and increases security risks. CodeGuardian addresses this challenge by combining automated vulnerability detection, Git-based forensic analysis, and automated patch generation into a single workflow. It scans GitHub repositories for security issues, identifies the exact commit and author responsible for introducing the vulnerable code using Git history analysis, visualizes how vulnerabilities evolve over time through a security timeline, and automatically generates secure patches that can be applied through a pull request with minimal developer intervention. By automating detection, investigation, and remediation, CodeGuardian helps development teams identify security issues earlier, trace vulnerabilities back to their origin, fix them faster, and maintain more secure and reliable codebases with significantly less manual effort.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges while building CodeGuardian was correctly linking detected vulnerabilities to the exact commit that introduced them. While Semgrep could identify vulnerable code and provide the file and line number, mapping that information back to the responsible commit required reliable integration with Git history. Initially, the system struggled to correctly extract commit metadata and sometimes returned incorrect or empty results when running git blame on dynamically cloned repositories. Another challenge was ensuring that automatic patches were actually applied to the correct lines in the source code, since matching code snippets directly often failed due to formatting differences. This was resolved by modifying the patching logic to apply fixes based on line numbers rather than string matching. Additionally, integrating Semgrep with the Node.js backend caused encoding issues on Windows systems due to Python’s default character encoding, which prevented scan results from being parsed correctly.  Overcoming these issues required careful debugging of Git commands, improving the patch generation logic, and stabilizing the backend scanning workflow to ensure vulnerabilities could be detected, traced, patched, and converted into pull requests reliably.

> Because Scammers deserve a Smarter Listener

![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![FAST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/FAST%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem

* **Phone call scams are rapidly increasing worldwide**, targeting individuals through impersonation and social engineering.
* Scammers often pretend to be **bank officials, government authorities, delivery services, or tech support** to gain trust.
* Victims are pressured to reveal **sensitive information** such as OTPs, card numbers, passwords, or to make urgent payments.
* Existing solutions mainly rely on **caller ID blocking or number blacklists**, which are ineffective because scammers frequently **change or spoof phone numbers**.
* Scam calls follow **psychological manipulation patterns**, including:

  * Creating **false urgency** (“Your account will be blocked immediately”)
  * Claiming **authority** (“I’m calling from the bank/police”)
  * Repeating **scripted phrases** used in call-center scam operations
  * Pressuring victims to **act quickly without thinking**
* Traditional spam filters cannot analyze **live call behavior or conversation context**, making real-time detection difficult.

---

### Our Approach

* Our system detects scam calls by analyzing **live audio streams during a call**.
* It uses **AI-based multi-modal analysis** to identify suspicious speech patterns, urgency, and conversation stages.
* The system generates a **real-time risk score**, warning users before they share sensitive information.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Key Challenges We Solved

* **Lack of real-world datasets**

  * Scam call audio datasets are extremely rare.
  * We **collected and created our own dataset** by recording multiple speakers simulating scam scenarios.

* **MFCC audio features alone were insufficient**

  * Initial phoneme-based analysis using MFCC features produced **high false positives**.
  * Scam detection cannot rely only on raw acoustic features.

* **Added multi-layer behavioral analysis**

  * Introduced an **Urgency Layer** that detects vocal stress, pitch spikes, and abnormal speech rate often used to pressure victims.
  * Built a **Repetition Detection Layer** to identify repeated scam keywords and scripted phrases commonly used in call-center fraud.

* **False positives still remained**

  * Even with acoustic and keyword layers, normal conversations sometimes triggered alerts.

* **Modeling scammer psychology**

  * To solve this, we designed a **Conversation Stage Detection Layer** using sentence transformers.
  * This tracks how scam calls progress through stages such as:

    * Greeting
    * Authority claim
    * Problem creation
    * Urgency escalation
    * Data/OTP request

* **Risk Fusion Engine**

  * Outputs from all models are combined using a **weighted risk scoring system**.
  * This significantly reduces false positives while maintaining real-time detection.

* **Android platform limitations**

  * Android **does not allow direct access to call audio for privacy reasons**.
  * To overcome this, we developed a **custom VoIP calling application** that captures audio streams securely for real-time analysis.

* **Real-time processing challenge**

  * Built a **streaming pipeline using WebSockets** to send 4-second audio chunks to the backend.
  * AI models analyze each chunk and return **continuous scam risk alerts during the call**.

problems in android was audio processing from call was strictly banned so we made our own app supporting our own VoIP

**Cyber Security**

### How the Project Fits the Cyber Security Track

* Our project addresses **voice-based social engineering attacks**, one of the fastest growing forms of cyber fraud worldwide.
* Instead of relying on **blacklists or caller ID filtering**, the system analyzes **live call audio behavior** to detect scam patterns in real time.
* The platform combines **speech analysis, behavioral pattern detection, and AI-based intent classification** to identify scam tactics such as authority impersonation, urgency creation, and sensitive data requests.
* By detecting these signals early, the system can **warn users before they reveal confidential information like OTPs, passwords, or banking details**.
* This transforms scam detection from a **reactive reporting system into a proactive AI-based cybersecurity defense layer for phone communications**.

### Sevatra
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sevatra-604a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/monojitgoswami69/Sevatra) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Diversion%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://diversion2k26.devfolio.co)

> Severity-Based Smart AI Triage System

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

Every minute a critical patient spends waiting for triage, bed assignment, or doctor allocation is a minute their brain, heart, or lungs can't afford to lose. Yet today, most emergency systems treat the ambulance ride as dead time and hospitals only begin preparing *after* the patient arrives.

**The result?** Chaotic, reactive emergency rooms. Preventable deaths.

---

## The Broken Status Quo

**Triage starts at the door, not in the ambulance.** Doctors see the patient for the first time on arrival — no prior data, no preparation, no head start. The clock has already been ticking for 10–20 minutes.

**Beds and doctors are assigned in the moment.** Staff scramble to find the right specialist and an available bed while the patient's condition worsens on a stretcher in the hallway.

**The ambulance ride is medically wasted.** That critical 10–20 minute window in transit? Gone. No data captured, no hospital alerted, no preparation triggered.

**Every patient enters the same queue.** Without a pre-calculated severity profile, a cardiac arrest patient waits alongside a minor fracture case until a doctor physically walks over to assess them.

---

## How Sevatra Fixes This — Before the Patient Even Arrives

Sevatra is an **end-to-end smart emergency medical response platform** with one core promise: *by the time the ambulance pulls in, the hospital is already ready.*

Here's the flow that makes it happen:

**① SOS Dispatch** — A patient or bystander triggers an emergency via the AmbiSevatra app in seconds. Automatic location detection and OTP-based verification ensure the right ambulance reaches the right person, fast.

**② Vitals Captured En Route** — While the patient is still in transit, paramedics log real-time vitals through the LifeSavatra portal: heart rate, SpO₂, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and temperature. The ambulance is no longer dead time, it's the first point of care.

**③ Automated Severity Scoring** — Sevatra's clinical algorithm instantly computes a severity score from 0–10 and classifies the patient into one of four categories: Recovering (0–2) routed to the General Ward, Stable (3–4) also to the General Ward, Serious (5–7) to the High Dependency Unit, and Critical (8–10) directly to the ICU.

**④ Pre-Arrival Hospital Preparation** — This is the core of what makes Sevatra different. The severity score automatically triggers real-time assignment of an available bed *and* the right doctor or specialist at the target hospital, all before the ambulance arrives. No scrambling. No delays. The hospital is fully armed with the patient's profile the moment they roll through the door.

**⑤ Fleet & Operator Management** — The OperatoSevatra dashboard ensures the nearest available ambulance is always dispatched, optimizing fleet deployment across the city.

---

## Why This Matters

For conditions like **cardiac arrest, stroke, severe trauma, and respiratory distress**, the first 10 minutes are everything. Sevatra doesn't just speed up the process — it fundamentally **shifts preparation from arrival to transit**, turning reactive chaos into a coordinated, pre-planned response.

> The ambulance ride is no longer wasted time.
> Hospital arrival is no longer the start of treatment — it's the continuation of it.

**Sevatra gives patients the one thing the current system can't: a hospital that's ready before they get there.**

**The problem it solves**

**🧠 The Problem SmartBraille AI Solves**

Braille learning today faces serious accessibility and quality gaps:
❌ Lack of trained teachers in many schools and rural areas
❌ No real-time correction while practicing Braille writing
❌ Learners cannot identify which specific dot is wrong
❌ Limited Bengali + English Braille support
❌ Low engagement — traditional learning feels repetitive and boring
❌ Parents and teachers struggle to track improvement objectively

As a result, learners often practice incorrectly, lose motivation, and progress slowly.
💡 **What People Can Use It For**
SmartBraille AI transforms Braille learning into an intelligent, guided experience.

👩‍🎓 For Students

1.Practice Braille writing with instant AI correction
2.Get voice feedback instead of waiting for a teacher
3.Take voice-based quizzes for interactive learning
4.Ask the AI tutor questions anytime
5.Track improvement through progress analytics
6.Learn in English or Bengali

👩‍🏫 For Teachers

1.Monitor student performance via dashboard
2.See accuracy %, mistake trends, and weekly reports
Save time in manual correction
3.Generate worksheets using Text → Braille converter
4.Conduct engaging classroom quiz sessions

👨‍👩‍👧 For Parents

1.Support children at home without expert knowledge
2.Understand progress through visual reports
3.Ensure correct learning habits early

🏫 For Schools & NGOs

1.Provide scalable Braille education
2.Reduce dependency on limited specialists
3.Deploy AI-assisted teaching in underserved regions

🚀 How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer
✅ Real-Time Error Detection

Instead of practicing blindly and reinforcing mistakes, learners get instant correction with heatmap highlights.

✅ Faster Learning Curve

Immediate feedback + gamification = higher motivation and quicker mastery.

✅ Safer Skill Development

Correct dot placement is critical in Braille literacy. The AI ensures students build accurate foundational skills.

✅ Teacher Time Optimization

Automated checking reduces workload and allows teachers to focus on conceptual teaching.

✅ Inclusive Multilingual Learning

Supports both English and Bengali, making it regionally adaptable.

**Challenges we ran into**

🚧 Challenges I Ran Into

While building SmartBraille AI, I faced a few key technical hurdles:

🔍 1. Inconsistent Braille Dot Detection

Lighting variations, shadows, and uneven paper surfaces caused incorrect dot detection.
Solution: I improved image preprocessing using OpenCV (adaptive thresholding, noise reduction, contour filtering) and standardized input resolution. This significantly improved detection accuracy.

🧠 2. CNN Misclassification

The model struggled with similar Braille characters that differ by just one dot.
Solution: I expanded the dataset, applied data augmentation (rotation, noise), and fine-tuned hyperparameters to improve generalization.

🎙️ 3. Voice Feedback Latency

Text-to-Speech responses had noticeable delay, affecting real-time experience.
Solution: Implemented asynchronous backend handling and cached common responses to reduce latency.

📷 4. Real-Time Camera Performance

Live detection was slow due to heavy image processing.
Solution: Optimized frame processing (processing every nth frame) and moved intensive logic to the backend.

**The problem it solves**

Our project is a predictive attendance tracking system designed to solve the limitations of traditional college attendance systems. Most existing systems only record attendance and display percentages, but they do not help students understand their risk level or how to recover if their attendance drops below the required threshold. This often leads to last-minute panic, manual calculations, and unnecessary academic stress.

Our system goes beyond simple record-keeping by introducing secure QR-based attendance marking along with intelligent mathematical analytics. It automatically calculates a student’s attendance percentage, categorizes them into safe, warning, or danger zones, and determines exactly how many future classes they must attend to reach the mandatory 75% requirement.

Instead of merely showing that attendance is low, it provides a clear recovery path, making the system proactive rather than reactive. Faculty benefit from automated tracking and risk detection, while students gain transparency, clarity, and better academic planning. Overall, the system transforms attendance management into a predictive, structured, and student-friendly monitoring platform that reduces manual effort and improves academic discipline.

### X10V AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/xv-ai-3031) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/bytes06runner/genie-tech) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ATVYotP1ojQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Diversion%202K26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://diversion2k26.devfolio.co)

> Multi-agent AI swarm

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem
Current AI assistants are fundamentally blind and isolated. To get help with a coding error, a financial chart, or a complex research paper, users have to painstakingly copy-paste context back and forth between tabs. Worse, when asked to execute tasks, standard LLMs hallucinate because they lack real-time, verified internet access. 

Current "RPA" (Robotic Process Automation) requires heavy, friction-filled OS installations, and traditional web scrapers break the second a website changes its UI. We realized the world doesn't need another chatbot. It needs an omnipresent, screen-aware intelligence layer.

## The Solution: X10V AI
**X10V AI** is a headless, semantic automation swarm. It lives directly in your browser as a floating Document Picture-in-Picture (PiP) command center. It physically "sees" whatever tab you are looking at—from Groww stock charts to VS Code terminals—and uses a multi-agent AI swarm powered by Google Gemini to analyze, debate, fact-check, and ultimately execute actions on your behalf.

### How the Swarm Works (Powered by Gemini)
Instead of relying on a single model to guess the right answer, X10V utilizes a cognitive architecture of three distinct agents that debate in real-time before taking action:

1. **The Visionary (Gemini 2.5 Flash):** When the user triggers the PiP command center, we capture the active tab's screen frame. Gemini's state-of-the-art multimodal extraction instantly converts the visual pixels into structured semantic text.
2. **Agent Alpha (The Impulse):** Powered by Groq's Llama 3 for ultra-low latency, Alpha reads the screen and formulates an immediate, aggressive hypothesis (e.g., "This stock is crashing, execute a sell order!").
3. **Agent Beta (The Sentinel & Deep Scraper):** Powered by Gemini 2.5 Flash, Beta audits Alpha. It dynamically generates search queries based on the screen context, spins up a headless Playwright Chromium instance, bypasses bot protections, and scrapes the raw DOM of live news sites to fact-check Alpha's claim. 
4. **Agent Gamma (The Arbiter):** Powered by Gemini, Gamma synthesizes the debate. Using strict JSON enforcement, it outputs the final consensus, structures the data into beautiful Markdown (or generates a downloadable PDF for students), and hands the execution command back to the system.

### Key Technical Innovations
* **Document PiP Architecture:** We bypassed standard screen-sharing limitations by rendering our entire React UI inside the `window.documentPictureInPicture` API, allowing the swarm terminal to float seamlessly over any active workflow.
* **Zero-Hallucination Deep Scraping:** By combining Gemini's logical routing with Playwright's headless browser execution, our RAG pipeline doesn't just read search snippets—it reads the actual source websites to prevent hallucinations.
* **Stateless Cognitive Friction:** Our multi-agent loop forces models to argue with each other, ensuring that no action (whether generating study notes or analyzing a trade) is executed without a rigorous, live-data audit.

### Tech Stack
* **Frontend:** React, Vite, TailwindCSS, Document PiP API, WebSockets.
* **Backend:** FastAPI, Python, Playwright (Async DOM Extraction), APScheduler.
* **AI Engine:** Google Gemini SDK (Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro) for Vision & Arbitration, Groq for rapid hypothesis generation.

**The problem it solves**

Indian students and early professionals face fragmented, unreliable, and scattered career information across multiple platforms. They must separately research entrance exams, stream selection, colleges, scholarships, resume building, and interview prep.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into (Short Version)

API Key Handling in Frontend
Browser-based apps don’t support process.env, forcing a shift to Vite’s import.meta.env with VITE_ prefixes to avoid runtime failures.

Development Port Conflicts
Vite dynamically reassigned ports when 5173 was occupied, causing access confusion during testing.

Context-Aware AI Chat
Initial responses lacked memory and depth. Prompt engineering was refined to include chat history and system instructions for more natural conversations.

Premium Feature Gating in SPA
Required persistent state management via React Context and conditional routing to restrict non-premium access.

React JSX Styling Issue
A <style jsx> attribute caused rendering warnings. Removing the unsupported jsx attribute resolved the issue.

**Best Beginners' Team**

Built mainly with React + Vite (no complex backend or DevOps).

Modular structure makes task division easy in a team.

Uses API-based AI instead of building ML models from scratch.

Demonstrates core skills: state management, routing, API integration, UI design.

Strong real-world idea, but technically manageable for beginners.

> A personal care tool for our elderly

![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![HC-05 Bluetooth Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/HC--05%20Bluetooth%20Module-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin%20REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Elevenlabs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Elevenlabs-333333?style=flat-square) ![ESP32-CAM](https://img.shields.io/badge/ESP32--CAM-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arduino Nano 33 BLE](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino%20Nano%2033%20BLE-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Elderly individuals living alone often face two major risks: **slow emergency response times and medication mismanagement.**

SAHAY makes existing tasks safer and easier by:

Passive Safety: Traditional SOS buttons are only useful if the user is conscious and able to reach them. SAHAY's IoT sensors and Voice SOS provide a safety net that works even when the user can't move.

Dignity through Autonomy: The "Genie" assistant allows elders to manage their day, check their health stats, and receive medicine reminders through simple conversation, reducing the cognitive load of modern smartphone interfaces.

Caregiver Peace of Mind: The dedicated Caregiver Dashboard provides a real-time "heartbeat" of the home, allowing family members to know their loved ones are safe without intrusive constant video surveillance

**Challenges we ran into**

DataHaven Integration: Merging a decentralized storage protocol into a standard Android Room database architecture was a significant hurdle. Ensuring that the decryption keys were handled securely in the app's keystore while maintaining the "read-only" speed of the dashboard required a Custom Content Provider logic.
Hardware Connectivity: During the early stages, the Arduino ID was failing to handshake with the heartbeat sensor over the BLE stack. This led to "stale data" bugs on the frontend. We resolved this by implementing a custom buffer logic on the ESP32 that ensures a stable data packet is sent only when a clear signal is acquired.
Model Training Failures: Initial speech-to-intent models for the voice SOS were failing due to background noise (TV, fans). We had to switch to a more robust noise-cancellation preprocessing layer before sending the audio fragments to the ElevenLabs API.

**Grand Prize**

# SAHAY: Human-Centric Elder Care Ecosystem
## ⚠️ The Problem
By 2050, **1 in 6 people** in the world will be over age 65. Most modern monitoring systems fail this demographic because:
*   **Too Expensive:** Hospital-grade setups or full-time nursing homes are financially unsustainable for the average family.
*   **Too Intrusive:** Constant camera surveillance strips elders of their dignity and privacy.
*   **Too Complex:** Modern smartphone interfaces are often a barrier, not a bridge, for seniors with tremors or declining eyesight.
## 🛡️ The SAHAY Solution
SAHAY creates a **"Safety Bubble"** that respects dignity while ensuring 24/7 security. It allows elders to **age in place** (at home) safely, massively reducing the burden on global healthcare systems.
*   **Voice-First Interface:** Our "Genie" assistant (ElevenLabs) allows elders to interact naturally without needing to navigate menus.
*   **Non-Intrusive IoT:** We use Arduino and ESP32 sensors to monitor heart rate, movement, and temperature—no cameras required.
*   **Decentralized Security:** Medical records are stored using **DataHaven** to ensure sensitive prescriptions are encrypted and owned only by the user.
## 🚀 Sustainable Product Roadmap
SAHAY’s modular architecture is designed for a multi-year growth strategy:
*   **New IoT Nodes:** Support for "Fall-Detecting Rugs" and Smart Pill Dispensers.
*   **Health Intelligence:** Predictive analytics to detect early signs of cognitive decline or dehydration before an emergency occurs.
*   **Care Network Evolution:** Expanding the Caregiver Dashboard into a "Care Team" interface for doctors and relatives.

### Beta-Test
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/betatest-9254) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Yajassardana/beta-test/) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://beta-test-psi.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/8afe914b5a624ba9a593e0e009e1fb47) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co)

> Fail safely. Parent better.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TTS](https://img.shields.io/badge/TTS-333333?style=flat-square) ![STT](https://img.shields.io/badge/STT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Replit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Replit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Claude-API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude--API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Video-Gen](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video--Gen-333333?style=flat-square) ![Avatar-Gen](https://img.shields.io/badge/Avatar--Gen-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Beta-Test** is a parenting simulator where an AI child (powered by Claude) presents realistic behavioral scenarios, like tantrums, lying, or emotional outbursts, grounded in developmental psychology and culturally authentic to Indian households.

The child responds dynamically to how the parent talks. Harshness and dismissal escalate it. Empathy and validation de-escalate it. After each interaction, a scorecard shows the child's emotional arc, what the parent said vs. what the child heard, and the specific technique that would have worked.

Voice interaction works in English and Hindi via Sarvam AI, so parents speak naturally instead of typing.

Who it's for: New-generation Indian parents in nuclear families who want to parent differently from how they were raised but don't know how to apply it in practice.

What it makes easier: Practicing real parenting responses in a safe environment before the stakes are real. Same idea as mock trading or flight simulators, but for talking to your child.

**Long-term vision:** Beta ("hey beta") evolves into a digital twin of your child, expanding into holistic development tracking and informed care.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Claude Haiku 4.5 Persistent 529 Overload Errors

Early in development, we chose Claude Haiku 4.5 (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) for the child AI. It immediately started returning HTTP 529 (API Overloaded) errors when called with `tool_use` + `tool_choice`, the exact pattern we needed for structured JSON enforcement. The errors were persistent across every attempt. We implemented a 3x retry loop with exponential backoff, but the errors kept firing. 

### Making the LLM Stay in Character as a Realistic Child

The hardest challenge was preventing Claude from breaking character. Claude naturally drifts toward being cooperative, educational, or easy to pacify. A real 5-year-old mid-tantrum does none of those things. We solved this with heavily engineered system prompts that include:

- Explicit anti-teaching instruction: *"You are a real child, not a teaching tool. Do not make it easy for the parent."*
- Reaction rule mappings: a natural language state machine that maps parent behaviors (logical explanations, threats, validation, specific AHA techniques) to realistic child emotional responses
- 2-3 one-shot example exchanges per scenario to set tone and texture, which we found more effective than detailed persona descriptions
- Conversation arc rules: the child can't just flip from angry to happy in one exchange. Emotional shifts require multiple exchanges of consistent empathy.

Each of the 4 scenarios gets its own complete system prompt because the child's personality, triggers, and de-escalation patterns are fundamentally different across scenarios.

### TTS Audio Choppiness with WebSocket Streaming

Sarvam AI's TTS WebSocket streaming produced choppy, stuttering audio playback. Two root causes: (1) our "done detection" used a debounce-based approach (counting empty frames), which fired falsely during natural gaps in chunk delivery, causing premature audio cutoff; (2) our pre-buffer of 150ms was too thin for real-world network jitter. We identified that Sarvam sends a `{"type": "Flushed"}` WebSocket message as the authoritative "all audio sent" signal, and replaced the fragile debounce logic with this event-driven approach. We also increased the pre-buffer to ~200ms for jitter absorption.

### STT Returning Empty Transcripts

Sarvam's speech-to-text service intermittently returned empty transcripts despite receiving valid audio data. Debugging required adding extensive logging: full response body from the API, audio blob sizes before sending, confidence scores, and duration metadata. We also added an explicit `language` parameter to prevent auto-detection failures on short audio clips, since Sarvam's language detection can misidentify brief utterances.

### Stale Closure Bug in Voice Auto-Send

When implementing auto-send (voice transcript automatically sends without pressing the Send button), we hit a classic React stale closure bug. The voice input callback captured a stale version of the `input` state, so `sendMessage()` would send an empty string even though the transcript was visible in the input field. We fixed this by creating `sendMessageDirect(text)` that accepts the transcript as a parameter, bypassing the stale state entirely. `useVoiceInput` stores its callback in a `useRef` that gets updated every render, so the callback always reads the latest function reference.

### Hindi Language Support Complexity

Supporting Hindi required changes across the entire stack: dual system prompt versions (EN + HI files), a separate tool schema with an additional `child_dialogue_devanagari` field, Devanagari-to-romanized-Hindi transliteration after STT (since the LLM works better with romanized input), language-aware intro video resolution with fallback from Hindi to English, and dev tools that support editing both language variants. The transliteration step was particularly tricky. We call Sarvam's `/transliterate` endpoint post-STT to convert Devanagari script to romanized Hindi before passing it to Claude.

### Token Efficiency Across Multi-Exchange Conversations

Each API call to Claude includes the full system prompt (~2K tokens), full conversation history (growing with each exchange), and the tool schema. By exchange 5-6, ~90% of input tokens are identical re-processing. We implemented Anthropic's prompt caching with `cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }` on the system prompt and the last `tool_result` in message history. This reduced costs by ~90% for cached reads and cut latency noticeably on later exchanges.

Team **aviato** -- [Yajas Sardana](https://github.com/Yajassardana)

### Aegis
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aegis-7558) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://build-india-aegis.streamlit.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/45nlCroHcPk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co)

> Beyond Motion. Context-Aware Protection for Bharat

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Image Processing - Open CV](https://img.shields.io/badge/Image%20Processing%20--%20Open%20CV-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🛡️ The Problem AEGIS Solves
Most modern CCTV systems are "dumb." They record everything but understand nothing. Homeowners are constantly bombarded with "Motion Detected" notifications caused by stray cats, passing cars, or wind, leading to "Notification Fatigue." When a real threat occurs, it’s often ignored because it looks just like every other alert.

AEGIS bridges the gap between raw video footage and actionable intelligence.

🔍 How it Makes Life Safer & Easier
1. Context-Aware Filtering
The Task: Checking your phone every time the camera pings.

The AEGIS Way: Instead of "Motion Detected," you get: "Zomato delivery partner at the door" or "Amazon package dropped off." It understands the intent of the visitor, allowing you to ignore the noise and focus on what matters.

2. Proactive Threat Detection (The "Loitering" Logic)
The Task: Relying on a guard or yourself to spot suspicious behavior.

The AEGIS Way: AEGIS doesn't just see a person; it measures behavior. If an unrecognized individual stands near your gate for more than 60 seconds without ringing the bell, AEGIS identifies it as a potential threat and triggers a high-priority alert.

3. Solving the "Indian Context"
The Task: Managing frequent doorstep interactions (Delivery, House-help, Utilities).

The AEGIS Way: Purpose-built for India, AEGIS recognizes the uniforms of major service providers (Swiggy, Zomato, Dunzo) and knows the typical rhythm of an Indian household. It acts as a Digital Chowkidar that never sleeps.

4. Emergency Automation
The Task: Manually calling for help or sounding an alarm during a crisis.

The AEGIS Way: If a high-level threat is detected (e.g., an intruder at 3 AM), AEGIS can automatically trigger a WhatsApp alert to your family group and play a pre-recorded siren through your system’s speakers, deterring criminals before they enter.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The API Latency & Rate Limit Trap
The Hurdle: Sending a raw video stream to Claude 3.5 Sonnet caused 10+ second delays and immediately hit API rate limits. High-resolution frames were too heavy for a real-time "Security Guard" experience.

The Fix: We implemented "Intelligent Event-Triggering" using OpenCV. Instead of constant streaming, we calculate frame differences locally. Only when significant motion is detected do we compress, resize to 640x480, and send a single JPEG to Claude. This reduced API calls by 90% while maintaining "instant" reasoning.

2. Streamlit’s Connection Persistence
The Hurdle: Streamlit re-runs the entire script upon any UI change, which repeatedly killed and restarted the cv2.VideoCapture object. This caused the camera feed to crash and prevented a continuous security log.

The Fix: We bypassed this by managing the camera and database connections within st.session_state. By wrapping the backend logic in a persistent state, we ensured the "AI Brain" kept monitoring the feed in the background even while we interacted with the dashboard.
