> Smart chhotu for kirana shop owners

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

### Pain Point
**85% of Indian shopkeepers (₹1-10L annual stores) use zero digital bookkeeping.** They lose money daily through:
- Pricing errors (selling below cost)
- No profit visibility (can't distinguish revenue from profit)
- Stock wastage (no low-stock alerts)
- Zero tax compliance records

**Why existing solutions fail:**
- Complex apps (QuickBooks, Tally) need training
- English-only → useless for low-literacy shopkeepers
- Typing overhead → too slow during busy hours
- High cost → ₹1000+/month for small stores

### Solution: Voice-First Accounting

**Speak in Hindi/Hinglish or any language, get instant bookkeeping.**

#### Key Features

1. **🎤 Zero Typing** - Just speak naturally
   - "50 kilo aloo aaya 30 rupaye kilo" → auto-records with cost tracking
   - "10 kilo aloo becha 40 rupaye" → updates inventory, calculates profit

2. **📊 Real Profit = Revenue - COGS - Expenses**
   - Most shopkeepers only track sales (revenue)
   - We calculate Cost of Goods Sold (weighted-avg costing) and expenses
   - Daily profit report: "आज ₹5000 बिक्री, ₹1200 मुनाफा"

3. **⚡ Feels Instant** (Parallel processing)
   - Ack in <1s: "हाँ भैया, लिख रहा हूँ..."
   - Full response in 3-5s (while ack plays)
   - User never waits for AI

4. **🧠 Multi-Intent Parsing**
   - "30 kilo becha 50 rupaye aur 500 ka kiraya diya"
   - → Processes BOTH sale + expense in one sentence

5. **🔄 Normalized Data** (Hindi/Hinglish → Clean English)
   - "आलू", "aloo", "potato", "potahto" → all same item
   - No duplicates, queryable for analytics/GST

### Impact: Today + Future

#### Today: Instant Bookkeeping
**For a vegetable vendor:**
- Before: Guesses prices, out-of-stock surprises, zero profit tracking
- After: Exact costs, real-time profit, low-stock alerts

#### Tomorrow: Intelligent Business Insights (Roadmap)

Once we have 2-3 weeks of data, Dukaan Buddy becomes a **friendly business advisor**:

**Expiry Alerts** (for perishables)
- "भैया, टमाटर 2 दिन में खराब हो जाएगा। आज ₹5 कम करके बेच दो?"
- Helps prevent wastage, maximize margin

**What Sells (Sales Velocity)**
- "आलू सबसे तेजी से बिकता है। स्टॉक ₹10K रखो, दूसरे सब्ज़ियों में ₹3K"
- Shows which items turn inventory fastest → lower capital tied up

**What Earns (Profit per Item)**
- "गाजर ₹5 profit/kg, प्याज ₹2 profit/kg। गाजर ज़्यादा स्टॉक रख"
- Many shopkeepers think high price = high profit (wrong!)
- We show actual profit margin per item

**Seasonal Patterns** (after 2-3 months)
- "गर्मी में लौकी/कद्दू की मांग बढ़ता है। पिछली साल भी ऐसा हुआ था"
- Helps plan inventory ahead

**Smart Discounting**
- "बैंगन आज ₹10 कीमत पर नहीं बिका। कल ₹8 करके देखो? आपके लिए ₹2 ज़्यादा मुनाफा होगा"
- Data-driven pricing, not guesses

**Friendly Tone (Key!)**
- Never says "You're doing it wrong"
- Always: "Here's what I observed... what do you think?"
- Like a trusted shop friend who's good with numbers
- Respects shopkeeper's experience, just adds data

**TAM:** 8M+ small shops in India. Most unbanked, most offline.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenge 1: Voice Infrastructure Nightmare → First Principles Win 🎤
**The Big One:** Spent **hours** trying to build WebSocket-based real-time streaming for voice. Downloaded libraries, set up event handlers, configured buffers... **nothing worked**. Kept hitting latency/dropout issues. Team was stressed.

**Root problem:** Overthinking. Tried to be "real-time" like professional speech-to-text services (Google, AWS). That's overkill for a hackathon MVP.

**First principles pivot:**
1. User speaks → **Record full audio to WAV file** (browser's Web Audio API, already built)
2. Send **entire file** via REST API (single HTTP POST)
3. Call Sarvam STT API (REST, not streaming)
4. Done. <500 bytes of clean code.

```javascript
// Before: Complex WebSocket setup, event handlers, buffering logic
// After:
const wavBlob = buildWav(recordedChunks, 16000);  // Records full audio
await fetch('/process', {body: formData});        // Single POST
```

**Result:** Works perfectly. No latency, no dropouts, no complexity. Voice records in 3-5 seconds, sends instantly.

**Learning:** **Hackathon = constraint-driven design.** First principles > library chasing. "Record then send" beats "stream then process" when you have 48 hours. Shipping > perfect architecture.

---

### Challenge 2: Hindi Breaking Databases 🇮🇳
**Problem:** Claude router output Hindi item names → database had keys like `"चीनी"` instead of `"sugar"`. Same item spoken as "चीनी"/"cheeni"/"sugar"/"Sugar" created 4 duplicates. Impossible to query/aggregate.

**Solution:** Built **translation + normalization layer**
- 50+ Hindi/Hinglish → English mappings
- Singularize ("potatoes" → "potato")
- Fuzzy match typos ("potahto" → "potato", 80% threshold)
- **Result:** Clean English keys, zero duplicates

**Learning:** For multilingual systems, normalize at storage layer. Accept messy input, enforce canonical form internally.

---

### Challenge 3: Regex Quick-Ack Missing 90% of Queries 🎯
**Problem:** Original intent detection used regex patterns. User says "बेटा छोटू, क्या है अभी बचा हुआ?" (natural speech) → no regex match → boring fallback ack.

**Root cause:** People don't speak in regex-friendly patterns. Tried to predict intent in <1ms — impossible.

**Solution:** Ditched intent detection. Built **20+ general natural acks** that work for ANYTHING:
- "हाँ भैया, सुन रहा हूँ..."
- "रुको, देखता हूँ..."
- "ठीक है, नोट करता हूँ..."
- Random pick each time (feels human)

**Result:** 100% response rate (no more "unknown"), simpler code (removed 100+ fragile regex lines)

**Learning:** Simple > Clever. General natural responses beat brittle pattern matching.

---

### Challenge 4: Parallel Processing Architecture 🏗️
**Problem:** Claude takes 3-5 seconds. Waiting → feels broken, users think it crashed.

**Bad approaches:**
- Show spinner: doesn't work for voice-only
- Wait for full response: 5s of silence = terrible UX

**Solution:** **Dual-track parallel**
1. Fire `/quick-ack` (no LLM) → <1ms response
2. Fire `/process` (full Claude pipeline) in parallel
3. Play ack immediately ("हाँ भैया, लिख रहा हूँ...")
4. Play full response when ready

**Result:** Feels instant (<1s feedback) while AI processes (3-5s backend)

**Learning:** For voice + AI latency, split fast ack from deep processing.

---

**Problem:** 85% of Indian shopkeepers have **zero digital accounting**. Manual → errors → money lost.

**Solution:** Voice + AI that understands Hindi/Hinglish. Most accessible accounting app + business advisor ever built.

**TAM:** 8M+ small shops in India. Most unbanked, most offline. This is software for people who can't use other software.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mosaic-95cc) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/divyanshkul/mosaic) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Build%20India:%20Anthropic%20x%20Replit%20x%20Lightspeed%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://buildindia2026.devfolio.co)

> Learn Anything

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We live in an era of collapsing attention spans. Traditional modes of learning,  blogs, papers, textbooks, are increasingly inaccessible to most people. Yet a new paradigm, pioneered by creators like 3Blue1Brown, has thrived: rigorous research paired with rich animations, making difficult topics genuinely approachable.

Our tool brings that same style to any topic, from any source, in any language.

Give it a URL, a PDF, or just a topic name: it generates an animated explainer video with 46 distinct scene types (from concept cards to LaTeX-rendered equations to animated charts), a structured knowledge graph mapping concept relationships, and adaptive quizzes grounded in Bloom's Taxonomy, testing skills from basic recall through higher-order critical thinking: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, and Create.

But unlike a 3Blue1Brown video, watching isn't the endpoint mastery is. Inspired by Khan Academy's mastery-based learning, quiz results map back to the knowledge graph, pinpointing exactly which concepts remain unmastered. The system then generates targeted follow-up content for weak areas, closing the loop between watching and truly understanding.

**Challenges we ran into**

The core risk of using LLMs for educational content is hallucination—confidently stated "facts" that are simply wrong. We addressed this with a multi-agent architecture where no single agent is trusted end-to-end. Four specialized agents (Graph, Script, Quiz, and Verification) each handle one pipeline stage, with outputs cross-checked through a generate → evaluate → refine loop.

The Graph Agent builds a knowledge graph from source material, validated for structural issues like orphan nodes and disconnected components before anything downstream sees it. 

The Script Agent generates narration grounded in the graph, with a checker enforcing full node coverage and correct prerequisite ordering via topological sort. 

The Verification Agent extracts individual factual claims from the script, searches the web and Wikipedia for evidence, then judges each claim as accurate, inaccurate, or needs-context with confidence scores. Inaccurate claims trigger automatic script correction with specific fixes rather than full regeneration. 

The Quiz Agent generates questions tied to graph nodes using Bloom's Taxonomy, with structural checks ensuring coverage across at least three cognitive levels and all taught concepts.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Money Machine is an AI agent swarm that autonomously scans, researches, and trades prediction markets using Claude, democratizing access to global information markets (poly market) for Indian users.

India has 600M+ smartphone users hungry for financial tools but locked out of global platforms. Our AI agent swarm bridges that gap, it researches global markets, explains them in plain language, and lets users learn to trade risk-free or trade behalf of them with correct information to take informed decision. Think of it as an AI-powered investment tutor that understands Indian cost sensitivity and open up indians to predictive information market.

AI-native -> Multi-agent swarm architecture: Deal Finder Agent → Research Agent (Tavily + Claude) → Safety Module → Auto-Invest Agent. Claude is the brain.

PS:-
The dashbord might feel like Hardcoded but everyhting is working. Some features not working in deployed site. But more than happy to show that all in demo.  

This is soo cool

**Challenges we ran into**

1.  Polymarket's API Wasn't Built for Bots Like Mine
The biggest early headache was Polymarket's CLOB API. I wanted my bot to fetch live market prices and order books, but the WebSocket feeds return raw order book deltas — not clean prices. I had to reverse-engineer how their frontend reconstructs prices from the outcomePrices and clobTokenIds fields. I ended up writing custom parsers that normalize this data into a format my agents can actually reason about, and built a WebSocket watcher that maintains a live connection and auto-reconnects on drops.

2.  Stopping the Bot from Going Full Degen
This was the scary one. When I first wired up the auto-invest pipeline, the bot would happily dump the entire wallet into a single sketchy market because the LLM gave it a high confidence score. I realized I needed proper guardrails — so I built a SafetyModule that enforces max order size limits, total exposure caps, per-market position limits, minimum liquidity thresholds, and spread tolerance checks. Every single trade goes through this validation layer before execution. Without this, the bot would've blown up the demo wallet in minutes.

3. Multi-Agent Coordination Without Losing Money
I'm running multiple agents — a deal finder that scans markets, a research agent that pulls live news via Tavily and sends it to Claude for analysis, and an auto-investor that executes trades. The tricky part was making them work together without race conditions. For example, the research agent might still be analyzing a market while the deal finder already flagged a new one. If both tried to invest simultaneously, the balance checks would fail. I ended up implementing sequential processing with per-market locking in the JSON database — each agent reads the latest wallet state before acting, so they never overspend.

4.  Loss Protection When Markets Move Against You
In prediction markets, a position can go from 70¢ to 5¢ overnight if news breaks. I needed the bot to not just buy — but also know when to cut losses. I built a price history tracker that records snapshots every minute via the watcher service, and the portfolio tracker recalculates P&L against live market prices. The dashboard shows real-time unrealized P&L so I can see exactly how much exposure I have and which positions are bleeding. Getting the totalValue = cash + positionValue calculation to stay accurate across API refreshes, WebSocket updates, and new trades was harder than it sounds — I went through three rewrites of the portfolio sync logic.

5. LLM Hallucinations in Market Analysis
When Claude analyzes a market like "US strikes Iran by March 31?", it sometimes confidently recommends a trade based on outdated training data rather than the fresh news I fed it. I had to restructure my prompts to force the model to cite specific sources from the Tavily research results and explicitly state when the evidence is insufficient. I also added a confidence tier system (High/Medium/Low/Manual) — the bot only auto-invests on High confidence, everything else goes to the discovery feed for manual review.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![gemini](https://img.shields.io/badge/gemini-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Inspiration

The idea came from seeing our own friends and seniors struggle during placement season. In our college (and so many others in **Tier-2/Tier-3 cities**), we have the coding skills, but we mess up because we don't have the right guidance.

**The Problems we saw our friends facing were:**
* **ATS Rejections:** We saw so many talented batchmates get rejected by ATS software just because their resume format was wrong.
* **Interview Anxiety:** Many would freeze up during HR rounds because they never practised speaking in English.
* **Limited Access:** Career counsellors are super expensive, so most of us just rely on random YouTube videos.
* **Fragmented Tools:** While some free tools exist, they are all segregated at different platforms, making it hard for a user to find and access each tool.

**The Solution:**
We wanted to build something that could be a **"Digital Senior"** for everyone—a personalised compass called **Ascend AI** that levels the confusion field & provides all career solutions at a single platform to make career guidance easily accessible to everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Major Build Challenges

During our build, we faced multiple problems. Some of the major issues included:

* **The "Hallucination" Problem:** At first, the roadmap generator would suggest courses that didn't exist or were 5 years old. We had to spend a lot of time tweaking the prompts to ground the AI and make it stick to general, verifiable topics.
* **PDF Parsing:** This was a headache because resumes come in weird formats—two columns, icons, tables. The AI used to get confused between the company name and the job title. We had to switch to Gemini’s vision capabilities to fix this.
* **Voice Loops:** The funniest (and most annoying) bug was during the mock interview—the mic would pick up the AI’s voice, send it back to the AI, and it would start talking to itself! I had to write some strict logic in the frontend to mute the mic the second the AI starts speaking.
* **Token Limits:** When users uploaded huge 4-page resumes, we hit API limits. I had to write a summarizer function to shrink the text down before sending it to the resume editor.

> Clarity_ED: Master your studies with AI clarity.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Authentication](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Authentication-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We have created a comprehensive product overview that outlines the core problem Clarity_ED addresses and how it simplifies and secures the academic journey for students.

Key Highlights:
The Problem: Addresses the "Snowball Effect" where falling behind leads to decision paralysis and burnout.
Use Cases: Dynamic catch-up planning, stress-aware study sessions, and integrated AI tutoring.
Improved Workflow: Replaces manual prioritization with a smart engine and offers one-tap replanning if life gets in the way.
Enhanced Safety: Focuses on mental well-being by monitoring feasibility and preventing unsustainable study habits.

The Problem: The "Snowball Effect" of Academic Overload
Students often face a common, high-stress scenario: a minor setback (illness, mental health break, or personal emergency) causes them to miss a few days of study.

Traditional tools fail in this moment because:

Static Schedules: To-do lists and calendars become "graveyards of late tasks" that don't adjust to reality.
Burden of Choice: When 20 tasks are overdue, students experience "decision paralysis," not knowing what to prioritize first.
Burnout Ignorance: Most tools push for maximum productivity, ignoring the student's current stress levels, which leads to inevitable burnout.
Our Solution: The Adaptive Recovery Engine
Clarity_ED isn't just a calendar; it's a dynamic recovery layer that sits on top of your curriculum.

1. What can people use it for?
Personalized Catch-up Plans: Generate a day-by-day roadmap to get back on track after falling behind.
Stress-Managed Study: Inform the app if you're feeling overwhelmed, and it will automatically prioritize essential core concepts over minor details.
Immediate Concept Clarification: Use the AI Tutor to break down complex topics that are blocking your progress.
Progress Visualization: Track your "Recovery Score" to see exactly how close you are to being back on schedule.
2. How it makes existing tasks easier
Zero-Effort Prioritization: You don't have to decide what to study. The engine calculates "Priority Scores" based on subject difficulty, credits, and deadlines.
One-Tap Replanning: If life happens and you miss a session, you don't "fail." You just tap "Replan," and the engine redistributes the remaining workload across your available time.
Integrated Focus: No switching apps. Start a Focus Timer directly from your schedule to stay in the zone.
3. How it makes studying safer
Stress-Aware Scheduling: By adjusting workload based on mental health and stress inputs, Clarity_ED prevents the "all-nighter" culture and helps maintain a sustainable pace.
Feasibility Monitoring: The app will explicitly warn you if your goal is physically impossible given your available hours, suggesting adjustments before you hit a wall.
Transparent Logic: By explaining why a task is high priority, it reduces the anxiety of "Am I studying the right thing?"

Clarity_ED transforms academic recovery from a source of panic into a structured, manageable, and healthy process. It's about moving from "I'm buried" to "I have a plan."

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development and rebranding of Clarity_ED, our team faced several technical hurdles. Here’s how we overcame them.

1. The Global Rebranding Ripple Effect
Challenge: Renaming the project from "Academic Recovery" to "Clarity_ED" wasn't just about changing text. It involved renaming core class identifiers like AcademicRecoveryApp. This immediately broke the project's unit and widget tests, causing the entire build pipeline to fail.

Solution: We performed a systematic codebase audit. After renaming the root application class in main.dart, we immediately updated the test suite in 
widget_test.dart to reference the new ClarityEdApp. This taught us the importance of high-level architectural changes being mirrored in the testing layer simultaneously.

2. Dealing with "Rigid Layouts" (Overflows)
Challenge: In the Daily Schedule screen, we used Row widgets for priority badges and session details. On narrower devices or with long subject names (e.g., "Advanced Theoretical Mathematics"), the UI would break with the dreaded "RenderFlex overflow" error.

Solution: We refactored the layout to be "Flexible-First."

We replaced rigid Row containers with Wrap, allowing badges to flow to the next line safely. We implemented Expanded and Flexible constraints on text elements, combined with TextOverflow.ellipsis. This shift from absolute horizontal layouts to relative, wrapping layouts made the app robust across all screen sizes.

3. Creating a "Premium" Feel within Constraints
Challenge: Designing the AI Tutor UI presented a hurdle: how to make it feel like a modern, "AI-first" experience using a pre-defined, somewhat rigid 
AppPageScaffold widget. Our initial designs for a pulsing AI status indicator caused linting errors because the scaffold didn't support a standard actions array in the way we expected.

Solution: Instead of rewriting the entire scaffold (which would have risked regressions elsewhere), we studied the existing widget's source code. We discovered we could leverage the trailing and titleWidget parameters to inject our custom animations. We used a ScaleTransition paired with an AnimationController to create the pulsing "AI Online" effect, achieving a premium look while respecting the existing architectural boundaries.

4. State Sync and Mock Logic
Challenge: We needed the AI Tutor to feel interactive without having a live backend API ready for every prompt.

Solution: We built a robust Mock Response Engine within the UI layer that detects keywords like "Quiz" or "Summarize". This allowed us to demo the "Quiz Mode" and "Summary" features instantly, providing a clear vision for how the final LLM integration should behave.

Key Takeaway: Every hurdle was solved by looking one layer deeper—whether it was checking the test suite after a rename, or reading the source of a custom widget to find a flexible entry point for design features.

> Find clarity in the chaos

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problems We Solve:

1-Decision Paralysis: We break down complex emergencies into a simple "Now/Next/Never" framework, restricting inputs to one binary question at a time to reduce cognitive load.

2-Sensory Overload: Our "Calm Harbor" interface uses deep, eye-resting tones and liquid-smooth transitions to combat chaotic energy.

3-Biological Panic: Using guided exhale synchronization and low-frequency audio loops, we help regulate your nervous system to kill panic at the source.

4-Lack of Immediate Guidance: We provide a professional, secure "cockpit" for crisis management that doesn't rely on third parties or external authorities.

**Challenges we ran into**

Problems faced:
1-The UI was a mess: Early on, text was overlapping everywhere because of the "glass" look. It was unreadable. I fixed it by forcing the app to show only one simple question at a time to clear the noise.

2-Sound wars: The background music and the panic alerts kept fighting each other. It sounded like chaos. I coded it so the music "ducks" out of the way when an alert hits so you can actually hear.

3-The SOS problem: I didn't want the app calling the cops behind your back. I solved it by making a massive "Call Emergency" button so you stay in control.

4-Frantic clicking: When people panic, they mash buttons. I added a "Stability Meter" that detects fast tapping and literally slows the whole app down to force you to take a breath.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/skillmap-f0dc) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://night-shift-amuhacks-5-0.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fbaFqSFhcIo) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-AMUHACKS%205.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://amuhacks-5.devfolio.co)

> Stop chasing trends. Start building foundations.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Students often pursue trending skills like AI, ML, or Web3 without understanding whether they have the foundational prerequisites required for those fields. Most learning platforms recommend courses based on popularity, not on structured self-diagnosis.

SkillMap solves this by diagnosing a student’s current competency before recommending what to learn next. It evaluates career-specific skills, models prerequisite dependencies between them, and generates a logically ordered roadmap that prioritizes missing and weak foundations. Instead of suggesting more content, it provides structured clarity on what to build first and why.

**Challenges we ran into**

Roadmap recommending mastered skills
Initially, the dependency resolver returned all required skills even when users scored full marks.
Fix: We added strict filtering so only Missing and Weak skills appear in the roadmap, ensuring diagnostic consistency.

Career paths not differentiated
All careers initially showed identical question sets.
Fix: We filtered questions and alignment scoring by career-specific required skills.

Dependency impact logic not scoped properly
High-impact gap detection was calculated globally instead of per career.
Fix: We limited dependency analysis to the selected career’s skill graph.

Frontend radar chart crash
A React and chart.js version mismatch caused runtime errors.
Fix: We aligned dependencies and rebuilt the environment.

Scalability concerns with hardcoded ordering
Hardcoding learning order would not scale and risk logical errors.
Fix: We modeled skills as a dependency graph and used Kahn’s topological sorting to compute learning order dynamically.

**The problem it solves**

## The Core Issue
First-semester students often struggle not because they lack motivation, but because they **don't know which skills to prioritize**. This misprioritization leads to:
- Preventable academic failures
- Unnecessary stress and anxiety
- Skill gaps that become irreversible as courses progress
- Higher dropout rates in early semesters

## How Kryva Helps

### For Students
- **Identifies critical skill gaps** before they cause irreversible damage
- **Prioritizes what to learn first** based on actual academic consequences, not guesswork
- **Provides actionable steps** tailored to your specific situation
- **Tracks progress** and adapts recommendations as you improve

### Makes Academic Life Easier By
- Removing the guesswork from study planning
- Preventing last-minute panic when foundational skills are missing
- Building confidence through strategic, consequence-aware learning
- Catching problems early when they're still fixable

## Real-World Use Case
Instead of randomly studying everything or following generic advice, students get a personalized roadmap that says: *"Focus on these 3 specific skills this week because without them, you'll struggle in next month's assignments."*

**Bottom line**: Kryva turns academic survival from a guessing game into an informed decision-making process.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Faced Building Kryva

## The Firebase Real-Time Sync Issue

### The Problem
Multiple assessment modules were updating student progress simultaneously in Firebase, causing **race conditions**. Student data would randomly overwrite itself—completed assessments would disappear or show incorrect progress percentages.

### The Breaking Point
During testing, a student completed three assessments back-to-back. The system recorded only one, lost another completely, and marked the third as 50% done when it was actually finished.

### How We Solved It
We implemented **Firebase transactions** for conflict resolution instead of direct writes, and restructured our data model to use separate subcollections for each assessment session. We also added a React-side buffer that batches updates before sending them to Firebase.

### The Takeaway
Real-time databases need careful handling of concurrent operations. Sometimes the fix isn't better code, it's better data architecture.

Team **Pixel** -- Aqdas Asim, Mohd Suleman

> Smart Solutions for Campus Problems

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In many college campuses, students face daily issues such as broken infrastructure, cleanliness problems, poor internet connectivity, and faulty classroom equipment. These problems are often reported informally, leading to delays, miscommunication, or no action at all.

CampusFix provides a centralized digital platform where students can easily report campus issues in real time. Instead of relying on verbal complaints or paperwork, every issue is logged, categorized, and tracked until resolution.

Key problems CampusFix addresses:

❌ No structured system for reporting campus problems

❌ Slow response due to manual processes

❌ Lack of transparency in issue status

❌ Difficulty in prioritizing urgent complaints

❌ Repeated reporting of the same problems

With CampusFix:

✅ Students can report issues in seconds

✅ AI automatically categorizes and analyzes sentiment

✅ Duplicate issues are detected

✅ Admins get a clear dashboard to manage complaints

✅ Faster resolution and improved accountability

CampusFix makes campus maintenance smarter, faster, and more transparent — improving student experience and operational efficiency.

**Challenges we ran into**

🚧 Challenges We Ran Into

During the development of CampusFix, we faced several technical and implementation challenges that helped us learn and improve the system.

🔐 Authentication & JWT Integration

Initially, we faced issues with JWT authentication where protected routes were not working correctly and users were getting unauthorized errors. This happened due to incorrect token handling and CORS configuration. We resolved this by properly configuring Flask-JWT-Extended and updating request headers to consistently send authorization tokens.

🗄 Supabase Database Constraints

While inserting users, we encountered duplicate email errors caused by unique constraints in Supabase. This helped us understand the importance of validating user input before database insertion. We fixed this by checking existing users before registration and adding proper error handling.

🔄 API Routing & Backend Structure

Our Flask routes were not loading properly at first due to incorrect imports and blueprint registration. Debugging logs helped us trace the problem and reorganize our backend folder structure.

🤖 AI Integration Challenges

Integrating sentiment analysis and automatic issue categorization was challenging because raw user input varied greatly. We improved accuracy by cleaning text input and adding fallback categories when confidence was low.

📤 GitHub Organization Push Rules

We faced restrictions on pushing code to our organization repository due to single-push policies. We solved this by organizing commits carefully and coordinating within the team before pushing final code.

Team **MergeInfinity** -- Sarangi Kini, Dhruv Patil, [Megh Bari](https://github.com/MeghBari124)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the key challenges during the development of this system was working with a primary dataset that included several medical parameters unfamiliar to common users. Since these parameters were not suitable for direct user input, we had to carefully align the backend logic with simplified and user-friendly frontend input fields. This required mapping complex dataset features to understandable inputs without affecting the accuracy of the model. Additionally, we introduced BMI and blood pressure measurements, which were not part of the original dataset. Integrating these new parameters required implementing multiple conditional statements in the JavaScript backend to correctly process and adapt the inputs to the model’s expected format, ensuring consistency and reliable predictions

**The problem it solves**

# 🌊 Coastal Guardian

**Coastal Guardian** is a modern web platform designed to empower communities in the fight against marine pollution. By combining AI vision with gamification, we turn every citizen into an active protector of our coastlines.

## 🚀 Key Features

### 🧠 AI-Powered Detection
Uses **OpenAI's CLIP Model** to intelligently analyze uploaded images. It doesn't just guess; it understands the context to identify:

- **Plastic Waste** (Bottles, bags)
- **Oil Spills** (Surface contamination)
- **Marine Debris** (Nets, ghost gear)
- **Solid Waste** (General trash)

### 📸 Smart Reporting
- **Dual-Mode Upload**: Snap a photo directly via camera or drag-and-drop from your gallery.
- **Auto-Geolocation**: Automatically extracts GPS data from images to pinpoint pollution hotspots on the global map.
- **Real-Time Analysis**: Get instant feedback on the type of pollution and confidence level.

### 🎮 Gamification & Rewards
- **Earn Points**: Get rewarded for every verified report.
- **Rank Up**: Progress from "New Recruit" to "Gold Guardian".
- **Eco-Store**: Redeem points for real-world sustainable gear like metal straws, solar power banks, and ocean-friendly apparel.

### 🌍 Social Impact
- **Share Your Badge**: Generate dynamic "Impact Cards" showcasing your rank and contribution.
- **Inspire Others**: One-click sharing to Twitter, LinkedIn, and WhatsApp to spread awareness.

### 🗺️ Live Pollution Map
- **Interactive Visualization**: See all reported incidents on a clustered map.
- **Filterable Data**: Sort reports by pollution type or status (Resolved/Pending).

---

## 🛠️ Tech Stack

### Frontend
- **React 18**
- **Tailwind CSS**
- **Lucide React**
- **React Leaflet**
- **HTML2Canvas**

### Backend
- **FastAPI**
- **OpenAI CLIP**
- **SQLite**
- **Pillow (PIL)**
- **JWT** & **BCrypt**

### Hybrid AI Research Pipeline
The `tech/` folder contains an advanced experimental pipeline that combines a **CNN classifier** with **CLIP** in a series architecture.

Instead of relying on a single model, this system merges the strengths of both:

- CNN handles detailed visual feature extraction
- CLIP provides contextual and semantic understanding
- Final predictions are derived from the strongest combined signal

This hybrid setup improves accuracy in real coastal environments where lighting, angles, and clutter can vary dramatically. It represents our best-performing research model and serves as a foundation for future upgrades.

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ Challenges We Faced

While building our project, we ran into several real-world challenges that helped us learn how to build a more reliable and practical system.

🧠 AI Misclassification & False Alerts

What went wrong:
At first, the AI sometimes marked clean beach images as pollution. This could have created unnecessary alerts and wasted effort.

How we fixed it:

We added a confidence threshold (85%)

Introduced a “No Waste” category for uncertain cases

Only high-confidence predictions are treated as actual pollution

This made the system more accurate and trustworthy.

📍 Location Data Issues

What went wrong:
Many images did not contain GPS data, which caused reports to appear without proper locations on the map.

How we fixed it:

Used GPS data from the image when available

Added browser-based location as a backup

Made sure every report has a location before submission

This ensured reliable location data across all devices.

🔐 User & Admin Access Control

What went wrong:
Managing different access levels for users and admins without affecting usability was challenging.

How we fixed it:

Implemented secure login using JWT

Protected important pages on the frontend

Added role checks on the backend

This kept the platform secure while remaining easy to use.

🗺️ Map Performance Issues

What went wrong:
As more pollution reports were added, the map started slowing down.

How we fixed it:

Optimized the data sent from the backend

Added filters to load only relevant markers

Reduced unnecessary map re-renders

This kept the map smooth and responsive.

🔗 Frontend & Backend Coordination

What went wrong:
Connecting image uploads, AI analysis, and database updates caused syncing issues at first.

How we fixed it:

Standardized API responses

Improved request–response handling

Used centralized state management

This made the entire system stable and consistent.

🚀 What We Learned

These challenges taught us that building real-world solutions is not just about features, but about accuracy, reliability, and user trust—especially for environmental and social impact projects.

**The problem it solves**

NaariSecure solves the problem of delayed or impossible emergency response by providing automatic, predictive, and continuous safety beyond manual SOS systems.

**Challenges we ran into**

- Designing a safety system that works even when the user cannot press SOS
- Handling real-time location tracking without draining battery
- Balancing user privacy with emergency data sharing
- Coordinating instant alerts to multiple stakeholders (guardians, portal, emergency services)
- Preventing false SOS triggers while keeping response fast

### Ascend AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/disha-darshak-ai-4fea) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Prof-chaos-5/Ascend-AI.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://bit.ly/4009waF) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co)

> From Confusion to Clarity: Your AI Career Guide!

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Cloud API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Cloud%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![gemini](https://img.shields.io/badge/gemini-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The idea came from seeing our own friends and seniors struggle during placement season. In our college (and so many others in Tier-2/Tier-3 cities), we have the coding skills, but we mess up because we don't have the right guidance.

We saw so many talented batchmates get rejected by ATS software just because their resume format was wrong, or freeze up during HR rounds because they never practised speaking in English. And career counsellors are super expensive, and so most of us just rely on random YouTube videos. 

And some tools exist too for free but they're all segregated at different platforms, making it hard for a user to find and access each tool. 

So,we wanted to build something that could be a "Digital Senior" for everyone—a personalised compass called Ascend AI that levels the confusion field & provides all career solutions at a single platform.

**Challenges we ran into**

During our build, we faced multiple problems, some of the major problems we faced were:

First, the "Hallucination" Problem: At first, the roadmap generator would suggest courses that didn't exist or were 5 years old. We had to spend a lot of time tweaking the prompts to ground the AI and make it stick to general, verifiable topics.

Second, PDF Parsing was a headache: Resumes come in weird formats—two columns, icons, tables. The AI used to get confused between the company name and the job title. We had to switch to Gemini’s vision capabilities to fix this.

Third, Voice Loops: The funniest (and most annoying) bug was during the mock interview—the mic would pick up the AI’s voice, send it back to the AI, and it would start talking to itself! I had to write some strict logic in the frontend to mute the mic the second the AI starts speaking.

Fourth, Token Limits: When users uploaded huge 4-page resumes, we hit API limits. I had to write a summarizer function to shrink the text down before sending it to the resume editor.

**Open Innovation**

Our project deals with the problem statement: "Students and workers lack visibility into skill gaps and employability risks. Analyze education data, skill trends, and job market signals to recommend upskilling paths." by providing career guidance and helper tools for upskilling one's career path

### CoLive
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/colive-4f63) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/chanchal-barak/CoLive) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://colive-match.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co)

> Turning Shared Spaces into Shared Comfort.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Finding a place to live is hard but finding the right people to live with is even harder—and that’s the real problem most platforms ignore. Students and young professionals often end up sharing spaces with strangers without knowing anything about their habits, schedules, cleanliness, budgets, or personalities. This leads to daily friction, unsafe situations, mental stress, and frequent relocation. CoLive-Match addresses this gap by focusing on people compatibility before property. Instead of just listing rooms, it helps individuals find roommates whose lifestyle, routines, and expectations align with theirs. It reduces conflicts, saves time lost in trial-and-error housing, and creates safer, more stable co-living environments—something current rental and PG platforms don’t actively solve.
In short, it shifts the focus from “finding a room fast” to “finding the right people to live with,” making co-living more stable, transparent, and easier to manage.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges while building Colive-Match was designing a system that actually matches people based on lifestyle compatibility, not just basic filters like budget or location. Early on, the matching logic felt too generic — it was giving similar results to any rental listing platform, which defeated the core purpose of the product.

We also ran into issues while structuring user inputs. People describe habits differently (for example, “late sleeper,” “night owl,” “works night shifts”), and converting that into something measurable for matching wasn’t straightforward. This led to inconsistent results during testing.

To solve this, we reworked the onboarding questions to be more behavior-focused and standardized the options instead of relying on open text. On the technical side, we simplified the compatibility logic first, tested it with small datasets, and then gradually layered more conditions. Iterating like this helped us move from a vague idea of “matching roommates” to something that actually reflects how people live day-to-day.

Another hurdle was making the interface feel trustworthy and not like a typical listing site. We kept refining the layout and flow until it felt more like a guided decision process rather than just browsing rooms.

**Open Innovation**

CoLive-Match fits naturally into the open innovation track because it addresses a real, everyday problem without being limited to a specific industry or sponsor brief. Housing and shared living affect students, interns, and working professionals across cities, yet most existing solutions focus only on listing rooms—not on whether the people living together are actually compatible.

This project takes a different approach by treating co-living as a people problem first and a property problem second. It brings in the idea of lifestyle-based matching, helping users find roommates they can realistically live with, not just spaces they can afford. That makes it relevant across campuses, urban housing, and migration scenarios where individuals move to unfamiliar cities and lack trusted networks.

Open innovation is about identifying gaps that haven’t been solved well and building practical solutions around them. CoLive-Match does exactly that—it rethinks how shared living decisions are made and introduces a system that prioritizes safety, comfort, and long-term compatibility instead of quick, transactional bookings.

### BrokeBuddy
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/brokebuddy-24b6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aakritixyz/broke-buddy) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.canva.com/design/DAG3L-Q69FQ/JagMME5zZGSwdTwCVh6kiw/edit?utm_content=DAG3L-Q69FQ&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=sharebutton) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co)

> Your Buddy for Smart Savings

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Figma](https://img.shields.io/badge/Figma-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

BrokeBuddy is designed to fix the "leaky bucket" problem in student finances, where small, impulsive daily expenses (like that Rs 150 coffee or extra snacks) prevent long-term financial security. It solves the disconnect between current spending and future goals by:

Reframing Opportunity Cost: Instead of just showing a "minus Rs 300" in a bank statement, the app warns users that "This pizza just delayed your new laptop by 1 week." It makes the trade-offs of spending visible and personal.

Lowering the Barrier to Entry for Investing: Most students feel they don't have enough money to "invest." BrokeBuddy makes it accessible through micro-investments, allowing users to put small, spare change into low-risk options suggested by the app’s AI.

Social Safety Net: The "Committee of Buddies" (P2P lending) removes the embarrassment and high interest rates of small debts. It formalizes lending between friends at a minimum rate, keeping money within the peer circle.

Gamifying Financial Discipline: By using "Buddycoins," streaks, and challenges, it turns the "chore" of budgeting into a game, encouraging Gen-Z users to stick to their habits for rewards rather than just out of duty.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a finance app for students involved more than just tracking numbers; it required balancing social trust with technical security.

The Bug/Hurdle: A major technical challenge was the automated expense tracking accuracy. Many students use a mix of UPI, cash, and digital wallets. Initially, the app struggled to categorize "mixed transactions" (e.g., a single UPI payment at a grocery store that included both essential food and "useless" snacks).

How I got over it: We implemented a split-transaction logic and a custom AI tagging system. Instead of guessing, the app prompts the user with a quick, friendly "Was that all groceries or did a snack sneak in?" notification. This human-in-the-loop approach improved data accuracy while reinforcing the "awareness" part of our mission.

The Social Lending Hurdle: Designing the P2P lending feature was tricky—we had to ensure it didn't ruin friendships! To solve this, we built a transparent repayment tracker with automated reminders. By making the "Buddy Buddy" system based on community-set rules rather than just informal "IOUs," we reduced the social anxiety and risk of default between friends.

**Beginner's track - Your first hack starts here!**

This is a Beginner Track because it focuses on creating a high-impact user experience for a problem we face every day: student financial instability. Our project, BrokeBuddy, demonstrates our ability to take complex financial concepts like 'opportunity cost' and 'micro-investing' and translate them into a simple, gamified mobile application using clean code and user-centric design.

### High Risk Pregnancy Detection
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/hybrid-clinical-and-machine-learning-framework-for-high-risk-pregnancy-detection-ffd7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AasmaGupta/Maternal-Health-Risk-Prediction) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HLyaAL6HoOZ74furwHS76WCmUlvSede5?usp=drive_link) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/rBul94YXeFU?si=HuBA-9li6xx9p4M8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co)

> Predict Earlier Personalize Better Protect Lives

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Matplotlib](https://img.shields.io/badge/Matplotlib-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

High-risk pregnancies contribute to millions of maternal and infant deaths globally, many of which occur due to late risk detection, limited screening tools, and lack of personalized clinical insight — especially in resource-constrained or rural settings. Patients are often unaware of the severity of their condition until complications arise, while healthcare providers must make decisions under time pressure with incomplete contextual data.

Existing approaches typically rely either on generalized clinical guidelines or black-box machine learning predictions. Clinical rule systems are interpretable but rigid and difficult to scale across diverse populations. Pure ML models identify patterns but often lack medical reasoning, transparency, and contextual awareness.

This project introduces a hybrid clinical + machine learning decision-support framework that:

Predicts pregnancy risk levels earlier using ensemble AI models

Integrates clinical thresholds with data-driven learning

Provides explainable outputs (SHAP, feature importance, PDP)

Supports both doctors and patients through separate interfaces

Enables personalized insight rather than generalized recommendations

By assisting early screening and interpretation, the system helps:

Reduce diagnostic delay

Support overloaded healthcare systems

Improve decision confidence

Promote preventive care awareness

Ultimately, the goal is not to replace clinicians, but to augment medical judgment with transparent AI-driven intelligence for safer maternal outcomes.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Feature inconsistency across pipelines
While training ensemble models, mismatches in feature counts and naming conventions caused prediction failures. This was resolved by building a unified preprocessing pipeline and saving the full pipeline object rather than individual models.

2. Model prediction bias toward a single class
Initial predictions frequently returned “Low Risk” due to dataset imbalance and preprocessing issues. I addressed this by validating feature distributions, reviewing class mappings, and verifying pipeline transformations using controlled test inputs.

3. Bridging ML backend with web interfaces

4. Explainability visualization integration
Dynamic visualization of SHAP and feature importance inside the UI required experimentation with rendering strategies and data flow optimization to ensure interpretability without slowing the interface.

5. Balancing usability vs technical depth
Designing both doctor and patient interfaces meant translating complex model outputs into meaningful insights. Iterative UI refinement ensured outputs remained understandable without oversimplifying clinical relevance.

These challenges strengthened the system’s robustness and helped shape it into a practical decision-support prototype rather than just a standalone ML model.

**Open Innovation**

This project fits the **Open Innovation** track because it addresses a real-world healthcare challenge that is not confined to a single domain, and early detection of high-risk pregnancies by combining machine learning, clinical reasoning, and accessible digital tools.

The solution bridges gaps between medical expertise and AI by integrating clinical rules with ensemble machine learning models to enable early risk screening, explainable insights, and personalized recommendations. It is designed to support doctors, patients, and underserved communities where access to specialized maternal care and decision-support tools is limited.

Rather than focusing on a narrow technical problem, the project tackles a broader societal issue, reducing maternal and infant health risks through accessible, interpretable, and scalable technology. Its hybrid architecture, explainability features, and deployable web interface demonstrate innovation beyond standard model-building, aligning directly with the spirit of Open Innovation by applying interdisciplinary thinking to improve real-world outcomes.

### LearnIt
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/learnit-b70b) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://learn-it-f999ebb5.base44.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co)

> Learn-Share-Repeat

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Learn – Share – Repeat:

The core idea is simple:
Learn a skill
Share a skill
Repeat the cycle, growing both knowledge and confidence

Learn New Skills from Real People:

Users can learn practical, academic, creative, or technical skills directly from individuals who already have experience in them.
Programming, design, languages, music, fitness, academics, and more
Learning from people, not just prerecorded content
Doubt-clearing and real-world explanations made easy
This makes learning more relatable, interactive, and effective than traditional one-way platforms.

Teach & Tutor Using Your Existing Skills:

Anyone can become a tutor on LearnIt—no formal degree required.
Share skills you already know
Teach beginners or intermediate learners
Gain teaching experience and confidence
Build a personal learning/teaching profile
This lowers the barrier to teaching and allows knowledge to flow freely across the community.

Peer-to-Peer Knowledge Exchange:

LearnIt creates a safe and collaborative environment where:
Learners and tutors interact directly
Users can switch roles: learner today, tutor tomorrow
Skills are exchanged, not gatekept
This makes the platform more inclusive and empowering.

How LearnIt Makes Learning Easier & Safer:

Easier:-
No need to search across multiple platforms
Learn and teach within the same ecosystem
Simple onboarding for both learners and tutors

Safer:-
Verified user profiles and skill listings
Community feedback and ratings
Clear learning goals and structured sessions

Why LearnIt Matters:-
Encourages continuous learning
Turns knowledge into a shared resource
Helps people grow without expensive courses
Builds a community driven by curiosity and collaboration
LearnIt doesn’t just teach skills — it builds learners who become teachers.

**Challenges we ran into**

Bug / Hurdle Faced While Building LearnIt:

One of the biggest hurdles we faced while building LearnIt was designing a system where a user can seamlessly switch between being a learner and a tutor without creating confusion in the app flow or data structure.

The Problem:

Initially, we treated learners and tutors as separate user types. This led to multiple issues:
Duplicate user profiles for the same person
Complex database relationships
Confusing navigation when a user wanted to both learn and teach
Difficulty maintaining consistency in user data (skills, sessions, ratings)
This went against the core idea of LearnIt — learn → share → repeat.

How We Solved It:

We rethought the problem from a role-based perspective instead of fixed user types.
Created a single user profile
Allowed users to toggle roles dynamically (learner / tutor)
Stored skills as attributes rather than identity
Used conditional UI rendering based on the current role
This simplified both the backend logic and the user experience.

The Outcome:

Cleaner and more scalable architecture
Smooth switching between learning and teaching
Reduced redundancy and fewer edge-case bugs
A UX that truly reflects the platform’s philosophy

Key Learning:

This hurdle taught us an important lesson:
Design decisions should reflect real user behavior, not assumptions.
By aligning the system design with how people naturally learn and share skills, we turned a major hurdle into one of LearnIt’s strongest features.

**Beginner's track - Your first hack starts here!**

LearnIt is being built as a learning-focused project while we ourselves are still early in our development journey. This hackathon is an opportunity for us to explore real-world problem solving, understand full-stack development, and learn how to turn an idea into a working product.

As beginners, we are experimenting with core concepts like user flows, backend logic, authentication, and database design while building LearnIt. The project reflects our learning process—iterating on ideas, overcoming challenges, and improving through feedback.

The Beginner’s Track perfectly aligns with our goal of learning by building, making mistakes, and growing as developers while creating something meaningful and impactful.

**Open Innovation**

LearnIt is an open-ended solution designed to address a real-world problem without being limited to a predefined problem statement. It reimagines how people learn and share skills by enabling anyone to be both a learner and a tutor within the same platform.

The project focuses on building a flexible, community-driven ecosystem where knowledge flows freely across domains such as academics, technology, and creative skills. By encouraging peer-to-peer learning and role-switching, LearnIt promotes innovation through collaboration rather than rigid structures.

This freedom to explore, iterate, and innovate aligns perfectly with the Open Innovation track, where creativity and impactful ideas are the core focus.

### SafeRoutes
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/saferoutes-b9d5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Arunima2007/safeRoute) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Lean%20In%20Hacks%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://leanin-hacks-7.devfolio.co)

> Route Smarter, Not Harder

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Maps API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Maps%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Folium](https://img.shields.io/badge/Folium-333333?style=flat-square) ![Plotly](https://img.shields.io/badge/Plotly-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problems SafeRoute is Solving:
1. Safety Concerns During Travel 🛡️

Problem: Women and vulnerable travelers often feel unsafe on certain routes, especially at night
Impact: Limited mobility, anxiety, and increased risk of crime
Solution: AI-powered safety scoring based on crime data, lighting conditions, and historical incidents

2. Lack of Multi-Factor Route Optimization ⚖️

Problem: Existing navigation apps (Google Maps, etc.) only optimize for time/distance
Impact: Users may take fast routes that are unsafe or heavily polluted
Solution: Comprehensive scoring across Safety, Speed, and Environmental factors

3. Air Quality & Environmental Health 🌱

Problem: Delhi has severe air pollution; some routes expose travelers to much higher PM2.5 levels
Impact: Respiratory issues, long-term health problems
Solution: Route recommendations that minimize exposure to pollution hotspots

4. Information Asymmetry 📊

Problem: Travelers lack access to integrated data about crime, traffic, pollution, and safety
Impact: Inability to make informed decisions about route choices
Solution: Transparent, data-driven insights with explainable AI scoring

5. One-Size-Fits-All Navigation 🎯

Problem: Current apps don't allow users to prioritize what matters most to them
Impact: Parents, elderly, women, and eco-conscious users have different needs
Solution: Customizable preferences (Safety First, Fastest, Eco-Friendly, Balanced)

6. Hidden Risk Factors ⚠️

Problem: Routes may look fine on paper but have hidden dangers (poor lighting, high crime areas)
Impact: Unexpected safety incidents
Solution: Predictive risk assessment using machine learning on historical data

Core Value Proposition:
"Most navigation apps get you there fast. SafeRoute Delhi gets you there safe, fast, AND sustainably—while giving you the power to choose what matters most."
This is particularly valuable for:

👩 Women traveling alone
👴 Elderly citizens
🌍 Environmentally conscious travelers
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Families with children
🏃 Late-night commuters

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into:1. Data Integration & API Limitations 🔌

Challenge: Integrating multiple data sources (Google Maps, crime data, air quality APIs) with different formats and rate limits
Impact: Inconsistent data availability and synchronization issues
Solution: Implemented caching mechanisms and fallback strategies for missing data points
2. Real-time Data Accuracy 📡

Challenge: Crime and pollution data often has delays; real-time traffic data can be expensive
Impact: Potential mismatch between predicted safety and actual conditions
Solution: Used historical patterns with time-based weighting and clearly communicated data freshness to users
3. Machine Learning Model Training 🤖

Challenge: Limited labeled training data for safety prediction; imbalanced dataset with more "safe" routes than "risky" ones
Impact: Model initially biased toward marking most routes as safe
Solution: Applied SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling) and feature engineering to improve model balance
4. Polyline Decoding & Route Visualization 🗺️

Challenge: Google Maps polyline encoding caused route rendering issues on folium maps
Impact: Routes appeared incorrectly or didn't display at all
Solution: Implemented robust polyline decoding with error handling and coordinate validation
5. Scoring Algorithm Calibration ⚖️

Challenge: Balancing three different metrics (safety, speed, eco) with different scales and priorities
Impact: One metric could dominate recommendations unfairly
Solution: Normalized all scores to 0-100 scale and implemented weighted composite scoring based on user preferences
6. Performance & Response Time ⏱️

Challenge: Analyzing multiple routes with ML predictions took too long (15-20 seconds)
Impact: Poor user experience and potential timeouts
Solution: Optimized route sampling, parallel processing, and API call batching
7. Frontend-Backend Communication 🔄

Challenge: Streamlit's stateful nature conflicted with dynamic API responses
Impact: Stale data showing after new searches, session state bugs
Solution: Implemented proper session state management with clear reset triggers
8. Geographic Coverage 🌍

Challenge: Safety and pollution data unavailable for all areas of Delhi NCR
Impact: Incomplete analysis for routes in less-monitored areas
Solution: Used interpolation for missing data and clearly indicated confidence levels
9. User Experience Design 🎨

Challenge: Presenting complex multi-metric analysis without overwhelming users
Impact: Initial versions were too technical and confusing
Solution: Progressive disclosure with tabs, visual scoring badges, and clear recommended route highlighting
10. API Cost Management 💰

Challenge: Google Maps API costs could escalate with multiple route requests
Impact: Budget constraints for hackathon/demo
Solution: Implemented request caching and limited alternative routes to top 3

> Preventing un-necessary expenses.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

So while researching the subject, we realized there were two main problems that lead to bad finance management for the youth especially:

**Small Transactions feel ignored:** People often spend small amounts on say a chocolate or for a taxi but never count it in their expenditure. To tackle this, we make the user enter their expenses everyday and keep a track of it, along with thee daily monthly and weekly cumulative expenditure.

**UPI is too smooth:** When you are not paying by cash, you feel like you're losing nothing which is ofcourse not true, to increase the friction in UPI payments, we introduce an overlay over payment apps like BHIM and phonepe which allows us to block the transaction TILL the user enters the amount so we can keep a track of it.

**UPI is too smooth:** Emergency funds are a big problem for our generation. You get your salary/pocket money and it's exhaused in the first half of the month and you're left broke. To solve this, make an emergency fund for a part of the money which you can only access by entering a set password, so you have time to think twice before spending your savings and also as a bonus keep some money away from intruders.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest problem was building the mobile app, which we therefore have not released yet. We will add it before the next round of the hackathon. Since we had a crunch of time, we are done with a web based protoype to show the basic functioning and UI ideas.

Things we will add:
1. grouping expenses using LLM
2. ML models to predict expenditure
3. QOL features like partnering up with other brands and introduce a reward system.

**Beginner's track - Your first hack starts here!**

We're all first year students and the product is also not fully polished, so it belongs here.
